name: _root_.AlgHomClass.unitization_injective'
informal: A sufficient condition for injectivity of `NonUnitalSubalgebra.unitization` when the scalars are a commutative ring. When the scalars are a field, one should use the more natural `NonUnitalStarSubalgebra.unitization_injective` whose hypothesis is easier to verify.

name: _root_.AlgHomClass.unitization_injective
informal: This is a generic version which allows us to prove both `NonUnitalSubalgebra.unitization_injective` and `NonUnitalStarSubalgebra.unitization_injective`.
signature: {F R S A : Type*} [Field R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A] [SetLike S A] [hSA : NonUnitalSubringClass S A] [hSRA : SMulMemClass S R A] (s : S) (h1 : 1 ∉ s) [FunLike F (Unitization R s) A] [AlgHomClass F R (Unitization R s) A] (f : F) (hf : ∀ x : s, f x = x) : Function.Injective f

name: divisor_closure_eq_closure
informal: Let x, y ∈ M₀. If x * y can be written as a product of units and prime elements, then x can be written as a product of units and prime elements.
signature: [CommMonoidWithZero M₀] [IsCancelMulZero M₀] (x y : M₀) (hxy : x * y ∈ closure { r : M₀ | IsUnit r ∨ Prime r}) : x ∈ closure { r : M₀ | IsUnit r ∨ Prime r}

name: Fin.sum_neg_one_pow_eq_zero
informal: This is a classic "telescoping sum" lemma. It says: `r₀ - (r₀ + r₁) + (r₁ + r₂) - (r₂+ r₃) + ⋯ ± (rₙ₋₁ + rₙ) ∓ rₙ = 0`. The chosen spelling, which gives definitional power over `d`, is influenced by downstream applications such as `Module.sum_neg_one_pow_finrank_eq_zero_of_exact`.
signature: {α : Type*} [AddCommGroup α] {n : ℕ} (d : Fin (n + 2) → α) (r : Fin (n + 1) → α) (h_first : d 0 = r 0) (h_mid : ∀ i : Fin n, d i.succ.castSucc = r i.castSucc + r i.succ) (h_last : d (Fin.last _) = r (Fin.last _)) : ∑ i, (-1) ^ i.val • d i = 0

name: length_le_sum_of_one_le
informal: If all elements in a list are bounded below by `1`, then the length of the list is bounded by the sum of the elements.
signature: (L : List ℕ) (h : ∀ i ∈ L, 1 ≤ i) : L.length ≤ L.sum

name: sum_Ico_Ico_comm

name: sum_Ico_Ico_comm'
informal: The two ways of summing over `(i, j)` in the range `a ≤ i < j < b` are equal.
signature: {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (a b : ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℕ → M) : (∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico a b, ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico (i + 1) b, f i j) = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico a b, ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico a j, f i j

name: tensor_ext₃'
informal: Extensionality lemma for morphisms from a module of the form `(M₁ ⊗ M₂) ⊗ M₃`.
signature: {f g : (M₁ ⊗ M₂) ⊗ M₃ ⟶ M₄} (h : ∀ m₁ m₂ m₃, f (m₁ ⊗ₜ m₂ ⊗ₜ m₃) = g (m₁ ⊗ₜ m₂ ⊗ₜ m₃)) : f = g

signature: {f g : M₁ ⊗ (M₂ ⊗ M₃) ⟶ M₄} (h : ∀ m₁ m₂ m₃, f (m₁ ⊗ₜ (m₂ ⊗ₜ m₃)) = g (m₁ ⊗ₜ (m₂ ⊗ₜ m₃))) : f = g

name: charP_of_injective_ringHom

name: charZero_of_injective_ringHom
informal: If a ring homomorphism `R →+* A` is injective and `R` has characteristic zero then so does `A`.

name: charZero_of_injective_algebraMap
informal: If the algebra map `R →+* A` is injective and `R` has characteristic zero then so does `A`.

name: expChar_of_injective_ringHom
informal: If a ring homomorphism `R →+* A` is injective then `A` has the same exponential characteristic as `R`.

name: expChar_of_injective_algebraMap
informal: If the algebra map `R →+* A` is injective then `A` has the same exponential characteristic as `R`.
signature: [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] (h : Function.Injective (algebraMap R A)) (q : ℕ) [ExpChar R q] : ExpChar A q

name: algebraRat.charP_zero
informal: A nontrivial `ℚ`-algebra has `CharP` equal to zero. This cannot be a (local) instance because it would immediately form a loop with the instance `DivisionRing.toRatAlgebra`. It's probably easier to go the other way: prove `CharZero R` and automatically receive an `Algebra ℚ R` instance.
signature: [Semiring R] [Algebra ℚ R] : CharP R 0

name: algebraRat.charZero
informal: A nontrivial `ℚ`-algebra has characteristic zero. This cannot be a (local) instance because it would immediately form a loop with the instance `DivisionRing.toRatAlgebra`. It's probably easier to go the other way: prove `CharZero R` and automatically receive an `Algebra ℚ R` instance.
signature: [Ring R] [Algebra ℚ R] : CharZero R

name: cast_ne_zero_of_ne_of_prime
informal: If a ring `R` is of characteristic `p`, then for any prime number `q` different from `p`, it is not zero in `R`.
signature: [Nontrivial R] {p q : ℕ} [CharP R p] (hq : q.Prime) (hneq : p ≠ q) : (q : R) ≠ 0

name: Int.cast_injOn_of_ringChar_ne_two
informal: If two integers from `{0, 1, -1}` result in equal elements in a ring `R` that is nontrivial and of characteristic not `2`, then they are equal.
signature: {R : Type*} [NonAssocRing R] [Nontrivial R] (hR : ringChar R ≠ 2) : ({0, 1, -1} : Set ℤ).InjOn ((↑) : ℤ → R)

name: isUnit_iff_not_dvd_char_of_ringChar_ne_zero
informal: A prime `p` is a unit in a commutative ring `R` of nonzero characteristic iff it does not divide the characteristic.
signature: (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hR : ringChar R ≠ 0) : IsUnit (p : R) ↔ ¬p ∣ ringChar R

name: isUnit_iff_not_dvd_char
informal: A prime `p` is a unit in a finite commutative ring `R` iff it does not divide the characteristic.
signature: (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [Finite R] : IsUnit (p : R) ↔ ¬p ∣ ringChar R

name: prime_dvd_char_iff_dvd_card
informal: The prime divisors of the characteristic of a finite commutative ring are exactly the prime divisors of its cardinality.
signature: {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Fintype R] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : p ∣ ringChar R ↔ p ∣ Fintype.card R

name: not_isUnit_prime_of_dvd_card

name: charP_zero_or_prime_power
informal: In a local ring the characteristic is either zero or a prime power.
signature: (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (q : ℕ) [char_R_q : CharP R q] : q = 0 ∨ IsPrimePow q

name: isEmpty_algebraRat_iff_mixedCharZero

signature: [CharZero R] : IsEmpty (Algebra ℚ R) ↔ ∃ p > 0, MixedCharZero R p

name: isSquare_of_charTwo'
informal: If `ringChar R = 2`, where `R` is a finite reduced commutative ring, then every `a : R` is a square.
signature: {R : Type*} [Finite R] [CommRing R] [IsReduced R] [CharP R 2] (a : R) : IsSquare a

name: charP_center_iff

signature: {R : Type u} [Ring R] {p : ℕ} : CharP (Subring.center R) p ↔ CharP R p

name: of.zero_exact

name: convs_succ

name: of_correctness_of_nth_stream_eq_none

signature: (nth_stream_eq_none : IntFractPair.stream v n = none) : v = (of v).convs (n - 1)

name: of_correctness_of_terminates
informal: If `GenContFract.of v` terminates, then there is `n : ℕ` such that the `n`th convergent is exactly `v`.

name: of_inv_fr_num_lt_num_of_pos

name: stream_succ_nth_fr_num_lt_nth_fr_num_rat

name: squashSeq_eq_self_of_terminated

name: squashSeq_nth_of_lt

name: squashGCF_eq_self_of_terminated

name: eq_zero_of_mul_eq_self_left

name: LieIdeal.solvable_iff_le_radical

signature: [IsNoetherian R L] (I : LieIdeal R L) : IsSolvable I ↔ I ≤ radical R L

name: ker_restrict_eq_bot_of_isCartanSubalgebra

signature: [IsNoetherian R L] [IsArtinian R L] (H : LieSubalgebra R L) [H.IsCartanSubalgebra] : LinearMap.ker ((killingForm R L).restrict H) = ⊥

name: isInternal_prime_power_torsion
informal: A finitely generated torsion module over a Dedekind domain is an internal direct sum of its `p i ^ e i`-torsion submodules where `p i` are factors of `(⊤ : Submodule R M).annihilator` and `e i` are their multiplicities.
signature: [Module.Finite R M] (hM : Module.IsTorsion R M) : DirectSum.IsInternal fun p : (factors (⊤ : Submodule R M).annihilator).toFinset => torsionBySet R M (p ^ (factors (⊤ : Submodule R M).annihilator).count ↑p : Ideal R)

name: of_rank_le
informal: A finitely-generated `R`-submodule of `V` of rank at least the `K`-rank of `V` is a lattice.
signature: [Module.Finite K V] [IsFractionRing R K] {M : Submodule R V} (hfg : M.FG) (hr : Module.rank K V ≤ Module.rank R M) : IsLattice K M where fg

name: Submodule.isInternal_prime_power_torsion_of_pid
informal: A finitely generated torsion module over a PID is an internal direct sum of its `p i ^ e i`-torsion submodules for some primes `p i` and numbers `e i`.
signature: [Module.Finite R M] (hM : Module.IsTorsion R M) : DirectSum.IsInternal fun p : (factors (⊤ : Submodule R M).annihilator).toFinset => torsionBy R M (IsPrincipal.generator (p : Ideal R) ^ (factors (⊤ : Submodule R M).annihilator).count ↑p)

name: IsAddTorsionFree.of_module_nnrat

name: IsAddTorsionFree.of_module_rat
informal: A `ℚ≥0`-module is torsion-free as a group. This instance will fire for any monoid `M`, so is local unless needed elsewhere.
signature: [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℚ M] : IsAddTorsionFree M where nsmul_right_injective n hn x y hxy

name: LinearEquiv.isScalarTower
informal: The module instance from `AddEquiv.module` is compatible with the `R`-module structures, if the `AddEquiv` is induced by an `R`-module isomorphism.

name: Real.finrank_eq_int_finrank_of_discrete

signature: {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {s : Set E} (hs : DiscreteTopology (span ℤ s)) : Set.finrank ℝ s = Set.finrank ℤ s

name: AddMonoidAlgebra.mem_ideal_span_of'_image
informal: If `x` belongs to the ideal generated by generators in `s`, then every element of the support of `x` factors additively through an element of `s`.
signature: [AddMonoid A] [Semiring k] {s : Set A} {x : AddMonoidAlgebra k A} : x ∈ Ideal.span (AddMonoidAlgebra.of' k A '' s) ↔ ∀ m ∈ x.coeff.support, ∃ m' ∈ s, ∃ d, m = d + m'

name: mem_closure_of_mem_span_closure
informal: If the image of an element `m : M` in `R[M]` belongs the submodule generated by the closure of some `s : Set M` then `m ∈ closure s`.
signature: [AddMonoid M] [Nontrivial R] {m : M} {s : Set M} (h : of' R M m ∈ Submodule.span R (Submonoid.closure <| of' R M '' s)) : m ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure s

name: funext_set
informal: Two multivariate polynomials over an integral domain are equal if they are equal when evaluated anywhere in a box with infinite sides.
signature: (h : ∀ x ∈ Set.pi .univ s, eval x p = eval x q) : p = q

name: exists_nat_pow_near
informal: Every x greater than or equal to 1 is between two successive natural-number powers of every y greater than one.

name: exists_mem_Ico_zpow
informal: Every positive `x` is between two successive integer powers of another `y` greater than one. This is the same as `exists_mem_Ioc_zpow`, but with ≤ and < the other way around.

name: exists_mem_Ioc_zpow
informal: Every positive `x` is between two successive integer powers of another `y` greater than one. This is the same as `exists_mem_Ico_zpow`, but with ≤ and < the other way around.

name: exists_pow_lt_of_lt_one
informal: For any `y < 1` and any positive `x`, there exists `n : ℕ` with `y ^ n < x`.
signature: (hx : 0 < x) (hy : y < 1) : ∃ n : ℕ, y ^ n < x

name: exists_isGLB
informal: A nonempty, bounded below set of real numbers has a greatest lower bound.
signature: (hne : s.Nonempty) (hbdd : BddBelow s) : ∃ x, IsGLB s x

name: sSup_nonpos
informal: As `sSup s = 0` when `s` is an empty set of reals, it suffices to show that all elements of `s` are nonpositive to show that `sSup s ≤ 0`.
signature: (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, x ≤ 0) : sSup s ≤ 0

name: iSup_nonpos
informal: As `⨆ i, f i = 0` when the domain of the real-valued function `f` is empty, it suffices to show that all values of `f` are nonpositive to show that `⨆ i, f i ≤ 0`.
signature: (hf : ∀ i, f i ≤ 0) : ⨆ i, f i ≤ 0

name: sInf_nonneg
informal: As `sInf s = 0` when `s` is an empty set of reals, it suffices to show that all elements of `s` are nonnegative to show that `0 ≤ sInf s`.
signature: (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, 0 ≤ x) : 0 ≤ sInf s

name: iInf_nonneg
informal: As `⨅ i, f i = 0` when the domain of the real-valued function `f` is empty, it suffices to show that all values of `f` are nonnegative to show that `0 ≤ ⨅ i, f i`.
signature: (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) : 0 ≤ iInf f

name: sSup_nonneg'
informal: As `sSup s = 0` when `s` is a set of reals that's unbounded above, it suffices to show that `s` contains a nonnegative element to show that `0 ≤ sSup s`.
signature: (hs : ∃ x ∈ s, 0 ≤ x) : 0 ≤ sSup s

name: iSup_nonneg'
informal: As `⨆ i, f i = 0` when the real-valued function `f` is unbounded above, it suffices to show that `f` takes a nonnegative value to show that `0 ≤ ⨆ i, f i`.
signature: (hf : ∃ i, 0 ≤ f i) : 0 ≤ ⨆ i, f i

name: sInf_nonpos'
informal: As `sInf s = 0` when `s` is a set of reals that's unbounded below, it suffices to show that `s` contains a nonpositive element to show that `sInf s ≤ 0`.
signature: (hs : ∃ x ∈ s, x ≤ 0) : sInf s ≤ 0

name: iInf_nonpos'
informal: As `⨅ i, f i = 0` when the real-valued function `f` is unbounded below, it suffices to show that `f` takes a nonpositive value to show that `0 ≤ ⨅ i, f i`.
signature: (hf : ∃ i, f i ≤ 0) : ⨅ i, f i ≤ 0

name: sSup_nonneg
informal: As `sSup s = 0` when `s` is a set of reals that's either empty or unbounded above, it suffices to show that all elements of `s` are nonnegative to show that `0 ≤ sSup s`.
signature: (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, 0 ≤ x) : 0 ≤ sSup s

name: iSup_nonneg
informal: As `⨆ i, f i = 0` when the domain of the real-valued function `f` is empty or unbounded above, it suffices to show that all values of `f` are nonnegative to show that `0 ≤ ⨆ i, f i`.
signature: (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) : 0 ≤ ⨆ i, f i

name: sInf_nonpos
informal: As `sInf s = 0` when `s` is a set of reals that's either empty or unbounded below, it suffices to show that all elements of `s` are nonpositive to show that `sInf s ≤ 0`.
signature: (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, x ≤ 0) : sInf s ≤ 0

name: iInf_nonpos
informal: As `⨅ i, f i = 0` when the domain of the real-valued function `f` is empty or unbounded below, it suffices to show that all values of `f` are nonpositive to show that `0 ≤ ⨅ i, f i`.
signature: (hf : ∀ i, f i ≤ 0) : ⨅ i, f i ≤ 0

name: prod_le_one
informal: If each `f i`, `i ∈ s` belongs to `[0, 1]`, then their product is less than or equal to one. See also `Finset.prod_le_one'` for the case of an ordered commutative multiplicative monoid.

name: MonovaryOn.sum_smul_sum_le_card_smul_sum
informal: **Chebyshev's Sum Inequality**: When `f` and `g` monovary together (e.g. they are both monotone/antitone), the scalar product of their sum is less than the size of the set times their scalar product.
signature: (hfg : MonovaryOn f g s) : (∑ i ∈ s, f i) • ∑ i ∈ s, g i ≤ #s • ∑ i ∈ s, f i • g i

name: AntivaryOn.card_smul_sum_le_sum_smul_sum
informal: **Chebyshev's Sum Inequality**: When `f` and `g` antivary together (e.g. one is monotone, the other is antitone), the scalar product of their sum is less than the size of the set times their scalar product.
signature: (hfg : AntivaryOn f g s) : #s • ∑ i ∈ s, f i • g i ≤ (∑ i ∈ s, f i) • ∑ i ∈ s, g i

name: MonovaryOn.sum_mul_sum_le_card_mul_sum
informal: **Chebyshev's Sum Inequality**: When `f` and `g` monovary together (e.g. they are both monotone/antitone), the product of their sum is less than the size of the set times their scalar product.
signature: (hfg : MonovaryOn f g s) : (∑ i ∈ s, f i) * ∑ i ∈ s, g i ≤ #s * ∑ i ∈ s, f i * g i

name: one_div_le_one_div
informal: For the single implications with fewer assumptions, see `one_div_le_one_div_of_le` and `le_of_one_div_le_one_div`

name: one_div_lt_one_div

name: one_div_le_one_div_of_neg

name: one_div_lt_one_div_of_neg
informal: For the single implications with fewer assumptions, see `one_div_lt_one_div_of_lt` and `lt_of_one_div_lt_one_div`

name: subsingleton_floorRing

name: subsingleton_floorSemiring

signature: {R} [Semiring R] [LinearOrder R] : Subsingleton (FloorSemiring R)

name: sum_le_sum_Ioc
informal: Sharp upper bound for the sum of a finset of integers that is bounded above, `Ioc` version.

name: sum_le_sum_range
informal: Sharp upper bound for the sum of a finset of integers that is bounded above, `range` version.
signature: {s : Finset ℤ} {c : ℤ} (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, x ≤ c) : ∑ x ∈ s, x ≤ ∑ n ∈ range #s, (c - n)

name: sum_Ico_le_sum
informal: Sharp lower bound for the sum of a finset of integers that is bounded below, `Ico` version.
signature: {s : Finset ℤ} {c : ℤ} (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, c ≤ x) : ∑ x ∈ Ico c (c + #s), x ≤ ∑ x ∈ s, x

name: sum_range_le_sum
informal: Sharp lower bound for the sum of a finset of integers that is bounded below, `range` version.
signature: {s : Finset ℤ} {c : ℤ} (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, c ≤ x) : ∑ n ∈ range #s, (c + n) ≤ ∑ x ∈ s, x

name: abs_sub_left_of_mem_uIcc
informal: If `c ∈ [a, b]`, then the distance between `a` and `c` is less than or equal to that of `a` and `b`

name: abs_sub_right_of_mem_uIcc
informal: If `x ∈ [a, b]`, then the distance between `c` and `b` is less than or equal to that of `a` and `b`

name: bddAbove_range_mul
informal: If `u v : α → β` are nonnegative and bounded above, then `u * v` is bounded above.

name: StrictAnti.const_smul
informal: Scalar multiplication on the left by a positive element preserves strict antitonicity.
signature: [PosSMulStrictMono α β] {γ : Type*} [Preorder γ] {f : γ → β} (hf : StrictAnti f) (ha : 0 < a) : StrictAnti fun x ↦ a • f x

name: Monotone.smul_const
informal: Scalar multiplication on the right by a nonnegative element preserves monotonicity.
signature: [SMulPosMono α β] {γ : Type*} [Preorder γ] {f : γ → α} (hf : Monotone f) (hb : 0 ≤ b) : Monotone fun x ↦ f x • b

name: Antitone.smul_const
informal: Scalar multiplication on the right by a nonnegative element preserves antitonicity.
signature: [SMulPosMono α β] {γ : Type*} [Preorder γ] {f : γ → α} (hf : Antitone f) (hb : 0 ≤ b) : Antitone fun x ↦ f x • b

name: StrictMono.smul_const
informal: Scalar multiplication on the right by a positive element preserves strict monotonicity.
signature: [SMulPosStrictMono α β] {γ : Type*} [Preorder γ] {f : γ → α} (hf : StrictMono f) (hb : 0 < b) : StrictMono fun x ↦ f x • b

name: StrictAnti.smul_const
informal: Scalar multiplication on the right by a positive element preserves strict antitonicity.
signature: [SMulPosStrictMono α β] {γ : Type*} [Preorder γ] {f : γ → α} (hf : StrictAnti f) (hb : 0 < b) : StrictAnti fun x ↦ f x • b

signature: {F' E₁' E₂' : Type*} [FunLike F' E₁' E₂'] [AddGroup E₁'] [LE E₁'] [AddRightMono E₁'] [AddGroup E₂'] [LE E₂'] [AddRightMono E₂'] [AddMonoidHomClass F' E₁' E₂'] (h : ∀ f : F', ∀ x, 0 ≤ x → 0 ≤ f x) : OrderHomClass F' E₁' E₂' where map_rel f a b hab

name: add_le_add_iff_right'
informal: Addition in `WithBot (WithTop α)` is right cancellative provided the element being cancelled is not `⊤` or `⊥`.

name: IsOrderedRing.toCharZero
informal: A nontrivial ordered ring is of characteristic zero. This is not made a global instance for performance reasons.
signature: [Nontrivial R] : CharZero R

name: Nat.geomSum_lt
informal: If all the elements of a finset of naturals are less than `n`, then the sum of their powers of `m ≥ 2` is less than `m ^ n`.

name: apply_intCast_le_one

name: mul_nonneg_of_three

signature: [ExistsAddOfLE R] [MulPosStrictMono R] [PosMulStrictMono R] [AddLeftMono R] [AddLeftReflectLE R] (a b c : R) : 0 ≤ a * b ∨ 0 ≤ b * c ∨ 0 ≤ c * a

name: mul_self_add_mul_self_eq_zero
informal: The sum of two squares is zero iff both elements are zero.
signature: [NoZeroDivisors R] [ExistsAddOfLE R] [PosMulMono R] [AddLeftMono R] : a * a + b * b = 0 ↔ a = 0 ∧ b = 0

name: two_mul_le_add_sq
informal: Binary, squared, and division-free **arithmetic mean-geometric mean inequality** (aka AM-GM inequality) for linearly ordered commutative semirings.
signature: [ExistsAddOfLE R] [MulPosStrictMono R] [AddLeftReflectLE R] [AddLeftMono R] (a b : R) : 2 * a * b ≤ a ^ 2 + b ^ 2

name: four_mul_le_sq_add
informal: Binary, squared, and division-free **arithmetic mean-geometric mean inequality** (aka AM-GM inequality) for linearly ordered commutative semirings.
signature: [ExistsAddOfLE R] [MulPosStrictMono R] [AddLeftReflectLE R] [AddLeftMono R] (a b : R) : 4 * a * b ≤ (a + b) ^ 2

name: two_mul_le_add_of_sq_le_mul

signature: [ExistsAddOfLE R] [MulPosStrictMono R] [PosMulStrictMono R] [AddLeftReflectLE R] [AddLeftMono R] {a b r : R} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (ht : r ^ 2 ≤ a * b) : 2 * r ≤ a + b

name: le_of_mul_eq_left

name: le_of_mul_eq_right

signature: (hp : IsStarProjection p) (hq : IsStarProjection q) (hpq : q * p = p) : p ≤ q

name: tsub_lt_tsub_iff_right

signature: (h : c ≤ a) : a - c < b - c ↔ a < b

name: OrderIso.map_tsub

name: leadingCoeff_multiset_prod'
informal: The leading coefficient of a product of polynomials is equal to the product of the leading coefficients, provided that this product is nonzero. See `Polynomial.leadingCoeff_multiset_prod` (without the `'`) for a version for integral domains, where this condition is automatically satisfied.
signature: (h : (t.map leadingCoeff).prod ≠ 0) : t.prod.leadingCoeff = (t.map leadingCoeff).prod

name: leadingCoeff_prod'
informal: The leading coefficient of a product of polynomials is equal to the product of the leading coefficients, provided that this product is nonzero. See `Polynomial.leadingCoeff_prod` (without the `'`) for a version for integral domains, where this condition is automatically satisfied.
signature: (h : (∏ i ∈ s, (f i).leadingCoeff) ≠ 0) : (∏ i ∈ s, f i).leadingCoeff = ∏ i ∈ s, (f i).leadingCoeff

name: natDegree_multiset_prod'
informal: The degree of a product of polynomials is equal to the sum of the degrees, provided that the product of leading coefficients is nonzero. See `Polynomial.natDegree_multiset_prod` (without the `'`) for a version for integral domains, where this condition is automatically satisfied.
signature: (h : (t.map fun f => leadingCoeff f).prod ≠ 0) : t.prod.natDegree = (t.map fun f => natDegree f).sum

name: natDegree_prod'
informal: The degree of a product of polynomials is equal to the sum of the degrees, provided that the product of leading coefficients is nonzero. See `Polynomial.natDegree_prod` (without the `'`) for a version for integral domains, where this condition is automatically satisfied.
signature: (h : (∏ i ∈ s, (f i).leadingCoeff) ≠ 0) : (∏ i ∈ s, f i).natDegree = ∑ i ∈ s, (f i).natDegree

name: natDegree_prod
informal: The degree of a product of polynomials is equal to the sum of the degrees. See `Polynomial.natDegree_prod'` (with a `'`) for a version for commutative semirings, where additionally, the product of the leading coefficients must be nonzero.
signature: (h : ∀ i ∈ s, f i ≠ 0) : (∏ i ∈ s, f i).natDegree = ∑ i ∈ s, (f i).natDegree

name: degree_multiset_prod

signature: [Nontrivial R] : t.prod.degree = (t.map fun f => degree f).sum

name: degree_prod
informal: The degree of a product of polynomials is equal to the sum of the degrees, where the degree of the zero polynomial is ⊥.
signature: [Nontrivial R] : (∏ i ∈ s, f i).degree = ∑ i ∈ s, (f i).degree

name: leadingCoeff_divByMonic_of_monic

name: natDegree_pos

signature: (h : Irreducible f) : 0 < f.natDegree

name: degree_pos
informal: An irreducible polynomial over a field must have positive degree.
signature: (h : Irreducible f) : 0 < f.degree

name: Splits.coeff_zero_eq_prod_roots_of_monic

name: Splits.nextCoeff_eq_neg_sum_roots_of_monic

name: exists_quadratic_eq_zero

name: HasDerivAt.comp_sub_const
informal: Translation in the domain does not change the derivative.
signature: (x a : 𝕜) (hf : HasDerivAt f f' (x - a)) : HasDerivAt (fun x ↦ f (x - a)) f' x

name: HasDerivWithinAt.nonneg_of_monotoneOn
informal: If a monotone function has a derivative within a set at a non-isolated point, then this derivative is nonnegative.
signature: (hx : AccPt x (𝓟 s)) (hd : HasDerivWithinAt g g' s x) (hg : MonotoneOn g s) : 0 ≤ g'

name: HasDerivAt.nonneg_of_monotone
informal: If a monotone function has a derivative, then this derivative is nonnegative.
signature: (hd : HasDerivAt g g' x) (hg : Monotone g) : 0 ≤ g'

name: HasDerivWithinAt.nonpos_of_antitoneOn
informal: If an antitone function has a derivative within a set at a non-isolated point, then this derivative is nonpositive.
signature: (hx : AccPt x (𝓟 s)) (hd : HasDerivWithinAt g g' s x) (hg : AntitoneOn g s) : g' ≤ 0

name: HasDerivAt.nonpos_of_antitone
informal: If an antitone function has a derivative, then this derivative is nonpositive.
signature: (hd : HasDerivAt g g' x) (hg : Antitone g) : g' ≤ 0

name: isLocalMin_of_deriv_Ioo
informal: The First-Derivative Test from calculus, minima version.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b c : ℝ} (g₀ : a < b) (g₁ : b < c) (h : ContinuousAt f b) (hd₀ : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Ioo a b)) (hd₁ : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Ioo b c)) (h₀ : ∀ x ∈ Ioo a b, deriv f x ≤ 0) (h₁ : ∀ x ∈ Ioo b c, 0 ≤ deriv f x) : IsLocalMin f b

name: isLocalMax_of_deriv'
informal: The First-Derivative Test from calculus, maxima version, expressed in terms of left and right filters.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} {b : ℝ} (h : ContinuousAt f b) (hd₀ : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[<] b, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (hd₁ : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[>] b, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (h₀ : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[<] b, 0 ≤ deriv f x) (h₁ : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[>] b, deriv f x ≤ 0) : IsLocalMax f b

name: isLocalMin_of_deriv'
informal: The First-Derivative Test from calculus, minima version, expressed in terms of left and right filters.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} {b : ℝ} (h : ContinuousAt f b) (hd₀ : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[<] b, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (hd₁ : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[>] b, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (h₀ : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[<] b, deriv f x ≤ 0) (h₁ : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[>] b, deriv f x ≥ 0) : IsLocalMin f b

name: eventually_nhdsWithin_sign_eq_of_deriv_pos
informal: If the derivative of `f` is positive at a root `x₀` of `f`, then locally the sign of `f x` matches `x - x₀`.
signature: (hf : deriv f x₀ > 0) (hx : f x₀ = 0) : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 x₀, sign (f x) = sign (x - x₀)

name: eventually_nhdsWithin_sign_eq_of_deriv_neg
informal: If the derivative of `f` is negative at a root `x₀` of `f`, then locally the sign of `f x` matches `x₀ - x`.
signature: (hf : deriv f x₀ < 0) (hx : f x₀ = 0) : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 x₀, sign (f x) = sign (x₀ - x)

name: isLocalMax_of_sign_deriv
informal: The First Derivative test with a hypothesis on the sign of the derivative, maximum version.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} {x₀ : ℝ} (h : ContinuousAt f x₀) (hf : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[≠] x₀, sign (deriv f x) = sign (x₀ - x)) : IsLocalMax f x₀

name: isLocalMin_of_sign_deriv
informal: The First Derivative test with a hypothesis on the sign of the derivative, minimum version.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} {x₀ : ℝ} (h : ContinuousAt f x₀) (hf : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[≠] x₀, sign (deriv f x) = sign (x - x₀)) : IsLocalMin f x₀

name: isLocalMin_of_deriv_deriv_pos
informal: The Second-Derivative Test from calculus, minimum version. Applies to functions like `x^2 + 1[x ≥ 0]` as well as twice differentiable functions.
signature: (hf : deriv (deriv f) x₀ > 0) (hd : deriv f x₀ = 0) (hc : ContinuousAt f x₀) : IsLocalMin f x₀

name: isLocalMax_of_deriv_deriv_neg
informal: The Second-Derivative Test from calculus, maximum version.
signature: (hf : deriv (deriv f) x₀ < 0) (hd : deriv f x₀ = 0) (hc : ContinuousAt f x₀) : IsLocalMax f x₀

name: AnalyticOnNhd.hasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn
informal: If a function is analytic on a neighborhood of a set `s`, then it has a Taylor series given by the sequence of its derivatives. Note that, if the function were just analytic on `s`, then one would have to use instead the sequence of derivatives inside the set, as in `AnalyticOn.hasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn`.
signature: [CompleteSpace F] (n : WithTop ℕ∞) (h : AnalyticOnNhd 𝕜 f s) : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f (ftaylorSeries 𝕜 f) s

name: CPolynomialOn.iteratedFDeriv
informal: If a function is polynomial on a set `s`, so are its successive Fréchet derivative.
signature: (h : CPolynomialOn 𝕜 f s) (n : ℕ) : CPolynomialOn 𝕜 (iteratedFDeriv 𝕜 n f) s

name: factorial_smul
informal: The iterated derivative of an analytic function, on vectors `(y, ..., y)`, is given by `n!` times the `n`-th term in the power series. For a more general result giving the full iterated derivative as a sum over the permutations of `Fin n`, see `HasFPowerSeriesOnBall.iteratedFDeriv_eq_sum`.
signature: (n : ℕ) : n ! • p n (fun _ ↦ y) = iteratedFDeriv 𝕜 n f x (fun _ ↦ y)

name: HasFDerivWithinAt.of_not_accPt
informal: If `x` is isolated in `s`, then `f` has any derivative at `x` within `s`, as this statement is empty.
signature: (h : ¬AccPt x (𝓟 s)) : HasFDerivWithinAt f f' s x

name: HasFDerivWithinAt.of_notMem_closure
informal: If `x` is not in the closure of `s`, then `f` has any derivative at `x` within `s`, as this statement is empty.
signature: (h : x ∉ closure s) : HasFDerivWithinAt f f' s x

name: DifferentiableOn.union_of_isOpen
informal: If a function is differentiable on two open sets, it is also differentiable on their union.
signature: (hf : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s) (hf' : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f t) (hs : IsOpen s) (ht : IsOpen t) : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f (s ∪ t)

name: differentiableOn_union_iff_of_isOpen
informal: A function is differentiable on two open sets iff it is differentiable on their union.
signature: (hs : IsOpen s) (ht : IsOpen t) : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f (s ∪ t) ↔ DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s ∧ DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f t

name: hasFDerivWithinAt_congr_set'
informal: In the case `y = x`, see also `hasFDerivWithinAt_congr_set_nhdsNE`, which does not require the domain to be a T₁ space.
signature: [T1Space E] (y : E) (h : s =ᶠ[𝓝[{y}ᶜ] x] t) : HasFDerivWithinAt f f' s x ↔ HasFDerivWithinAt f f' t x

name: differentiableWithinAt_congr_set'
informal: In the case `y = x`, see also `differentiableWithinAt_congr_set_nhdsNE`, which does not require the domain to be a T₁ space.
signature: [T1Space E] (y : E) (h : s =ᶠ[𝓝[{y}ᶜ] x] t) : DifferentiableWithinAt 𝕜 f s x ↔ DifferentiableWithinAt 𝕜 f t x

name: fderivWithin_congr_set'
informal: In the case `y = x`, see also `fderivWithin_congr_set_nhdsNE`, which does not require the domain to be a T₁ space.
signature: [T1Space E] (y : E) (h : s =ᶠ[𝓝[{y}ᶜ] x] t) : fderivWithin 𝕜 f s x = fderivWithin 𝕜 f t x

name: HasFDerivWithinAt.mapsTo_tangent_cone
informal: The image of a tangent cone under the differential of a map is included in the tangent cone to the image.
signature: (h : HasFDerivWithinAt f f' s x) : MapsTo f' (tangentConeAt 𝕜 s x) (tangentConeAt 𝕜 (f '' s) (f x))

name: HasFDerivWithinAt.uniqueDiffWithinAt
informal: If a set has the unique differentiability property at a point x, then the image of this set under a map with onto derivative has also the unique differentiability property at the image point.
signature: (h : HasFDerivWithinAt f f' s x) (hs : UniqueDiffWithinAt 𝕜 s x) (h' : DenseRange f') : UniqueDiffWithinAt 𝕜 (f '' s) (f x)

name: eq_implicitFunctionOfComplemented
informal: Any point in some neighborhood of `a` can be represented as `HasStrictFDerivAt.implicitFunctionOfComplemented` of some point.
signature: (hf : HasStrictFDerivAt f f' a) (hf' : f'.range = ⊤) (hker : f'.ker.ClosedComplemented) : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 a, hf.implicitFunctionOfComplemented f f' hf' hker (f x) (hf.implicitToOpenPartialHomeomorphOfComplemented f f' hf' hker x).snd = x

name: eq_implicitFunction
informal: Any point in some neighborhood of `a` can be represented as `HasStrictFDerivAt.implicitFunction` of some point.
signature: (hf : HasStrictFDerivAt f f' a) (hf' : f'.range = ⊤) : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 a, hf.implicitFunction f f' hf' (f x) (hf.implicitToOpenPartialHomeomorph f f' hf' x).snd = x

name: analyticAt_localInverse
informal: The local inverse of an analytic function (at a point where its derivative does not vanish) is itself analytic.
signature: (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x) (hf' : deriv f x ≠ 0) : AnalyticAt 𝕜 (hf.hasStrictDerivAt.localInverse _ _ _ hf') (f x)

name: isOpenMap_of_hasStrictDerivAt
informal: If a function has a non-zero strict derivative at all points, then it is an open map.
signature: {f' : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : ∀ x, HasStrictDerivAt f (f' x) x) (h0 : ∀ x, f' x ≠ 0) : IsOpenMap f

name: AnalyticOn.hasFPowerSeriesOnSubball
informal: If `f` is analytic on `Bᵣ(x₀)` and its Taylor series converges on this ball, then it converges to `f`.
signature: {r : ENNReal} (hr_pos : 0 < r) (h : AnalyticOn 𝕜 f (Metric.eball x r)) : letI p

name: contDiffOn_of_continuousOn_differentiableOn_deriv
informal: If the first `n` derivatives within a set of a function are continuous, and its first `n-1` derivatives are differentiable, then the function is `C^n`. This is not an equivalence in general, but this is an equivalence when the set has unique derivatives, see `contDiffOn_iff_continuousOn_differentiableOn_deriv`.
signature: {n : ℕ∞} (Hcont : ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℕ∞) ≤ n → ContinuousOn (fun x => iteratedDerivWithin m f s x) s) (Hdiff : ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℕ∞) < n → DifferentiableOn 𝕜 (fun x => iteratedDerivWithin m f s x) s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s

name: contDiffOn_of_differentiableOn_deriv
informal: To check that a function is `n` times continuously differentiable, it suffices to check that its first `n` derivatives are differentiable. This is slightly too strong as the condition we require on the `n`-th derivative is differentiability instead of continuity, but it has the advantage of avoiding the discussion of continuity in the proof (and for `n = ∞` this is optimal).
signature: {n : ℕ∞} (h : ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℕ∞) ≤ n → DifferentiableOn 𝕜 (iteratedDerivWithin m f s) s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s

name: contDiffOn_iff_continuousOn_differentiableOn_deriv
informal: The property of being `C^n`, initially defined in terms of the Fréchet derivative, can be reformulated in terms of the one-dimensional derivative on sets with unique derivatives.
signature: {n : ℕ∞} (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s ↔ (∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℕ∞) ≤ n → ContinuousOn (iteratedDerivWithin m f s) s) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℕ∞) < n → DifferentiableOn 𝕜 (iteratedDerivWithin m f s) s

name: contDiffOn_nat_iff_continuousOn_differentiableOn_deriv
informal: The property of being `C^n`, initially defined in terms of the Fréchet derivative, can be reformulated in terms of the one-dimensional derivative on sets with unique derivatives.
signature: {n : ℕ} (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) : ContDiffOn 𝕜 n f s ↔ (∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ n → ContinuousOn (iteratedDerivWithin m f s) s) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → DifferentiableOn 𝕜 (iteratedDerivWithin m f s) s

name: contDiff_iff_iteratedDeriv
informal: The property of being `C^n`, initially defined in terms of the Fréchet derivative, can be reformulated in terms of the one-dimensional derivative.
signature: {n : ℕ∞} : ContDiff 𝕜 n f ↔ (∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℕ∞) ≤ n → Continuous (iteratedDeriv m f)) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℕ∞) < n → Differentiable 𝕜 (iteratedDeriv m f)

name: contDiff_nat_iff_iteratedDeriv
informal: The property of being `C^n`, initially defined in terms of the Fréchet derivative, can be reformulated in terms of the one-dimensional derivative.
signature: {n : ℕ} : ContDiff 𝕜 n f ↔ (∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ n → Continuous (iteratedDeriv m f)) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → Differentiable 𝕜 (iteratedDeriv m f)

name: contDiff_of_differentiable_iteratedDeriv
informal: To check that a function is `n` times continuously differentiable, it suffices to check that its first `n` derivatives are differentiable. This is slightly too strong as the condition we require on the `n`-th derivative is differentiability instead of continuity, but it has the advantage of avoiding the discussion of continuity in the proof (and for `n = ∞` this is optimal).
signature: {n : ℕ∞} (h : ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℕ∞) ≤ n → Differentiable 𝕜 (iteratedDeriv m f)) : ContDiff 𝕜 n f

name: logDeriv_prod
informal: The logarithmic derivative of a finite product is the sum of the logarithmic derivatives.
signature: {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → 𝕜 → 𝕜'} {x : 𝕜} (hf : ∀ i ∈ s, f i x ≠ 0) (hd : ∀ i ∈ s, DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (f i) x) : logDeriv (∏ i ∈ s, f i ·) x = ∑ i ∈ s, logDeriv (f i) x

name: AnalyticAt.tendsto_mul_logDeriv_simple_zero
informal: At a simple zero of an analytic function, the logarithmic residue `(w - x) * logDeriv f w` tends to 1.
signature: [CompleteSpace 𝕜] {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {x : 𝕜} (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x) (hfx : f x = 0) (hf' : deriv f x ≠ 0) : Filter.Tendsto (fun w => (w - x) * logDeriv f w) (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 1)

name: norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment
informal: A function on `[a, b]` with the norm of the derivative within `[a, b]` bounded by `C` satisfies `‖f x - f a‖ ≤ C * (x - a)`, `derivWithin` version.
signature: {C : ℝ} (hf : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Icc a b)) (bound : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, ‖derivWithin f (Icc a b) x‖ ≤ C) : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, ‖f x - f a‖ ≤ C * (x - a)

name: norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment_01
informal: A function on `[0, 1]` with the norm of the derivative within `[0, 1]` bounded by `C` satisfies `‖f 1 - f 0‖ ≤ C`, `derivWithin` version.
signature: {C : ℝ} (hf : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)) (bound : ∀ x ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖derivWithin f (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) x‖ ≤ C) : ‖f 1 - f 0‖ ≤ C

name: eq_of_has_deriv_right_eq
informal: If two continuous functions on `[a, b]` have the same right derivative and are equal at `a`, then they are equal everywhere on `[a, b]`.
signature: (derivf : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Ici x) x) (derivg : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, HasDerivWithinAt g (f' x) (Ici x) x) (fcont : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (gcont : ContinuousOn g (Icc a b)) (hi : f a = g a) : ∀ y ∈ Icc a b, f y = g y

name: eq_of_derivWithin_eq
informal: If two differentiable functions on `[a, b]` have the same derivative within `[a, b]` everywhere on `[a, b)` and are equal at `a`, then they are equal everywhere on `[a, b]`.
signature: (fdiff : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Icc a b)) (gdiff : DifferentiableOn ℝ g (Icc a b)) (hderiv : EqOn (derivWithin f (Icc a b)) (derivWithin g (Icc a b)) (Ico a b)) (hi : f a = g a) : ∀ y ∈ Icc a b, f y = g y

name: is_const_of_fderivWithin_eq_zero
informal: If a function has zero Fréchet derivative at every point of a convex set, then it is a constant on this set.
signature: (hs : Convex ℝ s) (hf : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, fderivWithin 𝕜 f s x = 0) (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) : f x = f y

name: eqOn_of_fderivWithin_eq
informal: If two functions have equal Fréchet derivatives at every point of a convex set, and are equal at one point in that set, then they are equal on that set.
signature: (hs : Convex ℝ s) (hf : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s) (hg : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 g s) (hs' : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) (hf' : s.EqOn (fderivWithin 𝕜 f s) (fderivWithin 𝕜 g s)) (hx : x ∈ s) (hfgx : f x = g x) : s.EqOn f g

name: _root_.IsOpen.exists_is_const_of_fderiv_eq_zero
informal: If `f` has zero derivative on a connected open set, then `f` is constant on `s`.
signature: (hs : IsOpen s) (hs' : IsPreconnected s) (hf : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s) (hf' : s.EqOn (fderiv 𝕜 f) 0) : ∃ a, ∀ x ∈ s, f x = a

name: _root_.IsOpen.eqOn_of_fderiv_eq
informal: If two functions have equal Fréchet derivatives at every point of a connected open set, and are equal at one point in that set, then they are equal on that set.
signature: (hs : IsOpen s) (hs' : IsPreconnected s) (hf : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s) (hg : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 g s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, fderiv 𝕜 f x = fderiv 𝕜 g x) (hx : x ∈ s) (hfgx : f x = g x) : s.EqOn f g

name: norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasDerivWithin_le
informal: The mean value theorem on a convex set in dimension 1: if the derivative of a function is bounded by `C`, then the function is `C`-Lipschitz. Version with `HasDerivWithinAt`.
signature: {C : ℝ} (hf : ∀ x ∈ s, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (bound : ∀ x ∈ s, ‖f' x‖ ≤ C) (hs : Convex ℝ s) (xs : x ∈ s) (ys : y ∈ s) : ‖f y - f x‖ ≤ C * ‖y - x‖

name: norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_derivWithin_le
informal: The mean value theorem on a convex set in dimension 1: if the derivative of a function within this set is bounded by `C`, then the function is `C`-Lipschitz. Version with `derivWithin`
signature: {C : ℝ} (hf : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s) (bound : ∀ x ∈ s, ‖derivWithin f s x‖ ≤ C) (hs : Convex ℝ s) (xs : x ∈ s) (ys : y ∈ s) : ‖f y - f x‖ ≤ C * ‖y - x‖

name: norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le
informal: The mean value theorem on a convex set in dimension 1: if the derivative of a function is bounded by `C`, then the function is `C`-Lipschitz. Version with `deriv`.
signature: {C : ℝ} (hf : ∀ x ∈ s, DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x) (bound : ∀ x ∈ s, ‖deriv f x‖ ≤ C) (hs : Convex ℝ s) (xs : x ∈ s) (ys : y ∈ s) : ‖f y - f x‖ ≤ C * ‖y - x‖

name: _root_.lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_deriv_le
informal: The mean value theorem set in dimension 1: if the derivative of a function is bounded by `C`, then the function is `C`-Lipschitz. Version with `deriv` and `LipschitzWith`.
signature: {C : ℝ≥0} (hf : Differentiable 𝕜 f) (bound : ∀ x, ‖deriv f x‖₊ ≤ C) : LipschitzWith C f

name: _root_.is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero
informal: If `f : 𝕜 → G`, `𝕜 = R` or `𝕜 = ℂ`, is differentiable everywhere and its derivative equal zero, then it is a constant function.
signature: (hf : Differentiable 𝕜 f) (hf' : ∀ x, deriv f x = 0) (x y : 𝕜) : f x = f y

name: hasStrictFDerivAt_of_hasFDerivAt_of_continuousAt
informal: Over the reals or the complexes, a continuously differentiable function is strictly differentiable.
signature: (hder : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, HasFDerivAt f (f' y) y) (hcont : ContinuousAt f' x) : HasStrictFDerivAt f (f' x) x

name: StieltjesFunction.ae_hasDerivAt
informal: A Stieltjes function is almost everywhere differentiable, with derivative equal to the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the associated Stieltjes measure with respect to Lebesgue.
signature: (f : StieltjesFunction ℝ) : ∀ᵐ x, HasDerivAt f (rnDeriv f.measure volume x).toReal x

name: Monotone.ae_hasDerivAt
informal: A monotone function is almost everywhere differentiable, with derivative equal to the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the associated Stieltjes measure with respect to Lebesgue.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Monotone f) : ∀ᵐ x, HasDerivAt f (rnDeriv hf.stieltjesFunction.measure volume x).toReal x

name: MonotoneOn.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem
informal: A real function which is monotone on a set is differentiable Lebesgue-almost everywhere on this set. This version does not assume that `s` is measurable. For a formulation with `volume.restrict s` assuming that `s` is measurable, see `MonotoneOn.ae_differentiableWithinAt`.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} {s : Set ℝ} (hf : MonotoneOn f s) : ∀ᵐ x, x ∈ s → DifferentiableWithinAt ℝ f s x

name: MonotoneOn.ae_differentiableWithinAt
informal: A real function which is monotone on a set is differentiable Lebesgue-almost everywhere on this set. This version assumes that `s` is measurable and uses `volume.restrict s`. For a formulation without measurability assumption, see `MonotoneOn.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem`.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} {s : Set ℝ} (hf : MonotoneOn f s) (hs : MeasurableSet s) : ∀ᵐ x ∂volume.restrict s, DifferentiableWithinAt ℝ f s x

name: summable_of_summable_hasFDerivAt_of_isPreconnected
informal: Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x` on a preconnected open set. If the series converges at a point, and all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the derivatives, then the series converges everywhere on the set.
signature: (hu : Summable u) (hs : IsOpen s) (h's : IsPreconnected s) (hf : ∀ n x, x ∈ s → HasFDerivAt (f n) (f' n x) x) (hf' : ∀ n x, x ∈ s → ‖f' n x‖ ≤ u n) (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ s) (hf0 : Summable (f · x₀)) (hx : x ∈ s) : Summable fun n => f n x

name: summable_of_summable_hasDerivAt_of_isPreconnected
informal: Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x` on a preconnected open set. If the series converges at a point, and all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the derivatives, then the series converges everywhere on the set.
signature: (hu : Summable u) (ht : IsOpen t) (h't : IsPreconnected t) (hg : ∀ n y, y ∈ t → HasDerivAt (g n) (g' n y) y) (hg' : ∀ n y, y ∈ t → ‖g' n y‖ ≤ u n) (hy₀ : y₀ ∈ t) (hg0 : Summable (g · y₀)) (hy : y ∈ t) : Summable fun n => g n y

name: hasFDerivAt_tsum_of_isPreconnected
informal: Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x` on a preconnected open set. If the series converges at a point, and all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the derivatives, then the series is differentiable on the set and its derivative is the sum of the derivatives.
signature: (hu : Summable u) (hs : IsOpen s) (h's : IsPreconnected s) (hf : ∀ n x, x ∈ s → HasFDerivAt (f n) (f' n x) x) (hf' : ∀ n x, x ∈ s → ‖f' n x‖ ≤ u n) (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ s) (hf0 : Summable fun n => f n x₀) (hx : x ∈ s) : HasFDerivAt (fun y => ∑' n, f n y) (∑' n, f' n x) x

name: hasDerivAt_tsum_of_isPreconnected
informal: Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x` on a preconnected open set. If the series converges at a point, and all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the derivatives, then the series is differentiable on the set and its derivative is the sum of the derivatives.
signature: (hu : Summable u) (ht : IsOpen t) (h't : IsPreconnected t) (hg : ∀ n y, y ∈ t → HasDerivAt (g n) (g' n y) y) (hg' : ∀ n y, y ∈ t → ‖g' n y‖ ≤ u n) (hy₀ : y₀ ∈ t) (hg0 : Summable fun n => g n y₀) (hy : y ∈ t) : HasDerivAt (fun z => ∑' n, g n z) (∑' n, g' n y) y

name: summable_of_summable_hasDerivAt
informal: Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x`. If the series converges at a point, and all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the derivatives, then the series converges everywhere.
signature: (hu : Summable u) (hg : ∀ n y, HasDerivAt (g n) (g' n y) y) (hg' : ∀ n y, ‖g' n y‖ ≤ u n) (hg0 : Summable fun n => g n y₀) (y : 𝕜) : Summable fun n => g n y

name: hasDerivAt_tsum
informal: Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x`. If the series converges at a point, and all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the derivatives, then the series is differentiable and its derivative is the sum of the derivatives.
signature: (hu : Summable u) (hg : ∀ n y, HasDerivAt (g n) (g' n y) y) (hg' : ∀ n y, ‖g' n y‖ ≤ u n) (hg0 : Summable fun n => g n y₀) (y : 𝕜) : HasDerivAt (fun z => ∑' n, g n z) (∑' n, g' n y) y

name: differentiable_tsum
informal: Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x`. If all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the derivatives, then the series is differentiable. Note that our assumptions do not ensure the pointwise convergence, but if there is no pointwise convergence then the series is zero everywhere so the result still holds.
signature: (hu : Summable u) (hf : ∀ n x, HasFDerivAt (f n) (f' n x) x) (hf' : ∀ n x, ‖f' n x‖ ≤ u n) : Differentiable 𝕜 fun y => ∑' n, f n y

name: differentiable_tsum'
informal: Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x`. If all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the derivatives, then the series is differentiable. Note that our assumptions do not ensure the pointwise convergence, but if there is no pointwise convergence then the series is zero everywhere so the result still holds.
signature: (hu : Summable u) (hg : ∀ n y, HasDerivAt (g n) (g' n y) y) (hg' : ∀ n y, ‖g' n y‖ ≤ u n) : Differentiable 𝕜 fun z => ∑' n, g n z

name: tangentConeAt_inter_nhds
informal: Intersecting with a neighborhood of the point does not change the tangent cone.
signature: (ht : t ∈ 𝓝 x) : tangentConeAt 𝕜 (s ∩ t) x = tangentConeAt 𝕜 s x

name: tangentConeAt_subset_zero
informal: If `x` is not an accumulation point of `s`, then the tangent cone of `s` at `x` is a subset of `{0}`.
signature: [T2Space E] (hx : ¬AccPt x (𝓟 s)) : tangentConeAt 𝕜 s x ⊆ 0

name: UniqueDiffOn.mono_field
informal: Assume that `E` is a normed vector space over semirings `𝕜 ⊆ 𝕜'` and all points of `s` are points of unique differentiability with respect to the smaller semiring `𝕜`, then they are also points of unique differentiability with respect to the larger semiring `𝕜`.
signature: (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜' s

name: tangentConeAt_eq_univ
informal: The tangent cone at a non-isolated point in dimension 1 is the whole space.
signature: {s : Set 𝕜} {x : 𝕜} (hx : AccPt x (𝓟 s)) : tangentConeAt 𝕜 s x = univ

name: uniqueDiffWithinAt_iff_accPt
informal: In one dimension, a point is a point of unique differentiability of a set iff it is an accumulation point of the set.
signature: {s : Set 𝕜} {x : 𝕜} : UniqueDiffWithinAt 𝕜 s x ↔ AccPt x (𝓟 s)

name: mapsTo_tangentConeAt_pi
informal: The tangent cone of a product contains the tangent cone of each factor.
signature: [DecidableEq ι] {i : ι} (hi : ∀ j ≠ i, x j ∈ closure (s j)) : MapsTo (Pi.single i) (tangentConeAt 𝕜 (s i) (x i)) (tangentConeAt 𝕜 (Set.pi univ s) x)

name: UniqueDiffWithinAt.prod
informal: The product of two sets of unique differentiability at points `x` and `y` has unique differentiability at `(x, y)`.
signature: (hs : UniqueDiffWithinAt 𝕜 s x) (ht : UniqueDiffWithinAt 𝕜 t y) : UniqueDiffWithinAt 𝕜 (s ×ˢ t) (x, y)

name: UniqueDiffOn.prod
informal: The product of two sets of unique differentiability is a set of unique differentiability.
signature: (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) (ht : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 t) : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 (s ×ˢ t)

name: tangentConeAt_nonempty_of_properSpace
informal: In a proper space, the tangent cone at a non-isolated point is nontrivial.
signature: [ProperSpace E] {s : Set E} {x : E} (hx : AccPt x (𝓟 s)) : (tangentConeAt 𝕜 s x ∩ {0}ᶜ).Nonempty

name: sub_mem_posTangentConeAt_of_openSegment_subset
informal: If a subset of a real vector space contains an open segment, then the direction of this segment belongs to the positive tangent cone at its endpoints.
signature: (h : openSegment ℝ x y ⊆ s) : y - x ∈ tangentConeAt ℝ≥0 s x

name: mem_tangentConeAt_of_openSegment_subset
informal: If a subset of a real vector space contains an open segment, then the direction of this segment belongs to the tangent cone at its endpoints.
signature: (h : openSegment ℝ x y ⊆ s) : y - x ∈ tangentConeAt ℝ s x

name: mem_tangentConeAt_of_segment_subset
informal: If a subset of a real vector space contains a segment, then the direction of this segment belongs to the tangent cone at its endpoints.
signature: (h : segment ℝ x y ⊆ s) : y - x ∈ tangentConeAt ℝ s x

name: uniqueDiffOn_convex
informal: In a real vector space, a convex set with nonempty interior is a set of unique differentiability.
signature: (conv : Convex ℝ s) (hs : (interior s).Nonempty) : UniqueDiffOn ℝ s

name: monomial_has_deriv_aux
informal: Helper lemma for calculating the derivative of the monomial that appears in Taylor expansions.
signature: (t x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : HasDerivAt (fun y => (x - y) ^ (n + 1)) (-(n + 1) * (x - t) ^ n) t

name: taylor_mean_remainder_lagrange_iteratedDeriv
informal: A corollary of Taylor's theorem with the Lagrange form of the remainder.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} {x x₀ : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hx : x₀ ≠ x) (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ (n + 1) f (uIcc x₀ x)) : ∃ x' ∈ uIoo x₀ x, f x - taylorWithinEval f n (uIcc x₀ x) x₀ x = iteratedDeriv (n + 1) f x' * (x - x₀) ^ (n + 1) / (n + 1)!

name: taylor_integral_remainder_of_absolutelyContinuous
informal: **Taylor's theorem** with the Integral form of the remainder. We assume that `f` is `n`-times continuously differentiable on the closed set `uIcc x₀ x` and its `n`-th derivative is absolutely continuous on `uIcc x₀ x`. Then $$f(x) - (P_n f)(x₀, x) = \int_{x_0}^x \frac{f^{(n+1)}(t) (x - t)^n}{n!} dt,$$ where $P_n f$ denotes the Taylor polynomial of degree $n$ and $f^{(n+1)}$ is the $n+1$-th iterated derivative.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} {x x₀ : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hf₁ : ContDiffOn ℝ n f (uIcc x₀ x)) (hf₂ : AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval (iteratedDerivWithin n f (uIcc x₀ x)) x₀ x) : f x - taylorWithinEval f n (uIcc x₀ x) x₀ x = ∫ t in x₀..x, ((x - t) ^ n / n !) * iteratedDerivWithin (n + 1) f (uIcc x₀ x) t

name: taylor_integral_remainder
informal: **Taylor's theorem** with the Integral form of the remainder. We assume that `f` is `n+1`-times continuously differentiable on the closed set `uIcc x₀ x`. Then $$f(x) - (P_n f)(x₀, x) = \int_{x_0}^x \frac{f^{(n+1)}(t) (x - t)^n}{n!} dt,$$ where $P_n f$ denotes the Taylor polynomial of degree $n$ and $f^{(n+1)}$ is the $n+1$-th iterated derivative.
signature: [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F] {f : ℝ → F} {x x₀ : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ (n + 1 : ℕ) f (uIcc x₀ x)) : f x - taylorWithinEval f n (uIcc x₀ x) x₀ x = ∫ t in x₀..x, ((x - t) ^ n / n !) • iteratedDerivWithin (n + 1) f (uIcc x₀ x) t

name: abel_aux
informal: Auxiliary lemma for Abel's limit theorem. The difference between the sum `l` at 1 and the power series's value at a point `z` away from 1 can be rewritten as `1 - z` times a power series whose coefficients are tail sums of `l`.
signature: (h : Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∑ i ∈ range n, f i) atTop (𝓝 l)) {z : ℂ} (hz : ‖z‖ < 1) : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (1 - z) * ∑ i ∈ range n, (l - ∑ j ∈ range (i + 1), f j) * z ^ i) atTop (𝓝 (l - ∑' n, f n * z ^ n))

name: tendsto_tsum_powerSeries_nhdsWithin_stolzCone
informal: **Abel's limit theorem**. Given a power series converging at 1, the corresponding function is continuous at 1 when approaching 1 within any fixed Stolz cone.
signature: (h : Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∑ i ∈ range n, f i) atTop (𝓝 l)) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) : Tendsto (fun z ↦ ∑' n, f n * z ^ n) (𝓝[stolzCone s] 1) (𝓝 l)

name: tendsto_tsum_powerSeries_nhdsWithin_lt
informal: **Abel's limit theorem**. Given a real power series converging at 1, the corresponding function is continuous at 1 when approaching 1 from the left.
signature: (h : Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∑ i ∈ range n, f i) atTop (𝓝 l)) : Tendsto (fun x ↦ ∑' n, f n * x ^ n) (𝓝[<] 1) (𝓝 l)

name: angle_eq_abs_arg
informal: The angle between two non-zero complex numbers is the absolute value of the argument of their quotient. Note that this does not hold when `x` or `y` is `0` as the LHS is `π / 2` while the RHS is `0`.
signature: (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : angle x y = |(x / y).arg|

name: ringHom_eq_id_or_conj_of_continuous
informal: The only continuous ring homomorphisms from `ℂ` to `ℂ` are the identity and the complex conjugation.
signature: {f : ℂ →+* ℂ} (hf : Continuous f) : f = RingHom.id ℂ ∨ f = conj

name: ringHom_eq_ofReal_of_continuous
informal: The only continuous ring homomorphism from `ℝ` to `ℂ` is the identity.
signature: {f : ℝ →+* ℂ} (h : Continuous f) : f = ofRealHom

name: mem_slitPlane_of_norm_lt_one
informal: The slit plane includes the open unit ball of radius `1` around `1`.
signature: {z : ℂ} (hz : ‖z‖ < 1) : 1 + z ∈ slitPlane

name: subset_slitPlane_iff_of_subset_sphere
informal: A subset of the circle centered at the origin in `ℂ` of radius `r` is a subset of the `slitPlane` if it does not contain `-r`.
signature: {r : ℝ} {s : Set ℂ} (hs : s ⊆ sphere 0 r) : s ⊆ slitPlane ↔ (-r : ℂ) ∉ s

name: conformalAt_iff_differentiableAt_or_differentiableAt_comp_conj
informal: A complex function is conformal if and only if the function is holomorphic or antiholomorphic with a nonvanishing differential.
signature: {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z : ℂ} : ConformalAt f z ↔ (DifferentiableAt ℂ f z ∨ DifferentiableAt ℂ (f ∘ conj) (conj z)) ∧ fderiv ℝ f z ≠ 0

name: starConvex_ofReal_slitPlane
informal: The slit plane is star-shaped at a positive real number.
signature: {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) : StarConvex ℝ ↑x slitPlane

name: scale_id_mem_verticalClosedStrip_of_mem_verticalClosedStrip
informal: The transformation on ℂ that is used for `scale` maps the closed strip ``re ⁻¹' [l, u]`` to the closed strip ``re ⁻¹' [0, 1]``.

name: scale_id_mem_verticalStrip_of_mem_verticalStrip
informal: The transformation on ℂ that is used for `scale` maps the strip ``re ⁻¹' (l, u)`` to the strip ``re ⁻¹' (0, 1)``.

name: isOpen_re_lt_EReal
informal: An open left half-plane (with boundary real part given by an `EReal`) is an open set in the complex plane.
signature: (x : EReal) : IsOpen {z : ℂ | z.re < x}

name: isOpen_re_gt_EReal
informal: An open right half-plane (with boundary real part given by an `EReal`) is an open set in the complex plane.
signature: (x : EReal) : IsOpen {z : ℂ | x < z.re}

name: isOpen_im_lt_EReal
informal: An open lower half-plane (with boundary imaginary part given by an `EReal`) is an open set in the complex plane.

name: irreducible_of_coprime'

name: nonneg_of_iteratedDeriv_nonneg

name: nonneg_of_iteratedDeriv_nonneg
informal: An entire function whose iterated derivatives at `c` are all nonnegative real has nonnegative real values on `c + ℝ≥0`.
signature: {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : Differentiable ℂ f) {c : ℂ} (h : ∀ n, 0 ≤ iteratedDeriv n f c) ⦃z : ℂ⦄ (hz : c ≤ z) : 0 ≤ f z

name: apply_le_of_iteratedDeriv_nonneg
informal: An entire function whose iterated derivatives at `c` are all nonnegative real (except possibly the value itself) has values of the form `f c + nonneg. real` on the set `c + ℝ≥0`.
signature: {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} (hf : Differentiable ℂ f) (h : ∀ n ≠ 0, 0 ≤ iteratedDeriv n f c) ⦃z : ℂ⦄ (hz : c ≤ z) : f c ≤ f z

name: apply_le_of_iteratedDeriv_alternating
informal: An entire function whose iterated derivatives at `c` are all real with alternating signs (except possibly the value itself) has values of the form `f c + nonneg. real` along the set `c - ℝ≥0`.
signature: {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} (hf : Differentiable ℂ f) (h : ∀ n ≠ 0, 0 ≤ (-1) ^ n * iteratedDeriv n f c) ⦃z : ℂ⦄ (hz : z ≤ c) : f c ≤ f z

name: HasStrictDerivAt.real_of_complex
informal: If a complex function is differentiable at a real point, then the induced real function is also differentiable at this point, with a derivative equal to the real part of the complex derivative.

name: HasDerivAt.real_of_complex
informal: If a complex function `e` is differentiable at a real point, then the function `ℝ → ℝ` given by the real part of `e` is also differentiable at this point, with a derivative equal to the real part of the complex derivative.

name: HasDerivAt.comp_ofReal

name: HasDerivAt.ofReal_comp

name: taylorSeries_eq_on_ball'
informal: A function that is complex differentiable on the open ball of radius `r` around `c` is given by evaluating its Taylor series at `c` on this open ball.
signature: {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Metric.ball c r)) : ∑' n : ℕ, (n ! : ℂ)⁻¹ * iteratedDeriv n f c * (z - c) ^ n = f z

name: taylorSeries_eq_on_eball'
informal: A function that is complex differentiable on the open ball of radius `r ≤ ∞` around `c` is given by evaluating its Taylor series at `c` on this open ball.
signature: {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Metric.eball c r)) : ∑' n : ℕ, (n ! : ℂ)⁻¹ * iteratedDeriv n f c * (z - c) ^ n = f z

name: taylorSeries_eq_of_entire'
informal: A function that is complex differentiable on the complex plane is given by evaluating its Taylor series at any point `c`.
signature: {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : Differentiable ℂ f) : ∑' n : ℕ, (n ! : ℂ)⁻¹ * iteratedDeriv n f c * (z - c) ^ n = f z

name: eq_of_re_of_norm
informal: Criterion for equality in terms of real part and norm. Useful when working with the geometry of the fundamental domain.
signature: {τ τ' : ℍ} (hre : τ.re = τ'.re) (hnorm : ‖(τ : ℂ)‖ = ‖(τ' : ℂ)‖) : τ = τ'

name: gl_smul_eq_self_iff_re_eq
informal: If `g` is an upper triangular matrix with trace zero, then `g` fixes the vertical line `re z = b / (2 * d)`.
signature: (htrace : g.val.trace = 0) (hc : g 1 0 = 0) : g • z = z ↔ z.re = g 0 1 / (2 * g 1 1)

name: gl_smul_eq_self_iff_dist_sq_eq
informal: If `g` is an orientation reversing matrix with trace zero and `c ≠ 0`, then its action on the upper half plane has a half-circle of fixed points. In the hyperbolic geometry, this half-circle is a line. If `c = 0`, then this line is a vertical half-line in the usual geometry, see `gl_smul_eq_self_iff_re_eq`.
signature: (h : g.val.det < 0) (htrace : g.val.trace = 0) (hc : g 1 0 ≠ 0) : g • z = z ↔ dist (z : ℂ) (-g 1 1 / g 1 0) ^ 2 = (-g.val.det) / g 1 0 ^ 2

name: gl_smul_eq_self_iff_dist_eq
informal: If `g` is an orientation reversing matrix with trace zero and `c ≠ 0`, then its action on the upper half plane has a half-circle of fixed points. In the hyperbolic geometry, this half-circle is a line.
signature: (h : g.val.det < 0) (htrace : g.val.trace = 0) (hc : g 1 0 ≠ 0) : g • z = z ↔ dist (z : ℂ) (-g 1 1 / g 1 0) = √(-g.val.det) / |g 1 0|

name: exists_gl_smul_eq_self_iff_trace_eq_zero
informal: An orientation-reversing isometry of the hyperbolic plane has a fixed point iff the corresponding matrix has zero trace.
signature: (h : g.val.det < 0) : (∃ z : ℍ, g • z = z) ↔ g.val.trace = 0

name: isElliptic_of_exists_smul_eq_self
informal: If `g` is a non-scalar orientation preserving matrix with a fixed point in `ℍ`, then it's an elliptic matrix.
signature: (h : 0 < g.val.det) (hgc : g ∉ Subgroup.center _) (hfix : ∃ z : ℍ, g • z = z) : g.IsElliptic

name: gl_smul_eq_self_iff_eq_fixedPt
informal: The action of an elliptic orientation preserving matrix on `ℍ` has a unique fixed point given by `fixedPt`.
signature: (hpos : 0 < g.val.det) (hell : g.IsElliptic) : g • z = z ↔ z = fixedPt g hell

name: forall_smul_eq_self_iff_mem_center
informal: A matrix acts trivially on `ℍ` iff it belongs to the center of `GL(2, ℝ)`, i.e., it's a diagonal matrix.
signature: {g : GL (Fin 2) ℝ} : (∀ z : ℍ, g • z = z) ↔ g ∈ Subgroup.center _

name: det_smulFDeriv
informal: Determinant of the derivative of `g : ℍ → ℍ` considered as an `ℝ`-linear map. This is used in the proof that the action is measure-preserving. Note this formula applies for both orientation- preserving and orientation-reserving isometries.
signature: (g : GL (Fin 2) ℝ) (z : ℂ) : (smulFDeriv g z).det = SignType.sign g.det.val * g.det ^ 2 / ‖denom g z‖ ^ 4

name: volume_eq_lintegral

name: dist_log_im_le

name: dist_coe_le

name: le_dist_coe

signature: {f₁ f₂ : ℂ → ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (h₁f₁ : Meromorphic f₁) (h₂f₁ : ∀ z, meromorphicOrderAt f₁ z ≠ ⊤) (h₁f₂ : Meromorphic f₂) (h₂f₂ : ∀ z, meromorphicOrderAt f₂ z ≠ ⊤) : characteristic (f₁ * f₂) ⊤ r ≤ (characteristic f₁ ⊤ + characteristic f₂ ⊤) r

name: characteristic_mul_top_eventuallyLE
informal: Asymptotically, the characteristic function for the poles of `f * g` is less than or equal to the sum of the characteristic functions for the poles of `f` and `g`, respectively.
signature: {f₁ f₂ : ℂ → ℂ} (h₁f₁ : Meromorphic f₁) (h₂f₁ : ∀ z, meromorphicOrderAt f₁ z ≠ ⊤) (h₁f₂ : Meromorphic f₂) (h₂f₂ : ∀ z, meromorphicOrderAt f₂ z ≠ ⊤) : characteristic (f₁ * f₂) ⊤ ≤ᶠ[Filter.atTop] characteristic f₁ ⊤ + characteristic f₂ ⊤

name: logCounting_eventuallyLE
informal: The logarithmic counting function respects the `≤` relation asymptotically.

name: logCounting_mul_top_le
informal: For `1 ≤ r`, the logarithmic counting function for the poles of `f * g` is less than or equal to the sum of the logarithmic counting functions for the poles of `f` and `g`, respectively.

name: logCounting_mul_top_eventuallyLE
informal: Asymptotically, the logarithmic counting function for the zeros of `f * g` is less than or equal to the sum of the logarithmic counting functions for the zeros of `f` and `g`, respectively.
signature: {f₁ f₂ : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁f₁ : Meromorphic f₁) (h₂f₁ : ∀ z, meromorphicOrderAt f₁ z ≠ ⊤) (h₁f₂ : Meromorphic f₂) (h₂f₂ : ∀ z, meromorphicOrderAt f₂ z ≠ ⊤) : logCounting (f₁ * f₂) ⊤ ≤ᶠ[atTop] logCounting f₁ ⊤ + logCounting f₂ ⊤

name: proximity_mul_zero_le

name: of_one_lt_codim
