name: mem_convexHull_erase
informal: If `x` is in the convex hull of some finset `t` whose elements are not affine-independent, then it is in the convex hull of a strict subset of `t`.
signature: [DecidableEq E] {t : Finset E} (h : ¬AffineIndependent 𝕜 ((↑) : t → E)) {x : E} (m : x ∈ convexHull 𝕜 (↑t : Set E)) : ∃ y : (↑t : Set E), x ∈ convexHull 𝕜 (↑(t.erase y) : Set E)

name: MonotoneOn.convexOn_of_deriv
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on a convex set `D ⊆ ℝ`, is differentiable on its interior, and `f'` is monotone on the interior, then `f` is convex on `D`.
signature: {D : Set ℝ} (hD : Convex ℝ D) {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f D) (hf' : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (interior D)) (hf'_mono : MonotoneOn (deriv f) (interior D)) : ConvexOn ℝ D f

name: AntitoneOn.concaveOn_of_deriv
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on a convex set `D ⊆ ℝ`, is differentiable on its interior, and `f'` is antitone on the interior, then `f` is concave on `D`.
signature: {D : Set ℝ} (hD : Convex ℝ D) {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f D) (hf' : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (interior D)) (h_anti : AntitoneOn (deriv f) (interior D)) : ConcaveOn ℝ D f

name: StrictMono.strictConvexOn_univ_of_deriv
informal: If a function `f` is continuous and `f'` is strictly monotone on `ℝ` then `f` is strictly convex. Note that we don't require differentiability, since it is guaranteed at all but at most one point by the strict monotonicity of `f'`.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Continuous f) (hf'_mono : StrictMono (deriv f)) : StrictConvexOn ℝ univ f

name: StrictAnti.strictConcaveOn_univ_of_deriv
informal: If a function `f` is continuous and `f'` is strictly antitone on `ℝ` then `f` is strictly concave. Note that we don't require differentiability, since it is guaranteed at all but at most one point by the strict antitonicity of `f'`.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Continuous f) (hf'_anti : StrictAnti (deriv f)) : StrictConcaveOn ℝ univ f

name: convexOn_of_deriv2_nonneg
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on a convex set `D ⊆ ℝ`, is twice differentiable on its interior, and `f''` is nonnegative on the interior, then `f` is convex on `D`.
signature: {D : Set ℝ} (hD : Convex ℝ D) {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f D) (hf' : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (interior D)) (hf'' : DifferentiableOn ℝ (deriv f) (interior D)) (hf''_nonneg : ∀ x ∈ interior D, 0 ≤ deriv^[2] f x) : ConvexOn ℝ D f

name: concaveOn_of_deriv2_nonpos
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on a convex set `D ⊆ ℝ`, is twice differentiable on its interior, and `f''` is nonpositive on the interior, then `f` is concave on `D`.
signature: {D : Set ℝ} (hD : Convex ℝ D) {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f D) (hf' : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (interior D)) (hf'' : DifferentiableOn ℝ (deriv f) (interior D)) (hf''_nonpos : ∀ x ∈ interior D, deriv^[2] f x ≤ 0) : ConcaveOn ℝ D f

name: convexOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt2_nonneg
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on a convex set `D ⊆ ℝ`, is twice differentiable on its interior, and `f''` is nonnegative on the interior, then `f` is convex on `D`.
signature: {D : Set ℝ} (hD : Convex ℝ D) {f f' f'' : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f D) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ interior D, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (interior D) x) (hf'' : ∀ x ∈ interior D, HasDerivWithinAt f' (f'' x) (interior D) x) (hf''₀ : ∀ x ∈ interior D, 0 ≤ f'' x) : ConvexOn ℝ D f

name: concaveOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt2_nonpos
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on a convex set `D ⊆ ℝ`, is twice differentiable on its interior, and `f''` is nonpositive on the interior, then `f` is concave on `D`.
signature: {D : Set ℝ} (hD : Convex ℝ D) {f f' f'' : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f D) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ interior D, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (interior D) x) (hf'' : ∀ x ∈ interior D, HasDerivWithinAt f' (f'' x) (interior D) x) (hf''₀ : ∀ x ∈ interior D, f'' x ≤ 0) : ConcaveOn ℝ D f

name: strictConvexOn_of_deriv2_pos
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on a convex set `D ⊆ ℝ` and `f''` is strictly positive on the interior, then `f` is strictly convex on `D`. Note that we don't require twice differentiability explicitly as it is already implied by the second derivative being strictly positive, except at at most one point.
signature: {D : Set ℝ} (hD : Convex ℝ D) {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f D) (hf'' : ∀ x ∈ interior D, 0 < (deriv^[2] f) x) : StrictConvexOn ℝ D f

name: strictConcaveOn_of_deriv2_neg
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on a convex set `D ⊆ ℝ` and `f''` is strictly negative on the interior, then `f` is strictly concave on `D`. Note that we don't require twice differentiability explicitly as it already implied by the second derivative being strictly negative, except at at most one point.
signature: {D : Set ℝ} (hD : Convex ℝ D) {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f D) (hf'' : ∀ x ∈ interior D, deriv^[2] f x < 0) : StrictConcaveOn ℝ D f

name: StrictConvexOn.sup
informal: The pointwise maximum of strictly convex functions is strictly convex.
signature: (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (hg : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s g) : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s (f ⊔ g)

name: StrictConcaveOn.inf
informal: The pointwise minimum of strictly concave functions is strictly concave.
signature: (hf : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) (hg : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s g) : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s (f ⊓ g)

name: StrictConvexOn.eq_of_isMinOn
informal: A strictly convex function admits at most one global minimum.
signature: (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (hfx : IsMinOn f s x) (hfy : IsMinOn f s y) (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) : x = y

name: StrictConcaveOn.eq_of_isMaxOn
informal: A strictly concave function admits at most one global maximum.
signature: (hf : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) (hfx : IsMaxOn f s x) (hfy : IsMaxOn f s y) (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) : x = y

name: Absorbent.gauge_set_nonempty
informal: If the given subset is `Absorbent` then the set we take an infimum over in `gauge` is nonempty, which is useful for proving many properties about the gauge.
signature: (absorbs : Absorbent ℝ s) : { r : ℝ | 0 < r ∧ x ∈ r • s }.Nonempty

name: continuousAt_gauge_zero
informal: If `s` is a neighborhood of the origin, then `gauge s` is continuous at the origin. See also `continuousAt_gauge`.
signature: (hs : s ∈ 𝓝 0) : ContinuousAt (gauge s) 0

name: continuousAt_gauge
informal: If `s` is a convex neighborhood of the origin in a topological real vector space, then `gauge s` is continuous. If the ambient space is a normed space, then `gauge s` is Lipschitz continuous, see `Convex.lipschitz_gauge`.
signature: (hc : Convex ℝ s) (hs₀ : s ∈ 𝓝 0) : ContinuousAt (gauge s) x

name: ConvexOn.map_add_sum_le
informal: Convex **Jensen's inequality** where an element plays a distinguished role.
signature: (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) (h₁ : v + ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) (hv : 0 ≤ v) (hq : q ∈ s) : f (v • q + ∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) ≤ v • f q + ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)

name: ConcaveOn.map_add_sum_le
informal: Concave **Jensen's inequality** where an element plays a distinguished role.
signature: (hf : ConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) (h₁ : v + ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) (hv : 0 ≤ v) (hq : q ∈ s) : v • f q + ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ≤ f (v • q + ∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i)

name: StrictConvexOn.map_sum_lt
informal: Convex **strict Jensen inequality**. If the function is strictly convex, the weights are strictly positive and the indexed family of points is non-constant, then Jensen's inequality is strict. See also `StrictConvexOn.map_sum_eq_iff`.
signature: (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 < w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) (hp : ∃ j ∈ t, ∃ k ∈ t, p j ≠ p k) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) < ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)

name: StrictConcaveOn.lt_map_sum
informal: Concave **strict Jensen inequality**. If the function is strictly concave, the weights are strictly positive and the indexed family of points is non-constant, then Jensen's inequality is strict. See also `StrictConcaveOn.map_sum_eq_iff`.
signature: (hf : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 < w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) (hp : ∃ j ∈ t, ∃ k ∈ t, p j ≠ p k) : ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) < f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i)

name: StrictConvexOn.eq_of_le_map_sum
informal: A form of the **equality case of Jensen's equality**. For a strictly convex function `f` and positive weights `w`, if `f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)`, then the points `p` are all equal. See also `StrictConvexOn.map_sum_eq_iff`.
signature: (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 < w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) (h_eq : ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ≤ f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i)) : ∀ ⦃j⦄, j ∈ t → ∀ ⦃k⦄, k ∈ t → p j = p k

name: StrictConcaveOn.eq_of_map_sum_eq
informal: A form of the **equality case of Jensen's equality**. For a strictly concave function `f` and positive weights `w`, if `f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)`, then the points `p` are all equal. See also `StrictConcaveOn.map_sum_eq_iff`.
signature: (hf : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 < w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) (h_eq : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) ≤ ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)) : ∀ ⦃j⦄, j ∈ t → ∀ ⦃k⦄, k ∈ t → p j = p k

name: StrictConvexOn.map_sum_eq_iff_of_pos
informal: A form of the **equality case of Jensen's equality** for the case of strict convex and positive weights.
signature: (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 < w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ↔ ∀ ⦃j⦄, j ∈ t → ∀ ⦃k⦄, k ∈ t → p j = p k

name: StrictConcaveOn.map_sum_eq_iff_of_pos
informal: A form of the **equality case of Jensen's equality** for the case of strict concave and positive weights.
signature: (hf : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 < w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ↔ ∀ ⦃j⦄, j ∈ t → ∀ ⦃k⦄, k ∈ t → p j = p k

name: StrictConvexOn.map_sum_eq_iff_of_nonneg
informal: A form of the **equality case of Jensen's equality** for the case of strict convex and non-negative weights.
signature: (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ↔ ∀ ⦃j⦄, j ∈ t → w j ≠ 0 → ∀ ⦃k⦄, k ∈ t → w k ≠ 0 → p j = p k

name: StrictConcaveOn.map_sum_eq_iff_of_nonneg
informal: A form of the **equality case of Jensen's equality** for the case of strict concave and non-negative weights.
signature: (hf : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ↔ ∀ ⦃j⦄, j ∈ t → w j ≠ 0 → ∀ ⦃k⦄, k ∈ t → w k ≠ 0 → p j = p k

name: StrictConcaveOn.map_sum_eq_iff
informal: Canonical form of the **equality case of Jensen's equality**. For a strictly concave function `f` and positive weights `w`, we have `f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)` if and only if the points `p` are all equal (and in fact all equal to their center of mass w.r.t. `w`).
signature: (hf : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 < w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ↔ ∀ j ∈ t, p j = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i

name: StrictConvexOn.map_sum_eq_iff'
informal: Canonical form of the **equality case of Jensen's equality**. For a strictly convex function `f` and nonnegative weights `w`, we have `f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)` if and only if the points `p` with nonzero weight are all equal (and in fact all equal to their center of mass w.r.t. `w`).
signature: (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ↔ ∀ j ∈ t, w j ≠ 0 → p j = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i

name: StrictConcaveOn.map_sum_eq_iff'
informal: Canonical form of the **equality case of Jensen's equality**. For a strictly concave function `f` and nonnegative weights `w`, we have `f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)` if and only if the points `p` with nonzero weight are all equal (and in fact all equal to their center of mass w.r.t. `w`).
signature: (hf : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ↔ ∀ j ∈ t, w j ≠ 0 → p j = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i

name: IsCompact.extremePoints_nonempty
informal: **Krein-Milman lemma**: In an LCTVS, any nonempty compact set has an extreme point.
signature: (hscomp : IsCompact s) (hsnemp : s.Nonempty) : (s.extremePoints ℝ).Nonempty

name: closure_convexHull_extremePoints
informal: **Krein-Milman theorem**: In an LCTVS, any compact convex set is the closure of the convex hull of its extreme points.
signature: (hscomp : IsCompact s) (hAconv : Convex ℝ s) : closure (convexHull ℝ <| s.extremePoints ℝ) = s

name: Convex.mem_Icc
informal: A point is in an `Icc` iff it can be expressed as a convex combination of the endpoints.
signature: (h : x ≤ y) : z ∈ Icc x y ↔ ∃ a b, 0 ≤ a ∧ 0 ≤ b ∧ a + b = 1 ∧ a * x + b * y = z

name: Convex.mem_Ioo
informal: A point is in an `Ioo` iff it can be expressed as a strict convex combination of the endpoints.
signature: (h : x < y) : z ∈ Ioo x y ↔ ∃ a b, 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ a + b = 1 ∧ a * x + b * y = z

name: Convex.mem_Ioc
informal: A point is in an `Ioc` iff it can be expressed as a semistrict convex combination of the endpoints.
signature: (h : x < y) : z ∈ Ioc x y ↔ ∃ a b, 0 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ a + b = 1 ∧ a * x + b * y = z

name: Convex.mem_Ico
informal: A point is in an `Ico` iff it can be expressed as a semistrict convex combination of the endpoints.
signature: (h : x < y) : z ∈ Ico x y ↔ ∃ a b, 0 < a ∧ 0 ≤ b ∧ a + b = 1 ∧ a * x + b * y = z

name: one_add_mul_self_lt_rpow_one_add
informal: **Bernoulli's inequality** for real exponents, strict version: for `1 < p` and `-1 ≤ s`, with `s ≠ 0`, we have `1 + p * s < (1 + s) ^ p`.

name: one_add_mul_self_le_rpow_one_add
informal: **Bernoulli's inequality** for real exponents, non-strict version: for `1 ≤ p` and `-1 ≤ s` we have `1 + p * s ≤ (1 + s) ^ p`.

name: rpow_one_add_lt_one_add_mul_self
informal: **Bernoulli's inequality** for real exponents, strict version: for `0 < p < 1` and `-1 ≤ s`, with `s ≠ 0`, we have `(1 + s) ^ p < 1 + p * s`.

name: rpow_one_add_le_one_add_mul_self
informal: **Bernoulli's inequality** for real exponents, non-strict version: for `0 ≤ p ≤ 1` and `-1 ≤ s` we have `(1 + s) ^ p ≤ 1 + p * s`.

name: StarConvex.preimage_add_right
informal: The translation of a star-convex set is also star-convex.
signature: (hs : StarConvex 𝕜 (z + x) s) : StarConvex 𝕜 x ((fun x => z + x) ⁻¹' s)

name: StarConvex.preimage_add_left
informal: The translation of a star-convex set is also star-convex.
signature: (hs : StarConvex 𝕜 (x + z) s) : StarConvex 𝕜 x ((fun x => x + z) ⁻¹' s)

name: stdSimplex_of_isEmpty_index
informal: The standard simplex in the zero-dimensional space is empty.
signature: [IsEmpty ι] [Nontrivial 𝕜] : stdSimplex 𝕜 ι = ∅

name: barycenter_eq_centerMass
informal: The barycenter equals the (equal weight) center of mass of vertices (`Finset.centerMass`).
signature: [DecidableEq X] : (barycenter : stdSimplex 𝕜 X).val = Finset.centerMass Finset.univ (fun _ => (1 : 𝕜)) (fun i => Pi.single i 1)

name: extremePoints_closedBall_subset_sphere
informal: In a nontrivial normed space, the extreme points of the closed ball is contained in the sphere.
signature: [Nontrivial A] {x : A} {r : ℝ} : extremePoints ℝ (closedBall x r) ⊆ sphere x r

name: StrictConvexSpace.sphere_subset_extremePoints_closedBall
informal: In a strictly convex space, the sphere is contained in the extreme points of the closed ball when the radius is nonzero. In a nontrivial space, they are equal, see `extremePoints_closedBall_eq_sphere`.
signature: [StrictConvexSpace ℝ A] (a : A) {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) : sphere a r ⊆ extremePoints ℝ (closedBall a r)

name: StrictConvexSpace.of_strictConvex_unitClosedBall
informal: A real normed vector space is strictly convex provided that the unit ball is strictly convex.
signature: [LinearMap.CompatibleSMul E E 𝕜 ℝ] (h : StrictConvex 𝕜 (closedBall (0 : E) 1)) : StrictConvexSpace 𝕜 E

name: combo_mem_ball_of_ne
informal: If `x ≠ y` belong to the same closed ball, then a convex combination of `x` and `y` with positive coefficients belongs to the corresponding open ball.
signature: (hx : x ∈ closedBall z r) (hy : y ∈ closedBall z r) (hne : x ≠ y) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a + b = 1) : a • x + b • y ∈ ball z r

name: openSegment_subset_ball_of_ne
informal: If `x ≠ y` belong to the same closed ball, then the open segment with endpoints `x` and `y` is included in the corresponding open ball.
signature: (hx : x ∈ closedBall z r) (hy : y ∈ closedBall z r) (hne : x ≠ y) : openSegment ℝ x y ⊆ ball z r

name: norm_add_lt_of_not_sameRay
informal: In a strictly convex space, if `x` and `y` are not in the same ray, then `‖x + y‖ < ‖x‖ + ‖y‖`.
signature: (h : ¬SameRay ℝ x y) : ‖x + y‖ < ‖x‖ + ‖y‖

name: eq_of_norm_eq_of_norm_add_eq
informal: If `x` and `y` are two vectors in a strictly convex space have the same norm and the norm of their sum is equal to the sum of their norms, then they are equal.

name: IsVisible.eq_of_mem_interior
informal: One cannot see any point in the interior of a set.
signature: (hsxy : IsVisible 𝕜 s x y) (hy : y ∈ interior s) : x = y

name: IsVisible.mem_convexHull_isVisible
informal: All points of the convex hull of a set `s` visible from a point `x ∉ convexHull ℝ s` lie in the convex hull of such points that actually lie in `s`. Note that the converse does not hold.
signature: (hx : x ∉ convexHull ℝ s) (hy : y ∈ convexHull ℝ s) (hxy : IsVisible ℝ (convexHull ℝ s) x y) : y ∈ convexHull ℝ {z ∈ s | IsVisible ℝ (convexHull ℝ s) x z}

name: IsClosed.convexHull_subset_affineSpan_isVisible
informal: A set whose convex hull is closed lies in the cone based at a point `x` generated by its points visible from `x` through its convex hull.
signature: (hs : IsClosed (convexHull ℝ s)) (hx : x ∉ convexHull ℝ s) : convexHull ℝ s ⊆ affineSpan ℝ ({x} ∪ {y ∈ s | IsVisible ℝ (convexHull ℝ s) x y})

name: integral_mul_deriv_eq_neg_deriv_mul
informal: Integration by parts of Schwartz functions for the 1-dimensional derivative. Version for multiplication of scalar-valued Schwartz functions.
signature: (f : 𝓢(ℝ, 𝕜)) (g : 𝓢(ℝ, 𝕜)) : ∫ (x : ℝ), f x * (deriv g x) = -∫ (x : ℝ), deriv f x * (g x)

name: hasSum_sq_fourierCoeffOn
informal: **Parseval's identity**: for a function `f` which is square integrable on `(a,b]`, the sum of the squared norms of the Fourier coefficients equals the `L²` norm of `f`.
signature: {a b : ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hab : a < b) (hL2 : MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Ioc a b))) : HasSum (fun i => ‖fourierCoeffOn hab f i‖ ^ 2) ((b - a)⁻¹ • ∫ x in a..b, ‖f x‖ ^ 2)

name: hasSum_fourier_series_of_summable
informal: If the sequence of Fourier coefficients of `f` is summable, then the Fourier series converges uniformly to `f`.
signature: (h : Summable (fourierCoeff f)) : HasSum (fun i => fourierCoeff f i • fourier i) f

name: span_mFourierLp_closure_eq_top
informal: For each `1 ≤ p < ∞`, the linear span of the monomials `mFourier n` is dense in the `Lᵖ` space of functions on `UnitAddTorus d`.
signature: {p : ℝ≥0∞} [Fact (1 ≤ p)] (hp : p ≠ ∞) : (span ℂ (range (@mFourierLp d _ p _))).topologicalClosure = ⊤

name: hasSum_sq_mFourierCoeff
informal: **Parseval's identity** for norms: for an `L²` function `f` on `UnitAddTorus d`, the sum of the squared norms of the Fourier coefficients equals the `L²` norm of `f`.
signature: (f : L²(UnitAddTorus d)) : HasSum (fun i ↦ ‖mFourierCoeff f i‖ ^ 2) (∫ t, ‖f t‖ ^ 2)

name: hasSum_mFourier_series_of_summable
informal: If the sequence of Fourier coefficients of `f` is summable, then the Fourier series converges uniformly to `f`.
signature: (h : Summable (mFourierCoeff f)) : HasSum (fun i ↦ mFourierCoeff f i • mFourier i) f

name: hasSum_mFourier_series_apply_of_summable
informal: If the sequence of Fourier coefficients of `f` is summable, then the Fourier series of `f` converges everywhere pointwise to `f`.
signature: (h : Summable (mFourierCoeff f)) (x : UnitAddTorus d) : HasSum (fun i ↦ mFourierCoeff f i • mFourier i x) (f x)

name: fderiv_fourier
informal: The Fréchet derivative of the Fourier transform of `f` is the Fourier transform of `fun v ↦ -2 * π * I ⟪v, ⬝⟫ f v`.
signature: (hf_int : Integrable f) (hvf_int : Integrable (fun v ↦ ‖v‖ * ‖f v‖)) : fderiv ℝ (𝓕 f) = 𝓕 (fourierSMulRight (innerSL ℝ) f)

name: fourier_fderiv
informal: The Fourier integral of the Fréchet derivative of a function is obtained by multiplying the Fourier integral of the original function by `2πI ⟪v, w⟫`.
signature: (hf : Integrable f) (h'f : Differentiable ℝ f) (hf' : Integrable (fderiv ℝ f)) : 𝓕 (fderiv ℝ f) = fourierSMulRight (-innerSL ℝ) (𝓕 f)

name: iteratedFDeriv_fourier
informal: If `‖v‖^n * ‖f v‖` is integrable, then the `n`-th derivative of the Fourier transform of `f` is the Fourier transform of `fun v ↦ (-2 * π * I) ^ n ⟪v, ⬝⟫^n f v`.
signature: {N : ℕ∞} (hf : ∀ (n : ℕ), n ≤ N → Integrable (fun v ↦ ‖v‖ ^ n * ‖f v‖)) (h'f : AEStronglyMeasurable f) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ N) : iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (𝓕 f) = 𝓕 (fun v ↦ fourierPowSMulRight (innerSL ℝ) f v n)

name: fourier_iteratedFDeriv
informal: The Fourier integral of the `n`-th derivative of a function is obtained by multiplying the Fourier integral of the original function by `(2πI L w ⬝ )^n`.
signature: {N : ℕ∞} (hf : ContDiff ℝ N f) (h'f : ∀ (n : ℕ), n ≤ N → Integrable (iteratedFDeriv ℝ n f)) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ N) : 𝓕 (iteratedFDeriv ℝ n f) = (fun w ↦ fourierPowSMulRight (-innerSL ℝ) (𝓕 f) w n)

name: Continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq
informal: **Fourier inversion formula**: If a function `f` on a finite-dimensional real inner product space is continuous, integrable, and its Fourier transform `𝓕 f` is also integrable, then `𝓕⁻ (𝓕 f) = f`.
signature: (h : Continuous f) (hf : Integrable f) (h'f : Integrable (𝓕 f)) : 𝓕⁻ (𝓕 f) = f

name: Continuous.fourier_fourierInv_eq
informal: **Fourier inversion formula**: If a function `f` on a finite-dimensional real inner product space is continuous, integrable, and its Fourier transform `𝓕 f` is also integrable, then `𝓕 (𝓕⁻ f) = f`.
signature: (h : Continuous f) (hf : Integrable f) (h'f : Integrable (𝓕 f)) : 𝓕 (𝓕⁻ f) = f

name: Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier_of_rpow_decay_of_summable
informal: **Poisson's summation formula**, assuming that `f` decays as `|x| ^ (-b)` for some `1 < b` and its Fourier transform is summable.
signature: {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hc : Continuous f) {b : ℝ} (hb : 1 < b) (hf : IsBigO (cocompact ℝ) f fun x : ℝ => |x| ^ (-b)) (hFf : Summable fun n : ℤ => 𝓕 f n) (x : ℝ) : ∑' n : ℤ, f (x + n) = ∑' n : ℤ, 𝓕 f n * fourier n (x : UnitAddCircle)

name: lintegral_prod_lintegral_pow_le
informal: Special case of the grid-lines lemma `lintegral_mul_prod_lintegral_pow_le`, taking the extremal exponent `p = (#ι - 1)⁻¹`.
signature: [Fintype ι] [∀ i, SigmaFinite (μ i)] {p : ℝ} (hp : Real.HolderConjugate #ι p) {f} (hf : Measurable f) : ∫⁻ x, ∏ i, (∫⁻ xᵢ, f (update x i xᵢ) ∂μ i) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (#ι - 1 : ℝ)) ∂.pi μ ≤ (∫⁻ x, f x ∂.pi μ) ^ p

name: Matrix.toLin_conjTranspose
informal: The linear map associated to the conjugate transpose of a matrix corresponding to two orthonormal bases is the adjoint of the linear map associated to the matrix.
signature: (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : toLin v₂.toBasis v₁.toBasis Aᴴ = adjoint (toLin v₁.toBasis v₂.toBasis A)

name: Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_eq_adjoint
informal: The adjoint of the linear map associated to a matrix is the linear map associated to the conjugate transpose of that matrix.
signature: (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : A.conjTranspose.toEuclideanLin = A.toEuclideanLin.adjoint

name: InnerProductSpace.canonicalCovariantTensor_eq_sum
informal: Representation of the canonical covariant tensor in terms of an orthonormal basis.
signature: [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (v : OrthonormalBasis ι ℝ E) : InnerProductSpace.canonicalCovariantTensor E = ∑ i, (v i) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (v i)

name: Pi.comul_eq_adjoint
informal: The comultiplication on `n → 𝕜` corresponds to the Euclidean space adjoint of the multiplication map.
signature: {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] : comul = map (equiv n 𝕜).toLinearMap (equiv n 𝕜).toLinearMap ∘ₗ ((equiv n 𝕜).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ mul' 𝕜 (n → 𝕜) ∘ₗ map (equiv n 𝕜).toLinearMap (equiv n 𝕜).toLinearMap).adjoint ∘ₗ (equiv n 𝕜).symm.toLinearMap

name: Pi.counit_eq_adjoint
informal: The counit on `n → 𝕜` corresponds to the Euclidean space adjoint of the algebra linear map.
signature: {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] : counit = ((equiv n 𝕜).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ Algebra.linearMap 𝕜 (n → 𝕜)).adjoint ∘ₗ (equiv n 𝕜).symm.toLinearMap

name: laplacianWithin_congr_nhdsWithin
informal: If two functions agree in a neighborhood of a point, then so do their Laplacians.
signature: (h : f₁ =ᶠ[𝓝[s] x] f₂) (hs : UniqueDiffOn ℝ s) : Δ[s] f₁ =ᶠ[𝓝[s] x] Δ[s] f₂

name: laplacian_congr_nhds
informal: If two functions agree in a neighborhood of a point, then so do their Laplacians.
signature: (h : f₁ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f₂) : Δ f₁ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] Δ f₂

name: inner_map_complex
informal: The inner product on an inner product space of dimension 2 can be evaluated in terms of a complex-number representation of the space.
signature: [SeminormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace ℝ G] (f : G ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℂ) (x y : G) : ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ = (f y * conj (f x)).re

name: hausdorffMeasure_image
informal: Using Hausdorff measure with the domain dimension, the volume of the image is scaled by `LinearMap.normDet`.
signature: [MeasurableSpace U] [BorelSpace U] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] (f : U →ₗ[ℝ] V) (s : Set U) : μH[finrank ℝ U] (f '' s) = ENNReal.ofReal f.normDet * μH[finrank ℝ U] s

name: euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image
informal: Using Euclidean Hausdorff measure with the domain dimension, the volume of the image is scaled by `LinearMap.normDet`.
signature: [MeasurableSpace U] [BorelSpace U] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] (f : U →ₗ[ℝ] V) (s : Set U) : μHE[finrank ℝ U] (f '' s) = ENNReal.ofReal f.normDet * μHE[finrank ℝ U] s

name: euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume
informal: The volume of the image measured by Euclidean Hausdorff measure is equal to the Lebesgue measure scaled by `LinearMap.normDet`.
signature: [MeasurableSpace U] [BorelSpace U] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] (f : U →ₗ[ℝ] V) (s : Set U) : μHE[finrank ℝ U] (f '' s) = ENNReal.ofReal f.normDet * volume s

name: det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_of_same_orientation
informal: The change-of-basis matrix between two orthonormal bases with the same orientation has determinant 1.
signature: (h : e.toBasis.orientation = f.toBasis.orientation) : e.toBasis.det f = 1

name: det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_of_opposite_orientation
informal: The change-of-basis matrix between two orthonormal bases with the opposite orientations has determinant -1.
signature: (h : e.toBasis.orientation ≠ f.toBasis.orientation) : e.toBasis.det f = -1

name: det_eq_neg_det_of_opposite_orientation
informal: Two orthonormal bases with opposite orientations determine opposite "determinant" top-dimensional forms on `E`.
signature: (h : e.toBasis.orientation ≠ f.toBasis.orientation) : e.toBasis.det = -f.toBasis.det

name: isCompl_orthogonal
informal: If `K` admits an orthogonal projection, `K` and `Kᗮ` are complements of each other.
signature: [K.HasOrthogonalProjection] : IsCompl K Kᗮ where disjoint

name: finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal
informal: Given a finite-dimensional space `E` and subspace `K`, the dimensions of `K` and `Kᗮ` add to that of `E`.
signature: [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] (K : Submodule 𝕜 E) : finrank 𝕜 K + finrank 𝕜 Kᗮ = finrank 𝕜 E

name: finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal'
informal: Given a finite-dimensional space `E` and subspace `K`, the dimensions of `K` and `Kᗮ` add to that of `E`.
signature: [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] {K : Submodule 𝕜 E} {n : ℕ} (h_dim : finrank 𝕜 K + n = finrank 𝕜 E) : finrank 𝕜 Kᗮ = n

name: mem_span_singleton_of_inner_eq_zero_of_inner_eq_zero
informal: If a nonzero vector `w` and a vector `u` are both orthogonal to the same nonzero vector `v` in a two-dimensional inner product space, then `u` lies in the span of `w`.
signature: [Fact (finrank 𝕜 E = 2)] {u v w : E} (hv : v ≠ 0) (hw : w ≠ 0) (huv : ⟪v, u⟫_𝕜 = 0) (hwv : ⟪v, w⟫_𝕜 = 0) : u ∈ 𝕜 ∙ w

name: LinearIsometryEquiv.reflections_generate_dim
informal: The orthogonal group of `F` is generated by reflections; specifically each element `φ` of the orthogonal group is a product of at most as many reflections as the dimension of `F`. Special case of the **Cartan–Dieudonné theorem**.
signature: [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] (φ : F ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] F) : ∃ l : List F, l.length ≤ finrank ℝ F ∧ φ = (l.map fun v => reflection (ℝ ∙ v)ᗮ).prod

name: OrthogonalFamily.isInternal_iff
informal: An orthogonal family of subspaces of `E` satisfies `DirectSum.IsInternal` (that is, they provide an internal direct sum decomposition of `E`) if and only if their span has trivial orthogonal complement.
signature: [DecidableEq ι] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E} (hV : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => V i) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ) : DirectSum.IsInternal V ↔ (iSup V)ᗮ = ⊥

name: sup_orthogonal_of_hasOrthogonalProjection
informal: If `K` admits an orthogonal projection, then `K` and `Kᗮ` span the whole space.
signature: [K.HasOrthogonalProjection] : K ⊔ Kᗮ = ⊤

name: sup_orthogonal
informal: The sup of two orthogonal subspaces equals the subspace orthogonal to the inf.
signature: [CompleteSpace E] (K₁ K₂ : ClosedSubmodule 𝕜 E) : K₁ᗮ ⊔ K₂ᗮ = (K₁ ⊓ K₂)ᗮ

name: instStarOrderedRingRCLike
informal: Because this takes `ContinuousFunctionalCalculus ℝ (H →L[𝕜] H) IsSelfAdjoint` as an argument, and for the moment we only have this for `𝕜 := ℂ`, this is not registered as an instance.
signature: [ContinuousFunctionalCalculus ℝ (H →L[𝕜] H) IsSelfAdjoint] : StarOrderedRing (H →L[𝕜] H) where le_iff f g

name: IsSymmetric.continuous
informal: The **Hellinger--Toeplitz theorem**: if a symmetric operator is defined on a complete space, then it is automatically continuous.
signature: [CompleteSpace E] {T : E →ₗ[𝕜] E} (hT : IsSymmetric T) : Continuous T

name: _root_.RCLike.inner_tmul_eq
informal: In `ℝ` or `ℂ` fields, the inner product on tensor products is essentially just the inner product with multiplication instead of tensors, i.e., `⟪a ⊗ₜ b, c ⊗ₜ d⟫ = ⟪a * b, c * d⟫`.
signature: (a b c d : 𝕜) : inner 𝕜 (a ⊗ₜ[𝕜] b) (c ⊗ₜ[𝕜] d) = inner 𝕜 (a * b) (c * d)

name: Balanced.subset_balancedCore_of_subset
informal: The balanced core of `t` is maximal in the sense that it contains any balanced subset `s` of `t`.
signature: (hs : Balanced 𝕜 s) (h : s ⊆ t) : s ⊆ balancedCore 𝕜 t

name: Balanced.balancedHull_subset_of_subset
informal: The balanced hull of `s` is minimal in the sense that it is contained in any balanced superset `t` of `s`.
signature: (ht : Balanced 𝕜 t) (h : s ⊆ t) : balancedHull 𝕜 s ⊆ t

name: Balanced.smul_mono
informal: Scalar multiplication (by possibly different types) of a balanced set is monotone.
signature: (hs : Balanced 𝕝 s) {a : 𝕝} (h : ‖a‖ ≤ ‖b‖) : a • s ⊆ b • s

name: IsVonNBounded.extend_scalars
informal: If a set is von Neumann bounded with respect to a smaller field, then it is also von Neumann bounded with respect to a larger field. See also `Bornology.IsVonNBounded.restrict_scalars` below.
signature: [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] (𝕝 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕝] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜 𝕝] [Module 𝕝 E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕝 E] [IsScalarTower 𝕜 𝕝 E] {s : Set E} (h : IsVonNBounded 𝕜 s) : IsVonNBounded 𝕝 s

name: Module.Dual.exists_continuous_extension_of_le_seminorm_real
informal: **Hahn-Banach theorem** for linear functionals dominated by a continuous seminorm on polynormable spaces over `ℝ`.
signature: [Module ℝ E] [PolynormableSpace ℝ E] (S : Subspace ℝ E) (f : Dual ℝ S) {p : Seminorm ℝ E} (hp_cont : Continuous p) (hp : ∀ x, f x ≤ p x) : ∃ g : StrongDual ℝ E, (∀ x : S, g x = f x) ∧ ∀ x, |g x| ≤ p x

name: StrongDual.exists_extension
informal: **Hahn-Banach theorem** for continuous linear functionals on polynormable spaces over a field satisfying `IsRCLikeNormedField`.
signature: {𝕜} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜] [Module 𝕜 E] [PolynormableSpace 𝕜 E] (S : Submodule 𝕜 E) (f : StrongDual 𝕜 S) : ∃ g : StrongDual 𝕜 E, ∀ x : S, g x = f x

name: Submodule.ClosedComplemented.of_finiteDimensional
informal: A finite-dimensional submodule of a polynormable space over a field satisfying `IsRCLikeNormedField` is `Submodule.ClosedComplemented`.
signature: [PolynormableSpace 𝕜 F] (S : Submodule 𝕜 F) [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 S] : S.ClosedComplemented

name: withSeminorms_iff_mem_nhds_isVonNBounded
informal: In a topological vector space, the topology is generated by a single seminorm `p` iff the unit ball for this seminorm is a bounded neighborhood of `0`.
signature: [IsTopologicalAddGroup E] [ContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 E] {p : Seminorm 𝕜 E} : WithSeminorms (fun (_ : Fin 1) ↦ p) ↔ p.ball 0 1 ∈ 𝓝 0 ∧ IsVonNBounded 𝕜 (p.ball 0 1)

name: NormedSpace.toLocallyConvexSpace'
informal: Not an instance since `𝕜` can't be inferred. See `NormedSpace.toLocallyConvexSpace` for a slightly weaker instance version.
signature: [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [Module ℝ E] [IsScalarTower ℝ 𝕜 E] : LocallyConvexSpace ℝ E

name: toLinearMap₂'_zero_iff
informal: For `A` positive semidefinite, we have `x⋆ A x = 0` iff `A x = 0` (linear maps version).
signature: [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : PosSemidef A) (x : n → 𝕜) : Matrix.toLinearMap₂' 𝕜 A (star x) x = 0 ↔ A *ᵥ x = 0

name: PosSemidef.kronecker
informal: The kronecker product of two positive semi-definite matrices is positive semi-definite.
signature: {x : Matrix n n 𝕜} {y : Matrix m m 𝕜} (hx : x.PosSemidef) (hy : y.PosSemidef) : (x ⊗ₖ y).PosSemidef

name: PosDef.kronecker
informal: The kronecker of two positive definite matrices is positive definite.
signature: {x : Matrix n n 𝕜} {y : Matrix m m 𝕜} (hx : x.PosDef) (hy : y.PosDef) : (x ⊗ₖ y).PosDef

name: geom_mean_le_arith_mean
informal: **AM-GM inequality**: The geometric mean is less than or equal to the arithmetic mean.
signature: {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (w : ι → ℝ) (z : ι → ℝ) (hw : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ w i) (hw' : 0 < ∑ i ∈ s, w i) (hz : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ z i) : (∏ i ∈ s, z i ^ w i) ^ (∑ i ∈ s, w i)⁻¹ ≤ (∑ i ∈ s, w i * z i) / (∑ i ∈ s, w i)

name: geom_mean_le_arith_mean2_weighted
informal: **AM-GM inequality**: The geometric mean is less than or equal to the arithmetic mean, weighted version for two `NNReal` numbers.
signature: (w₁ w₂ p₁ p₂ : ℝ≥0) : w₁ + w₂ = 1 → p₁ ^ (w₁ : ℝ) * p₂ ^ (w₂ : ℝ) ≤ w₁ * p₁ + w₂ * p₂

name: harm_mean_le_geom_mean
informal: **HM-GM inequality**: The harmonic mean is less than or equal to the geometric mean.
signature: {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (w : ι → ℝ) (z : ι → ℝ) (hw : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < w i) (hw' : 0 < ∑ i ∈ s, w i) (hz : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < z i) : (∑ i ∈ s, w i) / (∑ i ∈ s, w i / z i) ≤ (∏ i ∈ s, z i ^ w i) ^ (∑ i ∈ s, w i)⁻¹

name: young_inequality_eq_iff_of_nonneg
informal: **Young's inequality** equality condition for nonnegative real numbers.
signature: {a b p q : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hpq : p.HolderConjugate q) : a * b = a ^ p / p + b ^ q / q ↔ a ^ p = b ^ q

name: young_inequality
informal: **Young's inequality**, `ℝ≥0` version. We use `{p q : ℝ≥0}` in order to avoid constructing witnesses of `0 ≤ p` and `0 ≤ q` for the denominators.
signature: (a b : ℝ≥0) {p q : ℝ≥0} (hpq : p.HolderConjugate q) : a * b ≤ a ^ (p : ℝ) / p + b ^ (q : ℝ) / q

name: young_inequality_real_eq_iff
informal: **Young's inequality** equality condition, `ℝ≥0` version with real conjugate exponents.
signature: (a b : ℝ≥0) {p q : ℝ} (hpq : p.HolderConjugate q) : a * b = a ^ p / p.toNNReal + b ^ q / q.toNNReal ↔ a ^ p = b ^ q

name: young_inequality_eq_iff
informal: **Young's inequality** equality condition, `ℝ≥0∞` version with real conjugate exponents.
signature: (a b : ℝ≥0∞) {p q : ℝ} (hpq : p.HolderConjugate q) : a * b = a ^ p / .ofReal p + b ^ q / .ofReal q ↔ (a = ⊤ ∧ b ≠ 0) ∨ (a ≠ 0 ∧ b = ⊤) ∨ a ^ p = b ^ q

name: inner_le_Lp_mul_Lq
informal: **Hölder inequality**: the scalar product of two functions is bounded by the product of their `L^p` and `L^q` norms when `p` and `q` are conjugate exponents. Version for sums over finite sets, with real-valued functions.
signature: (hpq : HolderConjugate p q) : ∑ i ∈ s, f i * g i ≤ (∑ i ∈ s, |f i| ^ p) ^ (1 / p) * (∑ i ∈ s, |g i| ^ q) ^ (1 / q)

name: Lp_add_le
informal: **Minkowski inequality**: the `L_p` seminorm of the sum of two vectors is less than or equal to the sum of the `L_p`-seminorms of the summands. A version for `Real`-valued functions.

name: inner_le_Lp_mul_Lq_of_nonneg
informal: **Hölder inequality**: the scalar product of two functions is bounded by the product of their `L^p` and `L^q` norms when `p` and `q` are conjugate exponents. Version for sums over finite sets, with real-valued nonnegative functions.
signature: (hpq : HolderConjugate p q) (hf : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ f i) (hg : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ g i) : ∑ i ∈ s, f i * g i ≤ (∑ i ∈ s, f i ^ p) ^ (1 / p) * (∑ i ∈ s, g i ^ q) ^ (1 / q)

name: Lp_add_le_of_nonneg
informal: **Minkowski inequality**: the `L_p` seminorm of the sum of two vectors is less than or equal to the sum of the `L_p`-seminorms of the summands. A version for `ℝ`-valued nonnegative functions.

name: Lp_add_le_tsum_of_nonneg
informal: **Minkowski inequality**: the `L_p` seminorm of the infinite sum of two vectors is less than or equal to the infinite sum of the `L_p`-seminorms of the summands, if these infinite sums both exist. A version for `ℝ`-valued functions. For an alternative version, convenient if the infinite sums are already expressed as `p`-th powers, see `Lp_add_le_hasSum_of_nonneg`.
signature: (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) (hg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) (hf_sum : Summable fun i => f i ^ p) (hg_sum : Summable fun i => g i ^ p) : (Summable fun i => (f i + g i) ^ p) ∧ (∑' i, (f i + g i) ^ p) ^ (1 / p) ≤ (∑' i, f i ^ p) ^ (1 / p) + (∑' i, g i ^ p) ^ (1 / p)

name: inner_le_Lp_mul_Lq
informal: **Hölder inequality**: the scalar product of two functions is bounded by the product of their `L^p` and `L^q` norms when `p` and `q` are conjugate exponents. Version for sums over finite sets, with `ℝ≥0∞`-valued functions.
signature: (hpq : p.HolderConjugate q) : ∑ i ∈ s, f i * g i ≤ (∑ i ∈ s, f i ^ p) ^ (1 / p) * (∑ i ∈ s, g i ^ q) ^ (1 / q)

name: Lp_add_le
informal: **Minkowski inequality**: the `L_p` seminorm of the sum of two vectors is less than or equal to the sum of the `L_p`-seminorms of the summands. A version for `ℝ≥0∞`-valued nonnegative functions.

name: rpow_arith_mean_le_arith_mean2_rpow
informal: Weighted generalized mean inequality, version for two elements of `ℝ≥0` and real exponents.
signature: (w₁ w₂ z₁ z₂ : ℝ≥0) (hw' : w₁ + w₂ = 1) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) : (w₁ * z₁ + w₂ * z₂) ^ p ≤ w₁ * z₁ ^ p + w₂ * z₂ ^ p

name: rpow_add_le_mul_rpow_add_rpow
informal: Unweighted mean inequality, version for two elements of `ℝ≥0` and real exponents.

name: rpow_arith_mean_le_arith_mean2_rpow
informal: Weighted generalized mean inequality, version for two elements of `ℝ≥0∞` and real exponents.
signature: (w₁ w₂ z₁ z₂ : ℝ≥0∞) (hw' : w₁ + w₂ = 1) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) : (w₁ * z₁ + w₂ * z₂) ^ p ≤ w₁ * z₁ ^ p + w₂ * z₂ ^ p

name: rpow_add_le_mul_rpow_add_rpow
informal: Unweighted mean inequality, version for two elements of `ℝ≥0∞` and real exponents.

name: eventually_analyticAt
informal: In a complete space, a function which is meromorphic at a point is analytic at all nearby points. The completeness assumption can be dispensed with if one assumes that `f` is meromorphic on a set around `x`, see `MeromorphicOn.eventually_analyticAt`.
signature: [CompleteSpace E] {f : 𝕜 → E} (h : MeromorphicAt f x) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≠] x, AnalyticAt 𝕜 f y

name: congr_codiscrete
informal: If `f` is meromorphic, if `g` agrees with `f` on a codiscrete set, then `g` is also meromorphic.
signature: (hf : Meromorphic f) (h₁ : f =ᶠ[codiscrete 𝕜] g) : Meromorphic g

name: _root_.meromorphic_congr_codiscrete
informal: If two functions differ only on a discrete set, then one is meromorphic iff so is the other.
signature: (h₁ : f =ᶠ[codiscrete 𝕜] g) : Meromorphic f ↔ Meromorphic g

name: mulSupport
informal: Helper Lemma: Identify the support of `d` as the mulsupport of the product defining the factorized rational function.
signature: (d : 𝕜 → ℤ) : (fun u ↦ (· - u) ^ d u).mulSupport = d.support

name: finprod_eq_fun
informal: Helper Lemma: If the support of `d` is finite, then evaluation of functions commutes with finprod, and the function `∏ᶠ u, (· - u) ^ d u` equals `fun x ↦ ∏ᶠ u, (x - u) ^ d u`.
signature: {d : 𝕜 → ℤ} (h : d.HasFiniteSupport) : (∏ᶠ u, (· - u) ^ d u) = fun x ↦ ∏ᶠ u, (x - u) ^ d u

name: analyticAt
informal: Factorized rational functions are analytic wherever the exponent is non-negative.
signature: {d : 𝕜 → ℤ} {x : 𝕜} (h : 0 ≤ d x) : AnalyticAt 𝕜 (∏ᶠ u, (· - u) ^ d u) x

name: ne_zero
informal: Factorized rational functions are non-zero wherever the exponent is zero.

name: extractFactor
informal: Helper Lemma for Computations: Extract one factor out of a factorized rational function.
signature: {d : 𝕜 → ℤ} (u₀ : 𝕜) (hd : d.HasFiniteSupport) : (∏ᶠ u, (· - u) ^ d u) = ((· - u₀) ^ d u₀) * (∏ᶠ u, (· - u) ^ (update d u₀ 0 u))

name: meromorphicOrderAt_ne_top
informal: Factorized rational functions are nowhere locally constant zero.
signature: {z : 𝕜} (d : 𝕜 → ℤ) : meromorphicOrderAt (∏ᶠ u, (· - u) ^ d u) z ≠ ⊤

name: frequently_zero_iff_eventuallyEq_zero
informal: The principle of isolated zeros: If `f` is meromorphic at `x`, then `f` vanishes eventually in a punctured neighborhood of `x` iff it vanishes frequently in punctured neighborhoods. See `AnalyticAt.frequently_zero_iff_eventually_zero` for a stronger result in the analytic case.
signature: (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : (∃ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] x, f z = 0) ↔ f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] 0

name: MeromorphicNFAt.meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg_iff_analyticAt
informal: If a function is meromorphic in normal form at `x`, then it has non-negative order iff it is analytic.
signature: (hf : MeromorphicNFAt f x) : 0 ≤ meromorphicOrderAt f x ↔ AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x

name: MeromorphicOn.meromorphicNFAt_mem_codiscreteWithin
informal: Meromorphic functions have normal form outside of a discrete subset in the domain of meromorphicity.
signature: {U : Set 𝕜} (hf : MeromorphicOn f U) : { x | MeromorphicNFAt f x } ∈ Filter.codiscreteWithin U

name: MeromorphicNFAt.meromorphicOrderAt_eq_zero_iff
informal: If `f` is meromorphic in normal form at `x`, then `f` has order zero iff it does not vanish at `x`. See `AnalyticAt.order_eq_zero_iff` for an analogous statement about analytic functions.
signature: (hf : MeromorphicNFAt f x) : meromorphicOrderAt f x = 0 ↔ f x ≠ 0

name: meromorphicNFAt_comp_iff_of_deriv_ne_zero
informal: A function is meromorphic in normal form at a point iff it is meromorphic in normal form after composition with an analytic function of nonvanishing derivative, such as translation.
signature: [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [CharZero 𝕜] {x : 𝕜} {g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hg : AnalyticAt 𝕜 g x) (hg' : deriv g x ≠ 0) : MeromorphicNFAt (f ∘ g) x ↔ MeromorphicNFAt f (g x)

name: tendsto_ne_zero_of_meromorphicOrderAt_eq_zero
informal: If the order of a meromorphic function is zero, then this function converges to a nonzero limit at this point. See also the iff version `tendsto_ne_zero_iff_meromorphicOrderAt_eq_zero`.
signature: (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (ho : meromorphicOrderAt f x = 0) : ∃ c ≠ 0, Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 c)

name: tendsto_zero_of_meromorphicOrderAt_pos
informal: If the order of a meromorphic function is positive, then this function converges to zero at this point. See also the iff version `tendsto_zero_iff_meromorphicOrderAt_pos`.
signature: (ho : 0 < meromorphicOrderAt f x) : Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 0)

name: tendsto_nhds_of_meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg
informal: If the order of a meromorphic function is nonnegative, then this function converges at this point. See also the iff version `tendsto_nhds_iff_meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg`.
signature: (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (ho : 0 ≤ meromorphicOrderAt f x) : ∃ c, Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 c)

name: tendsto_nhds_iff_meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg
informal: A meromorphic function converges to a limit iff its order is nonnegative.
signature: (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : (∃ c, Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 c)) ↔ 0 ≤ meromorphicOrderAt f x

name: tendsto_ne_zero_iff_meromorphicOrderAt_eq_zero
informal: A meromorphic function converges to a nonzero limit iff its order is zero.
signature: (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : (∃ c ≠ 0, Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 c)) ↔ meromorphicOrderAt f x = 0

name: tendsto_zero_iff_meromorphicOrderAt_pos
informal: A meromorphic function converges to zero iff its order is positive.
signature: (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) : (Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 0)) ↔ 0 < meromorphicOrderAt f x

name: meromorphicOrderAt_congr
informal: Meromorphic functions that agree in a punctured neighborhood of `z₀` have the same order at `z₀`.
signature: (hf₁₂ : f₁ =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] f₂) : meromorphicOrderAt f₁ x = meromorphicOrderAt f₂ x

name: AnalyticAt.meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg
informal: When seen as meromorphic functions, analytic functions have nonnegative order.
signature: (hf : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x) : 0 ≤ meromorphicOrderAt f x

name: meromorphicOrderAt_const_intCast
informal: The order of a constant function is `⊤` if the constant is zero and `0` otherwise.
signature: (z₀ : 𝕜) (n : ℤ) [Decidable ((n : 𝕜') = 0)] : meromorphicOrderAt (n : 𝕜 → 𝕜') z₀ = if (n : 𝕜') = 0 then ⊤ else (0 : WithTop ℤ)

name: meromorphicOrderAt_const_natCast
informal: The order of a constant function is `⊤` if the constant is zero and `0` otherwise.
signature: (z₀ : 𝕜) (n : ℕ) [Decidable ((n : 𝕜') = 0)] : meromorphicOrderAt (n : 𝕜 → 𝕜') z₀ = if (n : 𝕜') = 0 then ⊤ else (0 : WithTop ℤ)

name: meromorphicOrderAt_add
informal: The order of a sum is at least the minimum of the orders of the summands.
signature: (hf₁ : MeromorphicAt f₁ x) (hf₂ : MeromorphicAt f₂ x) : min (meromorphicOrderAt f₁ x) (meromorphicOrderAt f₂ x) ≤ meromorphicOrderAt (f₁ + f₂) x

name: meromorphicOrderAt_add_of_ne
informal: If two meromorphic functions have unequal orders, then the order of their sum is exactly the minimum of the orders of the summands.
signature: (hf₁ : MeromorphicAt f₁ x) (hf₂ : MeromorphicAt f₂ x) (h : meromorphicOrderAt f₁ x ≠ meromorphicOrderAt f₂ x) : meromorphicOrderAt (f₁ + f₂) x = min (meromorphicOrderAt f₁ x) (meromorphicOrderAt f₂ x)

name: meromorphicOrderAt_deriv_eq_sub_one
informal: The meromorphic order of the derivative is one less than the order of the original function. This however is not true if the characteristic of the domain field divides the original order, where the order of the derivative can rise to a larger integer.
signature: [CompleteSpace E] {f : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜} {n : ℤ} (hn : (n : 𝕜) ≠ 0) (hf : meromorphicOrderAt f x = ↑n) : meromorphicOrderAt (deriv f) x = ↑(n - 1)

name: meromorphicOrderAt_deriv
informal: Equivalent to `meromorphicOrderAt_deriv_eq_sub_one` with a slightly different statement so the conclusion matches more targets
signature: [CompleteSpace E] {f : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜} {n : ℤ} (hn : (↑(n + 1) : 𝕜) ≠ 0) (hf : meromorphicOrderAt f x = ↑(n + 1)) : meromorphicOrderAt (deriv f) x = ↑n

name: meromorphicOrderAt_logDeriv_eq_neg_one
informal: At zeros and poles of a meromorphic function `f`, the logarithmic derivative has a simple pole: its meromorphic order equals `-1`.
signature: [CharZero 𝕜] (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (h₁ : meromorphicOrderAt f x ≠ 0) (h₂ : meromorphicOrderAt f x ≠ ⊤) : meromorphicOrderAt (logDeriv f) x = -1

name: meromorphicOrderAt_logDeriv_nonneg
informal: At points where a meromorphic function has order zero, the meromorphic order of the logarithmic derivative is nonnegative.
signature: (hf : MeromorphicAt f x) (h : meromorphicOrderAt f x = 0) : 0 ≤ meromorphicOrderAt (logDeriv f) x

name: AnalyticAt.meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_of_eq_nhdsNE
informal: Definition of the trailing coefficient in case where `f` is meromorphic and a presentation of the form `f = (z - x) ^ order • g z` is given, with `g` analytic at `x`.
signature: (h₁g : AnalyticAt 𝕜 g x) (h : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] fun z ↦ (z - x) ^ (meromorphicOrderAt f x).untop₀ • g z) : meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f x = g x

name: MeromorphicAt.tendsto_nhds_meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt
informal: If `f` is meromorphic at `x`, then the trailing coefficient of `f` at `x` is the limit of the function `(· - x) ^ (-order) • f`.
signature: (h : MeromorphicAt f x) : Tendsto ((· - x) ^ (-(meromorphicOrderAt f x).untop₀) • f) (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f x))

name: MeromorphicAt.meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_ne_zero
informal: If `f` is meromorphic of finite order at `x`, then the trailing coefficient is not zero.
signature: (h₁ : MeromorphicAt f x) (h₂ : meromorphicOrderAt f x ≠ ⊤) : meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f x ≠ 0

name: MeromorphicAt.meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_mul
informal: The trailing coefficient of a product is the product of the trailing coefficients.
signature: {f₁ f₂ : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf₁ : MeromorphicAt f₁ x) (hf₂ : MeromorphicAt f₂ x) : meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt (f₁ * f₂) x = (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f₁ x) * (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f₂ x)

name: MeromorphicAt.meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_fun_mul
informal: The trailing coefficient of a product is the product of the trailing coefficients.
signature: {f₁ f₂ : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf₁ : MeromorphicAt f₁ x) (hf₂ : MeromorphicAt f₂ x) : meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt (fun z ↦ f₁ z * f₂ z) x = (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f₁ x) * (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f₂ x)

name: meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_inv
informal: The trailing coefficient of the inverse function is the inverse of the trailing coefficient.
signature: {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} : meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f⁻¹ x = (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f x)⁻¹

name: meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_fun_inv
informal: The trailing coefficient of the inverse function is the inverse of the trailing coefficient.
signature: {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} : meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt (fun z ↦ (f z)⁻¹) x = (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f x)⁻¹

name: MeromorphicAt.meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_zpow
informal: The trailing coefficient of the power of a function is the power of the trailing coefficient.
signature: {n : ℤ} {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁ : MeromorphicAt f x) : meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt (f ^ n) x = (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f x) ^ n

name: MeromorphicAt.meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_fun_zpow
informal: The trailing coefficient of the power of a function is the power of the trailing coefficient.
signature: {n : ℤ} {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁ : MeromorphicAt f x) : meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt (fun z ↦ f z ^ n) x = (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f x) ^ n

name: MeromorphicAt.meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_pow
informal: The trailing coefficient of the power of a function is the power of the trailing coefficient.
signature: {n : ℕ} {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁ : MeromorphicAt f x) : meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt (f ^ n) x = (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f x) ^ n

name: MeromorphicAt.meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_fun_pow
informal: The trailing coefficient of the power of a function is the power of the trailing coefficient.
signature: {n : ℕ} {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (h₁ : MeromorphicAt f x) : meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt (fun z ↦ f z ^ n) x = (meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f x) ^ n

name: AffineBasis.interior_convexHull
informal: Given a finite-dimensional normed real vector space, the interior of the convex hull of an affine basis is the set of points whose barycentric coordinates are strictly positive with respect to this basis. TODO Restate this result for affine spaces (instead of vector spaces) once the definition of convexity is generalised to this setting.
signature: {ι E : Type*} [Finite ι] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (b : AffineBasis ι ℝ E) : interior (convexHull ℝ (range b)) = {x | ∀ i, 0 < b.coord i x}

name: midpoint_fixed
informal: If an isometric self-homeomorphism of a normed vector space over `ℝ` fixes `x` and `y`, then it fixes the midpoint of `[x, y]`. This is a lemma for a more general Mazur-Ulam theorem, see below.
signature: {x y : PE} : ∀ e : PE ≃ᵢ PE, e x = x → e y = y → e (midpoint ℝ x y) = midpoint ℝ x y

name: exp_mem
informal: A subalgebra of `𝔸` that is closed topologically and under `ℚ`-scaling is closed under `exp`.
signature: {R S : Type*} [Monoid R] [SMul ℚ R] [MulAction R 𝔸] [Algebra ℚ 𝔸] [IsScalarTower ℚ R 𝔸] [SetLike S 𝔸] [SubsemiringClass S 𝔸] [SMulMemClass S R 𝔸] {s : S} (h_closed : IsClosed (s : Set 𝔸)) {x : 𝔸} (h : x ∈ s) : exp x ∈ s

name: exp_add_of_commute_of_mem_ball
informal: In a Banach-algebra `𝔸` over a normed field `𝕂` of characteristic zero, if `x` and `y` are in the disk of convergence and commute, then `NormedSpace.exp (x + y) = (NormedSpace.exp x) * (NormedSpace.exp y)`.
signature: [CharZero 𝕂] {x y : 𝔸} (hxy : Commute x y) (hx : x ∈ Metric.eball (0 : 𝔸) (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸).radius) (hy : y ∈ Metric.eball (0 : 𝔸) (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸).radius) : exp (x + y) = exp x * exp y

name: exp_add_of_mem_ball
informal: In a commutative Banach-algebra `𝔸` over a normed field `𝕂` of characteristic zero, `NormedSpace.exp (x+y) = (NormedSpace.exp x) * (NormedSpace.exp y)` for all `x`, `y` in the disk of convergence.
signature: [CharZero 𝕂] {x y : 𝔸} (hx : x ∈ Metric.eball (0 : 𝔸) (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸).radius) (hy : y ∈ Metric.eball (0 : 𝔸) (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸).radius) : exp (x + y) = exp x * exp y

name: exp_sum_of_commute
informal: In a Banach-algebra `𝔸` over `𝕂 = ℝ` or `𝕂 = ℂ`, if a family of elements `f i` mutually commute then `NormedSpace.exp (∑ i, f i) = ∏ i, NormedSpace.exp (f i)`.
signature: {ι} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → 𝔸) (h : (s : Set ι).Pairwise (Commute on f)) : exp (∑ i ∈ s, f i) = s.noncommProd (fun i => exp (f i)) fun _ hi _ hj _ => (h.of_refl hi hj).exp

name: expSeries_eq_expSeries
informal: If a normed ring `𝔸` is a normed algebra over two fields, then they define the same `expSeries` on `𝔸`.
signature: (n : ℕ) (x : 𝔸) : (expSeries 𝕂 𝔸 n fun _ => x) = expSeries 𝕂' 𝔸 n fun _ => x

name: differentiableOn_inverse_one_sub_smul
informal: In a Banach algebra `A` over `𝕜`, for `a : A` the function `fun z ↦ (1 - z • a)⁻¹` is differentiable on any closed ball centered at zero of radius `r < (spectralRadius 𝕜 a)⁻¹`.
signature: [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜 A] [CompleteSpace A] {a : A} {r : ℝ≥0} (hr : (r : ℝ≥0∞) < (spectralRadius 𝕜 a)⁻¹) : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 (fun z : 𝕜 => (1 - z • a)⁻¹ʳ) (Metric.closedBall 0 r)

name: expSeries_even_of_imaginary
informal: The even terms of `expSeries` are real, and correspond to the series for $\cos ‖q‖$.
signature: {q : Quaternion ℝ} (hq : q.re = 0) (n : ℕ) : expSeries ℝ (Quaternion ℝ) (2 * n) (fun _ => q) = ↑((-1 : ℝ) ^ n * ‖q‖ ^ (2 * n) / (2 * n)!)

name: expSeries_odd_of_imaginary
informal: The odd terms of `expSeries` are real, and correspond to the series for $\frac{q}{‖q‖} \sin ‖q‖$.
signature: {q : Quaternion ℝ} (hq : q.re = 0) (n : ℕ) : expSeries ℝ (Quaternion ℝ) (2 * n + 1) (fun _ => q) = (((-1 : ℝ) ^ n * ‖q‖ ^ (2 * n + 1) / (2 * n + 1)!) / ‖q‖) • q

name: exp_of_re_eq_zero
informal: The closed form for the quaternion exponential on imaginary quaternions.
signature: (q : Quaternion ℝ) (hq : q.re = 0) : exp q = ↑(Real.cos ‖q‖) + (Real.sin ‖q‖ / ‖q‖) • q

name: exp_eq
informal: The closed form for the quaternion exponential on arbitrary quaternions.
signature: (q : Quaternion ℝ) : exp q = exp q.re • (↑(Real.cos ‖q.im‖) + (Real.sin ‖q.im‖ / ‖q.im‖) • q.im)

name: spectralRadius_eq
informal: If `𝕜₁` is a normed field contained as subfield of a larger normed field `𝕜₂`, and if `a : A` is an element whose `𝕜₂` spectrum restricts to `𝕜₁`, then the spectral radii over each scalar field coincide.
signature: {𝕜₁ 𝕜₂ A : Type*} [NormedField 𝕜₁] [NormedField 𝕜₂] [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜₁ A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜₂ A] [NormedAlgebra 𝕜₁ 𝕜₂] [IsScalarTower 𝕜₁ 𝕜₂ A] {f : 𝕜₂ → 𝕜₁} {a : A} (h : SpectrumRestricts a f) : spectralRadius 𝕜₁ a = spectralRadius 𝕜₂ a

name: IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange
informal: If `K` is an algebraically closed dense subfield of a complete nonarchimedean normed field `L` of characteristic zero, then `L` is also algebraically closed.
signature: {K L : Type*} [Field K] [NontriviallyNormedField L] [CompleteSpace L] [CharZero L] [IsUltrametricDist L] [Algebra K L] (hi : DenseRange (algebraMap K L)) [IsAlgClosed K] : IsAlgClosed L

name: discreteTopology_or_nontriviallyNormedField
informal: A normed field is either nontrivially normed or has a discrete topology. In the discrete topology case, all the norms are 1, by `norm_eq_one_iff_ne_zero_of_discrete`. The nontrivially normed field instance is provided by a subtype with a proof that the forgetful inheritance to the existing `NormedField` instance is definitionally true. This allows one to have the new `NontriviallyNormedField` instance without data clashes.
signature: (𝕜 : Type*) [h : NormedField 𝕜] : DiscreteTopology 𝕜 ∨ Nonempty ({h' : NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜 // h'.toNormedField = h})

name: ProperSpace.of_nontriviallyNormedField_of_weaklyLocallyCompactSpace
informal: A weakly locally compact normed field is proper. This is a specialization of `ProperSpace.of_locallyCompactSpace` which holds for `NormedSpace`s but requires more imports.
signature: (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace 𝕜] : ProperSpace 𝕜

name: locallyCompactSpace
informal: If the absolute value of a normed field factors through an embedding into another normed field that is locally compact, then the completion of the first normed field is also locally compact.
signature: [LocallyCompactSpace L] (h : Isometry f) : LocallyCompactSpace v.Completion

name: NormedAddCommGroup.summable_imp_tendsto_of_complete
informal: In a complete normed additive group, every absolutely convergent series converges in the space.
signature: [CompleteSpace E] (u : ℕ → E) (hu : Summable (‖u ·‖)) : ∃ a, Tendsto (fun n => ∑ i ∈ range n, u i) atTop (𝓝 a)

name: opNorm_le_bound
informal: If one controls the norm of every `f x`, then one controls the norm of `f`.

name: opNorm_zero_iff
informal: For normed groups, an operator is zero iff its norm vanishes.
signature: {V₁ V₂ : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V₁] [NormedAddCommGroup V₂] {f : NormedAddGroupHom V₁ V₂} : ‖f‖ = 0 ↔ f = 0

name: norm_normedMk_eq_one
informal: The operator norm of the projection is `1` if there is an element whose norm is different from `0`.
signature: [NontrivialTopology M] : ‖normedMk (M

name: prod_sup_edist_ne_top_aux
informal: An auxiliary lemma used twice in the proof of `WithLp.prodPseudoMetricAux` below. Not intended for use outside this file.
signature: [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β] (f g : WithLp ∞ (α × β)) : edist f.fst g.fst ⊔ edist f.snd g.snd ≠ ⊤

name: range_proj_eq_span
informal: The range of the projection is the span of the first `n` basis elements.
signature: (n : ℕ) : (b.proj n).toLinearMap.range = Submodule.span 𝕜 (b '' ↑(Finset.range n))

name: enorm_proj_le_enormProjBound
informal: The enorm of any projection is bounded by the basis constant.
signature: (n : ℕ) : ‖b.proj n‖ₑ ≤ b.enormProjBound

name: bddAbove_range_nnnorm_proj
informal: The projection norms are bounded above in a complete space.
signature: [CompleteSpace X] : BddAbove (Set.range (fun n : ℕ ↦ ‖b.proj n‖₊))

name: norm_proj_le_nnnormProjBound
informal: The norm of any projection is bounded by the basis constant.
signature: [CompleteSpace X] (n : ℕ) : ‖b.proj n‖ ≤ b.nnnormProjBound

name: algebraMap_isometry
informal: In a normed algebra, the inclusion of the base field in the extended field is an isometry.
signature: [NormOneClass 𝕜'] : Isometry (algebraMap 𝕜 𝕜')

name: of_isInvertible
informal: An invertible continuous linear map has a continuous left inverse.
signature: (hf : IsInvertible f) : f.HasLeftInverse

name: of_injective_of_finiteDimensional
informal: If `f : E → F` is injective and `E` is finite-dimensional, `f` has a continuous left inverse.
signature: [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 F] (hf : Injective f) : f.HasLeftInverse

name: closedComplemented_range
informal: If `f` has a continuous left inverse, its range admits a closed complement.
signature: (hf : f.HasLeftInverse) : Submodule.ClosedComplemented f.range

name: of_isInvertible
informal: An invertible continuous linear map has a continuous right inverse.
signature: (hf : IsInvertible f) : f.HasRightInverse

name: of_surjective_of_finiteDimensional
informal: If `f : E → F` is surjective and `F` is finite-dimensional, `f` has a continuous right inverse.
signature: [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 F] (hf : Surjective f) : f.HasRightInverse

name: convexOn_norm
informal: The norm on a real normed space is convex on any convex set. See also `Seminorm.convexOn` and `convexOn_univ_norm`.

name: polar_closedBall
informal: The `polar` of closed ball in a normed space `E` is the closed ball of the dual with inverse radius.

name: IsLocalMax.norm_add_self
informal: If `f : α → E` is a function such that `norm ∘ f` has a local maximum at a point `c`, then the function `fun x => ‖f x + f c‖` has a local maximum at `c`.
signature: (h : IsLocalMax (norm ∘ f) c) : IsLocalMax (fun x => ‖f x + f c‖) c

name: FiniteDimensional.of_isCompact_closedBall₀
informal: **Riesz's theorem**: if a closed ball with center zero of positive radius is compact in a vector space, then the space is finite-dimensional.
signature: {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [Module 𝕜 V] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 V] {r : ℝ} (rpos : 0 < r) (h : IsCompact (Metric.closedBall (0 : V) r)) : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 V

name: FiniteDimensional.of_isCompact_closedBall
informal: **Riesz's theorem**: if a closed ball of positive radius is compact in a vector space, then the space is finite-dimensional.

name: FiniteDimensional.proper
informal: Any finite-dimensional vector space over a locally compact field is proper. We do not register this as an instance to avoid an instance loop when trying to prove the properness of `𝕜`, and the search for `𝕜` as an unknown metavariable. Declare the instance explicitly when needed.
signature: [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] : ProperSpace E

name: summable_norm_iff
informal: In a finite-dimensional vector space over `ℝ`, the series `∑ x, ‖f x‖` is unconditionally summable if and only if the series `∑ x, f x` is unconditionally summable. One implication holds in any complete normed space, while the other holds only in finite-dimensional spaces.
signature: {α E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {f : α → E} : (Summable fun x => ‖f x‖) ↔ Summable f

name: Module.Dual.norm_extendRCLike_le_seminorm

name: norm_extendRCLike_le_seminorm

name: norm_add
informal: If `x` and `y` are on the same ray, then the triangle inequality becomes the equality: the norm of `x + y` is the sum of the norms of `x` and `y`. The converse is true for a strictly convex space.
signature: (h : SameRay ℝ x y) : ‖x + y‖ = ‖x‖ + ‖y‖

name: sameRay_iff_inv_norm_smul_eq_of_ne
informal: Two nonzero vectors `x y` in a real normed space are on the same ray if and only if the unit vectors `‖x‖⁻¹ • x` and `‖y‖⁻¹ • y` are equal.
signature: (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) : SameRay ℝ x y ↔ ‖x‖⁻¹ • x = ‖y‖⁻¹ • y

name: sameRay_iff_of_norm_eq
informal: Two vectors of the same norm are on the same ray if and only if they are equal.
signature: (h : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖) : SameRay ℝ x y ↔ x = y

name: SameRay.eq_of_norm_eq
informal: If two points on the same ray have the same norm, then they are equal.

name: SameRay.norm_eq_iff
informal: The norms of two vectors on the same ray are equal if and only if they are equal.
signature: (h : SameRay ℝ x y) : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖ ↔ x = y

name: isBounded_iff_isVonNBounded

If `s` interpreted as a set in the space of maps `E → F` with topology of pointwise convergence is closed, then it is compact. name: discrete_gronwall
informal: Discrete Grönwall inequality, exponential form: if `u (n+1) ≤ (1 + c n) * u n + b n` with `b`, `c`, and `u n₀` non-negative, then `u n ≤ (u n₀ + ∑ b k) * exp (∑ c i)`.

name: mahlerMeasure_le_sqrt_sum_sq_norm_coeff

Combined with the multiplicativity of the Mahler measure (`mahlerMeasure_mul`), it gives the Mignotte bound on coefficients of polynomial factors. TODO: restate using a dedicated polynomial ℓ² norm once one is defined (see the TODO in `Mathlib.Analysis.Polynomial.Norm`).

name: abs_log_sub_add_sum_range_le
informal: A crude lemma estimating the difference between `log (1-x)` and its Taylor series at `0`, where the main point of the bound is that it tends to `0`. The goal is to deduce the series expansion of the logarithm, in `hasSum_pow_div_log_of_abs_lt_1`. TODO: use one of generic theorems about Taylor's series to prove this estimate.

name: hasDerivAt_half_log_one_add_div_one_sub_sub_sum_range
informal: Compute the derivative of the difference between $\frac{1}{2} * \log(\frac{1+x}{1-x})$ and its Taylor series at `0` up to order `n`. This is an auxiliary lemma for `sum_range_sub_log_div_le` and `sum_range_le_log_div`. Note that thanks to the geometric series, the derivative has a particularly simple form, and means that it is more convenient to avoid Taylor's theorem.

name: sum_range_sub_log_div_le
informal: A lemma estimating the difference between $\frac{1}{2} * \log(\frac{1+x}{1-x})$ and its Taylor series at `0`, where the bound tends to `0`. This bound is particularly useful for explicit estimates of logarithms. Note that thanks to the geometric series, the derivative has a particularly simple form, and means that it is more convenient to avoid Taylor's theorem for this proof.

name: sum_range_le_log_div
informal: For `0 ≤ x < 1`, the partial sums of the series expansion of $\frac{1}{2} * \log(\frac{1+x}{1-x})$ at `0` form a lower bound for it. This shows that the absolute value in `sum_range_sub_log_div_le` can be dropped, and gives explicit lower bounds for logarithms.

name: summable_indicator_mod_iff_summable
informal: A sequence `f` with values in an additive topological group `R` is summable on the residue class of `k` mod `m` if and only if `f (m*n + k)` is summable.
signature: {R : Type*} [AddCommGroup R] [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalAddGroup R] (m : ℕ) [hm : NeZero m] (k : ℕ) (f : ℕ → R) : Summable ({n : ℕ | (n : ZMod m) = k}.indicator f) ↔ Summable fun n ↦ f (m * n + k)

name: not_summable_of_antitone_of_neg
informal: If `f : ℕ → ℝ` is decreasing and has a negative term, then `f` is not summable.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℝ} (hf : Antitone f) {n : ℕ} (hn : f n < 0) : ¬ Summable f

name: not_summable_indicator_mod_of_antitone_of_neg
informal: If `f : ℕ → ℝ` is decreasing and has a negative term, then `f` restricted to a residue class is not summable.
signature: {m : ℕ} [hm : NeZero m] {f : ℕ → ℝ} (hf : Antitone f) {n : ℕ} (hn : f n < 0) (k : ZMod m) : ¬ Summable ({n : ℕ | (n : ZMod m) = k}.indicator f)

name: summable_indicator_mod_iff_summable_indicator_mod
informal: If a decreasing sequence of real numbers is summable on one residue class modulo `m`, then it is also summable on every other residue class mod `m`.
signature: {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] {f : ℕ → ℝ} (hf : Antitone f) {k : ZMod m} (l : ZMod m) (hs : Summable ({n : ℕ | (n : ZMod m) = k}.indicator f)) : Summable ({n : ℕ | (n : ZMod m) = l}.indicator f)

name: summable_indicator_mod_iff
informal: A decreasing sequence of real numbers is summable on a residue class if and only if it is summable.
signature: {m : ℕ} [NeZero m] {f : ℕ → ℝ} (hf : Antitone f) (k : ZMod m) : Summable ({n : ℕ | (n : ZMod m) = k}.indicator f) ↔ Summable f

name: conjugateEquiv_of_iso
informal: If `α` is a natural transformation between left adjoints whose conjugate natural transformation is an isomorphism, then `α` is an isomorphism. The converse is given in `conjugateEquiv_iso`.
signature: (α : L₂ ⟶ L₁) [IsIso (conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α)] : IsIso α

name: conjugateEquiv_symm_of_iso
informal: If `α` is a natural transformation between right adjoints whose conjugate natural transformation is an isomorphism, then `α` is an isomorphism. The converse is given in `conjugateEquiv_symm_iso`.
signature: (α : R₁ ⟶ R₂) [IsIso ((conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂).symm α)] : IsIso α

name: iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv
informal: When all four functors in a square are left adjoints, the mates operation can be iterated: ``` L₁ R₁ R₁ C --→ D C ←-- D C ←-- D F₁ ↓ ↗ ↓ F₂ F₁ ↓ ↘ ↓ F₂ U₁ ↑ ↙ ↑ U₂ E --→ F E ←-- F E ←-- F L₂ R₂ R₂ ``` In this case the iterated mate equals the conjugate of the original transformation and is thus an isomorphism if and only if the original transformation is. This explains why some Beck-Chevalley natural transformations are natural isomorphisms.
signature: (α : TwoSquare F₁ L₁ L₂ F₂) : (mateEquiv adj₄ adj₃ (mateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α)).natTrans = conjugateEquiv (adj₁.comp adj₄) (adj₃.comp adj₂) α

name: epi_leftTriple_rightToLeft_iff_mono_rightTriple_leftToRight
informal: For an adjoint quadruple `L ⊣ F ⊣ G ⊣ R` where `F` (and hence also `R`) is fully faithful and its domain / codomain has all pushouts resp. pullbacks, the natural transformation `G ⟶ L` is an epimorphism iff the natural transformation `F ⟶ R` is a monomorphism.
signature: [HasPullbacks C] [HasPushouts D] : Epi q.leftTriple.rightToLeft ↔ Mono q.rightTriple.leftToRight

name: epi_leftTriple_leftToRight_iff_mono_rightTriple_rightToLeft
informal: For an adjoint quadruple `L ⊣ F ⊣ G ⊣ R` where `L` and `G` are fully faithful and their domain and codomain have all pullbacks resp. pushouts, the natural transformation `L ⟶ G` is an epimorphism iff the natural transformation `R ⟶ F` is a monomorphism.
signature: [HasPullbacks C] [HasPushouts D] : Epi q.leftTriple.leftToRight ↔ Mono q.rightTriple.rightToLeft

name: conjugateEquiv_of_iso
informal: If `α` is a 2-morphism between left adjoints whose conjugate 2-morphism is an isomorphism, then `α` is an isomorphism. The converse is given in `conjugateEquiv_iso`.
signature: (α : l₂ ⟶ l₁) [IsIso (conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α)] : IsIso α

name: conjugateEquiv_symm_of_iso
informal: If `α` is a 2-morphism between right adjoints whose conjugate 2-morphism is an isomorphism, then `α` is an isomorphism. The converse is given in `conjugateEquiv_symm_iso`.
signature: (α : r₁ ⟶ r₂) [IsIso ((conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂).symm α)] : IsIso α

name: iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv
informal: When all four morphisms in a square are left adjoints, the mates operation can be iterated: ``` l₁ r₁ r₁ a --→ b a ←-- b a ←-- b f₁ ↓ ↗ ↓ f₂ f₁ ↓ ↘ ↓ f₂ u₁ ↑ ↙ ↑ u₂ c --→ d c ←-- d c ←-- d l₂ r₂ r₂ ``` In this case the iterated mate equals the conjugate of the original 2-morphism and is thus an isomorphism if and only if the original 2-morphism is. This explains why some Beck-Chevalley 2-morphisms are isomorphisms.
signature: (α : f₁ ≫ l₂ ⟶ l₁ ≫ f₂) : mateEquiv adj₄ adj₃ (mateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α) = conjugateEquiv (adj₁.comp adj₄) (adj₃.comp adj₂) α

name: id_eq_id
informal: The identity in the category of categories equals the identity functor.
signature: (X : Cat.{u, v}) : (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).toFunctor = 𝟭 X

name: id_eq_id

signature: (X : Quiv) : 𝟙 X = 𝟭q X

name: Functor.initial_of_isCofiltered_costructuredArrow

name: preservesFiniteLimits_of_isFiltered_costructuredArrow_yoneda

signature: [IsFiltered (CostructuredArrow yoneda A)] : PreservesFiniteLimits A where preservesFiniteLimits _ _ _

name: preservesLimitsOfShape_pempty_of_preservesTerminal
informal: Preserving the terminal object implies preserving all limits of the empty diagram.
signature: [PreservesLimit (Functor.empty.{0} C) G] : PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete PEmpty.{1}) G where preservesLimit

name: preservesColimitsOfShape_pempty_of_preservesInitial
informal: Preserving the initial object implies preserving all colimits of the empty diagram.
signature: [PreservesColimit (Functor.empty.{0} C) G] : PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete PEmpty.{1}) G where preservesColimit

name: hasBinaryBiproducts_of_finite_biproducts

signature: [HasFiniteBiproducts C] : HasBinaryBiproducts C

name: initial_iff_empty_of_preserves_of_reflects

name: eq_of_epi_fork_ι
informal: Two morphisms are equal if there is a fork whose inclusion is epi.
signature: (t : Fork f g) [Epi (Fork.ι t)] : f = g

name: eq_of_epi_equalizer
informal: If the equalizer of two morphisms is an epimorphism, then the two morphisms are equal.
signature: [HasEqualizer f g] [Epi (equalizer.ι f g)] : f = g

name: eq_of_mono_cofork_π
informal: Two morphisms are equal if there is a cofork whose projection is mono.
signature: (t : Cofork f g) [Mono (Cofork.π t)] : f = g

name: eq_of_mono_coequalizer
informal: If the coequalizer of two morphisms is a monomorphism, then the two morphisms are equal.
signature: [HasCoequalizer f g] [Mono (coequalizer.π f g)] : f = g

name: hasFiniteProducts_of_hasProducts
informal: If a category has all products then in particular it has finite products.
signature: [HasProducts.{w} C] : HasFiniteProducts C

name: hasFiniteCoproducts_of_hasCoproducts
informal: If a category has all coproducts then in particular it has finite coproducts.
signature: [HasCoproducts.{w} C] : HasFiniteCoproducts C

name: image.eq_fac
informal: As long as the category has equalizers, the image inclusion maps commute with `image.eqToIso`.
signature: [HasEqualizers C] (h : f = f') : image.ι f = (image.eqToIso h).hom ≫ image.ι f'

name: isPullback_equalizer_prod
informal: The equalizer of `f g : X ⟶ Y` is the pullback of the diagonal map `Y ⟶ Y × Y` along the map `(f, g) : X ⟶ Y × Y`.

name: isPushout_coequalizer_coprod
informal: The coequalizer of `f g : X ⟶ Y` is the pushout of the diagonal map `X ⨿ X ⟶ X` along the map `(f, g) : X ⨿ X ⟶ Y`.
signature: [HasCoequalizer f g] [HasBinaryCoproduct X X] : IsPushout (coprod.desc f g) (coprod.desc (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _)) (coequalizer.π f g) (f ≫ coequalizer.π f g)

name: hasPullback_symmetry
informal: Making this a global instance would make the typeclass search go in an infinite loop.
signature: [HasPullback f g] : HasPullback g f

name: hasPushout_symmetry
informal: Making this a global instance would make the typeclass search go in an infinite loop.
signature: [HasPushout f g] : HasPushout g f

name: mono_snd_of_is_pullback_of_mono
informal: Monomorphisms are stable under pullback in the first argument.
signature: {t : PullbackCone f g} (ht : IsLimit t) [Mono f] : Mono t.snd

name: mono_fst_of_is_pullback_of_mono
informal: Monomorphisms are stable under pullback in the second argument.
signature: {t : PullbackCone f g} (ht : IsLimit t) [Mono g] : Mono t.fst

name: InitialMonoClass.of_terminal
informal: To show a category is an `InitialMonoClass` it suffices to show the unique morphism from the initial object to a terminal object is a monomorphism.
signature: [HasInitial C] [HasTerminal C] (h : Mono (initial.to (⊤_ C))) : InitialMonoClass C

name: mono_of_isLimit_parallelFamily
informal: The wide equalizer morphism in any limit cone is a monomorphism.
signature: [Nonempty J] {c : Cone (parallelFamily f)} (i : IsLimit c) : Mono (Trident.ι c) where right_cancellation _ _ w

name: epi_of_isColimit_parallelFamily
informal: The wide coequalizer morphism in any colimit cocone is an epimorphism.
signature: [Nonempty J] {c : Cocone (parallelFamily f)} (i : IsColimit c) : Epi (c.ι.app one) where left_cancellation _ _ w

name: hasWidePushouts_shrink
informal: If a category has wide pushouts on a higher universe level it also has wide pushouts on a lower universe level.
signature: [HasWidePushouts.{max w w'} C] : HasWidePushouts.{w} C

name: hasWidePullbacks_shrink
informal: If a category has wide pullbacks on a higher universe level it also has wide pullbacks on a lower universe level.
signature: [HasWidePullbacks.{max w w'} C] : HasWidePullbacks.{w} C

name: hasZeroObject_of_hasInitial_object
informal: If there are zero morphisms, any initial object is a zero object.
signature: [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasInitial C] : HasZeroObject C

name: hasZeroObject_of_hasTerminal_object
informal: If there are zero morphisms, any terminal object is a zero object.
signature: [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasTerminal C] : HasZeroObject C

name: isPullback_of_isPushout

name: hasWeakEqualizer_of_hasWeakKernel
informal: A preadditive category has a weak equalizer for `f` and `g` if it has a weak kernel for `f - g`.
signature: [HasWeakKernel (f - g)] : HasWeakEqualizer f g

name: hasWeakKernel_of_hasWeakEqualizer
informal: A preadditive category has a weak kernel for `f - g` if it has a weak equalizer for `f` and `g`.
signature: [HasWeakEqualizer f g] : HasWeakKernel (f - g)

name: hasWeakEqualizers_of_hasWeakKernels
informal: If a preadditive category has all weak kernels, then it also has all weak equalizers.
signature: [HasWeakKernels C] : HasWeakEqualizers C

name: hasWeakLimit_cospan_of_hasLimit_pair_of_hasWeakLimit_parallelPair
informal: If the product `X ⨯ Y` and the weak equalizer of `π₁ ≫ f` and `π₂ ≫ g` exist, then the weak pullback of `f` and `g` exists: it is given by composing the equalizer with the projections.
signature: [HasLimit (pair X Y)] [HasWeakLimit (parallelPair (prod.fst ≫ f) (prod.snd ≫ g))] : HasWeakLimit (cospan f g)

name: mk'

signature: [Φ.IsLocalizedEquivalence] : Φ.IsRightDerivabilityStructure

name: IsLeftDerivabilityStructure.mk'
informal: If a localizer morphism `Φ` is a localized equivalence, then it is a left derivability structure if the categories of left resolutions are connected and the categories of left resolutions of arrows are nonempty.
