name: isEquivalence_imp
informal: If a localizer morphism induces an equivalence on some choice of localized categories, it will be so for any choice of localized categories.
signature: [G.IsEquivalence] : G'.IsEquivalence

name: IsLocalizedEquivalence.of_isLocalization_of_isLocalization
informal: When `Φ : LocalizerMorphism W₁ W₂`, if the composition `Φ.functor ⋙ L₂` is a localization functor for `W₁`, then `Φ` is a localized equivalence.
signature: [(Φ.functor ⋙ L₂).IsLocalization W₁] : IsLocalizedEquivalence Φ

name: IsLocalizedEquivalence.of_equivalence
informal: When the underlying functor `Φ.functor` of `Φ : LocalizerMorphism W₁ W₂` is an equivalence of categories and that `W₁` and `W₂` essentially correspond to each other via this equivalence, then `Φ` is a localized equivalence.
signature: [Φ.functor.IsEquivalence] (h : W₂ ≤ W₁.map Φ.functor) : IsLocalizedEquivalence Φ

name: map
informal: When `C` has pullbacks, then `F.map f` is representable with respect to `F` for any `f : a ⟶ b` in `C`.
signature: [Full F] [HasPullbacks C] {a b : C} (f : a ⟶ b) [∀ c (g : c ⟶ b), PreservesLimit (cospan f g) F] : F.relativelyRepresentable (F.map f)

name: hasEqualizer_of_hasKernel
informal: A preadditive category has an equalizer for `f` and `g` if it has a kernel for `f - g`.
signature: [HasKernel (f - g)] : HasEqualizer f g

name: hasKernel_of_hasEqualizer
informal: A preadditive category has a kernel for `f - g` if it has an equalizer for `f` and `g`.
signature: [HasEqualizer f g] : HasKernel (f - g)

name: hasCoequalizer_of_hasCokernel
informal: A preadditive category has a coequalizer for `f` and `g` if it has a cokernel for `f - g`.
signature: [HasCokernel (f - g)] : HasCoequalizer f g

name: hasCokernel_of_hasCoequalizer
informal: A preadditive category has a cokernel for `f - g` if it has a coequalizer for `f` and `g`.
signature: [HasCoequalizer f g] : HasCokernel (f - g)

name: hasEqualizers_of_hasKernels
informal: If a preadditive category has all kernels, then it also has all equalizers.
signature: [HasKernels C] : HasEqualizers C

name: hasCoequalizers_of_hasCokernels
informal: If a preadditive category has all cokernels, then it also has all coequalizers.
signature: [HasCokernels C] : HasCoequalizers C

name: HasFiniteBiproducts.of_hasFiniteProducts
informal: A preadditive category with finite products has finite biproducts.
signature: [HasFiniteProducts C] : HasFiniteBiproducts C

name: HasFiniteBiproducts.of_hasFiniteCoproducts
informal: A preadditive category with finite coproducts has finite biproducts.
signature: [HasFiniteCoproducts C] : HasFiniteBiproducts C

name: HasBinaryBiproducts.of_hasBinaryProducts
informal: In a preadditive category, if all binary products exist, then all binary biproducts exist.
signature: [HasBinaryProducts C] : HasBinaryBiproducts C

name: HasBinaryBiproducts.of_hasBinaryCoproducts
informal: In a preadditive category, if all binary coproducts exist, then all binary biproducts exist.
signature: [HasBinaryCoproducts C] : HasBinaryBiproducts C

name: biprod.add_eq_lift_id_desc

signature: [HasBinaryBiproduct X X] : f + g = biprod.lift (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X) ≫ biprod.desc f g

name: biprod.add_eq_lift_desc_id
informal: The existence of binary biproducts implies that there is at most one preadditive structure.
signature: [HasBinaryBiproduct Y Y] : f + g = biprod.lift f g ≫ biprod.desc (𝟙 Y) (𝟙 Y)

name: preservesProductsOfShape_of_preservesBiproductsOfShape

signature: [PreservesBiproductsOfShape J F] : PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F where preservesLimit {_}

name: preservesBiproductsOfShape_of_preservesProductsOfShape
informal: A functor between preadditive categories that preserves (zero morphisms and) finite products preserves finite biproducts.
signature: [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F] : PreservesBiproductsOfShape J F where preserves {_}

name: preservesCoproductsOfShape_of_preservesBiproductsOfShape
informal: A functor between preadditive categories that preserves (zero morphisms and) finite biproducts preserves finite coproducts.
signature: [PreservesBiproductsOfShape J F] : PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F where preservesColimit {_}

name: preservesBiproductsOfShape_of_preservesCoproductsOfShape
informal: A functor between preadditive categories that preserves (zero morphisms and) finite coproducts preserves finite biproducts.
signature: [PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F] : PreservesBiproductsOfShape J F where preserves {_}

name: preservesBinaryProducts_of_preservesBinaryBiproducts
informal: A functor between preadditive categories that preserves (zero morphisms and) binary biproducts preserves binary products.

informal: A functor between preadditive categories that preserves (zero morphisms and) binary products preserves binary biproducts.
signature: [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) F] : PreservesBinaryBiproducts F where preserves {_} {_}

name: preservesBinaryCoproducts_of_preservesBinaryBiproducts
informal: A functor between preadditive categories that preserves (zero morphisms and) binary biproducts preserves binary coproducts.
signature: [PreservesBinaryBiproducts F] : PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) F where preservesColimit {_}

name: preservesBinaryBiproducts_of_preservesBinaryCoproducts
informal: A functor between preadditive categories that preserves (zero morphisms and) binary coproducts preserves binary biproducts.
signature: [PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) F] : PreservesBinaryBiproducts F where preserves {_} {_}

name: isIso_of_hom_simple
informal: The part of **Schur's lemma** that holds in any preadditive category with kernels: that a nonzero morphism between simple objects is an isomorphism.
signature: [HasKernels C] {X Y : C} [Simple X] [Simple Y] {f : X ⟶ Y} (w : f ≠ 0) : IsIso f

name: isIso_iff_nonzero
informal: As a corollary of Schur's lemma for preadditive categories, any morphism between simple objects is (exclusively) either an isomorphism or zero.
signature: [HasKernels C] {X Y : C} [Simple X] [Simple Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) : IsIso f ↔ f ≠ 0

name: finrank_hom_simple_simple_eq_zero_of_not_iso
informal: Part of **Schur's lemma** for `𝕜`-linear categories: the hom space between two non-isomorphic simple objects is 0-dimensional.
signature: [HasKernels C] [Linear 𝕜 C] {X Y : C} [Simple X] [Simple Y] (h : (X ≅ Y) → False) : finrank 𝕜 (X ⟶ Y) = 0

name: epi_of_nonzero_to_simple

name: extensive_regular_generate_coherent

name: isSheaf_yoneda_obj
informal: Every Yoneda-presheaf is a sheaf for the regular topology.
signature: [Preregular C] (W : C) : Presieve.IsSheaf (regularTopology C) (yoneda.obj W)

name: op_comp_isSheaf_of_types
informal: If `F` is continuous, any sheaf (in an arbitrary universe) remains a sheaf when precomposing with `F.op` (SGA 4 III 1.5).
signature: [Functor.IsContinuous F J K] (G : Sheaf K (Type t)) : Presieve.IsSheaf J (F.op ⋙ G.obj)

name: compatiblePreserving
informal: A locally-fully-faithful and cover-dense functor preserves compatible families.
signature: [G.IsLocallyFaithful K] : CompatiblePreserving K G

name: restrictedTopology_eq_inducedTopology

signature: [F.IsContinuous (F.restrictedTopology K) K] : F.restrictedTopology K = F.inducedTopology K

name: coverage_eq_toCoverage_pretopology
informal: If `P` is also multiplicative, the coverage induced by `P` is the pretopology induced by `P`.
signature: [P.IsMultiplicative] : P.coverage = P.pretopology.toCoverage

name: grothendieckTopology_eq_toGrothendieck_pretopology

signature: [P.IsMultiplicative] : P.grothendieckTopology = P.pretopology.toGrothendieck

name: isSheafFor_of_preservesProduct

name: hasSubobjectClassifier_iff_isRepresentable

name: isSubterminal_of_mono_terminal_from

name: isSubterminal_of_isIso_diag

signature: (M N : ℕ) : rothNumberNat (M + N) ≤ rothNumberNat M + rothNumberNat N

name: ZMod.erdos_ginzburg_ziv_multiset
informal: The **Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv theorem** for `ℤ/nℤ` for multiset. Any multiset of at least `2 * n - 1` elements of `ℤ` contains a submultiset of `n` elements whose sum is divisible by `n`.
signature: (s : Multiset (ZMod n)) (hs : 2 * n - 1 ≤ Multiset.card s) : ∃ t ≤ s, Multiset.card t = n ∧ t.sum = 0

name: isAddFreimanIso_Iic

name: isAddFreimanIso_Iio
informal: **No wrap-around principle**. The first `k` elements of `Fin (n + 1)` are `m`-Freiman isomorphic to the first `k` elements of `ℕ` assuming there is no wrap-around.
signature: (hm : m ≠ 0) (hkmn : m * k ≤ n) : IsAddFreimanIso m (Iio (k : Fin (n + 1))) (Iio k) val

name: toColex_le_toColex_of_subset

name: toColex_lt_toColex_of_ssubset
informal: If `s ⊂ t`, then `s < t` in the colex order. Note the converse does not hold, as inclusion does not form a linear order.
signature: (h : s ⊂ t) : toColex s < toColex t

name: forall_le_mono
informal: If `s ≤ t` in colex, and all elements in `t` are small, then all elements in `s` are small.
signature: (hst : toColex s ≤ toColex t) (ht : ∀ b ∈ t, b ≤ a) : ∀ b ∈ s, b ≤ a

name: forall_lt_mono
informal: If `s ≤ t` in colex, and all elements in `t` are small, then all elements in `s` are small.

name: toColex_sdiff_lt_toColex_sdiff
informal: The colexicographic order is insensitive to removing the same elements from both sets.
signature: (hus : u ⊆ s) (hut : u ⊆ t) : toColex (s \ u) < toColex (t \ u) ↔ toColex s < toColex t

name: IsInitSeg.total

name: geomSum_le_geomSum_iff_toColex_le_toColex

name: geomSum_lt_geomSum_iff_toColex_lt_toColex
informal: For finsets of naturals, the colexicographic order is equivalent to the order induced by the `n`-ary expansion.
signature: (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ∑ i ∈ s, n ^ i < ∑ i ∈ t, n ^ i ↔ toColex s < toColex t

name: Nondegenerate.exists_injective_of_card_le

name: HasPoints.card_le

name: sigma_eq_iff_blocks_eq

name: card_nsmul_le_card_nsmul'
informal: **Double counting** argument. Considering `r` as a bipartite graph, the LHS is a lower bound on the number of edges while the RHS is an upper bound.
signature: [∀ a b, Decidable (r a b)] (hn : ∀ b ∈ t, n ≤ #(s.bipartiteBelow r b)) (hm : ∀ a ∈ s, #(t.bipartiteAbove r a) ≤ m) : #t • n ≤ #s • m

name: card_nsmul_lt_card_nsmul_of_lt_of_le
informal: **Double counting** argument. Considering `r` as a bipartite graph, the LHS is a strict lower bound on the number of edges while the RHS is an upper bound.
signature: [∀ a b, Decidable (r a b)] (hs : s.Nonempty) (hm : ∀ a ∈ s, m < #(t.bipartiteAbove r a)) (hn : ∀ b ∈ t, #(s.bipartiteBelow r b) ≤ n) : #s • m < #t • n

name: card_nsmul_lt_card_nsmul_of_le_of_lt
informal: **Double counting** argument. Considering `r` as a bipartite graph, the LHS is a lower bound on the number of edges while the RHS is a strict upper bound.
signature: [∀ a b, Decidable (r a b)] (ht : t.Nonempty) (hm : ∀ a ∈ s, m ≤ #(t.bipartiteAbove r a)) (hn : ∀ b ∈ t, #(s.bipartiteBelow r b) < n) : #s • m < #t • n

name: card_nsmul_lt_card_nsmul_of_lt_of_le'
informal: **Double counting** argument. Considering `r` as a bipartite graph, the LHS is a strict lower bound on the number of edges while the RHS is an upper bound.
signature: [∀ a b, Decidable (r a b)] (ht : t.Nonempty) (hn : ∀ b ∈ t, n < #(s.bipartiteBelow r b)) (hm : ∀ a ∈ s, #(t.bipartiteAbove r a) ≤ m) : #t • n < #s • m

name: card_nsmul_lt_card_nsmul_of_le_of_lt'
informal: **Double counting** argument. Considering `r` as a bipartite graph, the LHS is a lower bound on the number of edges while the RHS is a strict upper bound.
signature: [∀ a b, Decidable (r a b)] (hs : s.Nonempty) (hn : ∀ b ∈ t, n ≤ #(s.bipartiteBelow r b)) (hm : ∀ a ∈ s, #(t.bipartiteAbove r a) < m) : #t • n < #s • m

name: card_mul_le_card_mul
informal: **Double counting** argument. Considering `r` as a bipartite graph, the LHS is a lower bound on the number of edges while the RHS is an upper bound.
signature: [∀ a b, Decidable (r a b)] (hm : ∀ a ∈ s, m ≤ #(t.bipartiteAbove r a)) (hn : ∀ b ∈ t, #(s.bipartiteBelow r b) ≤ n) : #s * m ≤ #t * n

name: sum_card_eq_sum_biUnion_card
informal: Given a finite collection of finite subsets $B_1, \ldots, B_k$ and, for every $x \in \bigcup_i B_i$, let $C_x$ be the set of indices of the $B_i$'s that contain $x$. Then, $\sum_i |B_i| = \sum_x |C_x|$.
signature: [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] (B : α → Finset β) (s : Finset α) : ∑ j ∈ s, #(B j) = ∑ x ∈ s.biUnion B, #{j | j ∈ s ∧ x ∈ B j}

name: ruzsaSzemerediNumberNat_lower_bound
informal: Explicit lower bound on the **Ruzsa-Szemerédi problem**. There exists a graph with `n` vertices and `(n / 3 - 2) * (n - 3) / 6 * exp (-4 * √(log ((n - 3) / 6)))` edges such that each edge belongs to exactly one triangle.
signature: (n : ℕ) : (n / 3 - 2 : ℝ) * ↑((n - 3) / 6) * exp (-4 * √(log ↑((n - 3) / 6))) ≤ ruzsaSzemerediNumberNat n

name: encard_sdiff_eq
informal: For any two sets `B₁`, `B₂` in a family with the exchange property, the differences `B₁ \ B₂` and `B₂ \ B₁` have the same `ℕ∞`-cardinality.
signature: (exch : ExchangeProperty IsBase) (hB₁ : IsBase B₁) (hB₂ : IsBase B₂) : (B₁ \ B₂).encard = (B₂ \ B₁).encard

name: encard_isBase_eq
informal: Any two sets `B₁`, `B₂` in a family with the exchange property have the same `ℕ∞`-cardinality.
signature: (exch : ExchangeProperty IsBase) (hB₁ : IsBase B₁) (hB₂ : IsBase B₂) : B₁.encard = B₂.encard

name: exists_lt_sum_fiber_of_maps_to_of_nsmul_lt_sum
informal: The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by weight, strict inequality version: if the total weight of a finite set of pigeons is greater than `n • b`, and they are sorted into `n` pigeonholes, then for some pigeonhole, the total weight of the pigeons in this pigeonhole is greater than `b`.
signature: (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, f a ∈ t) (hb : #t • b < ∑ x ∈ s, w x) : ∃ y ∈ t, b < ∑ x ∈ s with f x = y, w x

name: exists_sum_fiber_lt_of_maps_to_of_sum_lt_nsmul
informal: The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by weight, strict inequality version: if the total weight of a finite set of pigeons is less than `n • b`, and they are sorted into `n` pigeonholes, then for some pigeonhole, the total weight of the pigeons in this pigeonhole is less than `b`.
signature: (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, f a ∈ t) (hb : ∑ x ∈ s, w x < #t • b) : ∃ y ∈ t, ∑ x ∈ s with f x = y, w x < b

name: exists_lt_sum_fiber_of_sum_fiber_nonpos_of_nsmul_lt_sum
informal: The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by weight, strict inequality version: if the total weight of a finite set of pigeons is greater than `n • b`, they are sorted into some pigeonholes, and for all but `n` pigeonholes the total weight of the pigeons there is nonpositive, then for at least one of these `n` pigeonholes, the total weight of the pigeons in this pigeonhole is greater than `b`.
signature: (ht : ∀ y ∉ t, ∑ x ∈ s with f x = y, w x ≤ 0) (hb : #t • b < ∑ x ∈ s, w x) : ∃ y ∈ t, b < ∑ x ∈ s with f x = y, w x

name: exists_le_sum_fiber_of_maps_to_of_nsmul_le_sum
informal: The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by weight, non-strict inequality version: if the total weight of a finite set of pigeons is greater than or equal to `n • b`, and they are sorted into `n > 0` pigeonholes, then for some pigeonhole, the total weight of the pigeons in this pigeonhole is greater than or equal to `b`.
signature: (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, f a ∈ t) (ht : t.Nonempty) (hb : #t • b ≤ ∑ x ∈ s, w x) : ∃ y ∈ t, b ≤ ∑ x ∈ s with f x = y, w x

name: exists_sum_fiber_le_of_maps_to_of_sum_le_nsmul
informal: The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by weight, non-strict inequality version: if the total weight of a finite set of pigeons is less than or equal to `n • b`, and they are sorted into `n > 0` pigeonholes, then for some pigeonhole, the total weight of the pigeons in this pigeonhole is less than or equal to `b`.
signature: (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, f a ∈ t) (ht : t.Nonempty) (hb : ∑ x ∈ s, w x ≤ #t • b) : ∃ y ∈ t, ∑ x ∈ s with f x = y, w x ≤ b

name: exists_le_sum_fiber_of_sum_fiber_nonpos_of_nsmul_le_sum
informal: The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by weight, non-strict inequality version: if the total weight of a finite set of pigeons is greater than or equal to `n • b`, they are sorted into some pigeonholes, and for all but `n > 0` pigeonholes the total weight of the pigeons there is nonpositive, then for at least one of these `n` pigeonholes, the total weight of the pigeons in this pigeonhole is greater than or equal to `b`.
signature: (hf : ∀ y ∉ t, ∑ x ∈ s with f x = y, w x ≤ 0) (ht : t.Nonempty) (hb : #t • b ≤ ∑ x ∈ s, w x) : ∃ y ∈ t, b ≤ ∑ x ∈ s with f x = y, w x

name: exists_lt_card_fiber_of_nsmul_lt_card_of_maps_to
informal: The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by heads: there is a pigeonhole with at least as many pigeons as the ceiling of the average number of pigeons across all pigeonholes.
signature: (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, f a ∈ t) (ht : #t • b < #s) : ∃ y ∈ t, b < #{x ∈ s | f x = y}

name: exists_card_fiber_lt_of_card_lt_nsmul
informal: The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by heads: there is a pigeonhole with at most as many pigeons as the floor of the average number of pigeons across all pigeonholes.
signature: (ht : #s < #t • b) : ∃ y ∈ t, #{x ∈ s | f x = y} < b

name: exists_le_sum_fiber_of_nsmul_le_sum
informal: The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons of different weights, non-strict inequality version: there is a pigeonhole with the total weight of pigeons in it greater than or equal to `b` provided that the total number of pigeonholes times `b` is less than or equal to the total weight of all pigeons.
signature: [Nonempty β] (hb : card β • b ≤ ∑ x, w x) : ∃ y, b ≤ ∑ x with f x = y, w x

name: exists_sum_fiber_le_of_sum_le_nsmul
informal: The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons of different weights, non-strict inequality version: there is a pigeonhole with the total weight of pigeons in it less than or equal to `b` provided that the total number of pigeonholes times `b` is greater than or equal to the total weight of all pigeons.
signature: [Nonempty β] (hb : ∑ x, w x ≤ card β • b) : ∃ y, ∑ x with f x = y, w x ≤ b

name: exists_lt_modEq_of_infinite
informal: If `s` is an infinite set of natural numbers and `k > 0`, then `s` contains two elements `m < n` that are equal mod `k`.
signature: {s : Set ℕ} (hs : s.Infinite) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) : ∃ m ∈ s, ∃ n ∈ s, m < n ∧ m ≡ n [MOD k]

name: schnirelmannDensity_setOfPred_mod_eq_one
informal: The Schnirelmann density of the set of naturals which are `1 mod m` is `m⁻¹`, for any `m ≠ 1`. Note that if `m = 1`, this set is empty.
signature: {m : ℕ} (hm : m ≠ 1) : schnirelmannDensity {n | n % m = 1} = (m⁻¹ : ℝ)

name: add_eq_univ_of_one_le_schirelmannDensity_add_schnirelmannDensity
informal: If two sets `A` and `B` have Schnirelmann densities with sum at least 1, and both sets contain zero, then every natural number is sum of an element of `A` and an element of `B`. Note that we cannot omit the assumption that both sets contain zero, as shown by the counterexample `A = B = Odd`.
signature: {A B : Set ℕ} [DecidablePred (· ∈ A)] [DecidablePred (· ∈ B)] (hA : 0 ∈ A) (hB : 0 ∈ B) (h : 1 ≤ schnirelmannDensity A + schnirelmannDensity B) : A + B = .univ

name: sup_sdiff_mem_of_mem_compression
informal: If `a` is in the family compression and can be compressed, then its compression is in the original family.
signature: (ha : a ∈ 𝓒 u v s) (hva : v ≤ a) (hua : Disjoint u a) : (a ⊔ u) \ v ∈ s

name: mem_of_mem_compression
informal: If `a` is in the `u, v`-compression but `v ≤ a`, then `a` must have been in the original family.
signature: (ha : a ∈ 𝓒 u v s) (hva : v ≤ a) (hvu : v = ⊥ → u = ⊥) : a ∈ s

name: four_functions_theorem
informal: The **Four Functions Theorem**, aka **Ahlswede-Daykin Inequality**.
signature: [DecidableEq α] (h₁ : 0 ≤ f₁) (h₂ : 0 ≤ f₂) (h₃ : 0 ≤ f₃) (h₄ : 0 ≤ f₄) (h : ∀ a b, f₁ a * f₂ b ≤ f₃ (a ⊓ b) * f₄ (a ⊔ b)) (s t : Finset α) : (∑ a ∈ s, f₁ a) * ∑ a ∈ t, f₂ a ≤ (∑ a ∈ s ⊼ t, f₃ a) * ∑ a ∈ s ⊻ t, f₄ a

name: Finset.le_card_infs_mul_card_sups
informal: An inequality of Daykin. Interestingly, any lattice in which this inequality holds is distributive.
signature: [DecidableEq α] (s t : Finset α) : #s * #t ≤ #(s ⊼ t) * #(s ⊻ t)

name: shadow_initSeg
informal: This is important for iterating Kruskal-Katona: the shadow of an initial segment is also an initial segment.
signature: [Fintype α] (hs : s.Nonempty) : ∂ (initSeg s) = initSeg (erase s <| min' s hs)

name: kruskal_katona
informal: The **Kruskal-Katona theorem**. Given a set family `𝒜` consisting of `r`-sets, and `𝒞` an initial segment of the colex order of the same size, the shadow of `𝒞` is smaller than the shadow of `𝒜`. In particular, this gives that the minimum shadow size is achieved by initial segments of colex.
signature: (h𝒜r : (𝒜 : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Sized r) (h𝒞𝒜 : #𝒞 ≤ #𝒜) (h𝒞 : IsInitSeg 𝒞 r) : #(∂ 𝒞) ≤ #(∂ 𝒜)

name: iterated_kk
informal: An iterated form of the Kruskal-Katona theorem. In particular, the minimum possible iterated shadow size is attained by initial segments.
signature: (h₁ : (𝒜 : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Sized r) (h₂ : #𝒞 ≤ #𝒜) (h₃ : IsInitSeg 𝒞 r) : #(∂^[k] 𝒞) ≤ #(∂^[k] 𝒜)

name: erdos_ko_rado
informal: The **Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem**. The maximum size of an intersecting family in `α` where all sets have size `r` is bounded by `(card α - 1).choose (r - 1)`. This bound is sharp.
signature: {𝒜 : Finset (Finset (Fin n))} {r : ℕ} (h𝒜 : (𝒜 : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Intersecting) (h₂ : (𝒜 : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Sized r) (h₃ : r ≤ n / 2) : #𝒜 ≤ (n - 1).choose (r - 1)

name: le_card_falling_div_choose
informal: A bound on any top part of the sum in LYM in terms of the size of `falling k 𝒜`.
signature: [Fintype α] (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α) (h𝒜 : IsAntichain (· ⊆ ·) (𝒜 : Set (Finset α))) : (∑ r ∈ range (k + 1), (#(𝒜 # (Fintype.card α - r)) : 𝕜) / (Fintype.card α).choose (Fintype.card α - r)) ≤ (falling (Fintype.card α - k) 𝒜).card / (Fintype.card α).choose (Fintype.card α - k)

name: support_top_of_nontrivial
informal: All vertices are in the support of the complete graph if there is more than one vertex.
signature: [Nontrivial V] : (⊤ : SimpleGraph V).support = Set.univ

name: isBipartiteWith_sum_degrees_eq
informal: If `G.IsBipartiteWith s t`, then the sum of the degrees of vertices in `s` is equal to the sum of the degrees of vertices in `t`. See `Finset.sum_card_bipartiteAbove_eq_sum_card_bipartiteBelow`.
signature: [G.LocallyFinite] (h : G.IsBipartiteWith s t) : ∑ v ∈ s, G.degree v = ∑ w ∈ t, G.degree w

name: card_edgeFinset_bipartiteDoubleCover
informal: The bipartite double cover of `G` has twice the number of edges as `G`.
signature: [Fintype V] [DecidableRel G.Adj] : #G.bipartiteDoubleCover.edgeFinset = 2 * #G.edgeFinset

name: nonempty_ends_of_infinite
informal: A locally finite preconnected infinite graph has at least one end.
signature: [LocallyFinite G] [Fact G.Preconnected] [Infinite V] : G.end.Nonempty

name: two_mul_extremalNumber_le_zarankiewicz_symm
informal: The symmetric Zarankiewicz function is at least twice a corresponding extremal number.
signature: [Nonempty α] [Nonempty β] (hs : card α = s) (ht : card β = t) : 2 * extremalNumber n (completeBipartiteGraph α β) ≤ zarankiewicz n n s t

name: exists_minimal_degree_vertex
informal: There exists a vertex of minimal degree. Note the assumption of being nonempty is necessary, as the lemma implies there exists a vertex.
signature: [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] : ∃ v, G.minDegree = G.degree v

name: le_minDegree_of_forall_le_degree
informal: In a nonempty graph, if `k` is at most the degree of every vertex, it is at most the minimum degree. Note the assumption that the graph is nonempty is necessary as long as `G.minDegree` is defined to be a natural.
signature: [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] (k : ℕ) (h : ∀ v, k ≤ G.degree v) : k ≤ G.minDegree

name: minDegree_lt_card
informal: In a nonempty graph, the minimal degree is less than the number of vertices.
signature: [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] : G.minDegree < Fintype.card V

name: exists_maximal_degree_vertex
informal: There exists a vertex of maximal degree. Note the assumption of being nonempty is necessary, as the lemma implies there exists a vertex.
signature: [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] : ∃ v, G.maxDegree = G.degree v

name: maxDegree_le_of_forall_degree_le
informal: In a graph, if `k` is at least the degree of every vertex, then it is at least the maximum degree.
signature: [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) (h : ∀ v, G.degree v ≤ k) : G.maxDegree ≤ k

name: maxDegree_lt_card_verts
informal: The maximum degree of a nonempty graph is less than the number of vertices. Note that the assumption that `V` is nonempty is necessary, as otherwise this would assert the existence of a natural number less than zero.
signature: [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nonempty V] : G.maxDegree < Fintype.card V

name: IsHamiltonian.toFinset_support
informal: The support of a Hamiltonian walk is the entire vertex set.
signature: (hp : p.IsHamiltonian) : p.support.toFinset = Finset.univ

name: incMatrix_apply'
informal: Entries of the incidence matrix can be computed given additional decidable instances.
signature: [Zero R] [One R] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableRel G.Adj] {a : α} {e : Sym2 α} : G.incMatrix R a e = if e ∈ G.incidenceSet a then 1 else 0

name: degree_starGraph_of_ne_center
informal: Every non-center vertex of a starGraph has degree one.
signature: [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] {r v : V} (h : v ≠ r) : (starGraph r).degree v = 1

name: ext_iff_of_exists
informal: An alternative extensionality principle for `PlacedTile` that avoids `HEq`, using existence of a common group element.
signature: {pt₁ pt₂ : PlacedTile ps} : pt₁ = pt₂ ↔ pt₁.index = pt₂.index ∧ ∃ g, ⟦g⟧ = pt₁.groupElts ∧ ⟦g⟧ = pt₂.groupElts

name: ext_iff_of_preimage
informal: An alternative extensionality principle for `PlacedTile` that avoids `HEq`, using equality of quotient preimages.
signature: {pt₁ pt₂ : PlacedTile ps} : pt₁ = pt₂ ↔ pt₁.index = pt₂.index ∧ (Quotient.mk _) ⁻¹' {pt₁.groupElts} = (Quotient.mk _) ⁻¹' {pt₂.groupElts}

name: exists_lt_ack_of_nat_primrec
informal: If `f` is primitive recursive, there exists `m` such that `f n < ack m n` for all `n`.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℕ} (hf : Nat.Primrec f) : ∃ m, ∀ n, f n < ack m n

name: eval_prec_succ
informal: Helper lemma for the evaluation of `prec` in the recursive case.
signature: (cf cg : Code) (a k : ℕ) : eval (prec cf cg) (Nat.pair a (Nat.succ k)) = do {let ih ← eval (prec cf cg) (Nat.pair a k); eval cg (Nat.pair a (Nat.pair k ih))}

name: exists_code
informal: A function is partial recursive if and only if there is a code implementing it. Therefore, `eval` is a **universal partial recursive function**.
signature: {f : ℕ →. ℕ} : Nat.Partrec f ↔ ∃ c : Code, eval c = f

name: fixed_point
informal: **Roger's fixed-point theorem**: any total, computable `f` has a fixed point. That is, under the interpretation given by `Nat.Partrec.Code.eval`, there is a code `c` such that `c` and `f c` have the same evaluation.
signature: {f : Code → Code} (hf : Computable f) : ∃ c : Code, eval (f c) = eval c

name: listFilter_listRange
informal: A helper lemma for proofs about bounded quantifiers on decidable relations.
signature: {R : ℕ → ℕ → Prop} (s : ℕ) [DecidableRel R] (hf : PrimrecRel R) : Primrec fun n ↦ (range s).filter (fun y ↦ R y n)

name: ite
informal: The computable functions are closed under if-then-else definitions with computable predicates.
signature: {f₁ f₂ : ℕ → ℕ} (hf₁ : Computable f₁) (hf₂ : Computable f₂) {c : ℕ → Prop} [DecidablePred c] (hc : ComputablePred c) : Computable fun k ↦ if c k then f₁ k else f₂ k

name: partrec_of_const
informal: If a function is recursive in a constant partial function, then it is partial recursive.
signature: {s} (hf : RecursiveIn {fun _ => s} f) : Partrec f

name: Partrec.turingReducible
informal: If a function is partial recursive, then it is recursive in every partial function.
signature: (pF : Partrec f) : f ≤ᵀ g

name: TuringReducible.partrec_of_const
informal: If a function is recursive in a constant partial function, then it is partial recursive.
signature: {s} (hf : f ≤ᵀ fun _ => s) : Partrec f

name: stepNormal_then
informal: The `stepNormal` function respects the `then k'` homomorphism. Note that this is an exact equality, not a simulation; the original and embedded machines move in lock-step until the embedded machine reaches the halt state.
signature: (c) (k k' : Cont) (v) : stepNormal c (k.then k') v = (stepNormal c k v).then k'

name: stepRet_then
informal: The `stepRet` function respects the `then k'` homomorphism. Note that this is an exact equality, not a simulation; the original and embedded machines move in lock-step until the embedded machine reaches the halt state.
signature: {k k' : Cont} {v} : stepRet (k.then k') v = (stepRet k v).then k'

name: ListBlank.exists_cons
informal: The `cons` and `head`/`tail` functions are mutually inverse, unlike in the case of `List` where this only holds for nonempty lists.
signature: {Γ} [Inhabited Γ] (l : ListBlank Γ) : ∃ a l', l = ListBlank.cons a l'

name: re_eq_add_conj
informal: A complex number `z` plus its conjugate `conj z` is `2` times its real part.
signature: (z : ℂ) : (z.re : ℂ) = (z + conj z) / 2

name: of
informal: This is not marked as an instance so that Lean doesn't always find this one and a more canonical value of `r` can be used.
signature: (p q : ℝ≥0∞) : HolderTriple p q (p⁻¹ + q⁻¹)⁻¹ where inv_add_inv_eq_inv

name: cancel_of_ne
informal: This lemma has an abbreviated name because it is used frequently.
signature: {a : ℝ≥0∞} (h : a ≠ ∞) : AddLECancellable a

name: cancel_of_lt
informal: This lemma has an abbreviated name because it is used frequently.
signature: {a : ℝ≥0∞} (h : a < ∞) : AddLECancellable a

name: cancel_of_lt'
informal: This lemma has an abbreviated name because it is used frequently.
signature: {a b : ℝ≥0∞} (h : a < b) : AddLECancellable a

name: cancel_coe
informal: This lemma has an abbreviated name because it is used frequently.
signature: {a : ℝ≥0} : AddLECancellable (a : ℝ≥0∞)

name: mul_iInf_of_ne
informal: If `a ≠ 0`, then right multiplication by `a` maps infimum to infimum. See also `ENat.iInf_mul` that assumes `[Nonempty ι]` but does not require `a ≠ 0`.
signature: (ha₀ : a ≠ 0) : a * ⨅ i, f i = ⨅ i, a * f i

name: iInf_mul_of_ne
informal: If `a ≠ 0`, then right multiplication by `a` maps infimum to infimum. See also `ENat.iInf_mul` that assumes `[Nonempty ι]` but does not require `a ≠ 0`.
signature: (ha₀ : a ≠ 0) : (⨅ i, f i) * a = ⨅ i, f i * a

name: pos_iff_ne_zero'
informal: The `Fin.pos_iff_ne_zero` in `Lean` only applies in `Fin (n+1)`. This one instead uses a `NeZero n` typeclass hypothesis.
signature: [NeZero n] (a : Fin n) : 0 < a ↔ a ≠ 0

name: exists_ne_and_ne_of_two_lt
informal: If working with more than two elements, we can always pick a third distinct from two existing elements.
signature: (i j : Fin n) (h : 2 < n) : ∃ k, k ≠ i ∧ k ≠ j

name: val_cast_of_lt
informal: Converting an in-range number to `Fin (n + 1)` produces a result whose value is the original number.
signature: {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {a : ℕ} (h : a < n) : (a : Fin n).val = a

name: odd_iff
informal: In `Fin n`, all elements are odd for odd `n`, otherwise an element is odd iff its `Fin.val` value is odd.
signature: [NeZero n] : Odd k ↔ Odd n ∨ Odd k.val

name: le_of_injective
informal: If we have an injective map from `Fin m` to `Fin n`, then `m ≤ n`. See also `Fintype.card_le_of_injective` for the generalisation to arbitrary finite types.
signature: (f : Fin m → Fin n) (hf : f.Injective) : m ≤ n

name: le_of_embedding
informal: If we have an embedding from `Fin m` to `Fin n`, then `m ≤ n`. See also `Fintype.card_le_of_embedding` for the generalisation to arbitrary finite types.
signature: (f : Fin m ↪ Fin n) : m ≤ n

name: lt_of_injective_of_notMem
informal: If we have an injective map from `Fin m` to `Fin n` whose image does not contain everything, then `m < n`. See also `Fintype.card_lt_of_injective_of_notMem` for the generalisation to arbitrary finite types.
signature: (f : Fin m → Fin n) (hf : f.Injective) {b : Fin n} (hb : b ∉ Set.range f) : m < n

name: le_of_surjective
informal: If we have a surjective map from `Fin m` to `Fin n`, then `m ≥ n`. See also `Fintype.card_le_of_surjective` for the generalisation to arbitrary finite types.
signature: (f : Fin m → Fin n) (hf : Function.Surjective f) : n ≤ m

name: card_range_le
informal: Any map from `Fin m` reaches at most `m` different values. See also `Fintype.card_range_le` for the generalisation to an arbitrary finite type.
signature: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (f : Fin m → α) : Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ m

name: _root_.finCongr_eq_equivCast
informal: While in many cases `finCongr` is better than `Equiv.cast`/`cast`, sometimes we want to apply a generic theorem about `cast`.
signature: (h : n = m) : finCongr h = .cast (h ▸ rfl)

name: cast_eq_cast
informal: While in many cases `Fin.cast` is better than `Equiv.cast`/`cast`, sometimes we want to apply a generic theorem about `cast`.
signature: (h : n = m) : (Fin.cast h : Fin n → Fin m) = _root_.cast (h ▸ rfl)

name: succAbove_lt_iff_castSucc_lt
informal: Embedding `i : Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` using a pivot `p` that is greater results in a value that is less than `p`.
signature: (p : Fin (n + 1)) (i : Fin n) : p.succAbove i < p ↔ castSucc i < p

name: lt_succAbove_iff_le_castSucc
informal: Embedding `i : Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` using a pivot `p` that is lesser results in a value that is greater than `p`.
signature: (p : Fin (n + 1)) (i : Fin n) : p < p.succAbove i ↔ p ≤ castSucc i

name: addCases_castAdd_natAdd
informal: Splitting a dependent finite sequence v into an initial part and a final part, and then concatenating these components, produces an identical sequence.
signature: {γ : Fin (m + n) → Sort*} (v : ∀ i, γ i) (i : Fin (m + n)) : addCases (fun i ↦ v (castAdd n i)) (fun j ↦ v (natAdd m j)) i = v i

name: forall_fin_add
informal: A finite sequence of properties `P` holds for `{0, ..., m + n - 1}` iff it holds separately for both `{0, ..., m - 1}` and `{m, ..., m + n - 1}`.
signature: {m n} (P : Fin (m + n) → Prop) : (∀ i, P i) ↔ (∀ i, P (castAdd _ i)) ∧ (∀ j, P (natAdd _ j))

name: antitone_pair_of_not_sorted
informal: If the tuple `f` is not the same as `f ∘ sort f`, then `f` has a pair of strictly decreasing entries.
signature: (h : f ≠ f ∘ sort f) : ∃ i j, i < j ∧ f j < f i

name: card_eq_fintypeCard
informal: The enumeration merely adds an ordering, leaving the cardinality as is.
signature: {α : Type u} [FinEnum α] [Fintype α] : card α = Fintype.card α

name: card_unique
informal: Any two enumerations of the same type have the same length.
signature: {α : Type u} (e₁ e₂ : FinEnum α) : e₁.card = e₂.card

name: card_pos_iff
informal: A type indexable by `Fin n` with positive `n` is inhabited and vice versa.
signature: {α : Type u} [FinEnum α] : 0 < card α ↔ Nonempty α

name: card_pos
informal: Any non-empty enumeration has more than one element.
signature: {α : Type*} [FinEnum α] [Nonempty α] : 0 < card α

name: card_eq_one
informal: Any enumeration of a type with unique inhabitant has length 1.
signature: (α : Type u) [FinEnum α] [Unique α] : card α = 1

name: filter_eq
informal: After filtering out everything that does not equal a given value, at most that value remains. This is equivalent to `filter_eq'` with the equality the other way.
signature: [DecidableEq β] (s : Finset β) (b : β) : s.filter (Eq b) = ite (b ∈ s) {b} ∅

name: filter_eq'
informal: After filtering out everything that does not equal a given value, at most that value remains. This is equivalent to `filter_eq` with the equality the other way.
signature: [DecidableEq β] (s : Finset β) (b : β) : (s.filter fun a => a = b) = ite (b ∈ s) {b} ∅

name: inter_nonempty_of_card_lt_card_add_card
informal: **Pigeonhole principle** for two finsets inside an ambient finset.
signature: (hts : t ⊆ s) (hus : u ⊆ s) (hstu : #s < #t + #u) : (t ∩ u).Nonempty

name: image_iterate_stabilises_lt_card
informal: Given a function `f` which sends the finite set `s` to itself, the sequence of images of `s` under iterates of `f` is eventually constant. Furthermore, the sequence of images stabilises in fewer than `#s` steps.
signature: [DecidableEq α] {f : α → α} {s : Finset α} (hs : Set.MapsTo f s s) (hs₀ : s.Nonempty) : ∃ n < #s, ∀ m, n ≤ m → s.image f^[m] = s.image f^[n]

name: image_iterate_stabilises_le_card
informal: Given a function `f` which sends the finite set `s` to itself, the sequence of images of `s` under iterates of `f` is eventually constant. Furthermore, the sequence of images stabilises in at most `#s` steps.
signature: [DecidableEq α] {f : α → α} {s : Finset α} (hs : Set.MapsTo f s s) : ∃ n ≤ #s, ∀ m, n ≤ m → s.image f^[m] = s.image f^[n]

name: nontrivial_of_image
informal: If the image of a finset is nontrivial, the finset is nontrivial. For the converse direction under an injectivity hypothesis see `Finset.Nontrivial.image_of_injOn`, and for the combined iff see `Finset.image_nontrivial_iff_of_injOn`.
signature: (h : (s.image f).Nontrivial) : s.Nontrivial

name: image_nontrivial_iff_of_injOn
informal: A finset is nontrivial iff its image under a function injective on the finset is.
signature: (hf : Set.InjOn f s) : (s.image f).Nontrivial ↔ s.Nontrivial

name: card_dvd_card_image₂_right
informal: If each partial application of `f` is injective, and images of `s` under those partial applications are disjoint (but not necessarily distinct!), then the size of `t` divides the size of `Finset.image₂ f s t`.
signature: (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, Injective (f a)) (hs : ((fun a => t.image <| f a) '' s).PairwiseDisjoint id) : #t ∣ #(image₂ f s t)

name: card_dvd_card_image₂_left
informal: If each partial application of `f` is injective, and images of `t` under those partial applications are disjoint (but not necessarily distinct!), then the size of `s` divides the size of `Finset.image₂ f s t`.
signature: (hf : ∀ b ∈ t, Injective fun a => f a b) (ht : ((fun b => s.image fun a => f a b) '' t).PairwiseDisjoint id) : #s ∣ #(image₂ f s t)

name: Nat.divisors_mul
informal: The divisors of a product of natural numbers are the pointwise product of the divisors of the factors.
signature: (m n : ℕ) : divisors (m * n) = divisors m * divisors n

name: Nat.Coprime.mul_injOn_divisors
informal: Products of divisors taken from coprime naturals are unique.
signature: {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m.Coprime n) : Set.InjOn (fun p : ℕ × ℕ ↦ p.1 * p.2) ↑(divisors m ×ˢ divisors n)

name: Fin.univ_succAbove
informal: Embed `Fin n` into `Fin (n + 1)` by inserting around a specified pivot `p : Fin (n + 1)` into the `univ`
signature: (n : ℕ) (p : Fin (n + 1)) : (univ : Finset (Fin (n + 1))) = Finset.cons p (univ.map <| Fin.succAboveEmb p) (by simp)

name: card_piFinset_const
informal: This lemma is specifically designed to be used backwards, whence the specialisation to `Fin n` as the indexing type doesn't matter in practice. The more general forward direction lemma here is `Fintype.card_piFinset`.
signature: {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (n : ℕ) : #(piFinset fun _ : Fin n ↦ s) = #s ^ n

name: card_pi_const
informal: This lemma is specifically designed to be used backwards, whence the specialisation to `Fin n` as the indexing type doesn't matter in practice. The more general forward direction lemma here is `Fintype.card_pi`.
signature: (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (n : ℕ) : card (Fin n → α) = card α ^ n

name: Finset.card_filter_length_eq_le
informal: The number of strings of length `s` in any finite set is at most `D^s`.
signature: [Fintype α] {T : Finset (List α)} {s : ℕ} : (T.filter (fun x => x.length = s)).card ≤ (Fintype.card α) ^ s

name: card_ofIsEmpty
informal: Note: this lemma is specifically about `Fintype.ofIsEmpty`. For a statement about arbitrary `Fintype` instances, use `Fintype.card_eq_zero`.
signature: [IsEmpty α] : @Fintype.card α Fintype.ofIsEmpty = 0

name: Fintype.card_compl_eq_card_compl
informal: If two subtypes of a fintype have equal cardinality, so do their complements.
signature: [Finite α] (p q : α → Prop) [Fintype { x // p x }] [Fintype { x // ¬p x }] [Fintype { x // q x }] [Fintype { x // ¬q x }] (h : Fintype.card { x // p x } = Fintype.card { x // q x }) : Fintype.card { x // ¬p x } = Fintype.card { x // ¬q x }

name: card_embedding_eq_of_infinite
informal: The cardinality of embeddings from an infinite type to a finite type is zero. This is a re-statement of the pigeonhole principle.
signature: {α β : Type*} [Infinite α] [Finite β] [Fintype (α ↪ β)] : ‖α ↪ β‖ = 0

name: univ_ofIsEmpty
informal: Note: this lemma is specifically about `Fintype.ofIsEmpty`. For a statement about arbitrary `Fintype` instances, use `Finset.univ_eq_empty`.
signature: [IsEmpty α] : @univ α Fintype.ofIsEmpty = ∅

name: Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite
informal: The pigeonhole principle for infinitely many pigeons in finitely many pigeonholes. If there are infinitely many pigeons in finitely many pigeonholes, then there are at least two pigeons in the same pigeonhole. See also: `Fintype.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt`, `Finite.exists_infinite_fiber`.
signature: {α β} [Infinite α] [Finite β] (f : α → β) : ∃ x y : α, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y

name: Finite.exists_infinite_fiber
informal: The strong pigeonhole principle for infinitely many pigeons in finitely many pigeonholes. If there are infinitely many pigeons in finitely many pigeonholes, then there is a pigeonhole with infinitely many pigeons. See also: `Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite`
signature: [Infinite α] [Finite β] (f : α → β) : ∃ y : β, Infinite (f ⁻¹' {y})

name: eq_of_mod_eq_of_natAbs_sub_lt_natAbs
informal: If two integers are congruent to a sufficiently large modulus, they are equal.
signature: {a b c : ℤ} (h1 : a % b = c) (h2 : natAbs (a - c) < natAbs b) : a = c

name: count_modEq_card
informal: There are `b / r + [v % r < b % r]` numbers in `[0, b)` congruent to `v` mod `r`, where `[·]` is the Iverson bracket.
signature: (v : ℕ) : b.count (· ≡ v [MOD r]) = b / r + if v % r < b % r then 1 else 0

name: ext_int'
informal: If two `MonoidWithZeroHom`s agree on `-1` and the _positive_ naturals then they are equal.
signature: [MonoidWithZero α] [FunLike F ℤ α] [MonoidWithZeroHomClass F ℤ α] {f g : F} (h_neg_one : f (-1) = g (-1)) (h_pos : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → f n = g n) : f = g

name: exists_least_of_bdd
informal: If `P : ℤ → Prop` is a predicate such that the set `{m : P m}` is bounded below and nonempty, then this set has the least element. This lemma uses classical logic to avoid assumption `[DecidablePred P]`. See `Int.leastOfBdd` for a constructive counterpart.
signature: {P : ℤ → Prop} (Hbdd : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ z : ℤ, P z → b ≤ z) (Hinh : ∃ z : ℤ, P z) : ∃ lb : ℤ, P lb ∧ ∀ z : ℤ, P z → lb ≤ z

name: exists_greatest_of_bdd
informal: If `P : ℤ → Prop` is a predicate such that the set `{m : P m}` is bounded above and nonempty, then this set has the greatest element. This lemma uses classical logic to avoid assumption `[DecidablePred P]`. See `Int.greatestOfBdd` for a constructive counterpart.
signature: {P : ℤ → Prop} (Hbdd : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ z : ℤ, P z → z ≤ b) (Hinh : ∃ z : ℤ, P z) : ∃ ub : ℤ, P ub ∧ ∀ z : ℤ, P z → z ≤ ub

name: natAbs_coe_sub_coe_le_of_le
informal: A specialization of `abs_sub_le_of_nonneg_of_le` for working with the signed subtraction of natural numbers.
signature: {a b n : ℕ} (a_le_n : a ≤ n) (b_le_n : b ≤ n) : natAbs (a - b : ℤ) ≤ n

name: natAbs_coe_sub_coe_lt_of_lt
informal: A specialization of `abs_sub_lt_of_nonneg_of_lt` for working with the signed subtraction of natural numbers.
signature: {a b n : ℕ} (a_lt_n : a < n) (b_lt_n : b < n) : natAbs (a - b : ℤ) < n

name: cancel_right_div_gcd
informal: To cancel a common factor `c` from a `ModEq` we must divide the modulus `m` by `gcd m c`.
signature: (hm : 0 < m) (h : a * c ≡ b * c [ZMOD m]) : a ≡ b [ZMOD m / gcd m c]

name: cancel_left_div_gcd
informal: To cancel a common factor `c` from a `ModEq` we must divide the modulus `m` by `gcd m c`.
signature: (hm : 0 < m) (h : c * a ≡ c * b [ZMOD m]) : a ≡ b [ZMOD m / gcd m c]

name: Sublist.of_cons_of_ne
informal: If the first element of two lists are different, then a sublist relation can be reduced.
signature: {a b} (h₁ : a ≠ b) (h₂ : a :: l₁ <+ b :: l₂) : a :: l₁ <+ l₂

name: ext_getElem
informal: If two lists `l₁` and `l₂` are the same length and `l₁[n]! = l₂[n]!` for all `n`, then the lists are equal.
signature: ! [Inhabited α] (hl : length l₁ = length l₂) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, l₁[n]! = l₂[n]!) : l₁ = l₂

name: Acc.list_chain'
informal: If an `r`-decreasing chain `l` is empty or its head is accessible by `r`, then `l` is accessible by the lexicographic order `List.Lex r`.
signature: {l : List.chains r} (acc : ∀ a ∈ l.val.head?, Acc r a) : Acc (List.lex_chains r) l

name: WellFounded.list_chain'
informal: If `r` is well-founded, the lexicographic order on `r`-decreasing chains is also.
signature: (hwf : WellFounded r) : WellFounded (List.lex_chains r)

name: Pairwise.destutter_eq_dedup
informal: If the elements of a list `l` are related pairwise by an antisymmetric relation `r`, then destuttering `l` by disequality produces the same result as deduplicating `l`. This is most useful when `r` is a strict or weak ordering.
signature: [DecidableEq α] {r : α → α → Prop} [Std.Antisymm r] : ∀ {l : List α}, l.Pairwise r → l.destutter (· ≠ ·) = l.dedup | [], h => by simp | [x], h => by simp | x :: y :: xs, h => by rw [pairwise_cons] at h rw [destutter_cons_cons, ← destutter_cons', ← destutter_cons', h.2.destutter_eq_dedup] obtain rfl | hxy

name: trichotomy
informal: For any natural numbers n, a, and b, one of the following holds: 1. n < a 2. n ≥ b 3. n ∈ Ico a b
signature: (n a b : ℕ) : n < a ∨ b ≤ n ∨ n ∈ Ico a b

name: erase_orderedInsert
informal: For a reflexive relation, insert then erasing is the identity.
signature: [DecidableEq α] [Std.Refl r] (x : α) (xs : List α) : (xs.orderedInsert r x).erase x = xs

name: erase_orderedInsert_of_notMem
informal: Inserting then erasing an element that is absent is the identity.
signature: [DecidableEq α] {x : α} {xs : List α} (hx : x ∉ xs) : (xs.orderedInsert r x).erase x = xs

name: orderedInsert_erase
informal: For an antisymmetric relation, erasing then inserting is the identity.
signature: [DecidableEq α] [Std.Antisymm r] (x : α) (xs : List α) (hx : x ∈ xs) (hxs : Pairwise r xs) : (xs.erase x).orderedInsert r x = xs

name: submatrix_diagonal
informal: Given a `(m × m)` diagonal matrix defined by a map `d : m → α`, if the reindexing map `e` is injective, then the resulting matrix is again diagonal.
signature: [Zero α] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq l] (d : m → α) (e : l → m) (he : Function.Injective e) : (diagonal d).submatrix e e = diagonal (d ∘ e)

name: toMatrix_toPEquiv_eq
informal: We can also define permutation matrices by permuting the rows of the identity matrix.
signature: [DecidableEq n] [Zero α] [One α] (σ : Equiv.Perm n) : σ.toPEquiv.toMatrix = (1 : Matrix n n α).submatrix σ id

name: wellFounded_isDershowitzMannaLT
informal: Over a well-founded order, the Dershowitz-Manna order on multisets is well-founded.
signature: [WellFoundedLT α] : WellFounded (IsDershowitzMannaLT : Multiset α → Multiset α → Prop)

name: nnreal_trichotomy
informal: Every real number is either zero, positive or negative, phrased using `ℝ≥0`.

name: NNReal.exists_lt_of_strictMono
informal: If `Γ₀ˣ` is nontrivial and `f : Γ₀ →*₀ ℝ≥0` is strictly monotone, then for any positive `r : ℝ≥0`, there exists `d : Γ₀ˣ` with `f d < r`.
signature: [h : Nontrivial Γ₀ˣ] {f : Γ₀ →*₀ ℝ≥0} (hf : StrictMono f) {r : ℝ≥0} (hr : 0 < r) : ∃ d : Γ₀ˣ, f d < r

name: Real.exists_lt_of_strictMono
informal: If `Γ₀ˣ` is nontrivial and `f : Γ₀ →*₀ ℝ≥0` is strictly monotone, then for any positive real `r`, there exists `d : Γ₀ˣ` with `f d < r`.
signature: [h : Nontrivial Γ₀ˣ] {f : Γ₀ →*₀ ℝ≥0} (hf : StrictMono f) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) : ∃ d : Γ₀ˣ, (f d : ℝ) < r

name: set_induction
informal: A subset of `ℕ` containing zero and closed under `Nat.succ` contains all of `ℕ`.
signature: {S : Set ℕ} (hb : 0 ∈ S) (h_ind : ∀ k : ℕ, k ∈ S → k + 1 ∈ S) (n : ℕ) : n ∈ S

name: bitIndices_sum_map_two_pow
informal: Together with `Nat.sum_map_bitIndices_two_pow`, this implies a bijection between `ℕ` and `Finset ℕ`. See `Finset.equivBitIndices` for this bijection.
signature: {L : List ℕ} (hL : List.SortedLT L) : (L.map (fun i ↦ 2 ^ i)).sum.bitIndices = L

name: bitwise_comm
informal: If `f` is a commutative operation on bools such that `f false false = false`, then `bitwise f` is also commutative.
signature: {f : Bool → Bool → Bool} (hf : ∀ b b', f b b' = f b' b) (n m : ℕ) : bitwise f n m = bitwise f m n

name: xor_range
informal: The xor of the numbers from 0 to n can be easily calculated using `n mod 4`.
signature: (n : ℕ) : (List.range (n + 1)).foldl (· ^^^ ·) 0 = match Fin.ofNat 4 n with | 0 => n | 1 => 1 | 2 => n + 1 | 3 => 0

name: append_lt
informal: Note that the LHS is the expression used within `Std.BitVec.append`, hence the name.

name: ext_nat''
informal: If two `MonoidWithZeroHom`s agree on the positive naturals they are equal.
signature: [ZeroHomClass F ℕ A] (f g : F) (h_pos : ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → f n = g n) : f = g

name: map_ofNat
informal: This lemma is not marked `@[simp]` lemma because its `#discr_tree_key` (for the LHS) would just be `DFunLike.coe _ _`, due to the `ofNat` that https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues/2867 forces us to include, and therefore it would negatively impact performance. If that issue is resolved, this can be marked `@[simp]`.
signature: [FunLike F R S] [RingHomClass F R S] (f : F) (n : ℕ) [Nat.AtLeastTwo n] : (f ofNat(n) : S) = OfNat.ofNat n

name: choose_le_succ_of_lt_half_left
informal: Show that `Nat.choose` is increasing for small values of the right argument.
signature: {r n : ℕ} (h : r < n / 2) : choose n r ≤ choose n (r + 1)

name: choose_le_centralBinom
informal: The central binomial coefficient is the largest binomial coefficient.
signature: (r n : ℕ) : choose (2 * n) r ≤ centralBinom n

name: four_pow_lt_mul_centralBinom
informal: An exponential lower bound on the central binomial coefficient. This bound is of interest because it appears in [Tochiori's refinement of Erdős's proof of Bertrand's postulate](tochiori_bertrand).
signature: (n : ℕ) (n_big : 4 ≤ n) : 4 ^ n < n * centralBinom n

name: succ_dvd_centralBinom
informal: A crucial lemma to ensure that Catalan numbers can be defined via their explicit formula `catalan n = n.centralBinom / (n + 1)`.
signature: (n : ℕ) : n + 1 ∣ n.centralBinom

name: factorization_factorial
informal: **Legendre's Theorem** The multiplicity of a prime in `n!` is the sum of the quotients `n / p ^ i`. This sum is expressed over the finset `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound greater than `log p n`.
signature: {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : ∀ {n b : ℕ}, log p n < b → (n)!.factorization p = ∑ i ∈ Ico 1 b, n / p ^ i | 0, b, _ => by simp | n + 1, b, hb => calc (n + 1)!.factorization p = (n + 1).factorization p + (n)!.factorization p

name: factorization_factorial_mul_succ
informal: The factorization of `p` in `(p * (n + 1))!` is one more than the sum of the factorizations of `p` in `(p * n)!` and `n + 1`.
signature: {n p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : (p * (n + 1))!.factorization p = (p * n)!.factorization p + (n + 1).factorization p + 1

name: factorization_choose_le_one
informal: Primes greater than about `sqrt n` appear only to multiplicity 0 or 1 in the binomial coefficient.
signature: (p_large : n < p ^ 2) : (choose n k).factorization p ≤ 1

name: factorization_centralBinom_of_two_mul_self_lt_three_mul
informal: Primes greater than about `2 * n / 3` and less than `n` do not appear in the factorization of `centralBinom n`.
signature: (n_big : 2 < n) (p_le_n : p ≤ n) (big : 2 * n < 3 * p) : (centralBinom n).factorization p = 0

name: factorization_centralBinom_eq_zero_of_two_mul_lt
informal: If a prime `p` has positive multiplicity in the `n`th central binomial coefficient, `p` is no more than `2 * n`
signature: (h : 2 * n < p) : (centralBinom n).factorization p = 0

name: prod_pow_factorization_choose
informal: A binomial coefficient is the product of its prime factors, which are at most `n`.
signature: (n k : ℕ) (hkn : k ≤ n) : (∏ p ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), p ^ (Nat.choose n k).factorization p) = choose n k

name: prod_pow_factorization_centralBinom
informal: The `n`th central binomial coefficient is the product of its prime factors, which are at most `2n`.
signature: (n : ℕ) : (∏ p ∈ Finset.range (2 * n + 1), p ^ (centralBinom n).factorization p) = centralBinom n

name: choose_modEq_choose_mul_prod_range_choose
informal: For primes `p`, `choose n k` is congruent to the product of `choose (⌊n / p ^ i⌋ % p) (⌊k / p ^ i⌋ % p)` over i < a, multiplied by `choose (⌊n / p ^ a⌋) (⌊k / p ^ a⌋)`, modulo `p`.
signature: (a : ℕ) : choose n k ≡ choose (n / p ^ a) (k / p ^ a) * ∏ i ∈ range a, choose (n / p ^ i % p) (k / p ^ i % p) [ZMOD p]

name: choose_modEq_prod_range_choose
informal: **Lucas's Theorem**: For primes `p`, `choose n k` is congruent to the product of `choose (⌊n / p ^ i⌋ % p) (⌊k / p ^ i⌋ % p)` over `i` modulo `p`.
signature: {a : ℕ} (ha₁ : n < p ^ a) (ha₂ : k < p ^ a) : choose n k ≡ ∏ i ∈ range a, choose (n / p ^ i % p) (k / p ^ i % p) [ZMOD p]

name: choose_modEq_prod_range_choose_nat
informal: **Lucas's Theorem**: For primes `p`, `choose n k` is congruent to the product of `choose (⌊n / p ^ i⌋ % p) (⌊k / p ^ i⌋ % p)` over `i` modulo `p`.
signature: {a : ℕ} (ha₁ : n < p ^ a) (ha₂ : k < p ^ a) : choose n k ≡ ∏ i ∈ range a, choose (n / p ^ i % p) (k / p ^ i % p) [MOD p]

name: minFac_dvd_gcd_choose_of_isPrimePow
informal: For a prime power `n`, the minimal prime factor divides the greatest common divisor of `choose n 1, ⋯, choose n (n - 1)`.
signature: (h : IsPrimePow n) : n.minFac ∣ (Icc 1 (n - 1)).gcd n.choose

name: gcd_choose_eq_minFac_of_isPrimePow
informal: For a prime power `n`, the greatest common divisor of `choose n 1, ⋯, choose n (n - 1)` is actually the minimal prime factor of `n`.
signature: (h : IsPrimePow n) : (Icc 1 (n - 1)).gcd n.choose = n.minFac

name: gcd_choose_eq_one_of_not_isPrimePow
informal: For a natural number `n` greater than `1`, assume that `n` is not a prime power, then the greatest common divisor of `choose n 1, ⋯, choose n (n - 1)` is `1`.
signature: (hn : 1 < n) (hpn : ¬ IsPrimePow n) : (Icc 1 (n - 1)).gcd n.choose = 1

name: sum_Icc_choose
informal: **Zhu Shijie's identity** aka hockey-stick identity, version with `Icc`.
signature: (n k : ℕ) : ∑ m ∈ Icc k n, m.choose k = (n + 1).choose (k + 1)

name: ofDigits_add_ofDigits_eq_ofDigits_zipWith_of_length_eq
informal: The addition of ofDigits of two lists is equal to ofDigits of digit-wise addition of them
signature: {b : ℕ} {l1 l2 : List ℕ} (h : l1.length = l2.length) : ofDigits b l1 + ofDigits b l2 = ofDigits b (l1.zipWith (· + ·) l2)

name: digits_lt_base'
informal: The digits in the base b+2 expansion of n are all less than b+2
signature: {b m : ℕ} : ∀ {d}, d ∈ digits (b + 2) m → d < b + 2

name: digits_lt_base
informal: The digits in the base b expansion of n are all less than b, if b ≥ 2
signature: {b m d : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) (hd : d ∈ digits b m) : d < b

name: lt_base_pow_length_digits'
informal: Any number m is less than (b+2)^(number of digits in the base b + 2 representation of m)
signature: {b m : ℕ} : m < (b + 2) ^ (digits (b + 2) m).length

name: lt_base_pow_length_digits
informal: Any number m is less than b^(number of digits in the base b representation of m)
signature: {b m : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) : m < b ^ (digits b m).length

name: ofDigits_div_eq_ofDigits_tail
informal: Interpreting as a base `p` number and dividing by `p` is the same as interpreting the tail.
signature: {p : ℕ} (hpos : 0 < p) (digits : List ℕ) (w₁ : ∀ l ∈ digits, l < p) : ofDigits p digits / p = ofDigits p digits.tail

name: ofDigits_div_pow_eq_ofDigits_drop
informal: Interpreting as a base `p` number and dividing by `p^i` is the same as dropping `i`.
signature: {p : ℕ} (i : ℕ) (hpos : 0 < p) (digits : List ℕ) (w₁ : ∀ l ∈ digits, l < p) : ofDigits p digits / p ^ i = ofDigits p (digits.drop i)

name: ofDigits_mod_pow_eq_ofDigits_take
informal: Interpreting as a base `p` number and modulo `p^i` is the same as taking the first `i` digits.
signature: {p : ℕ} (i : ℕ) (hpos : 0 < p) (digits : List ℕ) (w₁ : ∀ l ∈ digits, l < p) : ofDigits p digits % p ^ i = ofDigits p (digits.take i)

name: toDigitsCore_length
informal: The String representation produced by toDigitsCore has the proper length relative to the number of digits in `n < e` for some base `b`. Since this works with any base, it can be used for binary, decimal, and hex.
signature: (b f n e : Nat) (h_e_pos : 0 < e) (hlt : n < b ^ e) : (Nat.toDigitsCore b f n []).length ≤ e

name: toDigits_length
informal: The core implementation of `Nat.toDigits` returns a String with length less than or equal to the number of digits in the base-`b` number (represented by `e`). For example, the string representation of any number less than `b ^ 3` has a length less than or equal to 3.
signature: (b n e : Nat) : 0 < e → n < b ^ e → (Nat.toDigits b n).length ≤ e

name: repr_length
informal: The core implementation of `Nat.repr` returns a String with length less than or equal to the number of digits in the decimal number (represented by `e`). For example, the decimal string representation of any number less than 1000 (10 ^ 3) has a length less than or equal to 3.
signature: (n e : Nat) : 0 < e → n < 10 ^ e → (Nat.repr n).length ≤ e

name: base_pow_length_digits_le'
informal: Any non-zero natural number `m` is greater than (b+2)^((number of digits in the base (b+2) representation of m) - 1)
signature: (b m : ℕ) (hm : m ≠ 0) : (b + 2) ^ (digits (b + 2) m).length ≤ (b + 2) * m

name: base_pow_length_digits_le
informal: Any non-zero natural number `m` is greater than b^((number of digits in the base b representation of m) - 1)
signature: (b m : ℕ) (hb : 1 < b) : m ≠ 0 → b ^ (digits b m).length ≤ b * m

name: _root_.Nat.bijOn_ofDigits'
informal: The bijection `Nat.bijOn_ofDigits` stated as a bijection between `Finset`. This spelling can be helpful for some proofs.
signature: {b : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) (l : ℕ) : Set.BijOn (ofDigits b) (fixedLengthDigits hb l) (Finset.range (b ^ l))

name: _root_.Nat.bijOn_digitsAppend'
informal: The bijection `Nat.bijOn_digitsAppend` stated as a bijection between `Finset`. This spelling can be helpful for some proofs.
signature: {b : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) (l : ℕ) : Set.BijOn (digitsAppend b l) (Finset.range (b ^ l)) (fixedLengthDigits hb l)

name: fixedLengthDigits_succ_eq_disjiUnion
informal: The set `List.fixedLengthDigits b (l + 1)` is the disjoint union of the sets `List.consFixedLengthDigits b l d` where `d` ranges through the natural integers `< d`.
signature: {b : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) (l : ℕ) : fixedLengthDigits hb (l + 1) = Finset.disjiUnion (Finset.range b) (consFixedLengthDigits hb l) (pairwiseDisjoint_consFixedLengthDigits hb l)

name: Nat.sum_sum_digits_eq
informal: The formula for the sum of the sum of the digits in base `b` over the natural integers `< b ^ l`.
signature: {b : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) (l : ℕ) : ∑ x ∈ Finset.range (b ^ l), (b.digits x).sum = l * b ^ (l - 1) * b.choose 2

name: factorization_eq_zero_iff'
informal: The only numbers with empty prime factorization are `0` and `1`
signature: (n : ℕ) : n.factorization = 0 ↔ n = 0 ∨ n = 1

name: eq_pow_of_factorization_eq_single
informal: If the factorization of `n` contains just one number `p` then `n` is a power of `p`
signature: {n p k : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) (h : n.factorization = Finsupp.single p k) : n = p ^ k

name: exists_eq_two_pow_mul_odd
informal: Any nonzero natural number is the product of an odd part `m` and a power of two `2 ^ k`.
signature: {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : ∃ k m : ℕ, Odd m ∧ n = 2 ^ k * m

name: Icc_factorization_eq_pow_dvd
informal: The set of positive powers of prime `p` that divide `n` is exactly the set of positive natural numbers up to `n.factorization p`.
signature: (n : ℕ) {p : ℕ} (pp : Prime p) : Icc 1 (n.factorization p) = {i ∈ Ico 1 n | p ^ i ∣ n}

name: eq_iff_prime_padicValNat_eq
informal: Two positive naturals are equal if their prime padic valuations are equal
signature: (a b : ℕ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) : a = b ↔ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → padicValNat p a = padicValNat p b

name: card_multiples
informal: Exactly `n / p` naturals in `[1, n]` are multiples of `p`. See `Nat.card_multiples'` for an alternative spelling of the statement.
signature: (n p : ℕ) : #{e ∈ range n | p ∣ e + 1} = n / p

name: card_multiples'
informal: There are exactly `⌊N/n⌋` positive multiples of `n` that are `≤ N`. See `Nat.card_multiples` for a "shifted-by-one" version.
signature: (N n : ℕ) : #{k ∈ range N.succ | k ≠ 0 ∧ n ∣ k} = N / n

name: Prime.factorization_pow
informal: For prime `p` the only prime factor of `p^k` is `p` with multiplicity `k`
signature: {p k : ℕ} (hp : Prime p) : (p ^ k).factorization = single p k

name: prod_pow_factorization_eq_self
informal: Any Finsupp `f : ℕ →₀ ℕ` whose support is in the primes is equal to the factorization of the product `∏ (a : ℕ) ∈ f.support, a ^ f a`.
signature: (hf : ∀ p ∈ f.support, Prime p) : (f.prod (· ^ ·)).factorization = f

name: isPrimePow_iff_unique_prime_dvd
informal: An equivalent definition for prime powers: `n` is a prime power iff there is a unique prime dividing it.
signature: {n : ℕ} : IsPrimePow n ↔ ∃! p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n

name: perm_primeFactorsList_mul
informal: For positive `a` and `b`, the prime factors of `a * b` are the union of those of `a` and `b`
signature: {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) : (a * b).primeFactorsList ~ a.primeFactorsList ++ b.primeFactorsList

name: perm_primeFactorsList_mul_of_coprime
informal: For coprime `a` and `b`, the prime factors of `a * b` are the union of those of `a` and `b`
signature: {a b : ℕ} (hab : Coprime a b) : (a * b).primeFactorsList ~ a.primeFactorsList ++ b.primeFactorsList

name: mem_primeFactorsList_mul_left
informal: If `p` is a prime factor of `a` then `p` is also a prime factor of `a * b` for any `b > 0`
signature: {p a b : ℕ} (hpa : p ∈ a.primeFactorsList) (hb : b ≠ 0) : p ∈ (a * b).primeFactorsList

name: mem_primeFactorsList_mul_right
informal: If `p` is a prime factor of `b` then `p` is also a prime factor of `a * b` for any `a > 0`
signature: {p a b : ℕ} (hpb : p ∈ b.primeFactorsList) (ha : a ≠ 0) : p ∈ (a * b).primeFactorsList

name: fib_coprime_fib_succ
informal: Subsequent Fibonacci numbers are coprime, see https://proofwiki.org/wiki/Consecutive_Fibonacci_Numbers_are_Coprime
signature: (n : ℕ) : Nat.Coprime (fib n) (fib (n + 1))

name: clog_le_iff_le_pow
informal: For `b > 1`, `clog b` and `(b ^ ·)` form a Galois connection. See also `clog_le_of_le_pow` for the implication that does not require `1 < b`.
signature: {b : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b) {x y : ℕ} : clog b x ≤ y ↔ x ≤ b ^ y

name: clog_pow_left
informal: This lemma says that `⌈log (b ^ k) n⌉ = ⌈(⌈log b n⌉ / k)⌉`, using operations on natural numbers to express this equality. Since Lean has no dedicated function for the ceiling division, we use `(a + (b - 1)) / b` for `⌈a / b⌉`.
signature: (b k n : ℕ) : clog (b ^ k) n = (clog b n + (k - 1)) / k

name: pow_dvd_iff_le_padicValNat
informal: If `p > 1`, `n > 0`, then the first component of `maxPowDvdDiv` is the maximal power of `p` that divides `n`.
signature: {p k n : ℕ} (hp : p ≠ 1) (hn : n ≠ 0) : p ^ k ∣ n ↔ k ≤ padicValNat p n

name: ModEq.dvd'
informal: The forward direction of `modEq_iff_dvd'`, which does not require the `a ≤ b` assumption.
signature: (h : a ≡ b [MOD n]) : n ∣ b - a

name: of_mul_left
informal: Cancel left multiplication in the modulus. For cancelling left multiplication on both sides of the `≡`, see `nat.modeq.mul_left_cancel'`.
signature: (m : ℕ) (h : a ≡ b [MOD m * n]) : a ≡ b [MOD n]

name: of_mul_right
informal: Cancel right multiplication in the modulus. For cancelling right multiplication on both sides of the `≡`, see `nat.modeq.mul_right_cancel'`.
signature: (m : ℕ) : a ≡ b [MOD n * m] → a ≡ b [MOD n]

name: cancel_left_div_gcd
informal: To cancel a common factor `c` from a `ModEq` we must divide the modulus `m` by `gcd m c`
signature: (hm : 0 < m) (h : c * a ≡ c * b [MOD m]) : a ≡ b [MOD m / gcd m c]

name: cancel_right_div_gcd
informal: To cancel a common factor `c` from a `ModEq` we must divide the modulus `m` by `gcd m c`
signature: (hm : 0 < m) (h : a * c ≡ b * c [MOD m]) : a ≡ b [MOD m / gcd m c]

name: cancel_left_of_coprime
informal: A common factor that's coprime with the modulus can be cancelled from a `ModEq`
signature: (hmc : gcd m c = 1) (h : c * a ≡ c * b [MOD m]) : a ≡ b [MOD m]

name: cancel_right_of_coprime
informal: A common factor that's coprime with the modulus can be cancelled from a `ModEq`
signature: (hmc : gcd m c = 1) (h : a * c ≡ b * c [MOD m]) : a ≡ b [MOD m]

name: emultiplicity_factorial
informal: **Legendre's Theorem** The multiplicity of a prime in `n!` is the sum of the quotients `n / p ^ i`. This sum is expressed over the finset `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound greater than `log p n`.
signature: {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : ∀ {n b : ℕ}, log p n < b → emultiplicity p n ! = (∑ i ∈ Ico 1 b, n / p ^ i : ℕ) | 0, b, _ => by simp [Ico, hp.emultiplicity_one] | n + 1, b, hb => calc emultiplicity p (n + 1)! = emultiplicity p n ! + emultiplicity p (n + 1)

name: emultiplicity_factorial_mul_succ
informal: The multiplicity of `p` in `(p * (n + 1))!` is one more than the sum of the multiplicities of `p` in `(p * n)!` and `n + 1`.
signature: {n p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : emultiplicity p (p * (n + 1))! = emultiplicity p (p * n)! + emultiplicity p (n + 1) + 1

name: pow_dvd_factorial_iff
informal: A prime power divides `n!` iff it is at most the sum of the quotients `n / p ^ i`. This sum is expressed over the set `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound greater than `log p n`
signature: {p : ℕ} {n r b : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hbn : log p n < b) : p ^ r ∣ n ! ↔ r ≤ ∑ i ∈ Ico 1 b, n / p ^ i

name: filter_multiset_Ico_card_eq_of_periodic
informal: An interval of length `a` filtered over a periodic predicate of period `a` has cardinality equal to the number naturals below `a` for which `p a` is true.
signature: (n a : ℕ) (p : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (pp : Periodic p a) : card (filter p (Ico n (n + a))) = a.count p

name: filter_Ico_card_eq_of_periodic
informal: An interval of length `a` filtered over a periodic predicate of period `a` has cardinality equal to the number naturals below `a` for which `p a` is true.
signature: (n a : ℕ) (p : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (pp : Periodic p a) : ((Ico n (n + a)).filter p).card = a.count p

name: minFac_sq_le_self
informal: The square of the smallest prime factor of a composite number `n` is at most `n`.
signature: {n : ℕ} (w : 0 < n) (h : ¬Prime n) : minFac n ^ 2 ≤ n

name: exists_infinite_primes
informal: Euclid's theorem on the **infinitude of primes**. Here given in the form: for every `n`, there exists a prime number `p ≥ n`.
signature: (n : ℕ) : ∃ p, n ≤ p ∧ Prime p

name: Prime.pow_inj
informal: Two prime powers with positive exponents are equal only when the primes and the exponents are equal.
signature: {p q m n : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (h : p ^ (m + 1) = q ^ (n + 1)) : p = q ∧ m = n

name: primeFactors_prime_pow
informal: The only prime divisor of positive prime power `p^k` is `p` itself
signature: (hk : k ≠ 0) (hp : Prime p) : (p ^ k).primeFactors = {p}

name: mk_le_mk
informal: We now define a long list of structures on ℕ+ induced by similar structures on ℕ. Most of these behave in a completely obvious way, but there are a few things to be said about subtraction, division and powers.
signature: (n k : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hk : 0 < k) : (⟨n, hn⟩ : ℕ+) ≤ ⟨k, hk⟩ ↔ n ≤ k

name: factorMultiset_ofPrime
informal: Factoring a prime gives the corresponding one-element multiset.
signature: (p : Nat.Primes) : (p : ℕ+).factorMultiset = PrimeMultiset.ofPrime p

name: factorMultiset_gcd
informal: The gcd and lcm operations on positive integers correspond to the inf and sup operations on multisets.
signature: (m n : ℕ+) : factorMultiset (gcd m n) = factorMultiset m ⊓ factorMultiset n

name: count_factorMultiset
informal: The number of occurrences of p in the factor multiset of m is the same as the p-adic valuation of m.
signature: (m : ℕ+) (p : Nat.Primes) (k : ℕ) : (p : ℕ+) ^ k ∣ m ↔ k ≤ m.factorMultiset.count p

name: step_wf
informal: We will apply the above step recursively. The following result is used to ensure that the process terminates.
signature: (hr : u.r ≠ 0) : SizeOf.sizeOf u.step < SizeOf.sizeOf u

name: step_v
informal: The reduction step does not change the product vector.
signature: (hr : u.r ≠ 0) : u.step.v = u.v.swap

name: ext_nnrat'
informal: If monoid with zero homs `f` and `g` from `ℚ≥0` agree on the naturals then they are equal.
signature: (h : ∀ n : ℕ, f n = g n) : f = g

name: ext_nnrat_on_pnat
informal: If monoid with zero homs `f` and `g` from `ℚ≥0` agree on the positive naturals then they are equal.
signature: (same_on_pnat : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → f n = g n) : f = g

name: ext_rat'
informal: If monoid with zero homs `f` and `g` from `ℚ` agree on the integers then they are equal.
signature: (h : ∀ m : ℤ, f m = g m) : f = g

name: ext_rat_on_pnat
informal: If monoid with zero homs `f` and `g` from `ℚ` agree on the positive naturals and `-1` then they are equal.
signature: (same_on_neg_one : f (-1) = g (-1)) (same_on_pnat : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → f n = g n) : f = g

name: ncard_powerset_ncard
informal: Given a finite set `s`, the number of subsets of `s` with cardinality `n` is `s.ncard.choose n`. See also `Finset.card_powersetCard`.
signature: (hs : s.Finite) (n : ℕ) : {t ⊆ s | t.ncard = n}.ncard = s.ncard.choose n

name: Function.Surjective.card_le_card_add_one_iff
informal: A surjective function `f : α → β` decreases cardinality by at most one if and only if there is at most a collision between a unique pair of elements.
signature: {α β : Type*} [Finite α] {f : α → β} (hf : Function.Surjective f) : Nat.card α ≤ Nat.card β + 1 ↔ ∀ a b c d, f a = f b → f c = f d → a ≠ b → c ≠ d → {a, b} = ({c, d} : Set α)

name: Set.ncard_le_ncard_image_add_one_iff
informal: A function `f : α → β` decreases cardinality by at most one if and only if there is at most a collision between a unique pair of elements.
signature: {α β : Type*} (s : Set α) [Finite s] (f : α → β) : s.ncard ≤ (f '' s).ncard + 1 ↔ ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, ∀ c ∈ s, ∀ d ∈ s, f a = f b → f c = f d → a ≠ b → c ≠ d → {a, b} = ({c, d} : Set α)

name: Set.biUnion_empty_finset
informal: This is a hybrid of `Set.biUnion_empty` and `Finset.biUnion_empty` (the index set on the LHS is the empty finset, but `s` is a family of sets, not finsets).
signature: {ι X : Type*} {s : ι → Set X} : ⋃ i ∈ (∅ : Finset ι), s i = ∅

name: Set.finite_of_forall_not_lt_lt
informal: If a set `s` does not contain any triple of elements `x < y < z`, then `s` is finite.
signature: (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ z ∈ s, x < y → y < z → False) : Set.Finite s

name: Finite.finite_subsets
informal: There are finitely many subsets of a given finite set
signature: {α : Type u} {a : Set α} (h : a.Finite) : { b | b ⊆ a }.Finite

name: SurjOn.image_invFunOn_image
informal: This lemma is a special case of `rightInvOn_invFunOn.image_image`; it may make more sense to use the other lemma directly in an application.
signature: [Nonempty α] (hf : SurjOn f s t) : f '' f.invFunOn s '' t = t

name: range_unique
informal: The range of a function from a `Unique` type contains just the function applied to its single value.
signature: [Unique ι] : range f = {f default}

name: Nontrivial.image
informal: The image of a nontrivial set under an injective map is nontrivial.
signature: (hs : s.Nontrivial) (hf : Function.Injective f) : (f '' s).Nontrivial

name: ext
informal: Note: implementers of `SetLike` must copy this lemma in order to tag it with `@[ext]`.
signature: (h : ∀ x, x ∈ p ↔ x ∈ q) : p = q

name: mapOfSurjective_eq_map
informal: A special case of the equivalence closure of an equivalence relation r equaling r.
signature: (h : ker f ≤ r) (hf : Surjective f) : map r f = mapOfSurjective r f h hf

name: map_cast
informal: Casting out of `SignType` respects composition with suitable bundled homomorphism types.
signature: {α β F : Type*} [AddGroupWithOne α] [One β] [SubtractionMonoid β] [FunLike F α β] [AddMonoidHomClass F α β] [OneHomClass F α β] (f : F) (s : SignType) : f s = s

name: card_sym_eq_choose
informal: The *stars and bars* lemma: the cardinality of `Sym α k` is equal to `Nat.choose (card α + k - 1) k`.
signature: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (k : ℕ) [Fintype (Sym α k)] : card (Sym α k) = (card α + k - 1).choose k

name: card_toMultiset
informal: Mapping an unordered pair to an unordered list produces a multiset of size `2`.
signature: {α : Type*} (z : Sym2 α) : z.toMultiset.card = 2

name: inf_eq_inf_and_sup_eq_sup
informal: In a linear order, two symmetric squares are equal if and only if they have the same infimum and supremum.
signature: [LinearOrder α] {s t : Sym2 α} : s.inf = t.inf ∧ s.sup = t.sup ↔ s = t

name: isUnit_natCast_iff_not_dvd_pow
informal: In `ZMod (p ^ d)` with `0 < d`, a natural number is a unit iff `p` does not divide it.
signature: {p d a : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hd : 0 < d) : IsUnit (a : ZMod (p ^ d)) ↔ ¬ p ∣ a

name: Nat.range_mul_add
informal: The range of `(m * · + k)` on natural numbers is the set of elements `≥ k` in the residue class of `k` mod `m`.
signature: (m k : ℕ) : Set.range (fun n : ℕ ↦ m * n + k) = {n : ℕ | (n : ZMod m) = k ∧ k ≤ n}

name: eq_unit_mul_divisor
informal: Any element of `ZMod N` has the form `u * d` where `u` is a unit and `d` is a divisor of `N`.
signature: {N : ℕ} (a : ZMod N) : ∃ d : ℕ, d ∣ N ∧ ∃ (u : ZMod N), IsUnit u ∧ a = u * d

name: uniformEquicontinuous_birkhoffAverage
informal: If `f` is a non-strictly contracting map (i.e., it is Lipschitz with constant `1`) and `g` is a uniformly continuous, then the Birkhoff averages of `g` along orbits of `f` is a uniformly equicontinuous family of functions.
signature: (hf : LipschitzWith 1 f) (hg : UniformContinuous g) : UniformEquicontinuous (birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g)

name: forall_map_sub_of_Icc
informal: If a predicate depends only on `f x - x` and holds for all `0 ≤ x ≤ 1`, then it holds for all `x`.
signature: (P : ℝ → Prop) (h : ∀ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, P (f x - x)) (x : ℝ) : P (f x - x)

name: prob_eq_zero_or_one
informal: On a probability space, the (pre)ergodicity condition is a zero-one law.
signature: [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hf : PreErgodic f μ) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hs' : f ⁻¹' s = s) : μ s = 0 ∨ μ s = 1

name: Commute.invOn_fixedPoints_comp
informal: If self-maps `f` and `g` commute, then they are inverse of each other on the set of fixed points of `f ∘ g`. This is a particular case of `Function.invOn_fixedPoints_comp`.
signature: (h : Commute f g) : Set.InvOn f g (fixedPoints <| f ∘ g) (fixedPoints <| f ∘ g)

name: Commute.left_bijOn_fixedPoints_comp
informal: If self-maps `f` and `g` commute, then `f` is bijective on the set of fixed points of `f ∘ g`. This is a particular case of `Function.bijOn_fixedPoints_comp`.
signature: (h : Commute f g) : Set.BijOn f (fixedPoints <| f ∘ g) (fixedPoints <| f ∘ g)

name: Commute.right_bijOn_fixedPoints_comp
informal: If self-maps `f` and `g` commute, then `g` is bijective on the set of fixed points of `f ∘ g`. This is a particular case of `Function.bijOn_fixedPoints_comp`.
signature: (h : Commute f g) : Set.BijOn g (fixedPoints <| f ∘ g) (fixedPoints <| f ∘ g)

name: isClosed_fixedPoints
informal: The set of fixed points of a continuous map is a closed set.
signature: (hf : Continuous f) : IsClosed (fixedPoints f)

name: eq_of_apply_eq_same
informal: If `f` sends two periodic points `x` and `y` of the same positive period to the same point, then `x = y`. For a similar statement about points of different periods see `eq_of_apply_eq`.
signature: (hx : IsPeriodicPt f n x) (hy : IsPeriodicPt f n y) (hn : 0 < n) (h : f x = f y) : x = y

name: eq_of_apply_eq
informal: If `f` sends two periodic points `x` and `y` of positive periods to the same point, then `x = y`.
signature: (hx : IsPeriodicPt f m x) (hy : IsPeriodicPt f n y) (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (h : f x = f y) : x = y

name: map_eq_of_algebraicClosure_eq_bot
informal: If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `K / E` has no non-trivial algebraic subextensions (this means that it is purely transcendental), then the image of `algebraicClosure F E` in `K` is equal to `algebraicClosure F K`.
signature: [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] (h : algebraicClosure E K = ⊥) : (algebraicClosure F E).map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F E K) = algebraicClosure F K

name: eq_restrictScalars_of_isAlgebraic
informal: If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is algebraic, then `algebraicClosure F K` is equal to `algebraicClosure E K`.
signature: [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] : algebraicClosure F K = (algebraicClosure E K).restrictScalars F

name: Fintype.nonempty_field_iff
informal: A `Fintype` can be given a field structure iff its cardinality is a prime power.
signature: {α} [Fintype α] : Nonempty (Field α) ↔ IsPrimePow ‖α‖

name: Field.nonempty_iff
informal: There is a field structure on type if and only if its cardinality is a prime power.
signature: {α : Type u} : Nonempty (Field α) ↔ IsPrimePow #α

name: sum_subgroup_units_eq_zero
informal: The sum of a nontrivial subgroup of the units of a field is zero.
signature: [Ring K] [NoZeroDivisors K] {G : Subgroup Kˣ} [Fintype G] (hg : G ≠ ⊥) : ∑ x : G, (x.val : K) = 0

name: trace_to_zmod_nondegenerate
informal: The trace map from a finite field to its prime field is nondegenerate.
signature: (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F] [Algebra (ZMod (ringChar F)) F] {a : F} (ha : a ≠ 0) : ∃ b : F, Algebra.trace (ZMod (ringChar F)) F (a * b) ≠ 0

name: finiteDimensional_of_finite
informal: A galois extension with finite galois group is finite dimensional. The dimension is then equal to the order of the galois group via `IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank`.
signature: [IsGalois F E] [Finite Gal(E/F)] : FiniteDimensional F E

name: card_eq_finrank
informal: The cardinality of a Galois group equals the degree of the field extension. See `IsGaloisGroup.card_eq_finrank'` for a ring-theoretic generalization assuming finiteness.
signature: [IsGaloisGroup G K L] : Nat.card G = Module.finrank K L

name: cardinal_eq_cardinal_transcendence_basis_of_aleph0_lt'
informal: If `K` is an uncountable algebraically closed field, then its cardinality is the same as that of a transcendence basis. This is a simpler, but less general statement of `cardinal_eq_cardinal_transcendence_basis_of_aleph0_lt`.
signature: [Nontrivial R] (hv : IsTranscendenceBasis R v') (hR : #R ≤ ℵ₀) (hK : ℵ₀ < #K') : #K' = #ι'

name: ringEquiv_of_equiv_of_charZero
informal: Two uncountable algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero are isomorphic if they have the same cardinality.
signature: [CharZero K] [CharZero L] (hK : ℵ₀ < #K) (hKL : Nonempty (K ≃ L)) : Nonempty (K ≃+* L)

name: krullTopology_isTotallySeparated
informal: If `L/K` is an algebraic field extension, then the Krull topology on `Gal(L/K)` is totally separated.
signature: {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra.IsIntegral K L] : IsTotallySeparated (Set.univ : Set Gal(L/K))

name: stabilizer_isOpen_of_isIntegral
informal: If `L/K` is an algebraic field extension, then the stabilizer in `Gal(L/K)` of any element in `L` is open for the Krull topology.
signature: [Algebra.IsIntegral K L] (x : L) : IsOpen (MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) x : Set Gal(L/K))

name: isIntegrallyClosed_eq_field_fractions'
informal: For integrally closed domains, the minimal polynomial over the ring is the same as the minimal polynomial over the fraction field. Compared to `minpoly.isIntegrallyClosed_eq_field_fractions`, this version is useful if the element is in a ring that is already a `K`-algebra.
