signature: [IsDomain S] [Algebra K S] [IsScalarTower R K S] {s : S} (hs : IsIntegral R s) : minpoly K s = (minpoly R s).map (algebraMap R K)

name: AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom_surjective
informal: The group homomorphism given by restricting an algebra isomorphism to a normal subfield is surjective.
signature: [Normal F K₁] [Normal F E] : Function.Surjective (AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom K₁ : Gal(E/F) → K₁ ≃ₐ[F] K₁)

name: PerfectRing.ofSurjective
informal: For a reduced ring, surjectivity of the Frobenius map is a sufficient condition for perfection.
signature: (R : Type*) (p : ℕ) [CommRing R] [ExpChar R p] [IsReduced R] (h : Surjective <| frobenius R p) : PerfectRing R p

name: Subfield.bot_eq_of_zMod_algebra
informal: The smallest subfield of a field of characteristic `p` is (the image of) `ZMod p`. Note that the fact that the field `K` is of characteristic `p` is stated by the fact that it is `ZMod p`-algebra.
signature: {K : Type*} (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [Field K] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] : (⊥ : Subfield K) = (algebraMap (ZMod p) K).fieldRange

name: IsPurelyInseparable.tower_bot
informal: If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower such that `K / F` is purely inseparable, then `E / F` is also purely inseparable.
signature: [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [IsPurelyInseparable F K] : IsPurelyInseparable F E

name: IsPurelyInseparable.tower_top
informal: If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower such that `K / F` is purely inseparable, then `K / E` is also purely inseparable.
signature: [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [h : IsPurelyInseparable F K] : IsPurelyInseparable E K

name: IsPurelyInseparable.finSepDegree_eq_one
informal: A purely inseparable extension has finite separable degree one.
signature: [IsPurelyInseparable F E] : finSepDegree F E = 1

name: IsPurelyInseparable.insepDegree_eq
informal: A purely inseparable extension has inseparable degree equal to degree.
signature: [IsPurelyInseparable F E] : insepDegree F E = Module.rank F E

name: IsPurelyInseparable.finInsepDegree_eq
informal: A purely inseparable extension has finite inseparable degree equal to degree.
signature: [IsPurelyInseparable F E] : finInsepDegree F E = finrank F E

name: separableClosure_le_iff
informal: If `E / F` is algebraic, then an intermediate field of `E / F` contains the separable closure of `F` in `E` if and only if `E` is purely inseparable over it.
signature: [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] (L : IntermediateField F E) : separableClosure F E ≤ L ↔ IsPurelyInseparable L E

name: isSepClosed_iff_isPurelyInseparable_algebraicClosure
informal: If `E` is an algebraic closure of `F`, then `F` is separably closed if and only if `E / F` is purely inseparable.
signature: [IsAlgClosure F E] : IsSepClosed F ↔ IsPurelyInseparable F E

name: Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isSepClosed
informal: If `E / F` is an algebraic extension, `F` is separably closed, then `E` is also separably closed.
signature: [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F E] [IsSepClosed F] : IsSepClosed E

name: elemExponent_le_exponent
informal: An exponent of an element is less or equal than exponent of the extension.
signature: [HasExponent K L] (a : L) : elemExponent K a ≤ exponent K L

name: perfectClosure.eq_bot_of_isSeparable
informal: If `E / F` is separable, then the perfect closure of `F` in `E` is equal to `F`. Note that the converse is not necessarily true (see https://math.stackexchange.com/a/3009197) even when `E / F` is algebraic.
signature: [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] : perfectClosure F E = ⊥

name: adjoin_eq_adjoin_pow_expChar_of_isSeparable'
informal: If `E / F` is a separable field extension of exponential characteristic `q`, then `F(S) = F(S ^ q)` for any subset `S` of `E`.
signature: [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] (S : Set E) (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q] : adjoin F S = adjoin F ((· ^ q) '' S)

name: adjoin_simple_eq_adjoin_pow_expChar_pow_of_isSeparable'
informal: If `E / F` is a separable field extension of exponential characteristic `q`, then `F⟮a⟯ = F⟮a ^ q ^ n⟯` for any subset `a : E` and any natural number `n`.
signature: [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] (a : E) (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q] (n : ℕ) : F⟮a⟯ = F⟮a ^ q ^ n⟯

name: adjoin_simple_eq_adjoin_pow_expChar_of_isSeparable'
informal: If `E / F` is a separable field extension of exponential characteristic `q`, then `F⟮a⟯ = F⟮a ^ q⟯` for any `a : E`.
signature: [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] (a : E) (q : ℕ) [ExpChar F q] : F⟮a⟯ = F⟮a ^ q⟯

name: separableClosure.eq_restrictScalars_of_isSeparable
informal: If `K / E / F` is a field extension tower, such that `E / F` is separable, then `separableClosure F K` is equal to `separableClosure E K`.
signature: [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] : separableClosure F K = (separableClosure E K).restrictScalars F

name: exists_finset_maximalFor_isTranscendenceBasis_separableClosure
informal: In a finitely generated field extension, there exists a maximal separably generated field extension.
signature: [Algebra.EssFiniteType F E] : ∃ s : Finset E, MaximalFor (fun t : Set E ↦ IsTranscendenceBasis F ((↑) : t → E)) (fun t ↦ (separableClosure (adjoin F t) E).restrictScalars F) s

name: finSepDegree_eq_zero_of_transcendental
informal: If the field extension `E / F` is transcendental, then `Field.finSepDegree F E = 0`, which actually means that `Field.Emb F E` is infinite (see `Field.infinite_emb_of_transcendental`).
signature: [Algebra.Transcendental F E] : finSepDegree F E = 0

name: natSepDegree_ne_zero
informal: A non-constant polynomial has non-zero separable degree.
signature: (h : f.natDegree ≠ 0) : f.natSepDegree ≠ 0

name: natSepDegree_eq_natDegree_iff
informal: The separable degree of a non-zero polynomial is equal to its degree if and only if it is separable.
signature: (hf : f ≠ 0) : f.natSepDegree = f.natDegree ↔ f.Separable

name: natSepDegree_eq_natDegree_of_separable
informal: If a polynomial is separable, then its separable degree is equal to its degree.
signature: (h : f.Separable) : f.natSepDegree = f.natDegree

name: natSepDegree_eq_of_isAlgClosed
informal: The separable degree of a polynomial is equal to the number of distinct roots of it over any algebraically closed field.
signature: [DecidableEq E] [IsAlgClosed E] : f.natSepDegree = (f.aroots E).toFinset.card

name: natSepDegree_dvd_natDegree
informal: The separable degree of an irreducible polynomial divides its degree.
signature: (h : Irreducible f) : f.natSepDegree ∣ f.natDegree

name: finSepDegree_eq_finrank_of_isSeparable
informal: If `E / F` is a separable extension, then its separable degree is equal to its degree. When `E / F` is infinite, it means that `Field.Emb F E` has infinitely many elements. (But the cardinality of `Field.Emb F E` is not equal to `Module.rank F E` in general!)
signature: [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] : finSepDegree F E = finrank F E

name: IsSeparable.of_algebra_isSeparable_of_isSeparable
informal: If `K / E / F` is an extension tower such that `E / F` is separable, `x : K` is separable over `E`, then it's also separable over `F`.
signature: [Algebra E K] [IsScalarTower F E K] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] {x : K} (hsep : IsSeparable E x) : IsSeparable F x

name: exists_isTranscendenceBasis_and_isSeparable_of_perfectField
informal: Any finitely generated extension over perfect fields are separably generated.
signature: [PerfectField k] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k K] : ∃ s : Finset K, IsTranscendenceBasis k ((↑) : s → K) ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K)) K

name: mem_hull_of_convex
informal: The cone hull of a convex set is simply the union of the open halflines through that set.
signature: (hs : Convex 𝕜 s) : x ∈ hull 𝕜 s ↔ ∃ r : 𝕜, 0 < r ∧ x ∈ r • s where mp hx

name: coe_hull_of_convex
informal: The cone hull of a convex set is simply the union of the open halflines through that set.
signature: (hs : Convex 𝕜 s) : hull 𝕜 s = {x | ∃ r : 𝕜, 0 < r ∧ x ∈ r • s}

name: inner_vsub_altitudeFoot_vsub_altitudeFoot_eq_zero
informal: Altitudes are perpendicular to the faces containing their foot.
signature: {i j : Fin (n + 1)} (h : i ≠ j) : have : NeZero n

name: inner_vsub_vsub_altitudeFoot_eq_height_sq
informal: The inner product of an edge from `j` to `i` and the vector from the foot of `i` to `i` is the square of the height.
signature: [NeZero n] {i j : Fin (n + 1)} (h : i ≠ j) : ⟪s.points i -ᵥ s.points j, s.points i -ᵥ s.altitudeFoot i⟫ = s.height i ^ 2

name: abs_inner_vsub_altitudeFoot_lt_mul
informal: The inner product of two distinct altitudes has absolute value strictly less than the product of their lengths. Equivalently, neither vector is a multiple of the other; the angle between them is not 0 or π.
signature: {i j : Fin (n + 1)} (hij : i ≠ j) : |⟪s.points i -ᵥ s.altitudeFoot i, s.points j -ᵥ s.altitudeFoot j⟫| < s.height i * s.height j

name: neg_mul_lt_inner_vsub_altitudeFoot
informal: The inner product of two altitudes has value strictly greater than the negated product of their lengths.
signature: (i j : Fin (n + 1)) : -(s.height i * s.height j) < ⟪s.points i -ᵥ s.altitudeFoot i, s.points j -ᵥ s.altitudeFoot j⟫

name: eq_incenter_or_eq_excenter_singleton_of_oangle_eq
informal: An excenter lying on the internal angle bisector from a vertex is either the incenter or the excenter opposite that vertex.
signature: {signs : Finset (Fin 3)} (h : ∡ (t.points i₂) (t.points i₁) (t.excenter signs) = ∡ (t.excenter signs) (t.points i₁) (t.points i₃)) : t.excenter signs = t.incenter ∨ t.excenter signs = t.excenter {i₁}

name: norm_ofLp_crossProduct
informal: The L2 norm of the cross product of two real vectors (of type `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`) equals the product of their individual norms times the sine of the angle between them.
signature: (a b : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) : ‖toLp 2 (ofLp a ⨯₃ ofLp b)‖ = ‖a‖ * ‖b‖ * sin (angle a b)

name: norm_toLp_symm_crossProduct
informal: The L2 norm of the cross product of two real vectors (of type `Fin 3 → R`) equals the product of their individual L2 norms times the sine of the angle between them.
signature: (a b : Fin 3 → ℝ) : ‖toLp 2 (a ⨯₃ b)‖ = ‖toLp 2 a‖ * ‖toLp 2 b‖ * sin (angle (toLp 2 a) (toLp 2 b))

name: side_side_side
informal: **Side–Side–Side (SSS) congruence** If all three corresponding sides of two triangles are equal, then the triangles are congruent. This holds even if the triangles are degenerate.
signature: (hd₁ : dist a b = dist a' b') (hd₂ : dist b c = dist b' c') (hd₃ : dist c a = dist c' a') : ![a, b, c] ≅ ![a', b', c']

name: side_angle_side
informal: **Side–Angle–Side (SAS) congruence** If two triangles have two sides and the included angle equal, then the triangles are congruent. This holds even if the triangles are degenerate.
signature: (h : ∠ a b c = ∠ a' b' c') (hd₁ : dist a b = dist a' b') (hd₂ : dist b c = dist b' c') : ![a, b, c] ≅ ![a', b', c']

name: angle_side_angle
informal: **Angle–Side–Angle (ASA) congruence** If two triangles have two equal angles and the included side equal, then the triangles are congruent. We require that one of the triangles is non-degenerate, the non-collinearity of the other is then implied by the given equalities.
signature: (h : ¬Collinear ℝ {a, b, c}) (ha₁ : ∠ a b c = ∠ a' b' c') (hd : dist b c = dist b' c') (ha₂ : ∠ b c a = ∠ b' c' a') : ![a, b, c] ≅ ![a', b', c']

name: angle_angle_side
informal: **Angle–Angle–Side (AAS) congruence** If two triangles have two equal angles and a non-included side equal, then the triangles are congruent. We require that one of the triangles is non-degenerate, the non-collinearity of the other is then implied by the given equalities.
signature: (h : ¬Collinear ℝ {a, b, c}) (ha₁ : ∠ a b c = ∠ a' b' c') (ha₂ : ∠ b c a = ∠ b' c' a') (hd : dist c a = dist c' a') : ![a, b, c] ≅ ![a', b', c']

name: inv_height_eq_sum_mul_inv_dist
informal: The inverse of the distance from one vertex to the opposite face, expressed as a sum of multiples of that quantity for the other vertices. The multipliers, expressed here in terms of inner products, are equal to the cosines of angles between faces (informally, the inverse distances are proportional to the volumes of the faces and this is equivalent to expressing the volume of a face as the sum of the signed volumes of projections of the other faces onto that face).
signature: (i : Fin (n + 1)) : (s.height i)⁻¹ = ∑ j ∈ {k | k ≠ i}, -(⟪s.points i -ᵥ s.altitudeFoot i, s.points j -ᵥ s.altitudeFoot j⟫ / (s.height i * s.height j)) * (s.height j)⁻¹

name: inv_height_lt_sum_inv_height
informal: The inverse of the distance from one vertex to the opposite face is less than the sum of that quantity for the other vertices. This implies the existence of the excenter opposite that vertex; it also gives information about the location of the incenter (see `excenterWeights_empty_lt_inv_two`).
signature: [Nat.AtLeastTwo n] (i : Fin (n + 1)) : (s.height i)⁻¹ < ∑ j ∈ {k | k ≠ i}, (s.height j)⁻¹

name: excenterExists_singleton
informal: The existence of the excenter opposite a vertex (in two or more dimensions), expressed in terms of `ExcenterExists`.
signature: [Nat.AtLeastTwo n] (i : Fin (n + 1)) : s.ExcenterExists {i}

name: excenterWeights_empty_lt_inv_two
informal: The barycentric coordinates of the incenter are less than `2⁻¹` (thus, it lies closer on an angle bisector to the opposite side than to the vertex, or equivalently the image of the incenter under a homothety with scale factor 2 about a vertex lies outside the simplex).
signature: [n.AtLeastTwo] (i : Fin (n + 1)) : s.excenterWeights ∅ i < 2⁻¹

name: ExcenterExists.signedInfDist_excenter
informal: The signed distance between the excenter and its projection in the plane of each face is the exradius.
signature: {signs : Finset (Fin (n + 1))} (h : s.ExcenterExists signs) (i : Fin (n + 1)) : s.signedInfDist i (s.excenter signs) = (if i ∈ signs then -1 else 1) * SignType.sign (∑ j, s.excenterWeightsUnnorm signs j) * (s.exradius signs)

name: signedInfDist_incenter
informal: The signed distance between the incenter and its projection in the plane of each face is the inradius. In other words, the incenter is _internally_ tangent to the faces.
signature: (i : Fin (n + 1)) : s.signedInfDist i s.incenter = s.inradius

name: ExcenterExists.dist_excenter
informal: The distance between the excenter and its projection in the plane of each face is the exradius.
signature: {signs : Finset (Fin (n + 1))} (h : s.ExcenterExists signs) (i : Fin (n + 1)) : dist (s.excenter signs) (s.touchpoint signs i) = s.exradius signs

name: dist_incenter
informal: The distance between the incenter and its projection in the plane of each face is the inradius.
signature: (i : Fin (n + 1)) : dist s.incenter (s.touchpoint ∅ i) = s.inradius

name: excenter_eq_incenter_or_excenter_singleton
informal: An excenter of a triangle is either the incenter or the excenter opposite a vertex.
signature: (signs : Finset (Fin 3)) : t.excenter signs = t.incenter ∨ ∃ i, t.excenter signs = t.excenter {i}

name: excenter_eq_incenter_or_excenter_singleton_of_ne
informal: An excenter of a triangle is either the incenter or the excenter opposite one of three enumerated different vertices. This is intended for when it is known a point is an excenter and it is to be proved which excenter it is by elimination of the other cases.
signature: (signs : Finset (Fin 3)) {i₁ i₂ i₃ : Fin 3} (h₁₂ : i₁ ≠ i₂) (h₁₃ : i₁ ≠ i₃) (h₂₃ : i₂ ≠ i₃) : t.excenter signs = t.incenter ∨ t.excenter signs = t.excenter {i₁} ∨ t.excenter signs = t.excenter {i₂} ∨ t.excenter signs = t.excenter {i₃}

name: similar_of_angle_angle
informal: If two triangles have two pairs equal angles, then the triangles are similar.
signature: (h_not_col : ¬ Collinear ℝ {a, b, c}) (h₁ : ∠ a b c = ∠ a' b' c') (h₂ : ∠ b c a = ∠ b' c' a') : ![a, b, c] ∼ ![a', b', c']

name: similar_of_side_angle_side
informal: If two triangles have proportional adjacent sides and an equal included angle, then the triangles are similar.
signature: (h_not_col : ¬ Collinear ℝ {a, b, c}) (h_not_col' : ¬ Collinear ℝ {a', b', c'}) (h : ∠ a b c = ∠ a' b' c') (hd : dist a b * dist b' c' = dist b c * dist a' b') : ![a, b, c] ∼ ![a', b', c']

name: _root_.Similar.angle_eq
informal: For two similar triangles, the corresponding angles are equal.

name: _root_.Similar.angle_eq_all
informal: In two similar triangles, all three corresponding angles are equal.

name: center_mem_affineSpan_pair_iff_isDiameter
informal: The center lies on the line through two points of a sphere if and only if those points are the endpoints of a diameter.
signature: (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) : s.center ∈ line[ℝ, p₁, p₂] ↔ s.IsDiameter p₁ p₂

name: topologicalSemiring_of_contMDiffRing
informal: A `C^n` (semi)ring is a topological (semi)ring. This is not an instance for technical reasons, see note [Design choices about smooth algebraic structures].
signature: [Semiring R] [ContMDiffRing I n R] : IsTopologicalSemiring R

name: contMDiffOn_isOpenEmbedding_symm
informal: If the `ChartedSpace` structure on a manifold `M` is given by an open embedding `e : M → H`, then the inverse of `e` is `C^n`.
signature: [Nonempty M] : haveI

name: contMDiffOn_iff
informal: One can reformulate being `C^n` on a set as continuity on this set, and being `C^n` in any extended chart.
signature: [IsManifold I n M] [IsManifold I' n M'] : ContMDiffOn I I' n f s ↔ ContinuousOn f s ∧ ∀ (x : M) (y : M'), ContDiffOn 𝕜 n (extChartAt I' y ∘ f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm) ((extChartAt I x).target ∩ (extChartAt I x).symm ⁻¹' (s ∩ f ⁻¹' (extChartAt I' y).source))

name: contMDiffOn_iff_target
informal: One can reformulate being `C^n` on a set as continuity on this set, and being `C^n` in any extended chart in the target.
signature: [IsManifold I n M] [IsManifold I' n M'] : ContMDiffOn I I' n f s ↔ ContinuousOn f s ∧ ∀ y : M', ContMDiffOn I 𝓘(𝕜, E') n (extChartAt I' y ∘ f) (s ∩ f ⁻¹' (extChartAt I' y).source)

name: contMDiff_iff
informal: One can reformulate being `C^n` as continuity and being `C^n` in any extended chart.
signature: [IsManifold I n M] [IsManifold I' n M'] : ContMDiff I I' n f ↔ Continuous f ∧ ∀ (x : M) (y : M'), ContDiffOn 𝕜 n (extChartAt I' y ∘ f ∘ (extChartAt I x).symm) ((extChartAt I x).target ∩ (extChartAt I x).symm ⁻¹' f ⁻¹' (extChartAt I' y).source)

name: contMDiff_iff_target
informal: One can reformulate being `C^n` as continuity and being `C^n` in any extended chart in the target.
signature: [IsManifold I n M] [IsManifold I' n M'] : ContMDiff I I' n f ↔ Continuous f ∧ ∀ y : M', ContMDiffOn I 𝓘(𝕜, E') n (extChartAt I' y ∘ f) (f ⁻¹' (extChartAt I' y).source)

name: contMDiffWithinAt_iff_contMDiffOn_nhds
informal: A function is `C^n` within a set at a point, for `n : ℕ` or `n = ω`, if and only if it is `C^n` on a neighborhood of this point.
signature: [IsManifold I n M] [IsManifold I' n M'] (hn : n ≠ ∞) : ContMDiffWithinAt I I' n f s x ↔ ∃ u ∈ 𝓝[insert x s] x, ContMDiffOn I I' n f u

name: contMDiffAt_iff_contMDiffOn_nhds
informal: A function is `C^n` at a point, for `n : ℕ`, if and only if it is `C^n` on a neighborhood of this point.
signature: [IsManifold I n M] [IsManifold I' n M'] (hn : n ≠ ∞) : ContMDiffAt I I' n f x ↔ ∃ u ∈ 𝓝 x, ContMDiffOn I I' n f u

name: _root_.Convex.convex_isRCLikeNormedField
informal: If a set is `ℝ`-convex for some normed space structure, then it is `ℝ`-convex for the normed space structure coming from an `IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜`. Useful when constructing model spaces to avoid diamond issues when populating the field `convex_range'`.
signature: [NormedSpace ℝ E] [h : IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜] {s : Set E} (hs : Convex ℝ s) : letI

name: of_discreteTopology
informal: A discrete space `M` is a smooth manifold over the trivial model on a trivial normed space.
signature: [DiscreteTopology M] [Unique E] : IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf 𝕜 E) n M

name: isLocalStructomorphWithinAt_localInvariantProp
informal: For a groupoid `G` which is `ClosedUnderRestriction`, being a local structomorphism is a local invariant property.
signature: [ClosedUnderRestriction G] : LocalInvariantProp G G (IsLocalStructomorphWithinAt G)

name: MDifferentiableOn.union_of_isOpen
informal: If a function is differentiable on two open sets, it is also differentiable on their union.
signature: (hf : MDiff[s] f) (hf' : MDiff[t] f) (hs : IsOpen s) (ht : IsOpen t) : MDiff[s ∪ t] f

name: mdifferentiableOn_union_iff_of_isOpen
informal: A function is differentiable on two open sets iff it is differentiable on their union.
signature: (hs : IsOpen s) (ht : IsOpen t) : MDiff[s ∪ t] f ↔ MDiff[s] f ∧ MDiff[t] f

name: mfderivWithin_congr_set
informal: If two sets coincide locally, then derivatives within these sets are the same.
signature: (h : s =ᶠ[𝓝 x] t) : mfderiv[s] f x = mfderiv[t] f x

name: mfderivWithin_eventually_congr_set
informal: If two sets coincide locally, then derivatives within these sets coincide locally.
signature: (h : s =ᶠ[𝓝 x] t) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, mfderiv[s] f y = mfderiv[t] f y

name: to_iso
informal: An open immersion is an iso if the underlying continuous map is epi.
signature: [h' : Epi f.base] : IsIso f

name: to_iso
informal: An open immersion is an iso if the underlying continuous map is epi.
signature: [h' : Epi f.hom.base] : IsIso f

name: of_stalk_iso
informal: Suppose `X Y : SheafedSpace C`, where `C` is a concrete category, whose forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms, preserves limits and filtered colimits. Then a morphism `X ⟶ Y` that is a topological open embedding is an open immersion iff every stalk map is an iso.
signature: {X Y : LocallyRingedSpace} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsOpenEmbedding f.base) [stalk_iso : ∀ x : X.1, IsIso (f.stalkMap x)] : LocallyRingedSpace.IsOpenImmersion f

name: LinearOrderedAddCommGroup.discrete_or_denselyOrdered
informal: Any linearly ordered archimedean additive group is either isomorphic (and order-isomorphic) to the integers, or is densely ordered.
signature: (G : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] [LinearOrder G] [IsOrderedAddMonoid G] [Archimedean G] : Nonempty (G ≃+o ℤ) ∨ DenselyOrdered G

name: LinearOrderedAddCommGroup.discrete_iff_not_denselyOrdered
informal: Any linearly ordered archimedean additive group is either isomorphic (and order-isomorphic) to the integers, or is densely ordered, exclusively. (See also `LinearOrderedAddCommGroup.isAddCyclic_iff_not_denselyOrdered`.)
signature: (G : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] [LinearOrder G] [IsOrderedAddMonoid G] [Archimedean G] : Nonempty (G ≃+o ℤ) ↔ ¬ DenselyOrdered G

name: LinearOrderedAddCommGroup.isAddCyclic_iff_not_denselyOrdered
informal: Any non-trivial linearly ordered archimedean additive group is either cyclic, or densely ordered, exclusively.
signature: {A : Type*} [AddCommGroup A] [LinearOrder A] [IsOrderedAddMonoid A] [Archimedean A] [Nontrivial A] : IsAddCyclic A ↔ ¬ DenselyOrdered A

name: LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero.discrete_or_denselyOrdered
informal: Any nontrivial (has other than 0 and 1) linearly ordered mul-archimedean group with zero is either isomorphic (and order-isomorphic) to `ℤᵐ⁰`, or is densely ordered.
signature: (G : Type*) [LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero G] [Nontrivial Gˣ] [MulArchimedean G] : Nonempty (G ≃*o ℤᵐ⁰) ∨ DenselyOrdered G

name: LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero.discrete_iff_not_denselyOrdered
informal: Any nontrivial (has other than 0 and 1) linearly ordered mul-archimedean group with zero is either isomorphic (and order-isomorphic) to `ℤᵐ⁰`, or is densely ordered, exclusively
signature: (G : Type*) [LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero G] [Nontrivial Gˣ] [MulArchimedean G] : Nonempty (G ≃*o ℤᵐ⁰) ↔ ¬ DenselyOrdered G

name: Group.nat_card_center_add_sum_card_noncenter_eq_card
informal: The **class equation** for finite groups. The cardinality of a group is equal to the size of its center plus the sum of the size of all its nontrivial conjugacy classes.
signature: [Finite G] : Nat.card (Subgroup.center G) + ∑ᶠ x ∈ noncenter G, Nat.card x.carrier = Nat.card G

name: transferFocal_eq_pow
informal: The restriction of the transfer map to `H` acts like the power map `x ↦ x^n` mod `H*`, where `n = [G:H]`.
signature: [H.FiniteIndex] (x : H) : transferFocal H x = (x : H ⧸ H.focalSubgroupOf) ^ H.index

name: frattini_nongenerating
informal: The Frattini subgroup consists of "non-generating" elements in the following sense: If a subgroup together with the Frattini subgroup generates the whole group, then the subgroup is already the whole group.
signature: [IsCoatomic (Subgroup G)] {K : Subgroup G} (h : K ⊔ frattini G = ⊤) : K = ⊤

name: path_nonempty_of_hom
informal: If there exists a morphism `a → b` in a free groupoid, then there also exists a zigzag from `a` to `b` in the generating quiver.
signature: {G} [Groupoid.{u, u} G] [IsFreeGroupoid G] {a b : G} : Nonempty (a ⟶ b) → Nonempty (Path (symgen a) (symgen b))

name: distribSMulToLinearMap_injective_of_isTorsionFree
informal: On an additive group that is torsion-free as a `ℤ`-module, the linear map given by multiplication by `n : ℕ` is injective (when `n ≠ 0`).
signature: [IsTorsionFree ℤ M] {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : Function.Injective (DistribSMul.toLinearMap ℤ M n)

name: finrank_eq_of_finiteIndex
informal: If `A` is a subgroup of finite index of an additive group `M` that is finitely generated and torsion-free as a `ℤ`-module, then `A` and `M` have the same rank.
signature: [Module.Finite ℤ M] [IsTorsionFree ℤ M] (A : AddSubgroup M) [A.FiniteIndex] : finrank ℤ A = finrank ℤ M

name: nonempty_fixed_point_of_prime_not_dvd_card
informal: If a p-group acts on `α` and the cardinality of `α` is not a multiple of `p` then the action has a fixed point.
signature: (α) [MulAction G α] (hpα : ¬p ∣ Nat.card α) : (fixedPoints G α).Nonempty

name: IsCycle.support_congr
informal: Unlike `support_congr`, which assumes that `∀ (x ∈ g.support), f x = g x)`, here we have the weaker assumption that `∀ (x ∈ f.support), f x = g x`.
signature: (hf : IsCycle f) (hg : IsCycle g) (h : f.support ⊆ g.support) (h' : ∀ x ∈ f.support, f x = g x) : f = g

name: IsCycle.eq_on_support_inter_nonempty_congr
informal: If two cyclic permutations agree on all terms in their intersection, and that intersection is not empty, then the two cyclic permutations must be equal.
signature: (hf : IsCycle f) (hg : IsCycle g) (h : ∀ x ∈ f.support ∩ g.support, f x = g x) (hx : f x = g x) (hx' : x ∈ f.support) : f = g

name: IsCycleOn.isCycle_subtypePerm
informal: Note that the identity satisfies `IsCycleOn` for any subsingleton set, but not `IsCycle`.
signature: (hf : f.IsCycleOn s) (hs : s.Nontrivial) : (f.subtypePerm fun _ => hf.apply_mem_iff : Perm s).IsCycle

name: product_self_eq_disjiUnion_perm
informal: We can partition the square `s ×ˢ s` into shifted diagonals as such: ``` 01234 40123 34012 23401 12340 ``` The diagonals are given by the cycle `f`.
signature: (hf : f.IsCycleOn s) : s ×ˢ s = (range #s).disjiUnion (fun k => s.map ⟨fun i => (i, (f ^ k) i), fun _ _ => congr_arg Prod.fst⟩) (product_self_eq_disjiUnion_perm_aux hf)

name: subtypePerm_on_cycleFactorsFinset
informal: A permutation restricted to the support of a cycle factor is that cycle factor
signature: [DecidableEq α] [Fintype α] {g c : Perm α} (hc : c ∈ g.cycleFactorsFinset) : g.subtypePerm (mem_cycleFactorsFinset_support hc) = c.subtypePermOfSupport

name: List.exists_pw_disjoint_with_card
informal: For any `c : List ℕ` whose sum is at most `Fintype.card α`, we can find `o : List (List α)` whose members have no duplicate, whose lengths given by `c`, and which are pairwise disjoint
signature: {α : Type*} [Fintype α] {c : List ℕ} (hc : c.sum ≤ Fintype.card α) : ∃ o : List (List α), o.map length = c ∧ (∀ s ∈ o, s.Nodup) ∧ Pairwise List.Disjoint o

name: card_fixedPoints_modEq
informal: The number of fixed points of a `p ^ n`-th root of the identity function over a finite set and the set's cardinality have the same residue modulo `p`, where `p` is a prime.
signature: [DecidableEq α] {f : Function.End α} {p n : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hf : f ^ p ^ n = 1) : Fintype.card α ≡ Fintype.card f.fixedPoints [MOD p]

name: _root_.exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card
informal: For every prime `p` dividing the order of a finite group `G` there exists an element of order `p` in `G`. This is known as Cauchy's theorem.
signature: {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hdvd : p ∣ Fintype.card G) : ∃ x : G, orderOf x = p

name: Finset.univ_perm_fin_succ
informal: The set of all permutations of `Fin (n + 1)` can be constructed by augmenting the set of permutations of `Fin n` by each element of `Fin (n + 1)` in turn.
signature: {n : ℕ} : @Finset.univ (Perm <| Fin n.succ) _ = (Finset.univ : Finset <| Fin n.succ × Perm (Fin n)).map Equiv.Perm.decomposeFin.symm.toEmbedding

name: Finset.univ_perm_option
informal: The set of all permutations of `Option α` can be constructed by augmenting the set of permutations of `α` by each element of `Option α` in turn.
signature: {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [Fintype α] : @Finset.univ (Perm <| Option α) _ = (Finset.univ : Finset <| Option α × Perm α).map Equiv.Perm.decomposeOption.symm.toEmbedding

name: mclosure_swap_castSucc_succ
informal: Every finite symmetric group is generated by transpositions of adjacent elements.
signature: (n : ℕ) : Submonoid.closure (Set.range fun i : Fin n ↦ swap i.castSucc i.succ) = ⊤

name: card_commutator_le_of_finite_commutatorSet
informal: A theorem of Schur: The size of the commutator subgroup is bounded in terms of the number of commutators.
signature: [Finite (commutatorSet G)] : Nat.card (_root_.commutator G) ≤ cardCommutatorBound (Nat.card (commutatorSet G))

name: isThreeCycle_sq_of_three_mem_cycleType_five
informal: Part of proving $A_5$ is simple. Shows that the square of any element of $A_5$ with a 3-cycle in its cycle decomposition is a 3-cycle, so the normal closure of the original element must be $A_5$.
signature: {g : Perm (Fin 5)} (h : 3 ∈ cycleType g) : IsThreeCycle (g * g)

name: LinearOrderedAddCommGroup.isAddCyclic_iff_nonempty_equiv_int
informal: A linearly-ordered additive abelian group is cyclic iff it is isomorphic to `ℤ` as an ordered additive monoid.
signature: {A : Type*} [AddCommGroup A] [LinearOrder A] [IsOrderedAddMonoid A] [Nontrivial A] : IsAddCyclic A ↔ Nonempty (A ≃+o ℤ)

name: LinearOrderedCommGroup.isCyclic_iff_nonempty_equiv_int
informal: A linearly-ordered abelian group is cyclic iff it is isomorphic to `Multiplicative ℤ` as an ordered monoid.
signature: {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] [LinearOrder G] [IsOrderedMonoid G] [Nontrivial G] : IsCyclic G ↔ Nonempty (G ≃*o Multiplicative ℤ)

name: card_commute_odd
informal: If n is odd, then the Dihedral group of order $2n$ has $n(n+3)$ pairs of commuting elements.
signature: (hn : Odd n) : Nat.card { p : DihedralGroup n × DihedralGroup n // Commute p.1 p.2 } = n * (n + 3)

name: card_sylow_modEq_one
informal: A generalization of **Sylow's third theorem**. If the number of Sylow `p`-subgroups is finite, then it is congruent to `1` modulo `p`.
signature: [Fact p.Prime] [Finite (Sylow p G)] : Nat.card (Sylow p G) ≡ 1 [MOD p]

name: klDiv_eq_zero_iff
informal: **Converse Gibbs' inequality**: the Kullback-Leibler divergence between two finite measures is zero if and only if the two measures are equal.
signature: [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] : klDiv μ ν = 0 ↔ μ = ν

name: ext_linear
informal: Two affine maps are equal if they have equal linear maps and are equal at some point.
signature: {f g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2} (h₁ : f.linear = g.linear) {p : P1} (h₂ : f p = g p) : f = g

name: ext_linear_iff
informal: Two affine maps are equal if they have equal linear maps and are equal at some point.
signature: {f g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2} : f = g ↔ (f.linear = g.linear) ∧ (∃ p, f p = g p)

name: comp_apply
informal: Composition of affine maps acts as applying the two functions.
signature: (f : P2 →ᵃ[k] P3) (g : P1 →ᵃ[k] P2) (p : P1) : f.comp g p = f (g p)

name: decomp
informal: Decomposition of an affine map in the special case when the point space and vector space are the same.
signature: (f : V1 →ᵃ[k] V2) : (f : V1 → V2) = ⇑f.linear + fun _ => f 0

name: decomp'
informal: Decomposition of an affine map in the special case when the point space and vector space are the same.
signature: (f : V1 →ᵃ[k] V2) : (f.linear : V1 → V2) = ⇑f - fun _ => f 0

name: pi_ext_zero
informal: Two affine maps from a Pi-type of modules `(i : ι) → φv i` are equal if they are equal in their operation on `Pi.single` and at zero. Analogous to `LinearMap.pi_ext`. See also `pi_ext_nonempty`, which instead of agreement at zero requires `Nonempty ι`.
signature: (h : ∀ i x, f (Pi.single i x) = g (Pi.single i x)) (h₂ : f 0 = g 0) : f = g

name: vectorSpan_eq_span_vsub_finset_right_ne
informal: The `vectorSpan` is the span of the pairwise subtractions with a given point on the right, excluding the subtraction of that point from itself.
signature: [DecidableEq P] [DecidableEq V] {s : Finset P} {p : P} (hp : p ∈ s) : vectorSpan k (s : Set P) = Submodule.span k ((s.erase p).image (· -ᵥ p))

name: linear_eqOn_vectorSpan
informal: If two affine maps agree on a set, their linear parts agree on the vector span of that set.
signature: {V₂ P₂ : Type*} [AddCommGroup V₂] [Module k V₂] [AddTorsor V₂ P₂] {s : Set P₁} {f g : P₁ →ᵃ[k] P₂} (h_agree : s.EqOn f g) : Set.EqOn f.linear g.linear (vectorSpan k s)

name: eqOn_affineSpan
informal: Two affine maps which agree on a set, agree on its affine span.
signature: {V₂ P₂ : Type*} [AddCommGroup V₂] [Module k V₂] [AddTorsor V₂ P₂] {s : Set P₁} {f g : P₁ →ᵃ[k] P₂} (h_agree : s.EqOn f g) : Set.EqOn f g (affineSpan k s)

name: ext_on
informal: If two affine maps agree on a set that spans the entire space, then they are equal.
signature: {V₂ P₂ : Type*} [AddCommGroup V₂] [Module k V₂] [AddTorsor V₂ P₂] {s : Set P₁} {f g : P₁ →ᵃ[k] P₂} (h_span : affineSpan k s = ⊤) (h_agree : s.EqOn f g) : f = g

name: ext_on
informal: If two affine equivalences agree on a set that spans the entire space, then they are equal.
signature: {V₂ P₂ : Type*} [AddCommGroup V₂] [Module k V₂] [AddTorsor V₂ P₂] {s : Set P₁} (h_span : affineSpan k s = ⊤) (T₁ T₂ : P₁ ≃ᵃ[k] P₂) (h_agree : s.EqOn T₁ T₂) : T₁ = T₂

name: closedInterior_inter_shift_zero
informal: The base of a simplex shifted with parameter 0 intersects the closed interior only at the vertex.
signature: [ZeroLEOneClass k] : s.closedInterior ∩ (affineSpan k <| s.points '' {i}ᶜ).shift (s.points i) 0 = {s.points i}

name: disjoint_closedInterior_shift
informal: The base of a simplex shifted with parameter outside $[0, 1]$ does not intersect the closed interior.
signature: {x : k} (hx : x < 0 ∨ 1 < x) : Disjoint s.closedInterior <| (affineSpan k (s.points '' {i}ᶜ)).shift (s.points i) x

name: sum_centroidWeights_eq_one_of_cast_card_ne_zero
informal: The weights in the centroid sum to 1, if the number of points, converted to `k`, is not zero.
signature: (h : (#s : k) ≠ 0) : ∑ i ∈ s, s.centroidWeights k i = 1

name: sum_centroidWeights_eq_one_of_card_ne_zero
informal: In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid sum to 1 if the number of points is not zero.
signature: [CharZero k] (h : #s ≠ 0) : ∑ i ∈ s, s.centroidWeights k i = 1

name: sum_centroidWeights_eq_one_of_nonempty
informal: In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid sum to 1 if the set is nonempty.
signature: [CharZero k] (h : s.Nonempty) : ∑ i ∈ s, s.centroidWeights k i = 1

name: sum_centroidWeights_eq_one_of_card_eq_add_one
informal: In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid sum to 1 if the number of points is `n + 1`.
signature: [CharZero k] {n : ℕ} (h : #s = n + 1) : ∑ i ∈ s, s.centroidWeights k i = 1

name: sum_centroidWeightsIndicator
informal: The sum of the weights for the centroid indexed by a `Fintype`.
signature: [Fintype ι] : ∑ i, s.centroidWeightsIndicator k i = ∑ i ∈ s, s.centroidWeights k i

name: sum_centroidWeightsIndicator_eq_one_of_card_ne_zero
informal: In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid indexed by a `Fintype` sum to 1 if the number of points is not zero.
signature: [CharZero k] [Fintype ι] (h : #s ≠ 0) : ∑ i, s.centroidWeightsIndicator k i = 1

name: sum_centroidWeightsIndicator_eq_one_of_nonempty
informal: In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid indexed by a `Fintype` sum to 1 if the set is nonempty.
signature: [CharZero k] [Fintype ι] (h : s.Nonempty) : ∑ i, s.centroidWeightsIndicator k i = 1

name: sum_centroidWeightsIndicator_eq_one_of_card_eq_add_one
informal: In the characteristic zero case, the weights in the centroid indexed by a `Fintype` sum to 1 if the number of points is `n + 1`.
signature: [CharZero k] [Fintype ι] {n : ℕ} (h : #s = n + 1) : ∑ i, s.centroidWeightsIndicator k i = 1

name: map_le_lineMap_iff_slope_le_slope_left
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `a < c`, the point `(c, f c)` is non-strictly below the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f a c ≤ slope f a b`.
signature: (h : 0 < r * (b - a)) : f c ≤ lineMap (f a) (f b) r ↔ slope f a c ≤ slope f a b

name: lineMap_le_map_iff_slope_le_slope_left
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `a < c`, the point `(c, f c)` is non-strictly above the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f a b ≤ slope f a c`.
signature: (h : 0 < r * (b - a)) : lineMap (f a) (f b) r ≤ f c ↔ slope f a b ≤ slope f a c

name: map_lt_lineMap_iff_slope_lt_slope_left
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `a < c`, the point `(c, f c)` is strictly below the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f a c < slope f a b`.
signature: (h : 0 < r * (b - a)) : f c < lineMap (f a) (f b) r ↔ slope f a c < slope f a b

name: lineMap_lt_map_iff_slope_lt_slope_left
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `a < c`, the point `(c, f c)` is strictly above the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f a b < slope f a c`.
signature: (h : 0 < r * (b - a)) : lineMap (f a) (f b) r < f c ↔ slope f a b < slope f a c

name: map_le_lineMap_iff_slope_le_slope_right
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `c < b`, the point `(c, f c)` is non-strictly below the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f a b ≤ slope f c b`.
signature: (h : 0 < (1 - r) * (b - a)) : f c ≤ lineMap (f a) (f b) r ↔ slope f a b ≤ slope f c b

name: lineMap_le_map_iff_slope_le_slope_right
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `c < b`, the point `(c, f c)` is non-strictly above the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f c b ≤ slope f a b`.
signature: (h : 0 < (1 - r) * (b - a)) : lineMap (f a) (f b) r ≤ f c ↔ slope f c b ≤ slope f a b

name: map_lt_lineMap_iff_slope_lt_slope_right
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `c < b`, the point `(c, f c)` is strictly below the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f a b < slope f c b`.
signature: (h : 0 < (1 - r) * (b - a)) : f c < lineMap (f a) (f b) r ↔ slope f a b < slope f c b

name: lineMap_lt_map_iff_slope_lt_slope_right
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `c < b`, the point `(c, f c)` is strictly above the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f c b < slope f a b`.
signature: (h : 0 < (1 - r) * (b - a)) : lineMap (f a) (f b) r < f c ↔ slope f c b < slope f a b

name: map_le_lineMap_iff_slope_le_slope
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `a < c < b`, the point `(c, f c)` is non-strictly below the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f a c ≤ slope f c b`.
signature: (hab : a < b) (h₀ : 0 < r) (h₁ : r < 1) : f c ≤ lineMap (f a) (f b) r ↔ slope f a c ≤ slope f c b

name: lineMap_le_map_iff_slope_le_slope
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `a < c < b`, the point `(c, f c)` is non-strictly above the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f c b ≤ slope f a c`.
signature: (hab : a < b) (h₀ : 0 < r) (h₁ : r < 1) : lineMap (f a) (f b) r ≤ f c ↔ slope f c b ≤ slope f a c

name: map_lt_lineMap_iff_slope_lt_slope
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `a < c < b`, the point `(c, f c)` is strictly below the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f a c < slope f c b`.
signature: (hab : a < b) (h₀ : 0 < r) (h₁ : r < 1) : f c < lineMap (f a) (f b) r ↔ slope f a c < slope f c b

name: lineMap_lt_map_iff_slope_lt_slope
informal: Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `a < c < b`, the point `(c, f c)` is strictly above the segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f c b < slope f a c`.
signature: (hab : a < b) (h₀ : 0 < r) (h₁ : r < 1) : lineMap (f a) (f b) r < f c ↔ slope f c b < slope f a c

name: MultilinearMap.domCoprod_alternization
informal: Computing the `MultilinearMap.alternatization` of the `MultilinearMap.domCoprod` is the same as computing the `AlternatingMap.domCoprod` of the `MultilinearMap.alternatization`s.
signature: [DecidableEq ιa] [DecidableEq ιb] (a : MultilinearMap R' (fun _ : ιa => Mᵢ) N₁) (b : MultilinearMap R' (fun _ : ιb => Mᵢ) N₂) : MultilinearMap.alternatization (MultilinearMap.domCoprod a b) = a.alternatization.domCoprod (MultilinearMap.alternatization b)

name: mk_coord_apply
informal: Given a basis, the `i`th element of the dual basis evaluates to the Kronecker delta on the `j`th element of the basis.
signature: [DecidableEq ι] {i j : ι} : (Basis.mk hli hsp).coord i (v j) = if j = i then 1 else 0

name: sum_repr_mul_repr_mul
informal: Write out `B x y` as a sum over `B (b i) (b j)` if `b` is a basis. Version for bilinear maps, see `sum_repr_mul_repr_mulₛₗ` for the semi-bilinear version.
signature: {B : Mₗ →ₗ[Rₗ] Nₗ →ₗ[Rₗ] Pₗ} (x y) : ((b₁'.repr x).sum fun i xi => (b₂'.repr y).sum fun j yj => xi • yj • B (b₁' i) (b₂' j)) = B x y

name: commute_transvections_iff_of_basis
informal: A linear endomorphism of a free module of rank at least 2 that commutes with transvections consists of homotheties with central ratio.
signature: [Ring R] [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V] {ι : Type*} [Nontrivial ι] (b : Basis ι R V) {f : V →ₗ[R] V} (hcomm : ∀ i j (r : R) (_ : i ≠ j), Commute f (transvection (b.coord i) (r • b j))) : ∃ a : Subring.center R, f = a • 1

name: exists_eq_smul_id_of_forall_notLinearIndependent
informal: Over a commutative domain, an endomorphism `f` of a free module `V` such that `f v` and `v` are collinear, for all `v : V`, consists of homotheties.
signature: [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V] [Free R V] {f : V →ₗ[R] V} (h : ∀ v, ¬ LinearIndependent R ![v, f v]) : ∃ a : R, f = a • 1

name: real_algHom_eq_id_or_conj
informal: The identity and the complex conjugation are the only two `ℝ`-algebra homomorphisms of `ℂ`.
signature: (f : ℂ →ₐ[ℝ] ℂ) : f = AlgHom.id ℝ ℂ ∨ f = conjAe

name: iSupIndep.linearIndependent
informal: If a family of submodules is independent, then a choice of nonzero vector from each submodule forms a linearly independent family. See also `iSupIndep.linearIndependent'`.
signature: [IsDomain R] [IsTorsionFree R N] {ι : Type*} (p : ι → Submodule R N) (hp : iSupIndep p) {v : ι → N} (hv : ∀ i, v i ∈ p i) (hv' : ∀ i, v i ≠ 0) : LinearIndependent R v

name: bot_lt_ker_of_det_eq_zero
informal: If the determinant of a map vanishes, then the map is not injective.
signature: [IsDomain R] [Free R M] {f : M →ₗ[R] M} (hf : f.det = 0) : ⊥ < ker f

name: det_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot
informal: The determinant of a map vanishes iff the map is not injective.
signature: [IsDomain R] [Free R M] [Module.Finite R M] {f : M →ₗ[R] M} : f.det = 0 ↔ ker f ≠ ⊥

name: range_lt_top_of_det_eq_zero
informal: If the determinant of a map vanishes, then the map is not onto.
signature: [IsDomain R] [Free R M] {f : M →ₗ[R] M} (hf : f.det = 0) : range f < ⊤

name: _root_.LinearMap.det_dualMap
informal: The determinant of the transpose of an endomorphism coincides with its determinant.
signature: [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M] (f : M →ₗ[R] M) : f.dualMap.det = f.det

name: Submodule.finrank_quotient_le
informal: The dimension of a quotient is bounded by the dimension of the ambient space.
signature: [StrongRankCondition R] [Module.Finite R M] (s : Submodule R M) : finrank R (M ⧸ s) ≤ finrank R M

name: Submodule.finrank_le
informal: The dimension of a submodule is bounded by the dimension of the ambient space.
signature: [Module.Finite R M] (s : Submodule R M) : finrank R s ≤ finrank R M

name: Module.finrank_pos_iff_exists_ne_zero
informal: A finite rank torsion-free module has positive `finrank` iff it has a nonzero element.
signature: [IsDomain R] [IsTorsionFree R M] : 0 < finrank R M ↔ ∃ x : M, x ≠ 0

name: Module.finrank_pos_iff
informal: An `R`-finite torsion-free module has positive `finrank` iff it is nontrivial.
signature: [IsDomain R] [IsTorsionFree R M] : 0 < finrank R M ↔ Nontrivial M

name: FiniteDimensional.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_finrank_eq
informal: Two finite and free modules are isomorphic if they have the same (finite) rank.
signature: [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R M'] (cond : finrank R M = finrank R M') : Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] M')

name: FiniteDimensional.nonempty_linearEquiv_iff_finrank_eq
informal: Two finite and free modules are isomorphic if and only if they have the same (finite) rank.
signature: [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R M'] : Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] M') ↔ finrank R M = finrank R M'

name: finrank_top_le_finrank_of_isScalarTower_of_free
informal: Also see `Module.finrank_top_le_finrank_of_isScalarTower` for a version with different typeclass constraints.
signature: [Semiring S] [StrongRankCondition S] [Module S M] [Module R S] [FaithfulSMul R S] [Module.Finite R S] [IsScalarTower R S S] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.Free S M] : finrank S M ≤ finrank R M

name: rank_le_one_iff
informal: A vector space has dimension at most `1` if and only if there is a single vector of which all vectors are multiples.
signature: [Module.Free K V] : Module.rank K V ≤ 1 ↔ ∃ v₀ : V, ∀ v, ∃ r : K, r • v₀ = v

name: rank_eq_one_iff
informal: A vector space has dimension `1` if and only if there is a single non-zero vector of which all vectors are multiples.
signature: [Module.Free K V] : Module.rank K V = 1 ↔ ∃ v₀ : V, v₀ ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ v, ∃ r : K, r • v₀ = v

name: finrank_eq_one_iff
informal: A module has dimension 1 iff there is some `v : V` so `{v}` is a basis. See also `Module.Basis.nonempty_unique_index_of_finrank_eq_one`
signature: [Module.Free K V] (ι : Type*) [Unique ι] : finrank K V = 1 ↔ Nonempty (Basis ι K V)

name: finrank_eq_one_iff'
informal: A module has dimension 1 iff there is some nonzero `v : V` so every vector is a multiple of `v`.
signature: [Module.Free K V] : finrank K V = 1 ↔ ∃ v ≠ 0, ∀ w : V, ∃ c : K, c • v = w

name: finrank_le_one_iff
informal: A finite-dimensional module has dimension at most 1 iff there is some `v : V` so every vector is a multiple of `v`.
signature: [Module.Free K V] [Module.Finite K V] : finrank K V ≤ 1 ↔ ∃ v : V, ∀ w : V, ∃ c : K, c • v = w

name: exists_linearIndependent_pair_of_one_lt_rank
informal: Given a nonzero vector in a space of dimension `> 1`, one may find another vector linearly independent of the first one.
signature: [IsDomain R] [StrongRankCondition R] [IsTorsionFree R M] (h : 1 < Module.rank R M) {x : M} (hx : x ≠ 0) : ∃ y, LinearIndependent R ![x, y]

name: exists_linearIndependent_pair_of_one_lt_finrank
informal: Given a nonzero vector in a finite-dimensional space of dimension `> 1`, one may find another vector linearly independent of the first one.
signature: [IsDomain R] [Module.IsTorsionFree R M] (h : 1 < finrank R M) {x : M} (hx : x ≠ 0) : ∃ y, LinearIndependent R ![x, y]

name: Basis.card_le_card_of_linearIndependent_aux
informal: Let `R` satisfy the strong rank condition. If `m` elements of a free rank `n` `R`-module are linearly independent, then `m ≤ n`.
signature: {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [StrongRankCondition R] (n : ℕ) {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → Fin n → R) : LinearIndependent R v → m ≤ n

name: mk_finrank_eq_card_basis
informal: If a free module is of finite rank, then the cardinality of any basis is equal to its `finrank`.
signature: [Module.Finite R M] {ι : Type w} (h : Basis ι R M) : (finrank R M : Cardinal.{w}) = #ι

name: Module.finrank_top_le_finrank_of_isScalarTower
informal: Also see `Module.finrank_top_le_finrank_of_isScalarTower_of_free` for a version with different typeclass constraints.
signature: [Module.Finite R M] [Semiring S] [Module S M] [Module R S] [IsScalarTower R S S] [FaithfulSMul R S] [IsScalarTower R S M] : finrank S M ≤ finrank R M

name: finrank_quotient_torsion_eq
informal: Quotienting an additive commutative group by its torsion subgroup does not change its `ℤ`-`finrank`.
signature: {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] : Module.finrank ℤ (M ⧸ (AddCommGroup.torsion M).toIntSubmodule) = Module.finrank ℤ M

name: Basis.linearEquiv_dual_iff_finiteDimensional
informal: A vector space over a field is isomorphic to its dual if and only if it is finite-dimensional: a consequence of the Erdős-Kaplansky theorem.
signature: [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] : Nonempty (V ≃ₗ[K] Dual K V) ↔ FiniteDimensional K V

name: finite_dual_iff
informal: For an example of a non-free projective `K`-module `V` for which the forward implication fails, see https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05WG#comment-9913.
signature: [Free K V] : Module.Finite K (Dual K V) ↔ Module.Finite K V

name: span_eq_top_of_ne_zero
informal: Consider a reflexive module and a set `s` of linear forms. If for any `z ≠ 0` there exists `f ∈ s` such that `f z ≠ 0`, then `s` spans the whole dual space.
signature: [IsReflexive R M] {s : Set (M →ₗ[R] R)} [Projective R ((M →ₗ[R] R) ⧸ (span R s))] (h : ∀ z ≠ 0, ∃ f ∈ s, f z ≠ 0) : span R s = ⊤

name: eigenspaces_iSupIndep
informal: The eigenspaces of a linear operator form an independent family of subspaces of `M`. That is, any eigenspace has trivial intersection with the span of all the other eigenspaces.
signature: [IsDomain R] [IsTorsionFree R M] (f : End R M) : iSupIndep f.eigenspace

name: exists_eigenvalue
informal: In finite dimensions, over an algebraically closed field, every linear endomorphism has an eigenvalue.
signature: [IsAlgClosed K] [FiniteDimensional K V] [Nontrivial V] (f : End K V) : ∃ c : K, f.HasEigenvalue c

name: _root_.Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq
informal: If a submodule has maximal dimension in a finite-dimensional space, then it is equal to the whole space.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K V] {S : Submodule K V} (h : finrank K S = finrank K V) : S = ⊤

name: exists_relation_sum_zero_pos_coefficient_of_finrank_succ_lt_card
informal: A slight strengthening of `exists_nontrivial_relation_sum_zero_of_rank_succ_lt_card` available when working over an ordered field: we can ensure a positive coefficient, not just a nonzero coefficient.
signature: [FiniteDimensional L W] {t : Finset W} (h : finrank L W + 1 < t.card) : ∃ f : W → L, ∑ e ∈ t, f e • e = 0 ∧ ∑ e ∈ t, f e = 0 ∧ ∃ x ∈ t, 0 < f x

name: finiteDimensional_of_surjective
informal: The image under an onto linear map of a finite-dimensional space is also finite-dimensional.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K V] (f : V →ₗ[K] V₂) (hf : LinearMap.range f = ⊤) : FiniteDimensional K V₂

name: injective_iff_surjective
informal: On a finite-dimensional space, a linear map is injective if and only if it is surjective.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K V] {f : V →ₗ[K] V} : Injective f ↔ Surjective f

name: finrank_eq_rank'
informal: In a finite-dimensional space, its dimension (seen as a cardinal) coincides with its `finrank`. This is a copy of `finrank_eq_rank _ _` which creates easier typeclass searches.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K V] : (finrank K V : Cardinal.{v}) = Module.rank K V

name: finrank_eq_card_basis'
informal: If a vector space is finite-dimensional, then the cardinality of any basis is equal to its `finrank`.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K V] {ι : Type w} (h : Basis ι K V) : (finrank K V : Cardinal.{w}) = #ι

name: finrank_lt
informal: The dimension of a strict submodule is strictly bounded by the dimension of the ambient space. See also `Submodule.length_lt`.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K V] {s : Submodule K V} (h : s ≠ ⊤) : finrank K s < finrank K V

name: finrank_range_add_finrank_ker
informal: rank-nullity theorem : the dimensions of the kernel and the range of a linear map add up to the dimension of the source space.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K V] (f : V →ₗ[K] V₂) : finrank K (LinearMap.range f) + finrank K (LinearMap.ker f) = finrank K V

name: LinearEquiv.isOfFinOrder_of_finite_of_span_eq_top_of_mapsTo
informal: A linear equivalence which preserves a finite spanning set must have finite order.
signature: {R M : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] {Φ : Set M} (hΦ₁ : Φ.Finite) (hΦ₂ : span R Φ = ⊤) {e : M ≃ₗ[R] M} (he : MapsTo e Φ Φ) : IsOfFinOrder e

name: linearCombination_id_surjective
informal: Any module is a quotient of a free module. This is stated as surjectivity of `Finsupp.linearCombination R id : (M →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M`.
signature: (M) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] : Function.Surjective (linearCombination R (id : M → M))

name: finiteQuotientOfFreeOfRankEq
informal: A submodule of full rank of a free finite `ℤ`-module has a finite quotient. It can't be an instance because of the side condition `Module.finrank ℤ N = Module.finrank ℤ M`.
signature: [Module.Free ℤ M] [Module.Finite ℤ M] (N : Submodule ℤ M) (h : Module.finrank ℤ N = Module.finrank ℤ M) : Finite (M ⧸ N)

name: finiteQuotientOfFreeOfNeBot
informal: A nonzero ideal over a free finite extension of `ℤ` has a finite quotient. It can't be an instance because of the side condition `I ≠ ⊥`.
signature: [Module.Free ℤ S] [Module.Finite ℤ S] (I : Ideal S) (hI : I ≠ ⊥) : Finite (S ⧸ I)

name: exists_isNilpotent_isSemisimple
informal: **Jordan-Chevalley-Dunford decomposition**: an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space over a perfect field may be written as a sum of nilpotent and semisimple endomorphisms. Moreover these nilpotent and semisimple components are polynomial expressions in the original endomorphism.
signature: [PerfectField K] : ∃ᵉ (n ∈ adjoin K {f}) (s ∈ adjoin K {f}), IsNilpotent n ∧ IsSemisimple s ∧ f = n + s

name: eq_of_degree_le_of_eval_finset_eq
informal: Two polynomials, with the same degree and leading coefficient, which have the same evaluation on a set of distinct values with cardinality equal to the degree, are equal.
signature: (h_deg_le : f.degree ≤ #s) (h_deg_eq : f.degree = g.degree) (hlc : f.leadingCoeff = g.leadingCoeff) (h_eval : ∀ x ∈ s, f.eval x = g.eval x) : f = g

name: eval_interpolate_not_at_node
informal: This is the first barycentric form of the Lagrange interpolant.
signature: (hx : ∀ i ∈ s, x ≠ v i) : eval x (interpolate s v r) = eval x (nodal s v) * ∑ i ∈ s, nodalWeight s v i * (x - v i)⁻¹ * r i

name: eval_interpolate_not_at_node'
informal: This is the second barycentric form of the Lagrange interpolant.
signature: (hvs : Set.InjOn v s) (hs : s.Nonempty) (hx : ∀ i ∈ s, x ≠ v i) : eval x (interpolate s v r) = (∑ i ∈ s, nodalWeight s v i * (x - v i)⁻¹ * r i) / ∑ i ∈ s, nodalWeight s v i * (x - v i)⁻¹

name: LinearIndependent.update
informal: A linearly independent family of vectors `f` remains linearly independent when we substitute one of the terms with a vector `m` provided there exists a non-zero divisor `r`, such that `r • m` belongs to the span of `f` with non-zero-divisor coefficients.
signature: [DecidableEq ι] [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {f : ι → M} (hf : LinearIndependent R f) (i : ι) (m : M) (hg : ∃ r ∈ nonZeroDivisors R, ∃ l : ι →₀ R, l i ∈ nonZeroDivisors R ∧ r • m = linearCombination R f l) : LinearIndependent R (Function.update f i m)

name: BlockTriangular.inv_toBlock
informal: The inverse of an upper-left subblock of a block-triangular matrix `M` is the upper-left subblock of `M⁻¹`.
signature: [LinearOrder α] [Invertible M] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) (k : α) : (M.toBlock (fun i => b i < k) fun i => b i < k)⁻¹ = M⁻¹.toBlock (fun i => b i < k) fun i => b i < k

name: toBlock_inverse_eq_zero
informal: A lower-left subblock of the inverse of a block-triangular matrix is zero. This is a first step towards `BlockTriangular.inv_toBlock` below.
signature: [LinearOrder α] [Invertible M] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) (k : α) : (M⁻¹.toBlock (fun i => k ≤ b i) fun i => b i < k) = 0

name: circulant_mul
informal: The product of two circulant matrices `circulant v` and `circulant w` is the circulant matrix generated by `circulant v *ᵥ w`.
signature: [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring α] [Fintype n] [AddGroup n] (v w : n → α) : circulant v * circulant w = circulant (circulant v *ᵥ w)

name: reps_entries_le_m'
informal: An auxiliary result bounding the size of the entries of the representatives in `reps`
signature: {A : Δ m} (h : A ∈ reps m) (i j : Fin 2) : A.1 i j ∈ Finset.Icc (-|m|) |m|

name: IsHadamard.four_dvd_card
informal: An integer Hadamard matrix of order greater than two has order divisible by four. This is the standard divisibility obstruction in [Section 2.3][deLauneyFlannery2011].
signature: {A : Matrix n n ℤ} (hA : A.IsHadamard) (hcard : 2 < Fintype.card n) : 4 ∣ Fintype.card n

name: isHermitian_diagonal
informal: A diagonal matrix is Hermitian if the entries have the trivial `star` operation (such as on the reals).
signature: [TrivialStar α] [DecidableEq n] (v : n → α) : (diagonal v).IsHermitian

name: invOf_add_mul_mul
informal: The **Woodbury Identity** (`⅟` version). See `Matrix.invOf_add_mul_mul'` for the Binomial Inverse Theorem.
signature: [Invertible (A + U * C * V)] : ⅟(A + U * C * V) = ⅟A - ⅟A * U * ⅟(⅟C + V * ⅟A * U) * V * ⅟A

name: invOf_add_mul_mul'
informal: The **Binomial Inverse Theorem** (`⅟` version). See `Matrix.invOf_add_mul_mul` for the Woodbury identity.
signature: [Invertible (A + U * C * V)] : ⅟(A + U * C * V) = ⅟A - ⅟A * U * C * ⅟(C + C * V * ⅟A * U * C) * C * V * ⅟A

name: eval_det_mvPolynomialX
informal: Evaluating the generic determinant polynomial `det (mvPolynomialX m m R)` at a point `s` gives the determinant of the matrix obtained by substituting `s`.
signature: [DecidableEq m] [Fintype m] [CommRing R] (s : m × m → R) : MvPolynomial.eval s (det (mvPolynomialX m m R)) = det (Matrix.of fun i j : m => s (i, j))

name: posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self
informal: The conjugate transpose of a matrix multiplied by the matrix is positive semidefinite
signature: [StarOrderedRing R] (A : Matrix m n R) : PosSemidef (Aᴴ * A)

name: rank_submatrix_le
informal: Taking a subset of the rows and columns reduces the rank.
signature: [CommSemiring R] [StrongRankCondition R] [Fintype n₀] (A : Matrix m n R) (r : m₀ → m) (c : n₀ → n) : (A.submatrix r c).rank ≤ A.rank

name: rank_le_card_of_support_subset
informal: The rank of a matrix is at most the size of any finset containing all its nonzero rows.
signature: [CommSemiring R] [StrongRankCondition R] (A : Matrix m n R) (s : Finset m) (hz : Function.support A.row ⊆ s) : A.rank ≤ s.card

name: rank_eq_finrank_span_cols
informal: The rank of a matrix is the rank of the space spanned by its columns.
signature: [CommSemiring R] (A : Matrix m n R) : A.rank = finrank R (Submodule.span R (Set.range A.col))

name: rank_diagonal
informal: The rank of a diagonal matrix is the count of non-zero elements on its main diagonal
signature: [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq R] (w : m → R) : (diagonal w).rank = Fintype.card {i // (w i) ≠ 0}

name: rank_eq_finrank_span_row
informal: The rank of a matrix is the rank of the space spanned by its rows.
signature: [Field R] [Finite m] (A : Matrix m n R) : A.rank = finrank R (Submodule.span R (Set.range A.row))

name: Matrix.WithConv.IsIdempotentElem.isSelfAdjoint
informal: All matrices are intrinsically self-adjoint if they are convolutively idempotent.
signature: [Semiring α] [IsLeftCancelMulZero α] [StarRing α] {f : WithConv (Matrix m n α)} (hf : IsIdempotentElem f) : IsSelfAdjoint f

name: map_add_univ
informal: Additivity of a multilinear map along all coordinates at the same time, writing `f (m + m')` as the sum of `f (s.piecewise m m')` over all sets `s`.
signature: [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] (m m' : ∀ i, M₁ i) : f (m + m') = ∑ s : Finset ι, f (s.piecewise m m')

name: map_sum
informal: If `f` is multilinear, then `f (Σ_{j₁} g₁ j₁, ..., Σ_{jₙ} gₙ jₙ)` is the sum of `f (g₁ (r 1), ..., gₙ (r n))` where `r` ranges over all functions `r`. This follows from multilinearity by expanding successively with respect to each coordinate.
signature: [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] [∀ i, Fintype (α i)] : (f fun i => ∑ j, g i j) = ∑ r : ∀ i, α i, f fun i => g i (r i)

name: map_piecewise_sub_map_piecewise
informal: This calculates the differences between the values of a multilinear map at two arguments that differ on a finset `s` of `ι`. It requires a linear order on `ι` in order to express the result.
signature: [LinearOrder ι] (a b v : (i : ι) → M₁ i) (s : Finset ι) : f (s.piecewise a v) - f (s.piecewise b v) = ∑ i ∈ s, f fun j ↦ if j ∈ s then if j < i then a j else if j = i then a j - b j else b j else v j

name: map_add_sub_map_add_sub_linearDeriv
informal: This expresses the difference between the values of a multilinear map at two points "close to `x`" in terms of the "derivative" of the multilinear map at `x` and of "second-order" terms.
signature: [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] (x h h' : (i : ι) → M₁ i) : f (x + h) - f (x + h') - f.linearDeriv x (h - h') = ∑ s with 2 ≤ #s, (f (s.piecewise h x) - f (s.piecewise h' x))

name: IsPerfPair.of_injective
informal: If the coefficients are a field, and one of the spaces is finite-dimensional, it is sufficient to check only injectivity instead of bijectivity of the bilinear pairing.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K M] (h : Injective p) (h' : Injective p.flip) : p.IsPerfPair where bijective_left

name: IsPerfPair.of_injective'
informal: If the coefficients are a field, and one of the spaces is finite-dimensional, it is sufficient to check only injectivity instead of bijectivity of the bilinear pairing.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K N] (h : Injective p) (h' : Injective p.flip) : p.IsPerfPair

name: card'
informal: Cardinality formula for the points of `ℙ k V` if `k` and `V` are finite with less natural subtraction.
signature: [Finite V] : Nat.card V = Nat.card (ℙ k V) * (Nat.card k - 1) + 1

name: eq_zero_of_sameRay_self_neg
informal: If a vector is in the same ray as its negation, that vector is zero.
signature: [IsDomain R] [IsTorsionFree R M] (h : SameRay R x (-x)) : x = 0

name: Dual.eq_of_preReflection_mapsTo'
informal: This rather technical-looking lemma exists because it is exactly what is needed to establish a uniqueness result for root data. See the doc string of `Module.Dual.eq_of_preReflection_mapsTo` for further remarks.
signature: [CharZero R] [IsDomain R] [IsTorsionFree R M] {x : M} {Φ : Set M} (hΦ₁ : Φ.Finite) (hx : x ∈ span R Φ) {f g : Dual R M} (hf₁ : f x = 2) (hf₂ : MapsTo (preReflection x f) Φ Φ) (hg₁ : g x = 2) (hg₂ : MapsTo (preReflection x g) Φ Φ) : (span R Φ).subtype.dualMap f = (span R Φ).subtype.dualMap g

name: induction_on_cartanMatrix
informal: A characterisation of the connectedness of the Dynkin diagram for irreducible root pairings.
signature: [P.IsReduced] [P.IsIrreducible] (p : b.support → Prop) {i j : b.support} (hi : p i) (hp : ∀ i j, p i → b.cartanMatrix j i ≠ 0 → p j) : p j

name: subsingleton_of_finrank_eq_one
informal: If a free module has `Module.finrank` equal to `1`, then its special linear group is trivial.
signature: [Module.Free R V] (d1 : Module.finrank R V = 1) : Subsingleton (SpecialLinearGroup R V) where allEq u v

name: kronecker_mem_unitary
informal: The kronecker product of two unitary matrices is unitary. This is stated for `unitary` instead of `unitaryGroup` as it holds even for non-commutative coefficients.
signature: {R m : Type*} [Semiring R] [StarRing R] [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] {U₁ : Matrix n n R} {U₂ : Matrix m m R} (hU₁ : U₁ ∈ unitary (Matrix n n R)) (hU₂ : U₂ ∈ unitary (Matrix m m R)) : U₁ ⊗ₖ U₂ ∈ unitary (Matrix (n × m) (n × m) R)

name: imp_forall_iff
informal: We intentionally restrict the type of `α` in this lemma so that this is a safer to use in simp than `forall_comm`.
signature: {α : Type*} {p : Prop} {q : α → Prop} : (p → ∀ x, q x) ↔ ∀ x, p → q x

name: Perm.coe_subsingleton

signature: {α : Type*} [Subsingleton α] (e : Perm α) : (e : α → α) = id

name: optionCongr_eq_equivFunctor_mapEquiv
informal: When `α` and `β` are in the same universe, this is the same as the result of `EquivFunctor.mapEquiv`.
signature: {α β : Type u} (e : α ≃ β) : optionCongr e = EquivFunctor.mapEquiv Option e

name: exists_fixed_point_of_surjective
informal: If `f : α → α → β` is surjective, then every endofunction on `β` has a fixed point. This is an instance of Lawvere's fixed-point theorem applied to the category of types and functions. It is the diagonal argument underlying `cantor_surjective` and `cantor_injective`.
signature: {α β : Type*} (f : α → α → β) (hf : Surjective f) (g : β → β) : ∃ x, g x = x

name: cantor_surjective
informal: **Cantor's diagonal argument** implies that there are no surjective functions from `α` to `Set α`.
signature: {α} (f : α → Set α) : ¬Surjective f

name: not_surjective_Type
informal: There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean.
signature: {α : Type u} (f : α → Type max u v) : ¬Surjective f

name: IsCompact.closure_subset_measurableSet
informal: If `K` is a compact set in an R₁ space and `s ⊇ K` is a Borel measurable superset, then `s` includes the closure of `K` as well.
signature: [R1Space γ] {K s : Set γ} (hK : IsCompact K) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hKs : K ⊆ s) : closure K ⊆ s

name: MeasurableEmbedding.borelSpace
informal: Given a measurable embedding to a Borel space which is also a topological embedding, then the source space is also a Borel space.
signature: {α β : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] [TopologicalSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β] [TopologicalSpace β] [hβ : BorelSpace β] {e : α → β} (h'e : MeasurableEmbedding e) (h''e : IsInducing e) : BorelSpace α

name: tendsto_measure_cthickening_of_isCompact
informal: Given a compact set in a proper space, the measure of its `r`-closed thickenings converges to its measure as `r` tends to `0`.
signature: [MetricSpace α] [MeasurableSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α] [ProperSpace α] {μ : Measure α} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ] {s : Set α} (hs : IsCompact s) : Tendsto (fun r => μ (Metric.cthickening r s)) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 (μ s))

name: exists_borelSpace_of_countablyGenerated_of_separatesPoints
informal: If a measurable space is countably generated and separates points, it arises as the Borel sets of some second countable t4 topology (i.e. a separable metrizable one).
signature: (α : Type*) [m : MeasurableSpace α] [CountablyGenerated α] [SeparatesPoints α] : ∃ _ : TopologicalSpace α, SecondCountableTopology α ∧ T4Space α ∧ BorelSpace α

name: exists_opensMeasurableSpace_of_countablySeparated
informal: If a measurable space on `α` is countably generated and separates points, there is some second countable t4 topology on `α` (i.e. a separable metrizable one) for which every open set is measurable.
signature: (α : Type*) [m : MeasurableSpace α] [CountablySeparated α] : ∃ _ : TopologicalSpace α, SecondCountableTopology α ∧ T4Space α ∧ OpensMeasurableSpace α

name: generateFrom_squareCylinders
informal: The square cylinders formed from measurable sets generate the product σ-algebra.
signature: [∀ i, MeasurableSpace (α i)] : MeasurableSpace.generateFrom (squareCylinders fun i ↦ {s : Set (α i) | MeasurableSet s}) = MeasurableSpace.pi

name: _root_.MeasurableSet.isClopenable
informal: Given a Borel-measurable set in a Polish space, there exists a finer Polish topology making it clopen. This is in fact an equivalence, see `isClopenable_iff_measurableSet`.
signature: [PolishSpace α] [MeasurableSpace α] [BorelSpace α] {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) : IsClopenable s

name: _root_.Measurable.exists_continuous
informal: Given a Borel-measurable function from a Polish space to a second-countable space, there exists a finer Polish topology on the source space for which the function is continuous.
signature: {α β : Type*} [t : TopologicalSpace α] [PolishSpace α] [MeasurableSpace α] [BorelSpace α] [tβ : TopologicalSpace β] [MeasurableSpace β] [OpensMeasurableSpace β] {f : α → β} [SecondCountableTopology (range f)] (hf : Measurable f) : ∃ t' : TopologicalSpace α, t' ≤ t ∧ @Continuous α β t' tβ f ∧ @PolishSpace α t'

name: _root_.MeasurableSet.analyticSet_image
informal: The image of a measurable set in a standard Borel space under a measurable map is an analytic set.
signature: {X Y : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] [StandardBorelSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [OpensMeasurableSpace Y] {f : X → Y} [SecondCountableTopology (range f)] {s : Set X} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf : Measurable f) : AnalyticSet (f '' s)

name: measurablySeparable_range_of_disjoint
informal: The hard part of the Lusin separation theorem saying that two disjoint analytic sets are contained in disjoint Borel sets (see the full statement in `AnalyticSet.measurablySeparable`). Here, we prove this when our analytic sets are the ranges of functions from `ℕ → ℕ`.
signature: [T2Space α] [MeasurableSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α] {f g : (ℕ → ℕ) → α} (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g) (h : Disjoint (range f) (range g)) : MeasurablySeparable (range f) (range g)

name: AnalyticSet.measurablySeparable
informal: The **Lusin separation theorem**: if two analytic sets are disjoint, then they are contained in disjoint Borel sets.
signature: [T2Space α] [MeasurableSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α] {s t : Set α} (hs : AnalyticSet s) (ht : AnalyticSet t) (h : Disjoint s t) : MeasurablySeparable s t

name: AnalyticSet.measurableSet_of_compl
informal: **Suslin's Theorem**: in a Hausdorff topological space, an analytic set with an analytic complement is measurable.
signature: [T2Space α] [MeasurableSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α] {s : Set α} (hs : AnalyticSet s) (hsc : AnalyticSet sᶜ) : MeasurableSet s

name: ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding
informal: If `s` is Borel-measurable in a Polish space and `f` is continuous injective on `s`, then the restriction of `f` to `s` is a measurable embedding.
signature: [BorelSpace β] [TopologicalSpace γ] [PolishSpace γ] [MeasurableSpace γ] [BorelSpace γ] (hs : MeasurableSet s) (f_cont : ContinuousOn f s) (f_inj : InjOn f s) : MeasurableEmbedding (s.domRestrict f)

name: MeasurableSet.image_of_monotoneOn
informal: The image of a measurable set under a monotone map is measurable.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology β] (ht : MeasurableSet t) (hg : MonotoneOn g t) : MeasurableSet (g '' t)

name: MeasurableSet.image_of_antitoneOn
informal: The image of a measurable set under an antitone map is measurable.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology β] (ht : MeasurableSet t) (hg : AntitoneOn g t) : MeasurableSet (g '' t)

name: _root_.Measurable.factorsThrough
informal: If a function `g` is measurable with respect to the pullback along some function `f`, then to prove `g x = g y` it is enough to prove `f x = f y`.
signature: [MeasurableSpace Z] [MeasurableSingletonClass Z] (hg : Measurable[mY.comap f] g) : g.FactorsThrough f

name: _root_.Measurable.dependsOn_of_piLE
informal: If a function is measurable with respect to the σ-algebra generated by the first coordinates, then it only depends on those first coordinates.
signature: [MeasurableSpace Z] [MeasurableSingletonClass Z] (hf : Measurable[piLE i] f) : DependsOn f (Iic i)

name: StronglyMeasurable.dependsOn_of_piLE
informal: If a function is strongly measurable with respect to the σ-algebra generated by the first coordinates, then it only depends on those first coordinates.
signature: [TopologicalSpace Z] [PseudoMetrizableSpace Z] [T1Space Z] (hf : StronglyMeasurable[piLE i] f) : DependsOn f (Iic i)

name: _root_.Measurable.dependsOn_of_piFinset
informal: If a function is measurable with respect to the σ-algebra generated by the first coordinates, then it only depends on those first coordinates.
signature: [MeasurableSpace Z] [MeasurableSingletonClass Z] (hf : Measurable[piFinset s] f) : DependsOn f s

name: StronglyMeasurable.dependsOn_of_piFinset
informal: If a function is strongly measurable with respect to the σ-algebra generated by the first coordinates, then it only depends on those first coordinates.
signature: [TopologicalSpace Z] [PseudoMetrizableSpace Z] [T1Space Z] (hf : StronglyMeasurable[piFinset s] f) : DependsOn f s

name: measurable_image_of_fderivWithin
informal: If a function is differentiable and injective on a measurable set, then the image is measurable.
signature: (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) : MeasurableSet (f '' s)

name: measurableEmbedding_of_fderivWithin
informal: If a function is differentiable and injective on a measurable set `s`, then its restriction to `s` is a measurable embedding.
signature: (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (hf : InjOn f s) : MeasurableEmbedding (s.domRestrict f)

name: Continuous.locallyIntegrable
informal: A continuous function `f` is locally integrable with respect to any locally finite measure.
signature: [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] [SecondCountableTopologyEither X E] (hf : Continuous f) : LocallyIntegrable f μ

name: _root_.Measurable.add_stronglyMeasurable
informal: In a normed vector space, the addition of a measurable function and a strongly measurable function is measurable. Note that this is not true without further second-countability assumptions for the addition of two measurable functions.
signature: {α E : Type*} {_ : MeasurableSpace α} [AddCancelMonoid E] [TopologicalSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [PseudoMetrizableSpace E] {g f : α → E} (hg : Measurable g) (hf : StronglyMeasurable f) : Measurable (g + f)

name: _root_.Measurable.sub_stronglyMeasurable
informal: In a normed vector space, the subtraction of a measurable function and a strongly measurable function is measurable. Note that this is not true without further second-countability assumptions for the subtraction of two measurable functions.
signature: {α E : Type*} {_ : MeasurableSpace α} [AddGroup E] [TopologicalSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [ContinuousNeg E] [PseudoMetrizableSpace E] {g f : α → E} (hg : Measurable g) (hf : StronglyMeasurable f) : Measurable (g - f)

name: _root_.Measurable.stronglyMeasurable_add
informal: In a normed vector space, the addition of a strongly measurable function and a measurable function is measurable. Note that this is not true without further second-countability assumptions for the addition of two measurable functions.
signature: {α E : Type*} {_ : MeasurableSpace α} [AddCancelMonoid E] [TopologicalSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [PseudoMetrizableSpace E] {g f : α → E} (hg : Measurable g) (hf : StronglyMeasurable f) : Measurable (f + g)

name: _root_.stronglyMeasurable_iff_measurable
informal: In a space with second countable topology, strongly measurable and measurable are equivalent.
signature: [TopologicalSpace β] [PseudoMetrizableSpace β] [BorelSpace β] [SecondCountableTopology β] : StronglyMeasurable f ↔ Measurable f

name: _root_.Continuous.stronglyMeasurable
informal: A continuous function is strongly measurable when either the source space or the target space is second-countable.
signature: [MeasurableSpace α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α] [TopologicalSpace β] [PseudoMetrizableSpace β] [h : SecondCountableTopologyEither α β] {f : α → β} (hf : Continuous f) : StronglyMeasurable f

name: _root_.ContinuousOn.stronglyMeasurable_of_countable_compl
informal: If a function is continuous outside of a countable set, then it is strongly measurable.
signature: [MeasurableSpace α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSingletonClass α] [TopologicalSpace β] [PseudoMetrizableSpace β] [h : SecondCountableTopologyEither α β] {f : α → β} {s : Set α} (hf : ContinuousOn f s) (hs : (sᶜ).Countable) : StronglyMeasurable f

name: of_countable_not_continuousAt
informal: If a function is continuous outside of a countable set, then it is strongly measurable.
signature: [MeasurableSpace α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSingletonClass α] [TopologicalSpace β] [PseudoMetrizableSpace β] [h : SecondCountableTopologyEither α β] {f : α → β} (hf : Set.Countable {x | ¬ ContinuousAt f x}) : StronglyMeasurable f

name: tendsto_Lp_finite_of_tendstoInMeasure
informal: Forward direction of Vitali's convergence theorem: if `f` is a sequence of uniformly integrable functions that converge in measure to some function `g` in a finite measure space, then `f` converge in Lp to `g`.
signature: [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≠ ∞) (hf : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (f n) μ) (hg : MemLp g p μ) (hui : UnifIntegrable f p μ) (hfg : TendstoInMeasure μ f atTop g) : Tendsto (fun n ↦ eLpNorm (f n - g) p μ) atTop (𝓝 0)

name: tendstoInMeasure_iff_tendsto_Lp_finite
informal: **Vitali's convergence theorem**: A sequence of functions `f` converges to `g` in Lp if and only if it is uniformly integrable and converges to `g` in measure.
signature: [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≠ ∞) (hf : ∀ n, MemLp (f n) p μ) (hg : MemLp g p μ) : TendstoInMeasure μ f atTop g ∧ UnifIntegrable f p μ ↔ Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (f n - g) p μ) atTop (𝓝 0)

name: continuous_parametric_integral_of_continuous
informal: The parametric integral over a continuous function on a compact set is continuous, under mild assumptions on the topologies involved.
signature: [FirstCountableTopology X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [SecondCountableTopologyEither Y E] [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] {f : X → Y → E} (hf : Continuous f.uncurry) {s : Set Y} (hs : IsCompact s) : Continuous (∫ y in s, f · y ∂μ)

name: integrable_sum_dirac_iff
informal: A function `f` is integrable with respect to a countable sum of Dirac masses `Measure.sum (fun i ↦ (c i) • Measure.dirac (x i))` if and only if the sequence `fun i ↦ (c i).toReal * ‖f (x i)‖` is summable.
signature: (hc : ∀ i, c i ≠ ∞) : Integrable f (Measure.sum (fun i ↦ (c i) • .dirac (x i))) ↔ Summable (fun i ↦ (c i).toReal * ‖f (x i)‖) where mp h

name: integral_eq_of_hasDerivAt_off_countable
informal: **Fundamental theorem of calculus, part 2**. This version assumes that `f` is continuous on the interval and is differentiable off a countable set `s`. See also `intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right` for a version that only assumes right differentiability of `f`.
signature: [CompleteSpace E] (f f' : ℝ → E) {a b : ℝ} {s : Set ℝ} (hs : s.Countable) (Hc : ContinuousOn f [[a, b]]) (Hd : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ s, HasDerivAt f (f' x) x) (Hi : IntervalIntegrable f' volume a b) : ∫ x in a..b, f' x = f b - f a

name: tendsto_limUnder_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrableOn_Ioi

name: tendsto_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrableOn_Ioi
informal: If a function and its derivative are integrable on `(a, +∞)`, then the function tends to zero at `+∞`.
signature: (hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Ioi a, HasDerivAt f (f' x) x) (f'int : IntegrableOn f' (Ioi a)) (fint : IntegrableOn f (Ioi a)) : Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0)

name: _root_.HasCompactSupport.integral_Ioi_deriv_eq
informal: A special case of `integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto` where we assume that `f` is C^1 with compact support.

name: integrableOn_Ioi_deriv_of_nonneg

name: integrableOn_Ioi_deriv_of_nonneg'
informal: When a function has a limit at infinity, and its derivative is nonnegative, then the derivative is automatically integrable on `(a, +∞)`. Version assuming differentiability on `[a, +∞)`.
signature: (hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Ici a, HasDerivAt g (g' x) x) (g'pos : ∀ x ∈ Ioi a, 0 ≤ g' x) (hg : Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 l)) : IntegrableOn g' (Ioi a)

name: integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_nonneg'
