signature: (hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Ici a, HasDerivAt g (g' x) x) (g'pos : ∀ x ∈ Ioi a, 0 ≤ g' x) (hg : Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 l)) : ∫ x in Ioi a, g' x = l - g a

name: integrableOn_Ioi_deriv_of_nonpos
informal: When a function has a limit at infinity, and its derivative is nonpositive, then the derivative is automatically integrable on `(a, +∞)`. Version assuming differentiability on `(a, +∞)` and continuity at `a⁺`.
signature: (hcont : ContinuousWithinAt g (Ici a) a) (hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Ioi a, HasDerivAt g (g' x) x) (g'neg : ∀ x ∈ Ioi a, g' x ≤ 0) (hg : Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 l)) : IntegrableOn g' (Ioi a)

name: integrableOn_Ioi_deriv_of_nonpos'
informal: When a function has a limit at infinity, and its derivative is nonpositive, then the derivative is automatically integrable on `(a, +∞)`. Version assuming differentiability on `[a, +∞)`.
signature: (hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Ici a, HasDerivAt g (g' x) x) (g'neg : ∀ x ∈ Ioi a, g' x ≤ 0) (hg : Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 l)) : IntegrableOn g' (Ioi a)

name: integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_nonpos'
informal: When a function has a limit at infinity `l`, and its derivative is nonpositive, then the integral of the derivative on `(a, +∞)` is `l - g a` (and the derivative is integrable, see `integrable_on_Ioi_deriv_of_nonneg'`). Version assuming differentiability on `[a, +∞)`.
signature: (hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Ici a, HasDerivAt g (g' x) x) (g'neg : ∀ x ∈ Ioi a, g' x ≤ 0) (hg : Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 l)) : ∫ x in Ioi a, g' x = l - g a

name: tendsto_limUnder_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrableOn_Iic
informal: If the derivative of a function defined on the real line is integrable close to `-∞`, then the function has a limit at `-∞`.

name: tendsto_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrableOn_Iic

signature: (hderiv : ∀ x ∈ Iic a, HasDerivAt f (f' x) x) (f'int : IntegrableOn f' (Iic a)) (fint : IntegrableOn f (Iic a)) : Tendsto f atBot (𝓝 0)

name: _root_.HasCompactSupport.integral_Iic_deriv_eq
informal: A special case of `integral_Iic_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto` where we assume that `f` is C^1 with compact support.

name: integral_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrable
informal: If a function and its derivative are integrable on the real line, then the integral of the derivative is zero.

signature: (q : ℚ) : mulHeight₁ q = max q.num.natAbs q.den

name: logHeight₁_eq_log_max
informal: The logarithmic height of a rational number is the logarithm of the maximum of the absolute value of its numerator and its denominator.
signature: (q : ℚ) : logHeight₁ q = log ↑(max q.num.natAbs q.den)

name: mulHeight₁_natCast
informal: The multiplicative height of a positive natural number `n` cast to `ℚ` equals `n`.
signature: (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : mulHeight₁ (n : ℚ) = n

name: logHeight₁_natCast
informal: The logarithmic height of a positive natural number `n` cast to `ℚ` equals `log n`.
signature: (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : logHeight₁ (n : ℚ) = Real.log n

name: LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_congr'
informal: If `f` and `g` agree on large `n : ℕ`, then their `LSeries` have the same abscissa of absolute convergence.
signature: {f g : ℕ → ℂ} (h : f =ᶠ[atTop] g) : abscissaOfAbsConv f = abscissaOfAbsConv g

name: LSeries.summable_real_of_abscissaOfAbsConv_lt
informal: If `f` is real-valued and `x` is strictly greater than the abscissa of absolute convergence of `f`, then the real series `∑' n, f n / n ^ x` converges.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℝ} {x : ℝ} (h : abscissaOfAbsConv (f ·) < x) : Summable fun n : ℕ ↦ f n / (n : ℝ) ^ x

name: ArithmeticFunction.coe_mul
informal: The product of two arithmetic functions defines the same function as the Dirichlet convolution of the functions defined by them.
signature: {R : Type*} [Semiring R] (f g : ArithmeticFunction R) : f ⍟ g = ⇑(f * g)

name: term_convolution
informal: We give an expression of the `LSeries.term` of the convolution of two functions in terms of a sum over `Nat.divisorsAntidiagonal`.
signature: (f g : ℕ → ℂ) (s : ℂ) (n : ℕ) : term (f ⍟ g) s n = ∑ p ∈ n.divisorsAntidiagonal, term f s p.1 * term g s p.2

name: LSeriesHasSum.convolution
informal: The L-series of the convolution product `f ⍟ g` of two sequences `f` and `g` equals the product of their L-series, assuming both L-series converge.
signature: {f g : ℕ → ℂ} {s a b : ℂ} (hf : LSeriesHasSum f s a) (hg : LSeriesHasSum g s b) : LSeriesHasSum (f ⍟ g) s (a * b)

name: LSeries_convolution'
informal: The L-series of the convolution product `f ⍟ g` of two sequences `f` and `g` equals the product of their L-series, assuming both L-series converge.
signature: {f g : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hf : LSeriesSummable f s) (hg : LSeriesSummable g s) : LSeries (f ⍟ g) s = LSeries f s * LSeries g s

name: LSeries_convolution
informal: The L-series of the convolution product `f ⍟ g` of two sequences `f` and `g` equals the product of their L-series in their common half-plane of absolute convergence.
signature: {f g : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hf : abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re) (hg : abscissaOfAbsConv g < s.re) : LSeries (f ⍟ g) s = LSeries f s * LSeries g s

name: LSeriesSummable.convolution
informal: The L-series of the convolution product `f ⍟ g` of two sequences `f` and `g` is summable when both L-series are summable.
signature: {f g : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hf : LSeriesSummable f s) (hg : LSeriesSummable g s) : LSeriesSummable (f ⍟ g) s

name: LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_convolution_le
informal: The abscissa of absolute convergence of `f ⍟ g` is at most the maximum of those of `f` and `g`.
signature: (f g : ℕ → ℂ) : abscissaOfAbsConv (f ⍟ g) ≤ max (abscissaOfAbsConv f) (abscissaOfAbsConv g)

name: LSeriesHasSum_mul
informal: The L-series of the (convolution) product of two `ℂ`-valued arithmetic functions `f` and `g` equals the product of their L-series, assuming both L-series converge.
signature: {f g : ArithmeticFunction ℂ} {s a b : ℂ} (hf : LSeriesHasSum ↗f s a) (hg : LSeriesHasSum ↗g s b) : LSeriesHasSum ↗(f * g) s (a * b)

name: LSeries_mul'
informal: The L-series of the (convolution) product of two `ℂ`-valued arithmetic functions `f` and `g` equals the product of their L-series, assuming both L-series converge.
signature: {f g : ArithmeticFunction ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hf : LSeriesSummable ↗f s) (hg : LSeriesSummable ↗g s) : LSeries ↗(f * g) s = LSeries ↗f s * LSeries ↗g s

name: LSeries_mul
informal: The L-series of the (convolution) product of two `ℂ`-valued arithmetic functions `f` and `g` equals the product of their L-series in their common half-plane of absolute convergence.
signature: {f g : ArithmeticFunction ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hf : abscissaOfAbsConv ↗f < s.re) (hg : abscissaOfAbsConv ↗g < s.re) : LSeries ↗(f * g) s = LSeries ↗f s * LSeries ↗g s

name: LSeriesSummable_mul
informal: The L-series of the (convolution) product of two `ℂ`-valued arithmetic functions `f` and `g` is summable when both L-series are summable.
signature: {f g : ArithmeticFunction ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hf : LSeriesSummable ↗f s) (hg : LSeriesSummable ↗g s) : LSeriesSummable ↗(f * g) s

name: LSeries_hasDerivAt
informal: If `re s` is greater than the abscissa of absolute convergence of `f`, then the L-series of `f` is differentiable with derivative the negative of the L-series of the point-wise product of `log` with `f`.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (h : abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re) : HasDerivAt (LSeries f) (-LSeries (logMul f) s) s

name: LSeries_deriv
informal: If `re s` is greater than the abscissa of absolute convergence of `f`, then the derivative of this L-series at `s` is the negative of the L-series of `log * f`.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (h : abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re) : deriv (LSeries f) s = -LSeries (logMul f) s

name: LSeries_deriv_eqOn
informal: The derivative of the L-series of `f` agrees with the negative of the L-series of `log * f` on the right half-plane of absolute convergence.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℂ} : {s | abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re}.EqOn (deriv (LSeries f)) (-LSeries (logMul f))

name: LSeries_iteratedDeriv
informal: If `re s` is greater than the abscissa of absolute convergence of `f`, then the `m`th derivative of this L-series is `(-1)^m` times the L-series of `log^m * f`.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℂ} (m : ℕ) {s : ℂ} (h : abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re) : iteratedDeriv m (LSeries f) s = (-1) ^ m * LSeries (logMul^[m] f) s

name: LSeries_differentiableOn
informal: The L-series of `f` is complex differentiable in its open half-plane of absolute convergence.
signature: (f : ℕ → ℂ) : DifferentiableOn ℂ (LSeries f) {s | abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re}

name: LSeries_analyticOnNhd
informal: The L-series of `f` is holomorphic on its open half-plane of absolute convergence.
signature: (f : ℕ → ℂ) : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ (LSeries f) {s | abscissaOfAbsConv f < s.re}

name: LSeriesHasSum_one
informal: The L-series of the constant sequence `1` equals the Riemann zeta function on its domain of convergence `1 < re s`.
signature: {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : LSeriesHasSum 1 s (riemannZeta s)

name: riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re
informal: The Riemann Zeta Function does not vanish on the half-plane `re s > 1`.
signature: {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : riemannZeta s ≠ 0

name: riemannZeta_pos_of_one_lt
informal: The Riemann zeta function is positive in `ComplexOrder` for real arguments greater than 1. This means it is a positive real number: both `(riemannZeta x).re > 0` and `(riemannZeta x).im = 0`.
signature: {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 < x) : 0 < riemannZeta x

name: riemannZeta_re_pos_of_one_lt
informal: The real part of the Riemann zeta function is positive for real arguments greater than 1.
signature: {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 < x) : 0 < (riemannZeta x).re

name: riemannZeta_im_eq_zero_of_one_lt
informal: The Riemann zeta function is real-valued for real arguments greater than 1.
signature: {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 < x) : (riemannZeta x).im = 0

name: LSeriesSummable_vonMangoldt
informal: The L-series of the von Mangoldt function `Λ` converges at `s` when `re s > 1`.
signature: {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : LSeriesSummable ↗Λ s

name: completedLFunction_modOne_eq
informal: The completed L-function of the (unique) Dirichlet character mod 1 is the completed Riemann zeta function.
signature: {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ 1} : completedLFunction χ = completedRiemannZeta

name: rootNumber_modOne
informal: The root number of the unique Dirichlet character modulo 1 is 1.
signature: (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ 1) : rootNumber χ = 1

name: hasSum_hurwitzZeta_of_one_lt_re
informal: Formula for `hurwitzZeta s` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range. We restrict to `a ∈ Icc 0 1` to simplify the statement.
signature: {a : ℝ} (ha : a ∈ Icc 0 1) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : HasSum (fun n : ℕ ↦ 1 / (n + a : ℂ) ^ s) (hurwitzZeta a s)

name: tendsto_hurwitzZeta_sub_one_div_nhds_one
informal: Expression for `hurwitzZeta a 1` as a limit. (Mathematically `hurwitzZeta a 1` is undefined, but our construction assigns some value to it; this lemma is mostly of interest for determining what that value is).
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) : Tendsto (fun s ↦ hurwitzZeta a s - 1 / (s - 1) / Gammaℝ s) (𝓝 1) (𝓝 (hurwitzZeta a 1))

name: differentiable_hurwitzZeta_sub_hurwitzZeta
informal: The difference of two Hurwitz zeta functions is differentiable everywhere.
signature: (a b : UnitAddCircle) : Differentiable ℂ (fun s ↦ hurwitzZeta a s - hurwitzZeta b s)

name: completedHurwitzZetaEven_one_sub
informal: Functional equation for the even Hurwitz zeta function.
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) (s : ℂ) : completedHurwitzZetaEven a (1 - s) = completedCosZeta a s

name: completedHurwitzZetaEven₀_one_sub
informal: Functional equation for the even Hurwitz zeta function with poles removed.
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) (s : ℂ) : completedHurwitzZetaEven₀ a (1 - s) = completedCosZeta₀ a s

name: completedCosZeta_one_sub
informal: Functional equation for the even Hurwitz zeta function (alternative form).
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) (s : ℂ) : completedCosZeta a (1 - s) = completedHurwitzZetaEven a s

name: completedCosZeta₀_one_sub
informal: Functional equation for the even Hurwitz zeta function with poles removed (alternative form).
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) (s : ℂ) : completedCosZeta₀ a (1 - s) = completedHurwitzZetaEven₀ a s

name: differentiableAt_completedHurwitzZetaEven
informal: The even Hurwitz completed zeta is differentiable away from `s = 0` and `s = 1` (and also at `s = 0` if `a ≠ 0`)
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0 ∨ a ≠ 0) (hs' : s ≠ 1) : DifferentiableAt ℂ (completedHurwitzZetaEven a) s

name: differentiableAt_one_completedHurwitzZetaEven_sub_completedHurwitzZetaEven
informal: The difference of two completed even Hurwitz zeta functions is differentiable at `s = 1`.
signature: (a b : UnitAddCircle) : DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun s ↦ completedHurwitzZetaEven a s - completedHurwitzZetaEven b s) 1

name: hurwitzZetaEven_neg_two_mul_nat_add_one
informal: The trivial zeroes of the even Hurwitz zeta function.
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) (n : ℕ) : hurwitzZetaEven a (-2 * (n + 1)) = 0

name: differentiableAt_hurwitzZetaEven
informal: The Hurwitz zeta function is differentiable everywhere except at `s = 1`. This is true even in the delicate case `a = 0` and `s = 0` (where the completed zeta has a pole, but this is cancelled out by the Gamma factor).
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) {s : ℂ} (hs' : s ≠ 1) : DifferentiableAt ℂ (hurwitzZetaEven a) s

name: tendsto_hurwitzZetaEven_sub_one_div_nhds_one
informal: Expression for `hurwitzZetaEven a 1` as a limit. (Mathematically `hurwitzZetaEven a 1` is undefined, but our construction assigns some value to it; this lemma is mostly of interest for determining what that value is).
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) : Tendsto (fun s ↦ hurwitzZetaEven a s - 1 / (s - 1) / Gammaℝ s) (𝓝 1) (𝓝 (hurwitzZetaEven a 1))

name: hasSum_int_hurwitzZetaEven
informal: Formula for `hurwitzZetaEven` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range, with sum over `ℤ`.
signature: (a : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : HasSum (fun n : ℤ ↦ 1 / (↑|n + a| : ℂ) ^ s / 2) (hurwitzZetaEven a s)

name: hasSum_nat_hurwitzZetaEven
informal: Formula for `hurwitzZetaEven` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range, with sum over `ℕ` (version with absolute values)
signature: (a : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : HasSum (fun n : ℕ ↦ (1 / (↑|n + a| : ℂ) ^ s + 1 / (↑|n + 1 - a| : ℂ) ^ s) / 2) (hurwitzZetaEven a s)

name: hasSum_nat_hurwitzZetaEven_of_mem_Icc
informal: Formula for `hurwitzZetaEven` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range, with sum over `ℕ` (version without absolute values, assuming `a ∈ Icc 0 1`)
signature: {a : ℝ} (ha : a ∈ Icc 0 1) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : HasSum (fun n : ℕ ↦ (1 / (n + a : ℂ) ^ s + 1 / (n + 1 - a : ℂ) ^ s) / 2) (hurwitzZetaEven a s)

name: completedHurwitzZetaOdd_one_sub
informal: Functional equation for the odd Hurwitz zeta function.
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) (s : ℂ) : completedHurwitzZetaOdd a (1 - s) = completedSinZeta a s

name: completedSinZeta_one_sub
informal: Functional equation for the odd Hurwitz zeta function (alternative form).
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) (s : ℂ) : completedSinZeta a (1 - s) = completedHurwitzZetaOdd a s

name: hasSum_int_hurwitzZetaOdd
informal: Formula for `hurwitzZetaOdd` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range (sum over `ℤ`).
signature: (a : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : HasSum (fun n : ℤ ↦ SignType.sign (n + a) / (↑|n + a| : ℂ) ^ s / 2) (hurwitzZetaOdd a s)

name: hasSum_nat_hurwitzZetaOdd
informal: Formula for `hurwitzZetaOdd` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range, with sum over `ℕ` (version with absolute values)
signature: (a : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : HasSum (fun n : ℕ ↦ (SignType.sign (n + a) / (↑|n + a| : ℂ) ^ s - SignType.sign (n + 1 - a) / (↑|n + 1 - a| : ℂ) ^ s) / 2) (hurwitzZetaOdd a s)

name: hasSum_nat_hurwitzZetaOdd_of_mem_Icc
informal: Formula for `hurwitzZetaOdd` as a Dirichlet series in the convergence range, with sum over `ℕ` (version without absolute values, assuming `a ∈ Icc 0 1`)
signature: {a : ℝ} (ha : a ∈ Icc 0 1) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : HasSum (fun n : ℕ ↦ (1 / (n + a : ℂ) ^ s - 1 / (n + 1 - a : ℂ) ^ s) / 2) (hurwitzZetaOdd a s)

name: hurwitzZetaOdd_neg_two_mul_nat_sub_one
informal: The trivial zeroes of the odd Hurwitz zeta function.
signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) (n : ℕ) : hurwitzZetaOdd a (-2 * n - 1) = 0

name: hurwitzZeta_neg_nat
informal: Values of Hurwitz zeta functions at (strictly) negative integers. TODO: This formula is also correct for `k = 0`; but our current proof does not work in this case.
signature: (hk : k ≠ 0) (hx : x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : hurwitzZeta x (-k) = -1 / (k + 1) * ((Polynomial.bernoulli (k + 1)).map (algebraMap ℚ ℂ)).eval (x : ℂ)

name: LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_add_le
informal: The abscissa of absolute convergence of `f + g` is at most the maximum of those of `f` and `g`.
signature: (f g : ℕ → ℂ) : abscissaOfAbsConv (f + g) ≤ max (abscissaOfAbsConv f) (abscissaOfAbsConv g)

name: LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_sub_le
informal: The abscissa of absolute convergence of `f - g` is at most the maximum of those of `f` and `g`.
signature: (f g : ℕ → ℂ) : abscissaOfAbsConv (f - g) ≤ max (abscissaOfAbsConv f) (abscissaOfAbsConv g)

name: LSeries.tendsto_cpow_mul_atTop
informal: If the coefficients `f m` of an L-series are zero for `m ≤ n` and the L-series converges at some point, then `f (n+1)` is the limit of `(n+1)^x * LSeries f x` as `x → ∞`.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℂ} {n : ℕ} (h : ∀ m ≤ n, f m = 0) (ha : abscissaOfAbsConv f < ⊤) : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ ↦ (n + 1) ^ (x : ℂ) * LSeries f x) atTop (nhds (f (n + 1)))

name: LSeries.tendsto_atTop
informal: If the L-series of `f` converges at some point, then `f 1` is the limit of `LSeries f x` as `x → ∞`.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℂ} (ha : abscissaOfAbsConv f < ⊤) : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ ↦ LSeries f x) atTop (nhds (f 1))

name: LSeries_eventually_eq_zero_iff'
informal: The `LSeries` of `f` is zero for large real arguments if and only if either `f n = 0` for all `n ≠ 0` or the L-series converges nowhere.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℂ} : (fun x : ℝ ↦ LSeries f x) =ᶠ[atTop] 0 ↔ (∀ n ≠ 0, f n = 0) ∨ abscissaOfAbsConv f = ⊤

name: LSeries_eq_zero_iff
informal: Assuming `f 0 = 0`, the `LSeries` of `f` is zero if and only if either `f = 0` or the L-series converges nowhere.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℂ} (hf : f 0 = 0) : LSeries f = 0 ↔ f = 0 ∨ abscissaOfAbsConv f = ⊤

name: LSeries_sub_eventuallyEq_zero_of_LSeries_eventually_eq
informal: If the `LSeries` of `f` and of `g` converge somewhere and agree on large real arguments, then the L-series of `f - g` is zero for large real arguments.
signature: {f g : ℕ → ℂ} (hf : abscissaOfAbsConv f < ⊤) (hg : abscissaOfAbsConv g < ⊤) (h : (fun x : ℝ ↦ LSeries f x) =ᶠ[atTop] fun x ↦ LSeries g x) : (fun x : ℝ ↦ LSeries (f - g) x) =ᶠ[atTop] (0 : ℝ → ℂ)

name: LSeries.eq_of_LSeries_eventually_eq
informal: If the `LSeries` of `f` and of `g` converge somewhere and agree on large real arguments, then `f n = g n` whenever `n ≠ 0`.
signature: {f g : ℕ → ℂ} (hf : abscissaOfAbsConv f < ⊤) (hg : abscissaOfAbsConv g < ⊤) (h : (fun x : ℝ ↦ LSeries f x) =ᶠ[atTop] fun x ↦ LSeries g x) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : f n = g n

name: LSeries_eq_iff_of_abscissaOfAbsConv_lt_top
informal: If the `LSeries` of `f` and of `g` both converge somewhere, then they are equal if and only if `f n = g n` whenever `n ≠ 0`.
signature: {f g : ℕ → ℂ} (hf : abscissaOfAbsConv f < ⊤) (hg : abscissaOfAbsConv g < ⊤) : LSeries f = LSeries g ↔ ∀ n ≠ 0, f n = g n

name: _root_.riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re
informal: The Riemann Zeta Function does not vanish on the closed half-plane `re s ≥ 1`. (Note that the value at `s = 1` is a junk value, which happens to be nonzero.)
signature: ⦃s : ℂ⦄ (hs : 1 ≤ s.re) : riemannZeta s ≠ 0

name: iteratedDeriv_alternating
informal: If all values of a `ℂ`-valued arithmetic function are nonnegative reals and `x` is a real number in the domain of absolute convergence, then the `n`th iterated derivative of the associated L-series is nonnegative real when `n` is even and nonpositive real when `n` is odd.
signature: {a : ℕ → ℂ} (hn : 0 ≤ a) {x : ℝ} (h : LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv a < x) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ (-1) ^ n * iteratedDeriv n (LSeries a) x

name: positive
informal: If all values of `a : ℕ → ℂ` are nonnegative reals and `a 1` is positive, then `L a x` is positive real for all real `x` larger than `abscissaOfAbsConv a`.
signature: {a : ℕ → ℂ} (ha₀ : 0 ≤ a) (ha₁ : 0 < a 1) {x : ℝ} (hx : abscissaOfAbsConv a < x) : 0 < LSeries a x

name: iteratedDeriv_LSeries_alternating
informal: If all values of a `ℂ`-valued arithmetic function are nonnegative reals and `x` is a real number in the domain of absolute convergence, then the `n`th iterated derivative of the associated L-series is nonnegative real when `n` is even and nonpositive real when `n` is odd.
signature: (a : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) (hn : ∀ n, 0 ≤ a n) {x : ℝ} (h : LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv a < x) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ (-1) ^ n * iteratedDeriv n (LSeries (a ·)) x

name: LFunctionResidueClassAux_real
informal: The auxiliary function takes real values for real arguments `x > 1`.
signature: (ha : IsUnit a) {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 < x) : LFunctionResidueClassAux a x = (LFunctionResidueClassAux a x).re

name: not_summable_residueClass_prime_div
informal: The function `n ↦ Λ n / n` restricted to primes in an invertible residue class is not summable. This then implies that there must be infinitely many such primes.
signature: (ha : IsUnit a) : ¬ Summable fun n : ℕ ↦ (if n.Prime then residueClass a n else 0) / n

name: infinite_setOfPred_prime_and_eq_mod
informal: **Dirichlet's Theorem** on primes in arithmetic progression: if `q` is a positive integer and `a : ZMod q` is a unit, then there are infinitely many prime numbers `p` such that `(p : ZMod q) = a`.
signature: (ha : IsUnit a) : {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ (p : ZMod q) = a}.Infinite

name: forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod
informal: **Dirichlet's Theorem** on primes in arithmetic progression: if `q` is a positive integer and `a : ZMod q` is a unit, then there are infinitely many prime numbers `p` such that `(p : ZMod q) = a`.
signature: (ha : IsUnit a) (n : ℕ) : ∃ p > n, p.Prime ∧ (p : ZMod q) = a

name: forall_exists_prime_gt_and_zmodEq
informal: **Dirichlet's Theorem** on primes in arithmetic progression: if `q` is a positive integer and `a : ℤ` is coprime to `q`, then there are infinitely many prime numbers `p` such that `p ≡ a mod q`.
signature: (n : ℕ) {q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (h : IsCoprime a q) : ∃ p > n, p.Prime ∧ p ≡ a [ZMOD q]

name: forall_exists_prime_gt_and_modEq
informal: **Dirichlet's Theorem** on primes in arithmetic progression: if `q` is a positive integer and `a : ℕ` is coprime to `q`, then there are infinitely many prime numbers `p` such that `p ≡ a mod q`.
signature: (n : ℕ) {q a : ℕ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (h : a.Coprime q) : ∃ p > n, p.Prime ∧ p ≡ a [MOD q]

name: differentiableAt_completedZeta
informal: The completed Riemann zeta function `Λ(s)` is differentiable away from `s = 0` and `s = 1`.
signature: {s : ℂ} (hs : s ≠ 0) (hs' : s ≠ 1) : DifferentiableAt ℂ completedRiemannZeta s

name: completedRiemannZeta₀_one_sub
informal: Riemann zeta functional equation, formulated for `Λ₀`: for any complex `s` we have `Λ₀(1 - s) = Λ₀ s`.
signature: (s : ℂ) : completedRiemannZeta₀ (1 - s) = completedRiemannZeta₀ s

name: completedRiemannZeta_one_sub
informal: Riemann zeta functional equation, formulated for `Λ`: for any complex `s` we have `Λ (1 - s) = Λ s`.
signature: (s : ℂ) : completedRiemannZeta (1 - s) = completedRiemannZeta s

name: zeta_eq_tsum_one_div_nat_cpow
informal: The Riemann zeta function agrees with the naive Dirichlet-series definition when the latter converges. (Note that this is false without the assumption: when `re s ≤ 1` the sum is divergent, and we use a different definition to obtain the analytic continuation to all `s`.)
signature: {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : riemannZeta s = ∑' n : ℕ, 1 / (n : ℂ) ^ s

name: zeta_eq_tsum_one_div_nat_add_one_cpow
informal: Alternate formulation of `zeta_eq_tsum_one_div_nat_cpow` with a `+ 1` (to avoid relying on mathlib's conventions for `0 ^ s`).
signature: {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : riemannZeta s = ∑' n : ℕ, 1 / (n + 1 : ℂ) ^ s

name: zeta_nat_eq_tsum_of_gt_one
informal: Special case of `zeta_eq_tsum_one_div_nat_cpow` when the argument is in `ℕ`, so the power function can be expressed using naïve `pow` rather than `cpow`.
signature: {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 < k) : riemannZeta k = ∑' n : ℕ, 1 / (n : ℂ) ^ k

name: LFunction_modOne_eq
informal: The L-function of a function on `ZMod 1` is a scalar multiple of the Riemann zeta function.
signature: (Φ : ZMod 1 → ℂ) (s : ℂ) : LFunction Φ s = Φ 0 * riemannZeta s

name: completedLFunction_modOne_eq
informal: The completed L-function of a function `ZMod 1 → ℂ` is a scalar multiple of the completed Riemann zeta function.
signature: (Φ : ZMod 1 → ℂ) (s : ℂ) : completedLFunction Φ s = Φ 1 * completedRiemannZeta s

name: differentiable_completedLFunction
informal: Special case of `differentiableAt_completedLFunction` asserting differentiability everywhere under suitable hypotheses.
signature: (hΦ₂ : Φ 0 = 0) (hΦ₃ : ∑ j, Φ j = 0) : Differentiable ℂ (completedLFunction Φ)

name: LFunction_eq_completed_div_gammaFactor_even
informal: Relation between the completed L-function and the usual one (even case). We state it this way around so it holds at the poles of the gamma factor as well (except at `s = 0`, where it is genuinely false if `N > 1` and `Φ 0 ≠ 0`).
signature: (hΦ : Φ.Even) (s : ℂ) (hs : s ≠ 0 ∨ Φ 0 = 0) : LFunction Φ s = completedLFunction Φ s / Gammaℝ s

name: LFunction_eq_completed_div_gammaFactor_odd
informal: Relation between the completed L-function and the usual one (odd case). We state it this way around so it holds at the poles of the gamma factor as well.
signature: (hΦ : Φ.Odd) (s : ℂ) : LFunction Φ s = completedLFunction Φ s / Gammaℝ (s + 1)

name: IsCompact.inter_riemannZetaZeros_finite
informal: Any compact subset of `ℂ` contains only finitely many zeros of the Riemann zeta function.
signature: {S : Set ℂ} (hS : IsCompact S) : (S ∩ riemannZetaZeros).Finite

name: card_sqrts
informal: The number of square roots of `a` modulo `p` is determined by the Legendre symbol.
signature: (hp : p ≠ 2) (a : ℤ) : ↑{x : ZMod p | x ^ 2 = a}.toFinset.card = legendreSym p a + 1

name: eq_one_of_sq_sub_mul_sq_eq_zero
informal: The Legendre symbol `legendreSym p a = 1` if there is a solution in `ℤ/pℤ` of the equation `x^2 - a*y^2 = 0` with `y ≠ 0`.
signature: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {a : ℤ} (ha : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 0) {x y : ZMod p} (hy : y ≠ 0) (hxy : x ^ 2 - a * y ^ 2 = 0) : legendreSym p a = 1

name: eq_one_of_sq_sub_mul_sq_eq_zero'
informal: The Legendre symbol `legendreSym p a = 1` if there is a solution in `ℤ/pℤ` of the equation `x^2 - a*y^2 = 0` with `x ≠ 0`.
signature: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {a : ℤ} (ha : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 0) {x y : ZMod p} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hxy : x ^ 2 - a * y ^ 2 = 0) : legendreSym p a = 1

name: legendreSym.at_neg
informal: The value of the Legendre symbol at `-a` is `χ₄ p` times the value at `a`.
signature: (hp : p ≠ 2) (a : ℤ) : legendreSym p (-a) = χ₄ p * legendreSym p a

name: mod_four_ne_three_of_sq_eq_neg_sq'
informal: If two nonzero squares are negatives of each other in `ZMod p`, then `p % 4 ≠ 3`.
signature: {x y : ZMod p} (hy : y ≠ 0) (hxy : x ^ 2 = -y ^ 2) : p % 4 ≠ 3

name: Ico_map_valMinAbs_natAbs_eq_Ico_map_id
informal: The image of the map sending a nonzero natural number `x ≤ p / 2` to the absolute value of the integer in `(-p/2, p/2]` that is congruent to `a * x mod p` is the set of nonzero natural numbers `x` such that `x ≤ p / 2`.
signature: (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] (a : ZMod p) (hap : a ≠ 0) : ((Ico 1 (p / 2).succ).1.map fun (x : ℕ) => (a * x).valMinAbs.natAbs) = (Ico 1 (p / 2).succ).1.map fun a => a

name: gauss_lemma
informal: **Gauss' lemma**. The Legendre symbol can be computed by considering the number of naturals less than `p/2` such that `(a * x) % p > p / 2`.
signature: {p : ℕ} [h : Fact p.Prime] {a : ℤ} (hp : p ≠ 2) (ha0 : (a : ZMod p) ≠ 0) : legendreSym p a = (-1) ^ #{x ∈ Ico 1 (p / 2).succ | p / 2 < (a * x.cast : ZMod p).val}

name: sum_mul_div_add_sum_mul_div_eq_mul
informal: Each of the sums in this lemma is the cardinality of the set of integer points in each of the two triangles formed by the diagonal of the rectangle `(0, p/2) × (0, q/2)`. Adding them gives the number of points in the rectangle.
signature: (p q : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hq0 : (q : ZMod p) ≠ 0) : ∑ a ∈ Ico 1 (p / 2).succ, a * q / p + ∑ a ∈ Ico 1 (q / 2).succ, a * p / q = p / 2 * (q / 2)

name: eq_iff_eq
informal: We can move `qrSign m n` from one side of an equality to the other when `m` and `n` are odd.
signature: {m n : ℕ} (hm : Odd m) (hn : Odd n) (x y : ℤ) : qrSign m n * x = y ↔ x = qrSign m n * y

name: quadraticChar_card_card
informal: The relation between the values of the quadratic character of one field `F` at the cardinality of another field `F'` and of the quadratic character of `F'` at the cardinality of `F`.
signature: [DecidableEq F] (hF : ringChar F ≠ 2) {F' : Type*} [Field F'] [Fintype F'] [DecidableEq F'] (hF' : ringChar F' ≠ 2) (h : ringChar F' ≠ ringChar F) : quadraticChar F (Fintype.card F') = quadraticChar F' (quadraticChar F (-1) * Fintype.card F)

name: quadraticChar_odd_prime
informal: The value of the quadratic character at an odd prime `p` different from `ringChar F`.
signature: [DecidableEq F] (hF : ringChar F ≠ 2) {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp₁ : p ≠ 2) (hp₂ : ringChar F ≠ p) : quadraticChar F p = quadraticChar (ZMod p) (χ₄ (Fintype.card F) * Fintype.card F)

name: quadratic_reciprocity
informal: **The Law of Quadratic Reciprocity**: if `p` and `q` are distinct odd primes, then `(q / p) * (p / q) = (-1)^((p-1)(q-1)/4)`.
signature: (hp : p ≠ 2) (hq : q ≠ 2) (hpq : p ≠ q) : legendreSym q p * legendreSym p q = (-1) ^ (p / 2 * (q / 2))

name: quadratic_reciprocity'
informal: The Law of Quadratic Reciprocity: if `p` and `q` are odd primes, then `(q / p) = (-1)^((p-1)(q-1)/4) * (p / q)`.
signature: (hp : p ≠ 2) (hq : q ≠ 2) : legendreSym q p = (-1) ^ (p / 2 * (q / 2)) * legendreSym p q

name: quadratic_reciprocity_one_mod_four
informal: The Law of Quadratic Reciprocity: if `p` and `q` are odd primes and `p % 4 = 1`, then `(q / p) = (p / q)`.
signature: (hp : p % 4 = 1) (hq : q ≠ 2) : legendreSym q p = legendreSym p q

name: quadratic_reciprocity_three_mod_four
informal: The Law of Quadratic Reciprocity: if `p` and `q` are primes that are both congruent to `3` mod `4`, then `(q / p) = -(p / q)`.
signature: (hp : p % 4 = 3) (hq : q % 4 = 3) : legendreSym q p = -legendreSym p q

name: grahamConjecture_of_squarefree
informal: The special case of Graham's conjecture where all numbers are squarefree.
signature: {n : ℕ} (f : ℕ → ℕ) (hf' : ∀ k < n, Squarefree (f k)) : GrahamConjecture n f

name: bottom_row_coprime
informal: The two numbers `c`, `d` in the "bottom row" of `g=[[*,*],[c,d]]` in `SL(2, ℤ)` are coprime.
signature: {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (g : SL(2, R)) : IsCoprime ((↑g : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R) 1 0) ((↑g : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R) 1 1)

name: bottom_row_surj
informal: Every pair `![c, d]` of coprime integers is the "bottom row" of some element `g=[[*,*],[c,d]]` of `SL(2,ℤ)`.
signature: {R : Type*} [CommRing R] : Set.SurjOn (fun g : SL(2, R) => (↑g : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R) 1) Set.univ {cd | IsCoprime (cd 0) (cd 1)}

name: tendsto_lcRow0
informal: The map `lcRow0` is proper, that is, preimages of cocompact sets are finite in `[[* , *], [c, d]]`.
signature: {cd : Fin 2 → ℤ} (hcd : IsCoprime (cd 0) (cd 1)) : Tendsto (fun g : { g : SL(2, ℤ) // g 1 = cd } => lcRow0 cd ↑(↑g : SL(2, ℝ))) cofinite (cocompact ℝ)

name: smul_eq_lcRow0_add
informal: This replaces `(g•z).re = a/c + *` in the standard theory with the following novel identity: `g • z = (a c + b d) / (c^2 + d^2) + (d z - c) / ((c^2 + d^2) (c z + d))` which does not need to be decomposed depending on whether `c = 0`.

name: exists_row_one_eq_and_min_re
informal: Given `z : ℍ` and a bottom row `(c,d)`, among the `g : SL(2,ℤ)` with this bottom row, minimize `|(g•z).re|`.
signature: {cd : Fin 2 → ℤ} (hcd : IsCoprime (cd 0) (cd 1)) : ∃ g : SL(2, ℤ), g 1 = cd ∧ ∀ g' : SL(2, ℤ), g 1 = g' 1 → |(g • z).re| ≤ |(g' • z).re|

name: exists_smul_mem_fd
informal: First Fundamental Domain Lemma: Any `z : ℍ` can be moved to `𝒟` by an element of `SL(2,ℤ)`
signature: (z : ℍ) : ∃ g : SL(2, ℤ), g • z ∈ 𝒟

name: coe_truncatedFundamentalDomain
informal: Explicit description of the truncated fundamental domain as a subset of `ℂ`, given by obviously closed conditions.
signature: (y : ℝ) : UpperHalfPlane.coe '' truncatedFundamentalDomain y = {z | 0 ≤ z.im ∧ z.im ≤ y ∧ |z.re| ≤ 1 / 2 ∧ 1 ≤ ‖z‖}

name: isCompact_truncatedFundamentalDomain
informal: For any `y : ℝ`, the standard fundamental domain truncated at height `y` is compact.
signature: (y : ℝ) : IsCompact (truncatedFundamentalDomain y)

name: eq_zero_of_neg_one_mem
informal: If `-1 ∈ Γ` and `k` is odd, then every modular form of weight `k` for `Γ` is zero.
signature: [Γ.HasDetOne] (h_neg_one : -1 ∈ Γ) (hk : Odd k) (f : ModularForm Γ k) : f = 0

name: gnpow_eq_pow
informal: Bridge between the auto-derived graded-monoid power `GradedMonoid.GMonoid.gnpow` and the bespoke `ModularForm.pow`: as elements of `GradedMonoid (ModularForm Γ)`, the pair `⟨n • k, gnpow n f⟩` agrees with `⟨n * k, f.pow n⟩`.
signature: {Γ : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ)} [Γ.HasDetPlusMinusOne] {k : ℤ} (f : ModularForm Γ k) (n : ℕ) : (⟨n • k, GradedMonoid.GMonoid.gnpow n f⟩ : GradedMonoid (ModularForm Γ)) = ⟨(n : ℤ) * k, f.pow n⟩

name: CuspForm.isCuspForm_toModularFormₗ
informal: The underlying modular form (via `toModularFormₗ`) of a `CuspForm` is itself a cusp form.
signature: {Γ : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ)} [Γ.HasDetOne] (f : CuspForm Γ k) : ModularForm.IsCuspForm f.toModularFormₗ

name: isCuspForm_iff
informal: A modular form is a cusp form if and only if it vanishes at every cusp. This is the general characterization valid for any subgroup.
signature: [Γ.HasDetOne] (f : ModularForm Γ k) : IsCuspForm f ↔ ∀ {c}, IsCusp c Γ → c.IsZeroAt f k

name: isZeroAt_of_coeffZero_eq_zero
informal: An `𝒮ℒ` modular form with vanishing q-expansion constant term vanishes at every cusp.
signature: (f : ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k) (h : (qExpansion 1 f).coeff 0 = 0) {c : OnePoint ℝ} (hc : IsCusp c 𝒮ℒ) : c.IsZeroAt f k

name: isCuspForm_iff_coeffZero_eq_zero
informal: For `𝒮ℒ` modular forms, `IsCuspForm` is equivalent to the q-expansion having vanishing constant term.
signature: (f : ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k) : IsCuspForm f ↔ (qExpansion 1 f).coeff 0 = 0

name: sub_smul_isCuspForm
informal: Subtracting `(qExpansion 1 f).coeff 0 • g` from `f` (where `g` has constant qExpansion 1) gives a cusp form.
signature: (f g : ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k) (hg : (qExpansion 1 g).coeff 0 = 1) : ModularForm.IsCuspForm (f - (qExpansion 1 f).coeff 0 • g)

name: Subgroup.IsArithmetic.isCusp_iff_isCusp_SL2Z
informal: The cusps of any arithmetic subgroup are the same as those of `SL(2, ℤ)`.
signature: (𝒢 : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ)) [𝒢.IsArithmetic] {c : OnePoint ℝ} : IsCusp c 𝒢 ↔ IsCusp c 𝒮ℒ

name: differentiableOn_tprod_one_sub_pow_pow
informal: For any `k`, the function `q ↦ ∏' n, (1 - q^(n+1))^k` is differentiable on the open unit disc.
signature: (k : ℕ) : DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun q ↦ ∏' n, (1 - q ^ (n + 1)) ^ k) (Metric.ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

name: serreDerivative_mdifferentiable
informal: The Serre derivative preserves MDifferentiability. If `F : ℍ → ℂ` is MDifferentiable, then `serreDerivative k F` is also MDifferentiable.
signature: {F : ℍ → ℂ} (k : ℂ) (hF : MDiff F) : MDiff (serreDerivative k F)

name: discriminant_ne_zero
informal: The modular discriminant is non-vanishing on the upper half-plane.
signature: (z : ℍ) : Δ z ≠ 0

name: gammaSet_one_const
informal: For level `N = 1`, the gamma sets are all equal.
signature: (a a' : Fin 2 → ZMod 1) : gammaSet 1 r a = gammaSet 1 r a'

name: gammaSet_one_eq
informal: For level `N = 1`, the gamma sets simplify to only a `gcd` condition.
signature: (a : Fin 2 → ZMod 1) : gammaSet 1 r a = {v : Fin 2 → ℤ | (v 0).gcd (v 1) = r}

name: G2_eq_tsum_G2Term
informal: This shows `G2` can be defined as a certain absolutely convergent double sum.
signature: (z : ℍ) : G2 z = ∑' m, ∑' n, G2Term z ![m, n]

name: norm_le_tsum_norm
informal: The norm of the restricted sum is less than the full sum of the norms.
signature: (N : ℕ) (a : Fin 2 → ZMod N) (k : ℤ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (z : ℍ) : ‖eisensteinSeries a k z‖ ≤ ∑' (x : Fin 2 → ℤ), ‖eisSummand k x z‖

name: div_linear_zpow_differentiableOn
informal: Auxiliary lemma showing that for any `k : ℤ` the function `z → 1/(c*z+d)^k` is differentiable on `{z : ℂ | 0 < z.im}`.
signature: (k : ℤ) (a : Fin 2 → ℤ) : DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun z : ℂ => (a 0 * z + a 1) ^ (-k)) {z : ℂ | 0 < z.im}

name: eisSummand_extension_differentiableOn
informal: Auxiliary lemma showing that for any `k : ℤ` and `(a : Fin 2 → ℤ)` the extension of `eisSummand` is differentiable on `{z : ℂ | 0 < z.im}`.
signature: (k : ℤ) (a : Fin 2 → ℤ) : DifferentiableOn ℂ (↑ₕeisSummand k a) {z : ℂ | 0 < z.im}

name: summand_bound
informal: Upper bound for the summand `|c * z + d| ^ (-k)`, as a product of a function of `z` and a function of `c, d`.

name: summable_one_div_norm_rpow
informal: The function `ℤ ^ 2 → ℝ` given by `x ↦ ‖x‖ ^ (-k)` is summable if `2 < k`. We prove this by splitting into boxes using `Finset.box`.
signature: {k : ℝ} (hk : 2 < k) : Summable fun (x : Fin 2 → ℤ) ↦ ‖x‖ ^ (-k)

name: summable_jacobiTheta₂_term_iff
informal: The series defining the theta function is summable if and only if `0 < im τ`.
signature: (z τ : ℂ) : Summable (jacobiTheta₂_term · z τ) ↔ 0 < im τ

name: jacobiTheta₂_add_right
informal: The two-variable Jacobi theta function is periodic in `τ` with period 2.
signature: (z τ : ℂ) : jacobiTheta₂ z (τ + 2) = jacobiTheta₂ z τ

name: jacobiTheta₂_add_left
informal: The two-variable Jacobi theta function is periodic in `z` with period 1.
signature: (z τ : ℂ) : jacobiTheta₂ (z + 1) τ = jacobiTheta₂ z τ

name: qExpansion_eq_qExpansion_discriminant_mul
informal: The q-expansion of a level-1 modular form whose zeroth coefficient vanishes factors as the q-expansion of `Δ` times the q-expansion of the corresponding form of weight `k - 12` obtained via `discriminantEquiv`.
signature: (f : ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k) (hcusp : (qExpansion 1 f).coeff 0 = 0) : qExpansion 1 f = qExpansion 1 discriminant * qExpansion 1 (CuspForm.discriminantEquiv (toCuspForm f hcusp))

name: ModularForm.levelOne_odd_weight_rank_zero
informal: Modular forms of odd weight for `𝒮ℒ` are zero-dimensional.
signature: (hk : Odd k) : Module.rank ℂ (ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k) = 0

name: CuspForm.exists_smul_discriminant_of_weight_eq_twelve
informal: Every weight 12 cusp form for `𝒮ℒ` is a scalar multiple of the discriminant.
signature: (f : CuspForm 𝒮ℒ 12) : ∃ c : ℂ, c • CuspForm.discriminant = f

name: ModularForm.rank_eq_one_add_rank_cuspForm
informal: For even `k ≥ 3`, the rank of `𝒮ℒ` modular forms is one more than the rank of cusp forms.
signature: {k : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hk2 : Even k) : Module.rank ℂ (ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k) = 1 + Module.rank ℂ (CuspForm 𝒮ℒ k)

name: dimension_level_one
informal: The dimension formula for `𝒮ℒ` modular forms of even weight.
signature: (k : ℕ) (hk2 : Even k) : Module.rank ℂ (ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k) = if k ≡ 2 [MOD 12] then k / 12 else k / 12 + 1

name: sturm_bound_levelOne_nat
informal: **Sturm bound for level-1 modular forms (natural weight).** If a modular form `f` of weight `k : ℕ` has q-expansion of order strictly greater than `k / 12`, then `f` is identically zero.
signature: {k : ℕ} {f : ModularForm 𝒮ℒ (k : ℤ)} (h : (↑(k / 12) : ℕ∞) < (qExpansion 1 f).order) : f = 0

name: qExpansion_coeff_zero
informal: The zeroth coefficient of the `q`-expansion of a cusp form vanishes.
signature: (hh : 0 < h) (hΓ : h ∈ Γ.strictPeriods) : (qExpansion h f).coeff 0 = 0

name: sum_one_eq_card_units
informal: The sum over all values of the trivial multiplicative character on a finite ring is the cardinality of its unit group.
signature: [DecidableEq R] : (∑ a, (1 : MulChar R R') a) = Fintype.card Rˣ

name: realSpace.volume_eq_zero
informal: The set of points in the `realSpace` that are equal to `0` at a fixed place has volume zero.
signature: [NumberField K] (w : InfinitePlace K) : volume ({x : realSpace K | x w = 0}) = 0

name: liesOver_extensionEmbedding
informal: Assume that `w.Completion` forms an algebra over `v.Completion` with continuous scalar action, such that `IsScalarTower K v.Completion w.Completion`. If `w.embedding : L →+* ℂ` extends `v.embedding : K →+* ℂ`, then the corresponding embeddings to completions are also extensions.
signature: [ContinuousSMul v.Completion w.Completion] [ComplexEmbedding.LiesOver w.embedding v.embedding] : ComplexEmbedding.LiesOver (extensionEmbedding w) (extensionEmbedding v) where over

name: sum_inertiaDeg_eq_finrank
informal: The degree of `L` over `K` is equal to the sum of the inertia degrees of the places over `v`.
signature: [NumberField K] [NumberField L] : ∑ w ∈ v.placesOver L, v.inertiaDeg w = Module.finrank K L

name: discr_prime_pow
informal: We compute the absolute discriminant of a `p ^ k`-th cyclotomic field. Beware that in the cases `p ^ k = 1` and `p ^ k = 2` the formula uses `1 / 2 = 0` and `0 - 1 = 0`. See also the results below.
signature: [IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ k} ℚ K] : haveI : NumberField K

name: discr_prime_pow_succ
informal: We compute the absolute discriminant of a `p ^ (k + 1)`-th cyclotomic field. Beware that in the case `p ^ k = 2` the formula uses `1 / 2 = 0`. See also the results below.
signature: [IsCyclotomicExtension {p ^ (k + 1)} ℚ K] : haveI : NumberField K

name: discr_prime
informal: We compute the absolute discriminant of a `p`-th cyclotomic field where `p` is prime.
signature: [IsCyclotomicExtension {p} ℚ K] : haveI : NumberField K

name: IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.torsionOrder_eq
informal: The order of the torsion group of the `n`-th cyclotomic field is `n` if `n` is even and `2n` if `n` is odd.
signature: [NeZero n] [NumberField K] [hK : IsCyclotomicExtension {n} ℚ K] : torsionOrder K = if Even n then n else 2 * n

name: nrRealPlaces_eq_zero
informal: If `K` is an `n`-th cyclotomic extension of `ℚ`, where `2 < n`, then there are no real places of `K`.
signature: [IsCyclotomicExtension {n} ℚ K] (hn : 2 < n) : haveI

name: denseRange_algebraMap
informal: *Weak approximation for the infinite adele ring* The number field $K$ is dense in the infinite adele ring $\prod_v K_v$.
signature: [NumberField K] : DenseRange <| algebraMap K K∞

name: denseRange_algebraMap_pi
informal: *Weak approximation for infinite places* The number field `K` is dense when embedded diagonally in the product `(v : InfinitePlace K) → WithAbs v.1`, in which `WithAbs v.1` represents `K` equipped with the topology coming from the infinite place `v`.
signature: [NumberField K] : DenseRange <| algebraMap K ((v : InfinitePlace K) → WithAbs v.1)

name: unramifedPlacesOver_ncard_add_eq_finrank
informal: The degree of `L` over `K` is equal to the number of unramified places over `v` plus twice the number of ramified places over `v`.
signature: [NumberField K] [NumberField L] : (unramifiedPlacesOver L v).ncard + 2 * (ramifiedPlacesOver L v).ncard = Module.finrank K L

name: dvd_norm
informal: If `L/K` is a finite Galois extension of fields, then, for all `(x : 𝓞 L)` we have that `x ∣ algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L) (norm K x)`.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] (x : 𝓞 L) : x ∣ algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L) (norm K x)

name: equiv_real_or_padic
informal: **Ostrowski's Theorem**: every absolute value (with values in `ℝ`) on `ℚ` is equivalent to either the standard absolute value or a `p`-adic absolute value for a prime `p`.
signature: (f : AbsoluteValue ℚ ℝ) (hf_nontriv : f.IsNontrivial) : f ≈ real ∨ ∃! p, ∃ (_ : Fact p.Prime), f ≈ (padic p)

name: not_real_isEquiv_padic
informal: The standard absolute value on `ℚ` is not equivalent to any `p`-adic absolute value.
signature: (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ¬ real.IsEquiv (padic p)

name: mahlerSeries_apply_nat
informal: The value of a Mahler series at a natural number `n` is given by the finite sum of the first `m` terms, for any `n ≤ m`.
signature: (ha : Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 0)) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) : mahlerSeries a (m : ℤ_[p]) = ∑ i ∈ range (n + 1), m.choose i • a i

name: fwdDiff_mahlerSeries
informal: The coefficients of a Mahler series can be recovered from the sum by taking forward differences at `0`.
signature: (ha : Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 0)) (n) : Δ_[1]^[n] (mahlerSeries a) (0 : ℤ_[p]) = a n

name: triangle_ineq
informal: The `p`-adic norm respects the triangle inequality: the norm of `p + q` is at most the norm of `p` plus the norm of `q`.
signature: (q r : ℚ) : padicNorm p (q + r) ≤ padicNorm p q + padicNorm p r

name: int_eq_one_iff
informal: The `p`-adic norm of an integer `m` is one iff `p` doesn't divide `m`.
signature: (m : ℤ) : padicNorm p m = 1 ↔ ¬(p : ℤ) ∣ m

name: nat_eq_one_iff
informal: The `p`-adic norm of a natural `m` is one iff `p` doesn't divide `m`.
signature: (m : ℕ) : padicNorm p m = 1 ↔ ¬p ∣ m

name: nonarchimedean'
informal: Theorems about `padicNormE` are named with a `'` so the names do not conflict with the equivalent theorems about `norm` (`‖ ‖`).
signature: (q r : ℚ_[p]) : padicNormE (q + r : ℚ_[p]) ≤ max (padicNormE q) (padicNormE r)

name: add_eq_max_of_ne'
informal: Theorems about `padicNormE` are named with a `'` so the names do not conflict with the equivalent theorems about `norm` (`‖ ‖`).
signature: {q r : ℚ_[p]} : padicNormE q ≠ padicNormE r → padicNormE (q + r : ℚ_[p]) = max (padicNormE q) (padicNormE r)

name: le_padicValRat_add_of_le
informal: Sufficient conditions to show that the `p`-adic valuation of `q` is less than or equal to the `p`-adic valuation of `q + r`.
signature: {q r : ℚ} (hqr : q + r ≠ 0) (h : padicValRat p q ≤ padicValRat p r) : padicValRat p q ≤ padicValRat p (q + r)

name: min_le_padicValRat_add
informal: The minimum of the valuations of `q` and `r` is at most the valuation of `q + r`.
signature: {q r : ℚ} (hqr : q + r ≠ 0) : min (padicValRat p q) (padicValRat p r) ≤ padicValRat p (q + r)

name: padicValNat_le_nat_log
informal: The p-adic valuation of `n` is less than or equal to its logarithm w.r.t. `p`.
signature: (n : ℕ) : padicValNat p n ≤ Nat.log p n

name: nat_log_eq_padicValNat_iff
informal: The p-adic valuation of `n` is equal to the logarithm w.r.t. `p` iff `n` is less than `p` raised to one plus the p-adic valuation of `n`.
signature: {n : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hn : n ≠ 0) : Nat.log p n = padicValNat p n ↔ n < p ^ (padicValNat p n + 1)

name: Nat.log_ne_padicValNat_succ
informal: This is false for prime numbers other than 2: for `p = 3`, `n = 1`, one has `log 3 1 = padicValNat 3 2 = 0`.
signature: {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : log 2 n ≠ padicValNat 2 (n + 1)

name: padicValNat_eq_zero_of_mem_Ioo
informal: The `p`-adic valuation of `m` equals zero if it is between `p * k` and `p * (k + 1)` for some `k`.
signature: {m k : ℕ} (hm : m ∈ Set.Ioo (p * k) (p * (k + 1))) : padicValNat p m = 0

name: lift_spec
informal: One part of the universal property of `ℤ_[p]` as a projective limit. See also `PadicInt.lift_unique`.
signature: (n : ℕ) : (toZModPow n).comp (lift f_compat) = f n

name: is_pell_solution_iff_mem_unitary
informal: An element of `ℤ√d` has norm one (i.e., `a.re^2 - d*a.im^2 = 1`) if and only if it is contained in the submonoid of unitary elements. TODO: merge this result with `Pell.isPell_iff_mem_unitary`.
signature: {d : ℤ} {a : ℤ√d} : a.re ^ 2 - d * a.im ^ 2 = 1 ↔ a ∈ unitary (ℤ√d)

name: y_mul_pos
informal: The set of solutions with `x` and `y` positive is closed under multiplication.
signature: {a b : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) (hbx : 0 < b.x) (hby : 0 < b.y) : 0 < (a * b).y

name: x_pow_pos
informal: If `(x, y)` is a solution with `x` positive, then all its powers with natural exponents have positive `x`.
signature: {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (n : ℕ) : 0 < (a ^ n).x

name: y_pow_succ_pos
informal: If `(x, y)` is a solution with `x` and `y` positive, then all its powers with positive natural exponents have positive `y`.
signature: {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) (n : ℕ) : 0 < (a ^ n.succ).y

name: y_zpow_pos
informal: If `(x, y)` is a solution with `x` and `y` positive, then all its powers with positive exponents have positive `y`.
signature: {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) {n : ℤ} (hn : 0 < n) : 0 < (a ^ n).y

name: x_zpow_pos
informal: If `(x, y)` is a solution with `x` positive, then all its powers have positive `x`.
signature: {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (n : ℤ) : 0 < (a ^ n).x

name: sign_y_zpow_eq_sign_of_x_pos_of_y_pos
informal: If `(x, y)` is a solution with `x` and `y` positive, then the `y` component of any power has the same sign as the exponent.
signature: {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) (n : ℤ) : (a ^ n).y.sign = n.sign

name: exists_of_not_isSquare
informal: If `d` is a positive integer that is not a square, then there is a nontrivial solution to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1`.
signature: (h₀ : 0 < d) (hd : ¬IsSquare d) : ∃ x y : ℤ, x ^ 2 - d * y ^ 2 = 1 ∧ y ≠ 0

name: exists_iff_not_isSquare
informal: If `d` is a positive integer, then there is a nontrivial solution to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1` if and only if `d` is not a square.
signature: (h₀ : 0 < d) : (∃ x y : ℤ, x ^ 2 - d * y ^ 2 = 1 ∧ y ≠ 0) ↔ ¬IsSquare d

name: exists_nontrivial_of_not_isSquare
informal: If `d` is a positive integer that is not a square, then there exists a nontrivial solution to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1`.
signature: (h₀ : 0 < d) (hd : ¬IsSquare d) : ∃ a : Solution₁ d, a ≠ 1 ∧ a ≠ -1

name: exists_pos_of_not_isSquare
informal: If `d` is a positive integer that is not a square, then there exists a solution to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1` with `x > 1` and `y > 0`.
signature: (h₀ : 0 < d) (hd : ¬IsSquare d) : ∃ a : Solution₁ d, 1 < a.x ∧ 0 < a.y

name: exists_of_not_isSquare
informal: If `d` is positive and not a square, then a fundamental solution exists.
signature: (h₀ : 0 < d) (hd : ¬IsSquare d) : ∃ a : Solution₁ d, IsFundamental a

name: y_strictMono
informal: The map sending an integer `n` to the `y`-coordinate of `a^n` for a fundamental solution `a` is strictly increasing.
signature: {a : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a) : StrictMono fun n : ℤ => (a ^ n).y

name: zpow_ne_neg_zpow
informal: A power of a fundamental solution is never equal to the negative of a power of this fundamental solution.
signature: {a : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a) {n n' : ℤ} : a ^ n ≠ -a ^ n'

name: x_le_x
informal: The `x`-coordinate of a fundamental solution is a lower bound for the `x`-coordinate of any positive solution.
signature: {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 1 < a.x) : a₁.x ≤ a.x

name: y_le_y
informal: The `y`-coordinate of a fundamental solution is a lower bound for the `y`-coordinate of any positive solution.
signature: {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 1 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) : a₁.y ≤ a.y

name: mul_inv_y_nonneg
informal: If we multiply a positive solution with the inverse of a fundamental solution, the `y`-coordinate remains nonnegative.
signature: {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 1 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) : 0 ≤ (a * a₁⁻¹).y

name: mul_inv_x_pos
informal: If we multiply a positive solution with the inverse of a fundamental solution, the `x`-coordinate stays positive.
signature: {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 1 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) : 0 < (a * a₁⁻¹).x

name: mul_inv_x_lt_x
informal: If we multiply a positive solution with the inverse of a fundamental solution, the `x`-coordinate decreases.
signature: {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 1 < a.x) (hay : 0 < a.y) : (a * a₁⁻¹).x < a.x

name: eq_pow_of_nonneg
informal: Any nonnegative solution is a power with nonnegative exponent of a fundamental solution.
signature: {a₁ : Solution₁ d} (h : IsFundamental a₁) {a : Solution₁ d} (hax : 0 < a.x) (hay : 0 ≤ a.y) : ∃ n : ℕ, a = a₁ ^ n

name: existsUnique_pos_generator
informal: When `d` is positive and not a square, then the group of solutions to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1` has a unique positive generator (up to sign).
signature: (h₀ : 0 < d) (hd : ¬IsSquare d) : ∃! a₁ : Solution₁ d, 1 < a₁.x ∧ 0 < a₁.y ∧ ∀ a : Solution₁ d, ∃ n : ℤ, a = a₁ ^ n ∨ a = -a₁ ^ n

name: pos_generator_iff_fundamental
informal: A positive solution is a generator (up to sign) of the group of all solutions to the Pell equation `x^2 - d*y^2 = 1` if and only if it is a fundamental solution.
signature: (a : Solution₁ d) : (1 < a.x ∧ 0 < a.y ∧ ∀ b : Solution₁ d, ∃ n : ℤ, b = a ^ n ∨ b = -a ^ n) ↔ IsFundamental a

name: eq_pell
informal: Every solution to **Pell's equation** is recursively obtained from the initial solution `(1,0)` using the recursion `pell`.
signature: {x y : ℕ} (hp : x * x - d a1 * y * y = 1) : ∃ n, x = xn a1 n ∧ y = yn a1 n

name: primesBelow_card_eq_primeCounting'
informal: The cardinality of the finset `primesBelow n` equals the counting function `primeCounting'` at `n`.
signature: (n : ℕ) : #n.primesBelow = π' n

name: exists_prime_gt_modEq_one
informal: For any positive `k : ℕ` there exists an arbitrarily large prime `p` such that `p ≡ 1 [MOD k]`.
signature: {k : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (hk0 : k ≠ 0) : ∃ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p ∧ n < p ∧ p ≡ 1 [MOD k]

name: infinite_setOfPred_prime_modEq_one
informal: For any positive `k : ℕ` there are infinitely many primes `p` such that `p ≡ 1 [MOD k]`.
signature: {k : ℕ} (hk0 : k ≠ 0) : Set.Infinite {p : ℕ | Nat.Prime p ∧ p ≡ 1 [MOD k]}

name: pythagoreanTriple_comm
informal: Pythagorean triples are interchangeable, i.e `x * x + y * y = y * y + x * x = z * z`. This comes from additive commutativity.
signature: {x y z : ℤ} : PythagoreanTriple x y z ↔ PythagoreanTriple y x z

name: coprime_classification'
informal: By assuming `x` is odd and `z` is positive we get a slightly more precise classification of the Pythagorean triple `x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = z ^ 2`.
signature: {x y z : ℤ} (h : PythagoreanTriple x y z) (h_coprime : Int.gcd x y = 1) (h_parity : x % 2 = 1) (h_pos : 0 < z) : ∃ m n, x = m ^ 2 - n ^ 2 ∧ y = 2 * m * n ∧ z = m ^ 2 + n ^ 2 ∧ Int.gcd m n = 1 ∧ (m % 2 = 0 ∧ n % 2 = 1 ∨ m % 2 = 1 ∧ n % 2 = 0) ∧ 0 ≤ m

name: inertiaDeg'_pos'
informal: Variant with a weaker constraint, but on the prime upstairs instead.
signature: [P.IsPrime] [Module.Finite R S] [P.LiesOver p] : 0 < inertiaDeg' p P

name: isUnramifiedAt_bot
informal: In characteristic zero the generic point is unramified: if `S` is a domain that is integral over a characteristic-zero domain `R` and `R → S` is injective, then `S` is unramified at the zero ideal.
signature: [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S] [Module.IsTorsionFree R S] [CharZero R] [Algebra.IsIntegral R S] : IsUnramifiedAt R (⊥ : Ideal S)

name: isUnramifiedIn_bot
informal: In characteristic zero, the zero ideal is unramified in an integral domain extension.
signature: [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S] [FaithfulSMul R S] [CharZero R] [Algebra.IsIntegral R S] : IsUnramifiedIn S (⊥ : Ideal R)

name: isUnramifiedIn_iff_forall_ramificationIdx_eq_one
informal: A nonzero ideal of `R` is unramified in `S` if and only if every prime ideal of `S` lying over it has ramification index `1`.
signature: [IsDomain R] [Module.Finite ℤ R] [CharZero R] [EssFiniteType R S] [Algebra.IsIntegral R S] {𝔭 : Ideal R} : IsUnramifiedIn S 𝔭 ↔ ∀ (𝔓 : Ideal S) [𝔓.IsPrime], 𝔓.LiesOver 𝔭 → Ideal.ramificationIdx 𝔓 R = 1

name: compl_beattySeq
informal: Generalization of Rayleigh's theorem on Beatty sequences. Let `r` be a real number greater than 1, and `1/r + 1/s = 1`. Then the complement of `B_r` is `B'_s`.
signature: {r s : ℝ} (hrs : r.HolderConjugate s) : {beattySeq r k | k}ᶜ = {beattySeq' s k | k}

name: beattySeq_symmDiff_beattySeq'_pos
informal: Generalization of Rayleigh's theorem on Beatty sequences. Let `r` be a real number greater than 1, and `1/r + 1/s = 1`. Then `B⁺_r` and `B⁺'_s` partition the positive integers.
signature: {r s : ℝ} (hrs : r.HolderConjugate s) : {beattySeq r k | k > 0} ∆ {beattySeq' s k | k > 0} = {n | 0 < n}

name: Irrational.beattySeq_symmDiff_beattySeq_pos
informal: **Rayleigh's theorem** on Beatty sequences. Let `r` be an irrational number greater than 1, and `1/r + 1/s = 1`. Then `B⁺_r` and `B⁺_s` partition the positive integers.
signature: {r s : ℝ} (hrs : r.HolderConjugate s) (hr : Irrational r) : {beattySeq r k | k > 0} ∆ {beattySeq s k | k > 0} = {n | 0 < n}

name: irrational_nrt_of_notint_nrt
informal: If `x^n`, `n > 0`, is integer and is not the `n`-th power of an integer, then `x` is irrational.
signature: {x : ℝ} (n : ℕ) (m : ℤ) (hxr : x ^ n = m) (hv : ¬∃ y : ℤ, x = y) (hnpos : 0 < n) : Irrational x

name: irrational_nrt_of_n_not_dvd_multiplicity
informal: If `x^n = m` is an integer and `n` does not divide the `multiplicity p m`, then `x` is irrational.
signature: {x : ℝ} (n : ℕ) {m : ℤ} (hm : m ≠ 0) (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hxr : x ^ n = m) (hv : multiplicity (p : ℤ) m % n ≠ 0) : Irrational x

name: mainSum_lambdaSquared_eq_sum_sum_mul
informal: The main sum we get from Λ² coefficients is a quadratic form. Used to prove the Selberg sieve identity by choosing weights that maximize this sum.
signature: (w : ℕ → ℝ) : s.mainSum (lambdaSquared w) = ∑ d1 ∈ divisors s.prodPrimes, ∑ d2 ∈ divisors s.prodPrimes, s.nu d1 * w d1 * s.nu d2 * w d2 * (s.nu (d1.gcd d2))⁻¹

name: mainSum_lambdaSquared_eq_sum_mul_sum_sq
informal: The main sum we get from Λ² coefficients can be written as a diagonalized quadratic form with eigenvalues given by `1/selbergTerms`
signature: (w : ℕ → ℝ) : s.mainSum (lambdaSquared w) = ∑ l ∈ divisors s.prodPrimes, (s.selbergTerms l)⁻¹ * (∑ d ∈ divisors s.prodPrimes, if l ∣ d then s.nu d * w d else 0) ^ 2

name: prod_mem_factoredNumbers
informal: The product of the prime factors of `n` that are in `s` is an `s`-factored number.
signature: (s : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) : (n.primeFactorsList.filter (· ∈ s)).prod ∈ factoredNumbers s

name: factoredNumbers_compl
informal: The non-zero non-`s`-factored numbers are `≥ N` when `s` contains all primes less than `N`.
signature: {N : ℕ} {s : Finset ℕ} (h : primesBelow N ≤ s) : (factoredNumbers s)ᶜ \ {0} ⊆ {n | N ≤ n}

name: smoothNumbers_eq_factoredNumbers
informal: The `n`-smooth numbers agree with the `Finset.range n`-factored numbers.
signature: (n : ℕ) : smoothNumbers n = factoredNumbers (Finset.range n)

name: smoothNumbers_eq_factoredNumbers_primesBelow
informal: The `n`-smooth numbers agree with the `primesBelow n`-factored numbers.
signature: (n : ℕ) : smoothNumbers n = factoredNumbers n.primesBelow

name: primeFactors_subset_of_mem_smoothNumbers
informal: The `Finset` of prime factors of an `n`-smooth number is contained in the `Finset` of primes below `n`.
signature: {m n : ℕ} (hms : m ∈ n.smoothNumbers) : m.primeFactors ⊆ n.primesBelow

name: prod_mem_smoothNumbers
informal: The product of the prime factors of `n` that are less than `N` is an `N`-smooth number.
signature: (n N : ℕ) : (n.primeFactorsList.filter (· < N)).prod ∈ smoothNumbers N

name: smoothNumbers_succ
informal: The sets of `N`-smooth and of `(N+1)`-smooth numbers are the same when `N` is not prime. See `Nat.equivProdNatSmoothNumbers` for when `N` is prime.
signature: {N : ℕ} (hN : ¬ N.Prime) : (N + 1).smoothNumbers = N.smoothNumbers

name: eq_prod_primes_mul_sq_of_mem_smoothNumbers
informal: A `k`-smooth number can be written as a square times a product of distinct primes `< k`.
signature: {n k : ℕ} (h : n ∈ smoothNumbers k) : ∃ s ∈ k.primesBelow.powerset, ∃ m, n = m ^ 2 * (s.prod id)

name: roughNumbersUpTo_eq_biUnion
informal: The set of `k`-rough numbers `≤ N` can be written as the union of the sets of multiples `≤ N` of primes `k ≤ p ≤ N`.
signature: (N k) : roughNumbersUpTo N k = ((N + 1).primesBelow \ k.primesBelow).biUnion fun p ↦ {m ∈ Finset.range (N + 1) | m ≠ 0 ∧ p ∣ m}

name: roughNumbersUpTo_card_le
informal: The cardinality of the set of `k`-rough numbers `≤ N` is bounded by the sum of `⌊N/p⌋` over the primes `k ≤ p ≤ N`.
signature: (N k : ℕ) : #(roughNumbersUpTo N k) ≤ ((N + 1).primesBelow \ k.primesBelow).sum (fun p ↦ N / p)

name: Nat.euler_four_squares
informal: **Euler's four-square identity**, a version for natural numbers.
signature: (a b c d x y z w : ℕ) : ((a : ℤ) * x - b * y - c * z - d * w).natAbs ^ 2 + ((a : ℤ) * y + b * x + c * w - d * z).natAbs ^ 2 + ((a : ℤ) * z - b * w + c * x + d * y).natAbs ^ 2 + ((a : ℤ) * w + b * z - c * y + d * x).natAbs ^ 2 = (a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) * (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + z ^ 2 + w ^ 2)

name: one_half_le_sum_primes_ge_one_div
informal: The sum over primes `k ≤ p ≤ 4^(π(k-1)+1)` over `1/p` (as a real number) is at least `1/2`.
signature: (k : ℕ) : 1 / 2 ≤ ∑ p ∈ (4 ^ (k.primesBelow.card + 1)).succ.primesBelow \ k.primesBelow, (1 / p : ℝ)

name: Nat.Primes.summable_rpow
informal: The series over `p^r` for primes `p` converges if and only if `r < -1`.
signature: {r : ℝ} : Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes ↦ (p : ℝ) ^ r) ↔ r < -1

name: Nat.Prime.sq_add_sq
informal: **Fermat's theorem on the sum of two squares**. Every prime not congruent to 3 mod 4 is the sum of two squares. Also known as **Fermat's Christmas theorem**.
signature: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p % 4 ≠ 3) : ∃ a b : ℕ, a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 = p

name: sq_add_sq_mul
informal: The set of sums of two squares is closed under multiplication in any commutative ring. See also `sq_add_sq_mul_sq_add_sq`.
signature: {R} [CommRing R] {a b x y u v : R} (ha : a = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) (hb : b = u ^ 2 + v ^ 2) : ∃ r s : R, a * b = r ^ 2 + s ^ 2

name: Nat.sq_add_sq_mul
informal: The set of natural numbers that are sums of two squares is closed under multiplication.
signature: {a b x y u v : ℕ} (ha : a = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) (hb : b = u ^ 2 + v ^ 2) : ∃ r s : ℕ, a * b = r ^ 2 + s ^ 2

name: ZMod.isSquare_neg_one_mul
informal: If `-1` is a square modulo coprime natural numbers `m` and `n`, then `-1` is also a square modulo `m*n`.
signature: {m n : ℕ} (hc : m.Coprime n) (hm : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod m)) (hn : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n)) : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod (m * n))

name: Nat.eq_sq_add_sq_of_isSquare_mod_neg_one
informal: If `-1` is a square modulo the natural number `n`, then `n` is a sum of two squares.
signature: {n : ℕ} (h : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n)) : ∃ x y : ℕ, n = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2

name: ZMod.isSquare_neg_one_of_eq_sq_add_sq_of_isCoprime
informal: If the integer `n` is a sum of two squares of coprime integers, then `-1` is a square modulo `n`.
signature: {n x y : ℤ} (h : n = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) (hc : IsCoprime x y) : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n.natAbs)

name: ZMod.isSquare_neg_one_of_eq_sq_add_sq_of_coprime
informal: If the natural number `n` is a sum of two squares of coprime natural numbers, then `-1` is a square modulo `n`.
signature: {n x y : ℕ} (h : n = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) (hc : x.Coprime y) : IsSquare (-1 : ZMod n)

name: partialSum_add_remainder
informal: Split the sum defining a Liouville number into the first `k` terms and the rest.
signature: {m : ℝ} (hm : 1 < m) (k : ℕ) : partialSum m k + remainder m k = liouvilleNumber m

name: remainder_lt'
informal: An upper estimate on the remainder. This estimate works with `m ∈ ℝ` satisfying `1 < m` and is stronger than the estimate `LiouvilleNumber.remainder_lt` below. However, the latter estimate is more useful for the proof.

name: remainder_lt
informal: An upper estimate on the remainder. This estimate works with `m ∈ ℝ` satisfying `2 ≤ m` and is weaker than the estimate `LiouvilleNumber.remainder_lt'` above. However, this estimate is more useful for the proof.
signature: (n : ℕ) {m : ℝ} (m2 : 2 ≤ m) : remainder m n < 1 / (m ^ n !) ^ n

name: partialSum_eq_rat
informal: The sum of the `k` initial terms of the Liouville number to base `m` is a ratio of natural numbers where the denominator is `m ^ k!`.
signature: {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (k : ℕ) : ∃ p : ℕ, partialSum m k = p / ((m ^ k ! :) : ℝ)

name: mono
informal: If a number is Liouville with exponent `p`, then it is Liouville with any smaller exponent.
signature: (h : LiouvilleWith p x) (hle : q ≤ p) : LiouvilleWith q x

name: mul_rat
informal: The product of a Liouville number and a nonzero rational number is again a Liouville number.

name: mul_rat_iff
informal: The product `x * r`, `r : ℚ`, `r ≠ 0`, is a Liouville number with exponent `p` if and only if `x` satisfies the same condition.
signature: (hr : r ≠ 0) : LiouvilleWith p (x * r) ↔ LiouvilleWith p x

name: rat_mul_iff
informal: The product `r * x`, `r : ℚ`, `r ≠ 0`, is a Liouville number with exponent `p` if and only if `x` satisfies the same condition.
signature: (hr : r ≠ 0) : LiouvilleWith p (r * x) ↔ LiouvilleWith p x

name: Disjoint.of_orderEmbedding
