signature: [OrderBot α] [OrderBot β] {a₁ a₂ : α} : Disjoint (f a₁) (f a₂) → Disjoint a₁ a₂

name: Codisjoint.of_orderEmbedding
informal: If the images by an order embedding of two elements are codisjoint, then they are themselves codisjoint.
signature: [OrderTop α] [OrderTop β] {a₁ a₂ : α} : Codisjoint (f a₁) (f a₂) → Codisjoint a₁ a₂

name: IsCompl.of_orderEmbedding
informal: If the images by an order embedding of two elements are complements, then they are themselves complements.
signature: [BoundedOrder α] [BoundedOrder β] {a₁ a₂ : α} : IsCompl (f a₁) (f a₂) → IsCompl a₁ a₂

name: OrderEmbedding.range_inj
informal: Two order embeddings on a well-order are equal provided that their ranges are equal.
signature: [LinearOrder α] [WellFoundedLT α] [Preorder β] {f g : α ↪o β} : Set.range f = Set.range g ↔ f = g

name: eq_or_principal
informal: An initial segment embedding is either an isomorphism, or a principal segment embedding. See also `InitialSeg.ltOrEq`.
signature: [IsWellOrder β s] (f : r ≼i s) : Surjective f ∨ ∃ b, ∀ x, x ∈ Set.range f ↔ s x b

name: le_iff_reflTransGen_covBy
informal: In a locally finite partial order, `≤` is the reflexive transitive closure of `⋖`.
signature: [PartialOrder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] {x y : α} : x ≤ y ↔ ReflTransGen (· ⋖ ·) x y

name: monotone_iff_forall_wcovBy
informal: A function from a locally finite preorder is monotone if and only if it is monotone when restricted to pairs satisfying `a ⩿ b`.
signature: [Preorder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) : Monotone f ↔ ∀ a b : α, a ⩿ b → f a ≤ f b

name: monotone_iff_forall_covBy
informal: A function from a locally finite partial order is monotone if and only if it is monotone when restricted to pairs satisfying `a ⋖ b`.
signature: [PartialOrder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) : Monotone f ↔ ∀ a b : α, a ⋖ b → f a ≤ f b

name: strictMono_iff_forall_covBy
informal: A function from a locally finite preorder is strictly monotone if and only if it is strictly monotone when restricted to pairs satisfying `a ⋖ b`.
signature: [Preorder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) : StrictMono f ↔ ∀ a b : α, a ⋖ b → f a < f b

name: antitone_iff_forall_wcovBy
informal: A function from a locally finite preorder is antitone if and only if it is antitone when restricted to pairs satisfying `a ⩿ b`.
signature: [Preorder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) : Antitone f ↔ ∀ a b : α, a ⩿ b → f b ≤ f a

name: antitone_iff_forall_covBy
informal: A function from a locally finite partial order is antitone if and only if it is antitone when restricted to pairs satisfying `a ⋖ b`.
signature: [PartialOrder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) : Antitone f ↔ ∀ a b : α, a ⋖ b → f b ≤ f a

name: strictAnti_iff_forall_covBy
informal: A function from a locally finite preorder is strictly antitone if and only if it is strictly antitone when restricted to pairs satisfying `a ⋖ b`.
signature: [Preorder α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) : StrictAnti f ↔ ∀ a b : α, a ⋖ b → f b < f a

name: image_Ico_mod
informal: Note that while this lemma cannot be easily generalized to a type class, it holds for ℤ as well. See `Int.image_Ico_emod` for the ℤ version.
signature: (n a : ℕ) : (Ico n (n + a)).image (· % a) = range a

name: Icc_union_Icc
informal: We cannot replace `<` by `≤` in the hypotheses. Otherwise for `b < a = d < c` the l.h.s. is `∅` and the r.h.s. is `{a}`.
signature: (h₁ : min a b < max c d) (h₂ : min c d < max a b) : Icc a b ∪ Icc c d = Icc (min a c) (max b d)

name: monotone_iterate_of_le_map
informal: If `f` is a monotone map and `x ≤ f x` at some point `x`, then the iterates `f^[n] x` form a monotone sequence.
signature: (hf : Monotone f) (hx : x ≤ f x) : Monotone fun n => f^[n] x

name: antitone_iterate_of_map_le
informal: If `f` is a monotone map and `f x ≤ x` at some point `x`, then the iterates `f^[n] x` form an antitone sequence.
signature: (hf : Monotone f) (hx : f x ≤ x) : Antitone fun n => f^[n] x

name: strictMono_iterate_of_lt_map
informal: If `f` is a strictly monotone map and `x < f x` at some point `x`, then the iterates `f^[n] x` form a strictly monotone sequence.
signature: (hf : StrictMono f) (hx : x < f x) : StrictMono fun n => f^[n] x

name: strictAnti_iterate_of_map_lt
informal: If `f` is a strictly antitone map and `f x < x` at some point `x`, then the iterates `f^[n] x` form a strictly antitone sequence.
signature: (hf : StrictMono f) (hx : f x < x) : StrictAnti fun n => f^[n] x

name: krullDim_eq_iSup_height_add_coheight_of_nonempty
informal: The Krull dimension is the supremum of the elements' height plus coheight.
signature: [Nonempty α] : krullDim α = ↑(⨆ (a : α), height a + coheight a)

name: exists_lt_of_limsup_le
informal: If `Filter.limsup u atTop ≤ x`, then for all `ε > 0`, there exists a positive natural number `n` such that `u n < x + ε`.
signature: [AddZeroClass α] [AddLeftStrictMono α] {x ε : α} {u : ℕ → α} (hu_bdd : IsBoundedUnder LE.le atTop u) (hu : Filter.limsup u atTop ≤ x) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ n : PNat, u n < x + ε

name: exists_lt_of_le_liminf
informal: If `x ≤ Filter.liminf u atTop`, then for all `ε < 0`, there exists a positive natural number `n` such that ` x + ε < u n`.
signature: [AddZeroClass α] [AddLeftStrictMono α] {x ε : α} {u : ℕ → α} (hu_bdd : IsBoundedUnder GE.ge atTop u) (hu : x ≤ Filter.liminf u atTop) (hε : ε < 0) : ∃ n : PNat, x + ε < u n

name: exists_strictMono'
informal: If `α` is a preorder with no maximal elements, then there exists a strictly monotone function `ℕ → α` with any prescribed value of `f 0`.
signature: [NoMaxOrder α] (a : α) : ∃ f : ℕ → α, StrictMono f ∧ f 0 = a

name: exists_strictAnti'
informal: If `α` is a preorder with no maximal elements, then there exists a strictly antitone function `ℕ → α` with any prescribed value of `f 0`.
signature: [NoMinOrder α] (a : α) : ∃ f : ℕ → α, StrictAnti f ∧ f 0 = a

name: exists_strictMono
informal: If `α` is a nonempty preorder with no maximal elements, then there exists a strictly monotone function `ℕ → α`.
signature: [Nonempty α] [NoMaxOrder α] : ∃ f : ℕ → α, StrictMono f

name: exists_strictAnti
informal: If `α` is a nonempty preorder with no minimal elements, then there exists a strictly antitone function `ℕ → α`.
signature: [Nonempty α] [NoMinOrder α] : ∃ f : ℕ → α, StrictAnti f

name: Nat.stabilises_of_monotone
informal: A monotone function `f : ℕ → ℕ` bounded by `b`, which is constant after stabilising for the first time, stabilises in at most `b` steps.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℕ} {b n : ℕ} (hfmono : Monotone f) (hfb : ∀ m, f m ≤ b) (hfstab : ∀ m, f m = f (m + 1) → f (m + 1) = f (m + 2)) (hbn : b ≤ n) : f n = f b

name: Nat.stabilises_of_antitone
informal: An antitone function `f : ℕ → ℕ` which is constant after stabilising for the first time, stabilises in at most `f 0` steps. Compared to `WellFoundedLT.antitone_chain_condition`, this lemma requires the extra hypothesis `hfstab` and only applies to `ℕ`-valued functions, but in return it gives an explicit bound on the stabilisation index.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℕ} (hfmono : Antitone f) (hfstab : ∀ m, f m = f (m + 1) → f (m + 1) = f (m + 2)) : ∃ n ≤ f 0, ∀ m, n ≤ m → f m = f n

name: comp_of_bddAbove
informal: A composition `h' ∘ h` is Northcott when `h` is Northcott and preimages of bounded above sets under `h'` are bounded above.
signature: [Preorder β] [LE γ] [Northcott h] (H : ∀ c, BddAbove (h' ⁻¹' {x | x ≤ c})) : Northcott (h' ∘ h) where finite_le c

name: comp_of_finite_fibers
informal: A composition `h' ∘ h` is Northcott when `h'` is Northcott and the fibers of `h` are finite.
signature: [LE γ] [Northcott h'] [Filter.TendstoCofinite h] : Northcott (h' ∘ h) where finite_le c

name: leftOrdContinuous
informal: A left adjoint in a Galois connection is left-continuous in the order-theoretic sense.
signature: (gc : GaloisConnection f g) : LeftOrdContinuous f

name: rightOrdContinuous
informal: A right adjoint in a Galois connection is right-continuous in the order-theoretic sense.
signature: (gc : GaloisConnection f g) : RightOrdContinuous g

name: acc_iff_isEmpty_subtype_mem_range
informal: A value is accessible iff it isn't contained in any infinite decreasing sequence.
signature: {x} : Acc r x ↔ IsEmpty { f : ((· > ·) : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) ↪r r // x ∈ Set.range f } where mp acc

name: Infinite.exists_strictMono_or_strictAnti
informal: Every infinite linear order contains either a strictly increasing or a strictly decreasing sequence indexed by `ℕ`.
signature: (α : Type*) [LinearOrder α] [Infinite α] : ∃ f : ℕ → α, StrictMono f ∨ StrictAnti f

name: Finite.of_wellFoundedLT_wellFoundedGT
informal: A linear order that is well-founded in both directions is finite.
signature: (α : Type*) [LinearOrder α] [WellFoundedLT α] [WellFoundedGT α] : Finite α

name: wellFoundedGT_iff_monotone_chain_condition'
informal: The **monotone chain condition**: a preorder is co-well-founded iff every increasing sequence contains two non-increasing indices. See `wellFoundedGT_iff_monotone_chain_condition` for a stronger version on partial orders.
signature: [Preorder α] : WellFoundedGT α ↔ ∀ a : ℕ →o α, ∃ n, ∀ m, n ≤ m → ¬a n < a m

name: WellFoundedLT.antitone_chain_condition
informal: The **antitone chain** condition: an antitone sequence in a partially-ordered type with well-founded `<` is eventually constant. This is the dual of `WellFoundedGT.monotone_chain_condition`. It is provided for convenience, since it unbundles the antitone property from the order homomorphism.
signature: [PartialOrder α] [WellFoundedLT α] {f : ℕ → α} (hf : Antitone f) : ∃ n, ∀ m, n ≤ m → f n = f m

name: exists_extend_partial'
informal: For any set `t` containing no two distinct related elements, there is a representative function equal to the identity on `t`.
signature: (P : Partition u) (h : ∀ ⦃x y⦄, x ∈ t → y ∈ t → P.Rel x y → x = y) : ∃ f, IsRepFun P f ∧ EqOn f id t

name: lex_desc
informal: If we swap two strictly decreasing values in a function, then the result is lexicographically smaller than the original function.
signature: {α} [Preorder ι] [DecidableEq ι] [LT α] {f : ι → α} {i j : ι} (h₁ : i ≤ j) (h₂ : f j < f i) : toLex (f ∘ Equiv.swap i j) < toLex f

name: colex_asc
informal: If we swap two strictly increasing values in a function, then the result is colexicographically smaller than the original function.
signature: {α} [Preorder ι] [DecidableEq ι] [LT α] {f : ι → α} {i j : ι} (h₁ : i ≤ j) (h₂ : f i < f j) : toColex (f ∘ Equiv.swap i j) < toColex f

name: IsChain.symm
informal: This can be used to turn `IsChain (≥)` into `IsChain (≤)` and vice-versa.
signature: (h : IsChain r s) : IsChain (flip r) s

name: StrictMono.eq_id
informal: A strictly monotone self-map of a finite linear order is the identity.
signature: {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [Finite α] {f : α → α} (hf : StrictMono f) : f = id

name: StrictMono.apply_eq
informal: A strictly monotone self-map of a finite linear order fixes every point.
signature: {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [Finite α] {f : α → α} {x : α} (hf : StrictMono f) : f x = x

name: apply_add_index_le_apply_add_index_nat
informal: In ℕ, two entries in an `LTSeries` differ by at least the difference of their indices. (Expressed in a way that avoids subtraction).
signature: (p : LTSeries ℕ) (i j : Fin (p.length + 1)) (hij : i ≤ j) : p i + j ≤ p j + i

name: apply_add_index_le_apply_add_index_int
informal: In ℤ, two entries in an `LTSeries` differ by at least the difference of their indices. (Expressed in a way that avoids subtraction).
signature: (p : LTSeries ℤ) (i j : Fin (p.length + 1)) (hij : i ≤ j) : p i + j ≤ p j + i

name: head_add_length_le_nat
informal: In ℕ, the head and tail of an `LTSeries` differ at least by the length of the series
signature: (p : LTSeries ℕ) : p.head + p.length ≤ p.last

name: head_add_length_le_int
informal: In ℤ, the head and tail of an `LTSeries` differ at least by the length of the series
signature: (p : LTSeries ℤ) : p.head + p.length ≤ p.last

name: infiniteDimensionalOrder_of_strictMono
informal: If `f : α → β` is a strictly monotonic function and `α` is an infinite-dimensional type then so is `β`.
signature: [Preorder α] [Preorder β] (f : α → β) (hf : StrictMono f) [InfiniteDimensionalOrder α] : InfiniteDimensionalOrder β

name: biUnion_Ici_Ico_map_succ
informal: Union formula for `Set.Ico (f i) (f (Order.succ i))` over `i ∈ Ici a`. See also `iUnion_Ico_map_succ_eq_Ici` for the specialization `a = ⊥`.
signature: [SuccOrder α] [IsSuccArchimedean α] [LinearOrder β] {f : α → β} {a : α} (hf : ∀ i ∈ Ici a, f a ≤ f i) (h2f : ¬BddAbove (f '' Ici a)) : ⋃ i ∈ Ici a, Ico (f i) (f (succ i)) = Ici (f a)

name: biUnion_Ici_Ioc_map_succ
informal: Union formula for `Set.Ioc (f i) (f (Order.succ i))` over `i ∈ Ici a`. See also `iUnion_Ioc_map_succ_eq_Ioi` for the specialization `a = ⊥`.
signature: [SuccOrder α] [IsSuccArchimedean α] [LinearOrder β] {f : α → β} {a : α} (hf : ∀ i ∈ Ici a, f a ≤ f i) (h2f : ¬BddAbove (f '' Ici a)) : ⋃ i ∈ Ici a, Ioc (f i) (f (succ i)) = Ioi (f a)

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ioc_succ
informal: If `α` is a linear succ order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is a monotone function, then the intervals `Set.Ioc (f n) (f (Order.succ n))` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [SuccOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ioc (f n) (f (succ n)))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ico_succ
informal: If `α` is a linear succ order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is a monotone function, then the intervals `Set.Ico (f n) (f (Order.succ n))` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [SuccOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ico (f n) (f (succ n)))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ioo_succ
informal: If `α` is a linear succ order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is a monotone function, then the intervals `Set.Ioo (f n) (f (Order.succ n))` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [SuccOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ioo (f n) (f (succ n)))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ioc_pred
informal: If `α` is a linear pred order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is a monotone function, then the intervals `Set.Ioc (f Order.pred n) (f n)` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [PredOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ioc (f (pred n)) (f n))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ico_pred
informal: If `α` is a linear pred order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is a monotone function, then the intervals `Set.Ico (f Order.pred n) (f n)` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [PredOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ico (f (pred n)) (f n))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ioo_pred
informal: If `α` is a linear pred order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is a monotone function, then the intervals `Set.Ioo (f Order.pred n) (f n)` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [PredOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Monotone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ioo (f (pred n)) (f n))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ioc_succ
informal: If `α` is a linear succ order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is an antitone function, then the intervals `Set.Ioc (f (Order.succ n)) (f n)` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [SuccOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Antitone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ioc (f (succ n)) (f n))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ico_succ
informal: If `α` is a linear succ order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is an antitone function, then the intervals `Set.Ico (f (Order.succ n)) (f n)` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [SuccOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Antitone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ico (f (succ n)) (f n))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ioo_succ
informal: If `α` is a linear succ order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is an antitone function, then the intervals `Set.Ioo (f (Order.succ n)) (f n)` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [SuccOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Antitone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ioo (f (succ n)) (f n))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ioc_pred
informal: If `α` is a linear pred order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is an antitone function, then the intervals `Set.Ioc (f n) (f (Order.pred n))` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [PredOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Antitone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ioc (f n) (f (pred n)))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ico_pred
informal: If `α` is a linear pred order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is an antitone function, then the intervals `Set.Ico (f n) (f (Order.pred n))` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [PredOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Antitone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ico (f n) (f (pred n)))

name: pairwise_disjoint_on_Ioo_pred
informal: If `α` is a linear pred order, `β` is a preorder, and `f : α → β` is an antitone function, then the intervals `Set.Ioo (f n) (f (Order.pred n))` are pairwise disjoint.
signature: [PredOrder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} (hf : Antitone f) : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n => Ioo (f n) (f (pred n)))

name: lift_id'
informal: An order type lifted to a lower or equal universe equals itself.
signature: (o : OrderType.{max u v}) : lift.{u} o = o

name: wellFounded_iff_isEmpty_descending_chain
informal: A relation is well-founded iff it doesn't have any infinite descending chain. See `RelEmbedding.wellFounded_iff_isEmpty` for a version in terms of relation embeddings.
signature: {α} {r : α → α → Prop} : WellFounded r ↔ IsEmpty { f : ℕ → α // ∀ n, r (f (n + 1)) (f n) } where mp

name: StrictMono.id_le
informal: A strictly monotone function `f` on a well-order satisfies `x ≤ f x` for all `x`.
signature: [WellFoundedLT β] {f : β → β} (hf : StrictMono f) : id ≤ f

name: StrictMono.le_id
informal: A strictly monotone function `f` on a cowell-order satisfies `f x ≤ x` for all `x`.
signature: [WellFoundedGT β] {f : β → β} (hf : StrictMono f) : f ≤ id

name: IsPWO.of_linearOrder
informal: If `α` is a linear order with well-founded `<`, then any set in it is a partially well-ordered set. Note this does not hold without the linearity assumption.
signature: [WellFoundedLT α] (s : Set α) : s.IsPWO

name: exists_maximal_of_chains_bounded
informal: **Zorn's lemma** If every chain has an upper bound, then there exists a maximal element.
signature: (h : ∀ c, IsChain r c → ∃ ub, ∀ a ∈ c, a ≺ ub) (trans : ∀ {a b c}, a ≺ b → b ≺ c → a ≺ c) : ∃ m, ∀ a, m ≺ a → a ≺ m

name: IsCoatomic.of_isChain_bounded
informal: **Zorn's lemma**: A partial order is coatomic if every nonempty chain `c`, `⊤ ∉ c`, has an upper bound not equal to `⊤`.
signature: {α : Type*} [PartialOrder α] [OrderTop α] (h : ∀ c : Set α, IsChain (· ≤ ·) c → c.Nonempty → ⊤ ∉ c → ∃ x ≠ ⊤, x ∈ upperBounds c) : IsCoatomic α

name: IsAtomic.of_isChain_bounded
informal: **Zorn's lemma**: A partial order is atomic if every nonempty chain `c`, `⊥ ∉ c`, has a lower bound not equal to `⊥`.
signature: {α : Type*} [PartialOrder α] [OrderBot α] (h : ∀ c : Set α, IsChain (· ≤ ·) c → c.Nonempty → ⊥ ∉ c → ∃ x ≠ ⊥, x ∈ lowerBounds c) : IsAtomic α

name: measurePreserving_ofLp_multivariateGaussian
informal: Up to a measurable equivalence, `projectiveFamily I` is the centered multivariate Gaussian with covariance matrix `covMatrix I`.
signature: (I : Finset ℝ≥0) : MeasurePreserving ofLp (multivariateGaussian 0 (covMatrix I)) (projectiveFamily I) where measurable

name: measurePreserving_toLp_projectiveFamily
informal: Up to a measurable equivalence, `projectiveFamily I` is the centered multivariate Gaussian with covariance matrix `covMatrix I`.
signature: (I : Finset ℝ≥0) : MeasurePreserving (toLp 2) (projectiveFamily I) (multivariateGaussian 0 (covMatrix I)) where measurable

name: measurePreserving_eval_sub_eval_projectiveFamily
informal: The distribution of the increment of the real Brownian motion from time `s` to time `t` is the centered Gaussian with variance `t - s`.
signature: (I : Finset ℝ≥0) (s t : I) : MeasurePreserving (fun x ↦ x s - x t) (projectiveFamily I) (gaussianReal 0 (nndist s.1 t.1)) where measurable

name: measure_cdf
informal: The measure associated to the cdf of a probability measure is the same probability measure.
signature: [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : (cdf μ).measure = μ

name: MeasureTheory.Measure.eq_of_cdf
informal: If two real probability distributions have the same cdf, they are equal.
signature: (μ ν : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν] (h : cdf μ = cdf ν) : μ = ν

name: cond_isProbabilityMeasure
informal: The conditional probability measure of any finite measure on any set of positive measure is a probability measure.
signature: [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hcs : μ s ≠ 0) : IsProbabilityMeasure μ[|s]

name: integral_mul_eq_integral
informal: If `X` is a real-valued random variable that has pdf `f`, then the expectation of `X` equals `∫ x, x * f x ∂λ` where `λ` is the Lebesgue measure.
signature: [HasPDF X ℙ] : ∫ x, x * (pdf X ℙ volume x).toReal = ∫ x, X x ∂ℙ

name: indepFun_iff_pdf_prod_eq_pdf_mul_pdf
informal: Random variables are independent iff their joint density is a product of marginal densities.
signature: [IsFiniteMeasure ℙ] [SigmaFinite μ] [SigmaFinite ν] [HasPDF (fun ω ↦ (X ω, Y ω)) ℙ (μ.prod ν)] : IndepFun X Y ℙ ↔ pdf (fun ω ↦ (X ω, Y ω)) ℙ (μ.prod ν) =ᵐ[μ.prod ν] fun z ↦ pdf X ℙ μ z.1 * pdf Y ℙ ν z.2

name: beta_eq_betaIntegralReal
informal: Relation between the beta function and the gamma function over the reals.
signature: (α β : ℝ) (hα : 0 < α) (hβ : 0 < β) : beta α β = (betaIntegral α β).re

name: betaPDFReal_pos
informal: The beta pdf is positive for all positive reals with positive parameters.
signature: {α β x : ℝ} (hx1 : 0 < x) (hx2 : x < 1) (hα : 0 < α) (hβ : 0 < β) : 0 < betaPDFReal α β x

name: lintegral_exponentialPDF_of_nonpos
informal: The Lebesgue integral of the exponential pdf over nonpositive reals equals 0
signature: {x r : ℝ} (hx : x ≤ 0) : ∫⁻ y in Iio x, exponentialPDF r y = 0

name: exponentialPDFReal_pos
informal: The exponential pdf is positive for all positive reals
signature: {x r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hx : 0 < x) : 0 < exponentialPDFReal r x

signature: [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (hp : p ≠ 0) (f : ℕ → E) : ∫ n, f n ∂geometricMeasure p = ∑' n : ℕ, ((1 - p : ℝ) ^ n * p) • f n

name: integral_poissonMeasure

informal: In general, the annihilator of a simple module is called a primitive ideal, and it is always a two-sided prime ideal, but mathlib's `Ideal.IsPrime` is not the correct definition for noncommutative rings.
signature: {R} [CommRing R] [Module R M] [simple : IsSimpleModule R M] : (Module.annihilator R M).IsMaximal

name: annihilator_isRadical
informal: The annihilator of a semisimple module over a commutative ring is a radical ideal.
signature: (R) [CommRing R] [Module R M] [IsSemisimpleModule R M] : (Module.annihilator R M).IsRadical

name: bijective_or_eq_zero
informal: **Schur's Lemma** for linear maps between (possibly distinct) simple modules
signature: [IsSimpleModule R M] [IsSimpleModule R N] (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : Function.Bijective f ∨ f = 0

name: IsSimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_matrix_of_isAlgClosed
informal: The **Wedderburn–Artin Theorem** over algebraically closed fields: a finite-dimensional simple algebra over an algebraically closed field is isomorphic to a matrix algebra over the field.
signature: [IsSimpleRing R] [FiniteDimensional F R] : ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : NeZero n), Nonempty (R ≃ₐ[F] Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F)

name: IsSemisimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix_of_isAlgClosed
informal: The **Wedderburn–Artin Theorem** over algebraically closed fields: a finite-dimensional semisimple algebra over an algebraically closed field is isomorphic to a product of matrix algebras over the field.
signature: [IsSemisimpleRing R] [FiniteDimensional F R] : ∃ (n : ℕ) (d : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ i, NeZero (d i)) ∧ Nonempty (R ≃ₐ[F] Π i, Matrix (Fin (d i)) (Fin (d i)) F)

name: Smooth.exists_span_eq_top_isStandardSmooth
informal: If `S` is `R`-smooth, there exists a cover by basic opens `D(sᵢ)` such that `S[1/sᵢ]` is `R`-standard-smooth.
signature: [Smooth R S] : ∃ (s : Set S), Ideal.span s = ⊤ ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, IsStandardSmooth R (Localization.Away x)

name: isEmbedding_comap_of_surjective
informal: The embedding has closed range if the domain (and therefore the codomain) is a ring, see `PrimeSpectrum.isClosedEmbedding_comap_of_surjective`. On the other hand, `comap (Nat.castRingHom (ZMod 2))` does not have closed range.
signature: (hf : Surjective f) : IsEmbedding (comap f)

name: isQuotientMap_of_specializingMap
informal: If `f : Spec S → Spec R` is specializing and surjective, the topology on `Spec R` is the quotient topology induced by `f`.
signature: (h₂ : SpecializingMap (comap f)) : Topology.IsQuotientMap (comap f)

name: isQuotientMap_of_generalizingMap
informal: If `f : Spec S → Spec R` is generalizing and surjective, the topology on `Spec R` is the quotient topology induced by `f`.
signature: (h₂ : GeneralizingMap (comap f)) : Topology.IsQuotientMap (comap f)

name: Algebra.trace_quotient_eq_of_isDedekindDomain
informal: The trace map on `B → A` coincides with the trace map on `B⧸pB → A⧸p`.
signature: (x) [IsDedekindDomain R] [IsDomain S] [Module.IsTorsionFree R S] [Module.Finite R S] [IsIntegrallyClosed S] : Algebra.trace (R ⧸ p) (S ⧸ pS) (Ideal.Quotient.mk pS x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk p (Algebra.intTrace R S x)

name: prime_factors_irreducible
informal: If an irreducible has a prime factorization, then it is an associate of one of its prime factors.
signature: [CommMonoidWithZero α] {a : α} {f : Multiset α} (ha : Irreducible a) (pfa : (∀ b ∈ f, Prime b) ∧ f.prod ~ᵤ a) : ∃ p, a ~ᵤ p ∧ f = {p}

name: generator_eq_exp_neg_one_of_mem_range
informal: The generator of a discrete valuation in `ℤᵐ⁰` that contains `exp (-1)` in its range is equal to `exp (-1)`.
signature: (hπ : exp (-1) ∈ Set.range v) : hv.generator = Units.mk0 (exp (-1 : ℤ) : ℤᵐ⁰) (by simp)

name: associated_of_isUniformizer
informal: If two elements of `K₀` are uniformizers, then they are associated.
signature: {π₁ π₂ : K₀} (h1 : IsUniformizer v π₁) (h2 : IsUniformizer v π₂) : Associated π₁ π₂

name: pow_coeff_zero_ne_zero_of_unit
informal: For any unit `x : Lˣ`, we prove that a certain power of the valuation of zeroth coefficient of the minimal polynomial of `x` over `K` is nonzero. This lemma is helpful for defining the valuation on `L` inducing `v`.
signature: [FiniteDimensional K L] (x : L) (hx : IsUnit x) : v ((minpoly K x).coeff 0) ^ (finrank K L / (minpoly K x).natDegree) ≠ (0 : Γ₀)

name: zero_of_hom_zero
informal: If `v` is a rank one valuation and `x : Γ₀` has image `0` under `RankOne.hom v`, then `x = 0`.
signature: {x : ValueGroup₀ (.ofClass v)} (hx : hom v x = 0) : x = 0

name: hom_eq_zero_iff
informal: If `v` is a rank one valuation, then `x : Γ₀` has image `0` under `RankOne.hom v` if and only if `x = 0`.
signature: {x : ValueGroup₀ (.ofClass v)} : hom v x = 0 ↔ x = 0

name: eq_zero_of_p_mul_eq_zero
informal: If `k` is a perfect ring of characteristic `p`, then the ring of Witt vectors `𝕎 k` is `p`-torsion free.

name: mem_span_p_iff_coeff_zero_eq_zero
informal: If `k` is a perfect ring of characteristic `p`, a Witt vector `x : 𝕎 k` falls in ideal generated by `p` if and only if its zeroth coefficient is `0`.
signature: (x : 𝕎 k) : x ∈ (Ideal.span {(p : 𝕎 k)}) ↔ x.coeff 0 = 0

name: verschiebung_zmod
informal: Verschiebung is the same as multiplication by `p` on the ring of Witt vectors of `ZMod p`.
signature: (x : 𝕎 (ZMod p)) : verschiebung x = x * p

name: mul_eq_self
informal: If `α` is an infinite type, then `α × α` and `α` have the same cardinality.
signature: {c : Cardinal} (hc : ℵ₀ ≤ c) : c * c = c

name: mul_eq_max
informal: If `α` and `β` are infinite types, then the cardinality of `α × β` is the maximum of the cardinalities of `α` and `β`.
signature: {a b : Cardinal} (ha : ℵ₀ ≤ a) (hb : ℵ₀ ≤ b) : a * b = max a b

name: add_eq_self
informal: If `α` is an infinite type, then `α ⊕ α` and `α` have the same cardinality.
signature: {c : Cardinal} (h : ℵ₀ ≤ c) : c + c = c

name: add_eq_max
informal: If `α` is an infinite type, then the cardinality of `α ⊕ β` is the maximum of the cardinalities of `α` and `β`.
signature: {a b : Cardinal} (ha : ℵ₀ ≤ a) : a + b = max a b

name: exists_rel_mk_fibers_lt
informal: Infinite types permit a relation where fewer elements than its cardinality are missed along all verticals and fewer elements than its cardinality are hit along all horizontals.
signature: (α : Type*) [Infinite α] : ∃ r : α → α → Prop, (∀ x, #{y // ¬ r x y} < #α) ∧ (∀ y, #{x // r x y} < #α)

name: bddAbove_iff_small
informal: A set of cardinals is bounded above iff it's small, i.e. it corresponds to a usual ZFC set.
signature: {s : Set Cardinal.{u}} : BddAbove s ↔ Small.{u} s

name: lift_iSup_le
informal: To prove that the lift of a supremum is bounded by some cardinal `t`, it suffices to show that the lift of each cardinal is bounded by `t`.
signature: {ι : Type v} {f : ι → Cardinal.{w}} {t : Cardinal} (hf : BddAbove (range f)) (w : ∀ i, lift.{u} (f i) ≤ t) : lift.{u} (iSup f) ≤ t

name: lift_iSup_le_lift_iSup
informal: To prove an inequality between the lifts to a common universe of two different supremums, it suffices to show that the lift of each cardinal from the smaller supremum if bounded by the lift of some cardinal from the larger supremum.
signature: {ι : Type v} {ι' : Type v'} {f : ι → Cardinal.{w}} {f' : ι' → Cardinal.{w'}} (hf : BddAbove (range f)) (hf' : BddAbove (range f')) {g : ι → ι'} (h : ∀ i, lift.{w'} (f i) ≤ lift.{w} (f' (g i))) : lift.{w'} (iSup f) ≤ lift.{w} (iSup f')

name: isCofinal_of_isCofinal_sUnion
informal: If the union of `s` is cofinal and `s` is smaller than the cofinality, then `s` has a cofinal member.
signature: {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α] {s : Set (Set α)} (h₁ : IsCofinal (⋃₀ s)) (h₂ : #s < Order.cof α) : ∃ x ∈ s, IsCofinal x

name: _root_.Order.isNormal_enum_iff_isClub
informal: Club sets in regular cardinals correspond one to one with normal functions.
signature: [IsRegularCardinalOrder α] {s : Set α} {hs : IsCofinal s} : IsNormal (Subtype.val ∘ enum s hs) ↔ IsClub s

name: exists_ord_cof_eq
informal: Every well-order has a cofinal subset of order type `(cof α).ord`.
signature: [LinearOrder α] [WellFoundedLT α] : ∃ s : Set α, IsCofinal s ∧ typeLT s = (Order.cof α).ord

name: exists_ord_cof_eq_of_isCofinal
informal: Every cofinal set has a cofinal subset of order type `(cof α).ord`.
signature: [LinearOrder α] [WellFoundedLT α] {s : Set α} (hs : IsCofinal s) : ∃ t ⊆ s, IsCofinal t ∧ typeLT t = (Order.cof α).ord

name: mk_subtype_le_of_countable_eventually_mem_aux
informal: If a set `t` is eventually covered by a countable family of sets, all with cardinality at most `a`, then the cardinality of `t` is also bounded by `a`. Superseded by `mk_le_of_countable_eventually_mem` which does not assume that the indexing set lives in the same universe.
signature: {α ι : Type u} {a : Cardinal} [Countable ι] {f : ι → Set α} {l : Filter ι} [NeBot l] {t : Set α} (ht : ∀ x ∈ t, ∀ᶠ i in l, x ∈ f i) (h'f : ∀ i, #(f i) ≤ a) : #t ≤ a

name: mk_sigma_congr'
informal: Similar to `mk_sigma_congr` with indexing types in different universes. This is not a strict generalization.
signature: {ι : Type u} {ι' : Type v} {f : ι → Type max w (max u v)} {g : ι' → Type max w (max u v)} (e : ι ≃ ι') (h : ∀ i, #(f i) = #(g (e i))) : #(Σ i, f i) = #(Σ i, g i)

name: mk_pi_congr'
informal: Similar to `mk_pi_congr` with indexing types in different universes. This is not a strict generalization.
signature: {ι : Type u} {ι' : Type v} {f : ι → Type max w (max u v)} {g : ι' → Type max w (max u v)} (e : ι ≃ ι') (h : ∀ i, #(f i) = #(g (e i))) : #(Π i, f i) = #(Π i, g i)

name: infinite_pigeonhole_card_lt
informal: A function whose domain's cardinality is infinite and strictly greater than its codomain's has a fiber with cardinality strictly great than the codomain.
signature: {β α : Type u} (f : β → α) (h : #α < #β) (hβ : ℵ₀ ≤ #β) : ∃ a : α, #α < #(f ⁻¹' {a})

name: exists_infinite_fiber
informal: A function whose domain's cardinality is infinite and strictly greater than its codomain's has an infinite fiber.
signature: {β α : Type u} (f : β → α) (h : #α < #β) [Infinite β] : ∃ a : α, Infinite (f ⁻¹' {a})

name: exists_uncountable_fiber
informal: A function whose domain's cardinality is uncountable and strictly greater than its codomain's has an uncountable fiber.
signature: {β α : Type u} (f : β → α) (h : #α < #β) [Uncountable β] : ∃ a : α, Uncountable (f ⁻¹' {a})

name: le_range_of_union_finset_eq_univ
informal: If an infinite type `β` can be expressed as a union of finite sets, then the cardinality of the collection of those finite sets must be at least the cardinality of `β`.
signature: {α β : Type*} [Infinite β] (f : α → Finset β) (w : ⋃ a, (f a : Set β) = Set.univ) : #β ≤ #(range f)

name: toNat_inj_of_lt_aleph0
informal: Two finite cardinals are equal iff they are equal their `Cardinal.toNat` projections are equal.
signature: (hc : c < ℵ₀) (hd : d < ℵ₀) : toNat c = toNat d ↔ c = d

name: mul_div_gc
informal: Multiplication and division by a non-zero ordinal form a Galois connection.
signature: {a : Ordinal} (ha : a ≠ 0) : GaloisConnection (a * ·) (· / a)

name: card_typein_min_le_mk
informal: The cardinality of a set is an upper-bound for the cardinality of the order type of the set's mex (minimum excluded value). See `not_lt_enum_ord_mk_min_compl` for the `α` version.
signature: [IsWellOrder α r] {s : Set α} (hs : sᶜ.Nonempty) : (typein r <| IsWellFounded.wf.min (r

name: exists_ord_eq
informal: There exists a well-order on `α` whose order type is exactly `ord #α`.
signature: (α) : ∃ (r : α → α → Prop) (_ : IsWellOrder α r), ord #α = type r

name: exists_ord_eq_type_lt
informal: There exists a well-order on `α` whose order type is exactly `ord #α`.
signature: (α) : ∃ (_ : LinearOrder α) (_ : WellFoundedLT α), ord #α = typeLT α

name: fst_le_log
informal: Every exponent in the Cantor normal form `CNF b o` is less or equal to `log b o`.
signature: {b o : Ordinal.{u}} {x : Ordinal × Ordinal} : x ∈ CNF b o → x.1 ≤ log b o

name: snd_lt
informal: Every coefficient in the Cantor normal form `CNF b o` is less than `b`.
signature: {b o : Ordinal.{u}} (hb : 1 < b) {x : Ordinal × Ordinal} : x ∈ CNF b o → x.2 < b

name: eq_enumOrd
informal: A characterization of `enumOrd`: it is the unique strict monotonic function with range `s`.
signature: (f : Ordinal → Ordinal) (hs : ¬ BddAbove s) : enumOrd s = f ↔ StrictMono f ∧ range f = s

name: isNormal_enumOrd
informal: If `s` is closed under nonempty suprema, then its enumerator function is normal. See also `enumOrd_isNormal_iff_isClosed`.
signature: (H : ∀ t ⊆ s, t.Nonempty → BddAbove t → sSup t ∈ s) (hs : ¬ BddAbove s) : IsNormal (enumOrd s)

name: not_bddAbove_fp_family
informal: A generalization of the fixed point lemma for normal functions: any family of normal functions has an unbounded set of common fixed points.
signature: [Small.{u} ι] (H : ∀ i, IsNormal (f i)) : ¬ BddAbove (⋂ i, Function.fixedPoints (f i))

name: derivFamily_eq_enumOrd
informal: For a family of normal functions, `Ordinal.derivFamily` enumerates the common fixed points.
signature: [Small.{u} ι] (H : ∀ i, IsNormal (f i)) : derivFamily f = enumOrd (⋂ i, Function.fixedPoints (f i))

name: not_bddAbove_fp
informal: The fixed point lemma for normal functions: any normal function has an unbounded set of fixed points.
signature: (H : IsNormal f) : ¬ BddAbove (Function.fixedPoints f)

name: lfpApprox_eq_of_mem_fixedPoints
informal: The approximations of the least fixed point stabilize at a fixed point of `f`
signature: (hab : a ≤ b) (hf : lfpApprox f x a ∈ fixedPoints f) : lfpApprox f x b = lfpApprox f x a

name: lfpApprox_mem_fixedPoints_of_eq
informal: If the sequence of ordinal-indexed approximations takes a value twice, then it actually stabilised at that value.
signature: (hx : x ≤ f x) (hab : a < b) (hac : a ≤ c) (hf : lfpApprox f x a = lfpApprox f x b) : lfpApprox f x c ∈ fixedPoints f

name: iSup_lfpApprox_eq_of_mem_fixedPoints
informal: If `lfpApprox f x a` is a fixed point, then the supremum of the whole ordinal-indexed sequence equals the value at `a`.
signature: (hf : lfpApprox f x a ∈ fixedPoints f) : ⨆ i : Ordinal, lfpApprox f x i = lfpApprox f x a

name: nextFixed_eq_iSup_lfpApprox
informal: The ordinal-indexed supremum of `lfpApprox` equals `nextFixed`: the least fixed point greater than or equal to `x`.
signature: (hx : x ≤ f x) : (f.nextFixed x hx).val = ⨆ a : Ordinal, lfpApprox f x a

name: gfpApprox_eq_of_mem_fixedPoints
informal: The approximations of the greatest fixed point stabilize at a fixed point of `f`
signature: {a b : Ordinal} (h_ab : a ≤ b) (h : gfpApprox f x a ∈ fixedPoints f) : gfpApprox f x b = gfpApprox f x a

name: iInf_gfpApprox_eq_of_mem_fixedPoints
informal: If `gfpApprox f x a` is a fixed point, then the infimum of the whole ordinal-indexed sequence equals the value at `a`.
signature: (hf : gfpApprox f x a ∈ fixedPoints f) : ⨅ i : Ordinal, gfpApprox f x i = gfpApprox f x a

name: prevFixed_eq_iInf_gfpApprox
informal: The ordinal-indexed infimum of `gfpApprox` equals `prevFixed`: the greatest fixed point less than or equal to `x`.
signature: (hx : f x ≤ x) : (f.prevFixed x hx).val = ⨅ a : Ordinal, gfpApprox f x a

name: comp_isNormal
informal: If `f` is a fundamental sequence for a limit ordinal `o` and `g` is normal, then `g ∘ f` is a fundamental sequence for `g o`.
signature: {g : Ordinal → Ordinal} (hg : IsNormal g) (hf : IsFundamentalSeq f) (ho : IsSuccLimit o) : IsFundamentalSeq fun i ↦ ⟨g (f i), hg.strictMono (f i).2⟩ where strictMono

name: eq_univ_of_powerset_subset
informal: An induction principle for sets. If every subset of a class is a member, then the class is universal.
signature: {A : Class} (hA : powerset A ⊆ A) : A = univ

name: iota_ex
informal: Unlike the other set constructors, the `iota` definite descriptor is a set for any set input, but not constructively so, so there is no associated `Class → Set` function.
signature: (A) : iota.{u} A ∈ univ.{u}

name: Equiv.eq
informal: Two pre-sets are equivalent iff they have the same members.
signature: {x y : PSet} : Equiv x y ↔ toSet x = toSet y

name: rank_sUnion_le
informal: For the rank of `⋃₀ x`, we only have `rank (⋃₀ x) ≤ rank x ≤ rank (⋃₀ x) + 1`. This inequality is split into `rank_sUnion_le` and `le_succ_rank_sUnion`.
signature: (x : PSet) : rank (⋃₀ x) ≤ rank x

name: rank_sUnion_le
informal: For the rank of `⋃₀ x`, we only have `rank (⋃₀ x) ≤ rank x ≤ rank (⋃₀ x) + 1`. This inequality is split into `rank_sUnion_le` and `le_succ_rank_sUnion`.
signature: (x : ZFSet) : rank (⋃₀ x) ≤ rank x

name: exists_mem_vonNeumann
informal: Every set is in some element of the von Neumann hierarchy.
signature: (x : ZFSet) : ∃ o, x ∈ V_ o

name: derive_trans
informal: Helper lemma to chain together a `simp` proof and the result of `mkProdPrf`.
signature: {α} [Mul α] {a b c d : α} (h : a = b) (h' : c * b = d) : c * a = d

name: derive_trans₂
informal: Helper lemma to chain together two `simp` proofs and the result of `mkProdPrf`.
signature: {α} [Mul α] {a b c d e : α} (h : a = b) (h' : b = c) (h'' : d * c = e) : d * a = e

name: eventually_pos
informal: Eventually all functions from a well-formed basis are positive.
signature: {basis : Basis} (h : WellFormedBasis basis) : ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∀ f ∈ basis, 0 < f x

name: head_eventually_pos
informal: The first function in a well-formed basis is eventually positive.
signature: {basis_hd : ℝ → ℝ} {basis_tl : Basis} (h : WellFormedBasis (basis_hd :: basis_tl)) : ∀ᶠ x in atTop, 0 < basis_hd x

name: tail_isLittleO_head
informal: All functions in the tail of a well-formed basis are little-o of the basis' head.
signature: {hd : ℝ → ℝ} {tl : Basis} (h : WellFormedBasis (hd :: tl)) {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : f ∈ tl) : (Real.log ∘ f) =o[atTop] (Real.log ∘ hd)

name: tail_pow_majorized_head
informal: Any power of function from a well-formed basis' tail is Majorized by basis' head with zero exponent.
signature: {hd f : ℝ → ℝ} {tl : Basis} (h_basis : WellFormedBasis (hd :: tl)) (hf : f ∈ tl) (r : ℝ) : Majorized (f ^ r) hd 0

name: replaceFun
informal: One can replace `f` in `Approximates` with the function that eventually equals `f`.
signature: {ms : MultiseriesExpansion (basis_hd :: basis_tl)} {f : ℝ → ℝ} (h_equiv : ms.toFun =ᶠ[atTop] f) (h_approx : ms.Approximates) : (ms.replaceFun f).Approximates

name: neg_leadingExp_tendsto_zero
informal: If `f` can be approximated by multiseries with negative leading exponent, then it tends to zero.
signature: {basis_hd : ℝ → ℝ} {basis_tl : Basis} {ms : MultiseriesExpansion (basis_hd :: basis_tl)} (h_neg : ms.leadingExp < 0) (h_approx : ms.Approximates) : Tendsto ms.toFun atTop (𝓝 0)

name: of_eventuallyEq
informal: Replacing the first argument of `Majorized` by an eventually equal function preserves it.
signature: (h_eq : g =ᶠ[atTop] f) (h : Majorized f b exp) : Majorized g b exp

name: self
informal: For any function `f` tending to infinity, `f ^ exp` is majorized by `f` with exponent `exp`.
signature: (h : Tendsto f atTop atTop) : Majorized (f ^ exp) f exp

name: const
informal: Constants are majorized with exponent `exp = 0` by any functions which tends to infinity.
signature: (h_tendsto : Tendsto b atTop atTop) {c : ℝ} : Majorized (fun _ ↦ c) b 0

name: add
informal: The sum of two functions that are majorized with exponents `f_exp` and `g_exp` is majorized with exponent `exp` whenever `exp ≥ max f_exp g_exp`.
signature: {f_exp g_exp : ℝ} (hf : Majorized f b f_exp) (hg : Majorized g b g_exp) (hf_exp : f_exp ≤ exp) (hg_exp : g_exp ≤ exp) : Majorized (f + g) b exp

name: mul
informal: The product of two functions that are majorized with exponents `f_exp` and `g_exp` is majorized with exponent `f_exp + g_exp`.
signature: {f_exp g_exp : ℝ} (hf : Majorized f b f_exp) (hg : Majorized g b g_exp) (h_pos : ∀ᶠ t in atTop, 0 < b t) : Majorized (f * g) b (f_exp + g_exp)

name: neg_toFun
informal: Flipping the sign of `coef` flips the sign of `toFun`. The theorem is stated in this form, because it allows one to rewrite the `t.toFun basis` expression. It is used below in cases where we want to reduce the case of `t.coef < 0` to `t.coef > 0`.
signature: {t : Monomial} {basis : Basis} : t.toFun basis = -t.neg.toFun basis

name: encode_injective
informal: The `encode` function is injective. Used internally by the `Countable` deriving handler.
signature: {α : Sort*} [Countable α] : Function.Injective (encode : α → ℕ)

name: cons_eq_imp_init
informal: Initialize the injectivity argument. Pops the constructor tag.
signature: {p : Prop} {a b b' : ℕ} (h : b = b' → p) : Nat.pair a b = Nat.pair a b' → p

name: cons_eq_imp
informal: Generic step of the injectivity argument, pops the head of the pairs. Used in the recursive steps where we need to supply an additional injectivity argument.
signature: {p : Prop} {a b a' b' : ℕ} (h : a = a' → b = b' → p) : Nat.pair a b = Nat.pair a' b' → p

name: JacobiSym.mod_left
informal: The value depends only on the residue class of `a` mod `b`.
signature: (a : ℤ) (b ab' : ℕ) (ab r b' : ℤ) (hb' : (b : ℤ) = b') (hab : a % b' = ab) (h : (ab' : ℤ) = ab) (hr : jacobiSymNat ab' b = r) : jacobiSym a b = r

name: jacobiSymNat.even_even
informal: The symbol vanishes when both entries are even (and `b / 2 ≠ 0`).
signature: (a b : ℕ) (hb₀ : Nat.beq (b / 2) 0 = false) (ha : a % 2 = 0) (hb₁ : b % 2 = 0) : jacobiSymNat a b = 0

name: jacobiSymNat.double_even
informal: If `a` is divisible by `4` and `b` is odd, then we can remove the factor `4` from `a`.
signature: (a b c : ℕ) (r : ℤ) (ha : a % 4 = 0) (hb : b % 2 = 1) (hc : a / 4 = c) (hr : jacobiSymNat c b = r) : jacobiSymNat a b = r

name: IsNatPowT.trans
informal: This is the key to making the proof proceed as a balanced tree of applications instead of a linear sequence. It is just modus ponens after unwrapping the definitions.
signature: {p : Prop} {b' c' : ℕ} (h1 : IsNatPowT p a b c) (h2 : IsNatPowT (Nat.pow a b = c) a b' c') : IsNatPowT p a b' c'

name: DiscreteTopology.instContinuousSMul
informal: If `R` is a discrete topological ring, then any topological ring `S` which is an `R`-algebra is also a topological `R`-algebra. NB: This could be an instance but the signature makes it very expensive in search. See https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/15339 for the regressions caused by making this an instance.
signature: [IsTopologicalSemiring A] [DiscreteTopology R] : ContinuousSMul R A

name: Filter.tendsto_cocompact_mul_left₀
informal: Left-multiplication by a nonzero element of a topological division ring is proper, i.e., inverse images of compact sets are compact.
signature: [SeparatelyContinuousMul K] {a : K} (ha : a ≠ 0) : Filter.Tendsto (fun x : K => a * x) (Filter.cocompact K) (Filter.cocompact K)

name: Filter.tendsto_cocompact_mul_right₀
informal: Right-multiplication by a nonzero element of a topological division ring is proper, i.e., inverse images of compact sets are compact.
signature: [SeparatelyContinuousMul K] {a : K} (ha : a ≠ 0) : Filter.Tendsto (fun x : K => x * a) (Filter.cocompact K) (Filter.cocompact K)

name: DivisionRing.finite_of_compactSpace_of_t2Space
informal: Compact Hausdorff topological fields are finite. This is not an instance, as it would apply to every `Finite` goal, causing slowly failing typeclass search in some cases.
signature: {K} [DivisionRing K] [TopologicalSpace K] [IsTopologicalRing K] [CompactSpace K] [T2Space K] : Finite K

name: Set.isClosed_centralizer
informal: In a Hausdorff magma with continuous multiplication, the centralizer of any set is closed.
signature: {M : Type*} (s : Set M) [Mul M] [TopologicalSpace M] [SeparatelyContinuousMul M] [T2Space M] : IsClosed (centralizer s)

name: Filter.Tendsto.inv₀
informal: If a function converges to a nonzero value, its inverse converges to the inverse of this value. We use the name `Filter.Tendsto.inv₀` as `Filter.Tendsto.inv` is already used in multiplicative topological groups.
signature: {a : G₀} (hf : Tendsto f l (𝓝 a)) (ha : a ≠ 0) : Tendsto (fun x => (f x)⁻¹) l (𝓝 a⁻¹)

name: ContinuousInv₀.of_nhds_one
informal: If a group with zero has continuous multiplication and `fun x ↦ x⁻¹` is continuous at one, then it is continuous at any unit.
signature: (h : Tendsto Inv.inv (𝓝 (1 : G₀)) (𝓝 1)) : ContinuousInv₀ G₀ where continuousAt_inv₀ x hx

name: tendsto_tsum_compl_atTop_zero
informal: The sum over the complement of a finset tends to `0` when the finset grows to cover the whole space. This does not need a summability assumption, as otherwise all sums are zero.
signature: {α : Type*} {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∑' x, f x ≠ ∞) : Tendsto (fun s : Finset α => ∑' b : { x // x ∉ s }, f b) atTop (𝓝 0)

name: hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat
informal: A series of non-negative real numbers converges to `r` in the sense of `HasSum` if and only if the sequence of partial sum converges to `r`.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℝ≥0} {r : ℝ≥0} : HasSum f r ↔ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, f i) atTop (𝓝 r)

name: tendsto_sum_nat_add
informal: For `f : ℕ → ℝ≥0`, then `∑' k, f (k + i)` tends to zero. This does not require a summability assumption on `f`, as otherwise all sums are zero.
signature: (f : ℕ → ℝ≥0) : Tendsto (fun i => ∑' k, f (k + i)) atTop (𝓝 0)

name: hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat_of_nonneg
informal: A series of non-negative real numbers converges to `r` in the sense of `HasSum` if and only if the sequence of partial sum converges to `r`.
signature: {f : ℕ → ℝ} (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) (r : ℝ) : HasSum f r ↔ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, f i) atTop (𝓝 r)

name: cauchySeq_of_dist_le_of_summable
informal: If the distance between consecutive points of a sequence is estimated by a summable series, then the original sequence is a Cauchy sequence.
signature: (d : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ n, dist (f n) (f n.succ) ≤ d n) (hd : Summable d) : CauchySeq f

name: tendsto_smul_zero
informal: If `M` is a linearly topologized `R`-module and `i ↦ m i` tends to zero, then `i ↦ a i • m i` still tends to zero for any family `a : ι → R`.
signature: [IsLinearTopology R M] {ι : Type*} {f : Filter ι} (a : ι → R) (m : ι → M) (ha : Tendsto m f (𝓝 0)) : Tendsto (a • m) f (𝓝 0)

name: _root_.IsCentralScalar.isLinearTopology_iff
informal: If the left and right actions of `R` on `M` coincide, then a topology is `Rᵐᵒᵖ`-linear if and only if it is `R`-linear.
signature: [Module Rᵐᵒᵖ M] [IsCentralScalar R M] : IsLinearTopology Rᵐᵒᵖ M ↔ IsLinearTopology R M

name: map_sum
informal: If `f` is continuous alternating, then `f (Σ_{j₁} g₁ j₁, ..., Σ_{jₙ} gₙ jₙ)` is the sum of `f (g₁ (r 1), ..., gₙ (r n))` where `r` ranges over all functions `r`. This follows from multilinearity by expanding successively with respect to each coordinate.
signature: [∀ i, Fintype (α i)] : (f fun i => ∑ j, g' i j) = ∑ r : ∀ i, α i, f fun i => g' i (r i)

name: ContinuousNeg.of_continuousConstSMul
informal: A topological module over a ring has continuous negation. This cannot be an instance, because it would cause search for `[Module ?R M]` with unknown `R`.
signature: [ContinuousConstSMul R M] : ContinuousNeg M where continuous_neg

name: TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.span
informal: The span of a separable subset with respect to a separable scalar ring is again separable.
signature: {R M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Semiring R] [Module R M] [TopologicalSpace M] [TopologicalSpace R] [SeparableSpace R] [ContinuousAdd M] [ContinuousSMul R M] {s : Set M} (hs : IsSeparable s) : IsSeparable (Submodule.span R s : Set M)

name: continuum_le_cardinal_of_nontriviallyNormedField
informal: A complete nontrivially normed field has cardinality at least continuum.
signature: (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] : 𝔠 ≤ #𝕜

name: cardinal_eq_of_mem_nhds_zero
informal: In a topological vector space over a nontrivially normed field, any neighborhood of zero has the same cardinality as the whole space. See also `cardinal_eq_of_mem_nhds`.
signature: {E : Type*} (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [Zero E] [MulActionWithZero 𝕜 E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] {s : Set E} (hs : s ∈ 𝓝 (0 : E)) : #s = #E

name: cardinal_eq_of_mem_nhds
informal: In a topological vector space over a nontrivially normed field, any neighborhood of a point has the same cardinality as the whole space.
signature: {E : Type*} (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [AddGroup E] [MulActionWithZero 𝕜 E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] {s : Set E} {x : E} (hs : s ∈ 𝓝 x) : #s = #E

name: cardinal_eq_of_isOpen
informal: In a topological vector space over a nontrivially normed field, any nonempty open set has the same cardinality as the whole space.
signature: {E : Type*} (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [AddGroup E] [MulActionWithZero 𝕜 E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] {s : Set E} (hs : IsOpen s) (h's : s.Nonempty) : #s = #E

name: continuum_le_cardinal_of_isOpen
informal: In a nontrivial topological vector space over a complete nontrivially normed field, any nonempty open set has cardinality at least continuum.
signature: {E : Type*} (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] [Nontrivial E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] {s : Set E} (hs : IsOpen s) (h's : s.Nonempty) : 𝔠 ≤ #s

name: Set.Countable.dense_compl
informal: In a nontrivial topological vector space over a complete nontrivially normed field, any countable set has dense complement.
signature: {E : Type u} (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] [Nontrivial E] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E] [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] {s : Set E} (hs : s.Countable) : Dense sᶜ

name: IsCompl.isTopCompl_iff_continuous_symm_prodEquivOfIsCompl
informal: Two complementary submodules are topological complements if and only if the linear equivalence `Submodule.prodEquivOfIsCompl` is continuous in the inverse direction.
signature: (h : IsCompl p q) : IsTopCompl p q ↔ Continuous (p.prodEquivOfIsCompl q h).symm

name: continuous_prodEquivOfIsCompl
informal: The linear equivalence `Submodule.prodEquivOfIsCompl` from a pair of complementary submodules is always continuous.
signature: (h : IsCompl p q) : Continuous (p.prodEquivOfIsCompl q h)

name: IsCompl.isTopCompl_iff_isHomeomorph_prodEquivOfIsCompl
informal: Two complementary submodules are topological complements if and only if the linear equivalence `Submodule.prodEquivOfIsCompl` is a homeomorphism.
signature: (h : IsCompl p q) : IsTopCompl p q ↔ IsHomeomorph (p.prodEquivOfIsCompl q h)

name: IsCompl.isTopCompl_iff_continuous_quotientEquivOfIsCompl
informal: Two complementary submodules are topological complements if and only if the linear equivalence `Submodule.quotientEquivOfIsCompl` is continuous.
signature: (h : IsCompl p q) : IsTopCompl p q ↔ Continuous (p.quotientEquivOfIsCompl q h)

name: eqOn_closure_span
informal: If two continuous linear maps are equal on a set `s`, then they are equal on the closure of the `Submodule.span` of this set.
signature: [T2Space M₂] {s : Set M₁} {f g : M₁ →SL[σ₁₂] M₂} (h : Set.EqOn f g s) : Set.EqOn f g (closure (Submodule.span R₁ s : Set M₁))

name: ext_on
informal: If the submodule generated by a set `s` is dense in the ambient module, then two continuous linear maps equal on `s` are equal.
signature: [T2Space M₂] {s : Set M₁} (hs : Dense (Submodule.span R₁ s : Set M₁)) {f g : M₁ →SL[σ₁₂] M₂} (h : Set.EqOn f g s) : f = g

name: _root_.Submodule.topologicalClosure_map
informal: Under a continuous linear map, the image of the `TopologicalClosure` of a submodule is contained in the `TopologicalClosure` of its image.
signature: [RingHomSurjective σ₁₂] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [ContinuousSMul R₁ M₁] [ContinuousAdd M₁] [ContinuousSMul R₂ M₂] [ContinuousAdd M₂] (f : M₁ →SL[σ₁₂] M₂) (s : Submodule R₁ M₁) : s.topologicalClosure.map (f : M₁ →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂) ≤ (s.map (f : M₁ →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂)).topologicalClosure

name: _root_.DenseRange.topologicalClosure_map_submodule
informal: Under a dense continuous linear map, a submodule whose `TopologicalClosure` is `⊤` is sent to another such submodule. That is, the image of a dense set under a map with dense range is dense.
signature: [RingHomSurjective σ₁₂] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [ContinuousSMul R₁ M₁] [ContinuousAdd M₁] [ContinuousSMul R₂ M₂] [ContinuousAdd M₂] {f : M₁ →SL[σ₁₂] M₂} (hf' : DenseRange f) {s : Submodule R₁ M₁} (hs : s.topologicalClosure = ⊤) : (s.map (f : M₁ →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂)).topologicalClosure = ⊤

name: unique_topology_of_t2
informal: If `𝕜` is a nontrivially normed field, any T2 topology on `𝕜` which makes it a topological vector space over itself (with the norm topology) is *equal* to the norm topology.
signature: {t : TopologicalSpace 𝕜} (h₁ : @IsTopologicalAddGroup 𝕜 t _) (h₂ : @ContinuousSMul 𝕜 𝕜 _ hnorm.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace t) (h₃ : @T2Space 𝕜 t) : t = hnorm.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace

name: LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional
informal: Any linear map on a finite-dimensional space over a complete field is continuous.
signature: [T2Space E] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] (f : E →ₗ[𝕜] F') : Continuous f

name: LinearMap.isClosedEmbedding_of_injective
informal: An injective linear map with finite-dimensional domain is a closed embedding.
signature: [T2Space E] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] [T2Space F] {f : E →ₗ[𝕜] F} (hf : LinearMap.ker f = ⊥) : IsClosedEmbedding f

name: FiniteDimensional.of_totallyBounded_nhds_zero
informal: **Riesz's theorem**: a T2 topological vector space over a complete non-trivial normed field which admits a totally bounded neighborhood of `0` is finite-dimensional.
signature: {U : Set Eᵤ} (hU_nhds : U ∈ 𝓝 (0 : Eᵤ)) (hU_tb : TotallyBounded U) : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 Eᵤ

name: FiniteDimensional.of_locallyCompactSpace
informal: **Riesz's theorem**: a locally compact topological vector space is finite-dimensional.
signature: [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace E] : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E

name: closure_inverse_graph
informal: If `f` is invertible and closable as well as its closure being invertible, then the graph of the inverse of the closure is given by the closure of the graph of the inverse.
signature: (hf : LinearMap.ker f.toFun = ⊥) (hf' : f.IsClosable) (hcf : LinearMap.ker f.closure.toFun = ⊥) : f.closure.inverse.graph = f.inverse.graph.topologicalClosure

name: inverse_isClosable_iff
informal: Assuming that `f` is invertible and closable, then the closure is invertible if and only if the inverse of `f` is closable.
signature: (hf : LinearMap.ker f.toFun = ⊥) (hf' : f.IsClosable) : f.inverse.IsClosable ↔ LinearMap.ker f.closure.toFun = ⊥

name: inverse_closure
informal: If `f` is invertible and closable, then taking the closure and the inverse commute.
signature: (hf : LinearMap.ker f.toFun = ⊥) (hf' : f.IsClosable) (hcf : LinearMap.ker f.closure.toFun = ⊥) : f.inverse.closure = f.closure.inverse

name: Convex.locallyPathConnectedSpace

signature: [Module ℝ E] [ContinuousSMul ℝ E] [LocallyConvexSpace ℝ E] {S : Set E} (hS : Convex ℝ S) : LocallyPathConnectedSpace S

name: Disjoint.exists_open_convexes
informal: In a locally convex space, every two disjoint convex sets such that one is compact and the other is closed admit disjoint convex open neighborhoods.

name: of_continuous_id
informal: If `A` is a topological `R`-module and the identity map from (`A` with its given topology) to (`A` with the module topology) is continuous, then the topology on `A` is the module topology.

One inclusion -- follows from the continuity hypothesis; the other is because the module topology -- is the inf of all the topologies making `A` a topological module. eq_moduleTopology'

name: isOpenMap_of_surjective
informal: A linear surjection to a module with the module topology is open.
signature: [TopologicalSpace B] [IsModuleTopology R B] [ContinuousAdd A] [ContinuousSMul R A] {φ : A →ₗ[R] B} (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) : IsOpenMap φ

name: map_add_univ

name: map_sum
informal: If `f` is continuous multilinear, then `f (Σ_{j₁} g₁ j₁, ..., Σ_{jₙ} gₙ jₙ)` is the sum of `f (g₁ (r 1), ..., gₙ (r n))` where `r` ranges over all functions `r`. This follows from multilinearity by expanding successively with respect to each coordinate.
signature: [DecidableEq ι] [∀ i, Fintype (α i)] : (f fun i => ∑ j, g i j) = ∑ r : ∀ i, α i, f fun i => g i (r i)

name: Rat.denseRange_cast

name: tendsto_pow_neg_atTop

name: IsSemitopologicalSemiring.continuousNeg_of_mul
informal: If `R` is a ring with a separately continuous multiplication, then negation is continuous as well since it is just multiplication with `-1`.

name: IsSemitopologicalSemiring.toIsSemitopologicalRing

name: IsTopologicalSemiring.toIsTopologicalRing

name: isClosed_sphere
