signature: (γ : Γ₀ˣ) : ({↑γ} : Set Γ₀) ∈ 𝓝 (γ : Γ₀)

name: MeasurableSet.residualEq_isOpen
informal: Any Borel set differs from some open set by a meager set.
signature: [MeasurableSpace α] [BorelSpace α] (h : MeasurableSet s) : ∃ u : Set α, IsOpen u ∧ s =ᵇ u

name: separableSpace_iff_countable
informal: A topological space with discrete topology is separable iff it is countable.
signature: [DiscreteTopology α] : SeparableSpace α ↔ Countable α

name: _root_.Pairwise.countable_of_isOpen_disjoint
informal: In a separable space, a family of nonempty disjoint open sets is countable.
signature: [SeparableSpace α] {ι : Type*} {s : ι → Set α} (hd : Pairwise (Disjoint on s)) (ho : ∀ i, IsOpen (s i)) (hne : ∀ i, (s i).Nonempty) : Countable ι

name: _root_.Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_isOpen
informal: In a separable space, a family of nonempty disjoint open sets is countable.
signature: [SeparableSpace α] {ι : Type*} {s : ι → Set α} {a : Set ι} (h : a.PairwiseDisjoint s) (ho : ∀ i ∈ a, IsOpen (s i)) (hne : ∀ i ∈ a, (s i).Nonempty) : a.Countable

name: _root_.Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior
informal: In a separable space, a family of disjoint sets with nonempty interiors is countable.
signature: [SeparableSpace α] {ι : Type*} {s : ι → Set α} {a : Set ι} (h : a.PairwiseDisjoint s) (ha : ∀ i ∈ a, (interior (s i)).Nonempty) : a.Countable

name: exists_countable_dense_bot_top
informal: If `α` is a separable topological space with a partial order, then there exists a countable dense set `s : Set α` that contains those of both bottom and top elements of `α` that actually exist. For a dense set containing neither bot nor top elements, see `exists_countable_dense_no_bot_top`.
signature: (α : Type*) [TopologicalSpace α] [SeparableSpace α] [PartialOrder α] : ∃ s : Set α, s.Countable ∧ Dense s ∧ (∀ x, IsBot x → x ∈ s) ∧ ∀ x, IsTop x → x ∈ s

name: firstCountableTopology_induced
informal: If `β` is a first-countable space, then its induced topology via `f` on `α` is also first-countable.
signature: (α β : Type*) [t : TopologicalSpace β] [FirstCountableTopology β] (f : α → β) : @FirstCountableTopology α (t.induced f)

name: secondCountableTopology_induced
informal: If `β` is a second-countable space, then its induced topology via `f` on `α` is also second-countable.
signature: (α β) [t : TopologicalSpace β] [SecondCountableTopology β] (f : α → β) : @SecondCountableTopology α (t.induced f)

name: IsTopologicalBasis.exists_countable_biUnion_of_isOpen
informal: In a second countable topological space, any open set is a countable union of elements in a given topological basis.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] {t : Set (Set α)} (ht : IsTopologicalBasis t) {u : Set α} (hu : IsOpen u) : ∃ s ⊆ t, s.Countable ∧ u = ⋃ a ∈ s, a

name: IsTopologicalBasis.exists_countable
informal: In a second countable topological space, any topological basis contains a countable subset which is also a topological basis.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] {t : Set (Set α)} (ht : IsTopologicalBasis t) : ∃ s ⊆ t, s.Countable ∧ IsTopologicalBasis s

name: exists_countable_of_generateFrom
informal: In a second countable topological space, any family generating the topology admits a countable generating subfamily.
signature: {α : Type*} [ts : TopologicalSpace α] [SecondCountableTopology α] {t : Set (Set α)} (ht : ts = generateFrom t) : ∃ s ⊆ t, s.Countable ∧ ts = generateFrom s

name: RelCWComplex.openCell_congr
informal: If two open cells are equal, so are the underlying cells.
signature: [RelCWComplex C D] (n : ℕ) {s t : cell C n} (st : openCell n s = openCell n t) : s = t

name: RelCWComplex.isClosed_of_disjoint_openCell_or_isClosed_inter_closedCell
informal: If for every cell either `A ∩ openCell n j` is empty or `A ∩ closedCell n j` is closed then `A` is closed.
signature: [RelCWComplex C D] [T2Space X] {A : Set X} (hAC : A ⊆ C) (hDA : IsClosed (A ∩ D)) (h : ∀ n (_ : 0 < n), ∀ (j : cell C n), Disjoint A (openCell n j) ∨ IsClosed (A ∩ closedCell n j)) : IsClosed A

name: CWComplex.isClosed_of_disjoint_openCell_or_isClosed_inter_closedCell
informal: If for every cell either `A ∩ openCell n j` is empty or `A ∩ closedCell n j` is closed then `A` is closed.
signature: [CWComplex C] [T2Space X] {A : Set X} (hAC : A ⊆ C) (h : ∀ n (_ : 0 < n), ∀ (j : cell C n), Disjoint A (openCell n j) ∨ IsClosed (A ∩ closedCell n j)) : IsClosed A

name: RelCWComplex.Subcomplex.union_closedCell
informal: A subcomplex is the union of its closed cells and its base.
signature: [T2Space X] [RelCWComplex C D] (E : Subcomplex C) : D ∪ ⋃ (n : ℕ) (j : E.I n), closedCell (C

name: mem_fixedPoints_of_iteratedDerivedSet_succ_eq
informal: If the iterated derived set stops changing at a successor stage, then `sᵈ[a]` is a fixed point of `relDerivSet`.
signature: (ha : sᵈ[a + 1] = sᵈ[a]) : sᵈ[a] ∈ fixedPoints relDerivedSet

name: isIso_of_bijective
informal: Any continuous bijection of light profinite spaces induces an isomorphism.
signature: (bij : Function.Bijective f) : IsIso f

name: functor_initial
informal: If the projection maps in the cone are epimorphic and the cone is limiting, then `LightProfinite.Extend.functor` is initial.
signature: (hc : IsLimit c) [∀ i, Epi (c.π.app i)] : Initial (functor c)

name: functorOp_final
informal: If the projection maps in the cone are epimorphic and the cone is limiting, then `LightProfinite.Extend.functorOp` is final.
signature: (hc : IsLimit c) [∀ i, Epi (c.π.app i)] : Final (functorOp c)

name: functor_initial
informal: If the projection maps in the cone are epimorphic and the cone is limiting, then `Profinite.Extend.functor` is initial. TODO: investigate how to weaken the assumption `∀ i, Epi (c.π.app i)` to `∀ i, ∃ j (_ : j ⟶ i), Epi (c.π.app j)`.
signature: (hc : IsLimit c) [∀ i, Epi (c.π.app i)] : Initial (functor c)

name: functorOp_final
informal: If the projection maps in the cone are epimorphic and the cone is limiting, then `Profinite.Extend.functorOp` is final.
signature: (hc : IsLimit c) [∀ i, Epi (c.π.app i)] : Final (functorOp c)

name: range_pullback_map
informal: If the map `S ⟶ T` is mono, then there is a description of the image of `W ×ₛ X ⟶ Y ×ₜ Z`.
signature: {W X Y Z S T : TopCat.{u}} (f₁ : W ⟶ S) (f₂ : X ⟶ S) (g₁ : Y ⟶ T) (g₂ : Z ⟶ T) (i₁ : W ⟶ Y) (i₂ : X ⟶ Z) (i₃ : S ⟶ T) [H₃ : Mono i₃] (eq₁ : f₁ ≫ i₃ = i₁ ≫ g₁) (eq₂ : f₂ ≫ i₃ = i₂ ≫ g₂) : Set.range (pullback.map f₁ f₂ g₁ g₂ i₁ i₂ i₃ eq₁ eq₂) = (pullback.fst g₁ g₂) ⁻¹' Set.range i₁ ∩ (pullback.snd g₁ g₂) ⁻¹' Set.range i₂

name: denseRange_coe
informal: If `X` is not a compact space, then the natural embedding `X → OnePoint X` has dense range.
signature: [NoncompactSpace X] : DenseRange ((↑) : X → OnePoint X)

name: not_continuous_cofiniteTopology_of_symm
informal: If `X` is an infinite type with discrete topology (e.g., `ℕ`), then the identity map from `CofiniteTopology (OnePoint X)` to `OnePoint X` is not continuous.
signature: [Infinite X] [DiscreteTopology X] : ¬Continuous (@CofiniteTopology.of (OnePoint X)).symm

name: le_nhds_of_unique_clusterPt
informal: If a filter has a unique cluster point `y` in a compact topological space, then the filter is less than or equal to `𝓝 y`.
signature: [CompactSpace X] {l : Filter X} {y : X} (h : ∀ x, ClusterPt x l → x = y) : l ≤ 𝓝 y

name: isCompactSystem_isCompact_isClosed
informal: The set of compact and closed sets is a compact system.
signature: (α : Type*) [TopologicalSpace α] : IsCompactSystem {s : Set α | IsCompact s ∧ IsClosed s}

name: isCompactSystem_insert_univ_isCompact_isClosed
informal: The set of sets which are either compact and closed, or `univ`, is a compact system.
signature: (α : Type*) [TopologicalSpace α] : IsCompactSystem (insert univ {s : Set α | IsCompact s ∧ IsClosed s})

name: IsLindelof.inter_right
informal: The intersection of a Lindelöf set and a closed set is a Lindelöf set.
signature: (hs : IsLindelof s) (ht : IsClosed t) : IsLindelof (s ∩ t)

name: IsLindelof.inter_left
informal: The intersection of a closed set and a Lindelöf set is a Lindelöf set.
signature: (ht : IsLindelof t) (hs : IsClosed s) : IsLindelof (s ∩ t)

name: IsLindelof.diff
informal: The set difference of a Lindelöf set and an open set is a Lindelöf set.
signature: (hs : IsLindelof s) (ht : IsOpen t) : IsLindelof (s \ t)

name: exists_compact_superset
informal: In a weakly locally compact space, every compact set is contained in the interior of a compact set.
signature: [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X] {K : Set X} (hK : IsCompact K) : ∃ K', IsCompact K' ∧ K ⊆ interior K'

name: disjoint_nhds_cocompact
informal: In a weakly locally compact space, the filters `𝓝 x` and `cocompact X` are disjoint for all `X`.
signature: [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X] (x : X) : Disjoint (𝓝 x) (cocompact X)

name: connectedComponent_pi
informal: The connected component of `x` in a product space is the product of the connected components of its coordinates.
signature: [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (X i)] (x : ∀ i, X i) : connectedComponent x = univ.pi fun i ↦ connectedComponent (x i)

name: subsingleton_of_disjoint_isClosed_iUnion_eq_univ
informal: In a preconnected space, any finite disjoint cover by non-empty closed subsets has at most one element.
signature: [Finite ι] (h_closed : ∀ i, IsClosed (s i)) (h_Union : ⋃ i, s i = univ) : Subsingleton ι

name: Topology.IsCoinducing.locallyConnectedSpace
informal: Any topology coinduced by a locally connected topology is locally connected.
signature: [LocallyConnectedSpace α] [TopologicalSpace β] {f : α → β} (hf : IsCoinducing f) : LocallyConnectedSpace β

name: Pi.locallyConnectedSpace_of_finite_not_preconnectedSpace
informal: If each `X i` is locally connected and all but finitely many are preconnected, then `∀ i, X i` is locally connected.
signature: [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (X i)] [∀ i, LocallyConnectedSpace (X i)] (hfinite : {i | ¬PreconnectedSpace (X i)}.Finite) : LocallyConnectedSpace (∀ i, X i)

name: Pi.locallyConnectedSpace_iff
informal: A product of spaces is locally connected iff it is empty, or every factor is locally connected and all but finitely many factors are preconnected.
signature: [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (X i)] : LocallyConnectedSpace (∀ i, X i) ↔ IsEmpty (∀ i, X i) ∨ (∀ i, LocallyConnectedSpace (X i)) ∧ {i | ¬PreconnectedSpace (X i)}.Finite

name: locallyPathConnectedSpace_iff_isOpen_pathComponentIn
informal: A space is locally path-connected iff all path components of open subsets are open.
signature: {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] : LocallyPathConnectedSpace X ↔ ∀ (x : X) (u : Set X), IsOpen u → IsOpen (pathComponentIn u x)

name: locallyPathConnectedSpace_iff_pathComponentIn_mem_nhds
informal: A space is locally path-connected iff all path components of open subsets are neighbourhoods.
signature: {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] : LocallyPathConnectedSpace X ↔ ∀ x : X, ∀ u : Set X, IsOpen u → x ∈ u → pathComponentIn u x ∈ nhds x

name: IsPathConnected.prod
informal: The product of two path-connected sets is path-connected.
signature: (hs : IsPathConnected s) (ht : IsPathConnected t) : IsPathConnected (s ×ˢ t)

name: DiscreteTopology.preimage_of_continuous_injective
informal: Let `s` be a discrete subset of a topological space. Then the preimage of `s` by a continuous injective map is also discrete.
signature: {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (s : Set Y) [DiscreteTopology s] {f : X → Y} (hc : Continuous f) (hinj : Function.Injective f) : DiscreteTopology (f ⁻¹' s)

name: Topology.IsInducing.sumElim
informal: If `f` and `g` are inducing maps whose ranges are separated, then `Sum.elim f g` is inducing.
signature: (hf : IsInducing f) (hg : IsInducing g) (hFg : Disjoint (closure (range f)) (range g)) (hfG : Disjoint (range f) (closure (range g))) : IsInducing (Sum.elim f g)

name: Topology.IsInducing.disjoint_of_sumElim_aux
informal: If `Sum.elim f g` is inducing, `closure (range f)` and `range g` must be disjoint. This is an auxiliary result towards proving `isInducing_sumElim`.
signature: (h : IsInducing (Sum.elim f g)) : Disjoint (closure (range f)) (range g)

name: Topology.IsEmbedding.sumElim
informal: If `f` and `g` are embeddings whose ranges are separated, `Sum.elim f g` is an embedding.
signature: (hf : IsEmbedding f) (hg : IsEmbedding g) (hFg : Disjoint (closure (range f)) (range g)) (hfG : Disjoint (range f) (closure (range g))) : IsEmbedding (Sum.elim f g)

name: polynomialFunctions.topologicalClosure
informal: Polynomial functions in are dense in `C(s, ℝ)` when `s` is compact. See `polynomialFunctions_closure_eq_top` for the special case `s = Set.Icc a b` which does not use the full Stone-Weierstrass theorem. Of course, that version could be used to prove this one as well.
signature: (s : Set ℝ) [CompactSpace s] : (polynomialFunctions s).topologicalClosure = ⊤

name: polynomialFunctions.starClosure_topologicalClosure
informal: The star subalgebra generated by polynomials functions is dense in `C(s, 𝕜)` when `s` is compact and `𝕜` is either `ℝ` or `ℂ`.
signature: {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] (s : Set 𝕜) [CompactSpace s] : (polynomialFunctions s).starClosure.topologicalClosure = ⊤

name: polynomialFunctions_closure_eq_top
informal: The **Weierstrass Approximation Theorem**: polynomials functions on `[a, b] ⊆ ℝ` are dense in `C([a,b],ℝ)` (While we could deduce this as an application of the Stone-Weierstrass theorem, our proof of that relies on the fact that `abs` is in the closure of polynomials on `[-M, M]`, so we may as well get this done first.)
signature: (a b : ℝ) : (polynomialFunctions (Set.Icc a b)).topologicalClosure = ⊤

name: ContinuousOn.mono_dom
informal: If a function is continuous on a set for some topologies, then it is continuous on the same set with respect to any finer topology on the source space.
signature: {α β : Type*} {t₁ t₂ : TopologicalSpace α} {t₃ : TopologicalSpace β} (h₁ : t₂ ≤ t₁) {s : Set α} {f : α → β} (h₂ : @ContinuousOn α β t₁ t₃ f s) : @ContinuousOn α β t₂ t₃ f s

name: ContinuousOn.mono_rng
informal: If a function is continuous on a set for some topologies, then it is continuous on the same set with respect to any coarser topology on the target space.
signature: {α β : Type*} {t₁ : TopologicalSpace α} {t₂ t₃ : TopologicalSpace β} (h₁ : t₂ ≤ t₃) {s : Set α} {f : α → β} (h₂ : @ContinuousOn α β t₁ t₂ f s) : @ContinuousOn α β t₁ t₃ f s

name: continuousWithinAt_congr_set
informal: If two sets coincide around `x`, then being continuous within one or the other at `x` is equivalent. See also `continuousWithinAt_congr_set'` which requires that the sets coincide locally away from a point `y`, in a T1 space.
signature: (h : s =ᶠ[𝓝 x] t) : ContinuousWithinAt f s x ↔ ContinuousWithinAt f t x

name: continuousWithinAt_of_not_accPt
informal: A function is continuous at a point `x` within a set `s` if `x` is not an accumulation point of `s`.
signature: (h : ¬AccPt x (𝓟 s)) : ContinuousWithinAt f s x

name: compl_finite_mem_codiscreteWithin
informal: In a `T1Space`, complements of finite sets are codiscrete within any set.
signature: {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [T1Space X] {s t : Set X} (h : t.Finite) : tᶜ ∈ codiscreteWithin s

name: _root_.BoundedVariationOn.exists_tendsto_left
informal: A bounded variation function has a limit on its left within a set.
signature: [CompleteSpace E] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] {f : α → E} {s : Set α} (hf : BoundedVariationOn f s) (x : α) : ∃ l, Tendsto f (𝓝[s ∩ Iio x] x) (𝓝 l)

name: _root_.BoundedVariationOn.exists_tendsto_right
informal: A bounded variation function has a limit on its right within a set.
signature: [CompleteSpace E] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] {f : α → E} {s : Set α} (hf : BoundedVariationOn f s) (x : α) : ∃ l, Tendsto f (𝓝[s ∩ Ioi x] x) (𝓝 l)

name: _root_.BoundedVariationOn.tendsto_leftLim
informal: A bounded variation function tends to its left-limit on its left.
signature: [CompleteSpace E] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] {f : α → E} (hf : BoundedVariationOn f univ) (x : α) : Tendsto f (𝓝[<] x) (𝓝 (f.leftLim x))

name: _root_.BoundedVariationOn.tendsto_rightLim
informal: A bounded variation function tends to its right-limit on its right.
signature: [CompleteSpace E] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] {f : α → E} (hf : BoundedVariationOn f univ) (x : α) : Tendsto f (𝓝[>] x) (𝓝 (f.rightLim x))

name: MonotoneOn.eVariationOn_eq
informal: The variation of a monotone real-valued function on `s ∩ Icc a b` equals its increment `f b - f a`.
signature: (hf : MonotoneOn f s) (as : a ∈ s) (bs : b ∈ s) : eVariationOn f (s ∩ Icc a b) = .ofReal (f b - f a)

name: edist_le_ediam_of_mem
informal: If two points belong to some set, their edistance is bounded by the diameter of the set
signature: (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) : edist x y ≤ ediam s

name: ediam_le
informal: If the distance between any two points in a set is bounded by some constant, this constant bounds the diameter.
signature: {d : ℝ≥0∞} (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, edist x y ≤ d) : ediam s ≤ d

name: ediam_union_le_add_edist
informal: The extended diameter of a union is controlled by the diameter of the sets, and the edistance between two points in the sets.
signature: (xs : x ∈ s) (yt : y ∈ t) : ediam (s ∪ t) ≤ ediam s + edist x y + ediam t

name: ediam_union_le
informal: If two sets have nonempty intersection, then the extended diameter of their union is estimated from above by the sum of their union.
signature: (h : (s ∩ t).Nonempty) : ediam (s ∪ t) ≤ ediam s + ediam t

name: ExtremallyDisconnected.disjoint_closure_of_disjoint_isOpen
informal: Lemma 2.2 in [Gleason, *Projective topological spaces*][gleason1958]: in an extremally disconnected space, if $U_1$ and $U_2$ are disjoint open sets, then $\overline{U_1}$ and $\overline{U_2}$ are also disjoint.
signature: [ExtremallyDisconnected A] {U₁ U₂ : Set A} (h : Disjoint U₁ U₂) (hU₁ : IsOpen U₁) (hU₂ : IsOpen U₂) : Disjoint (closure U₁) (closure U₂)

name: isHomeomorph_iff_continuous_bijective
informal: A map from a compact space to a T2 space is a homeomorphism iff it is continuous and bijective.
signature: [CompactSpace X] [T2Space Y] : IsHomeomorph f ↔ Continuous f ∧ Bijective f

name: StronglyLocallyContractibleSpace.locallyContractible
informal: The strong notion (contractible neighborhood basis) implies the classical notion (null-homotopic inclusions). The converse is false by the Borsuk-Mazurkiewicz counterexample [borsuk_mazurkiewicz1934]; see also [MO88628] for discussion and the Whitehead manifold example.
signature: [StronglyLocallyContractibleSpace X] : LocallyContractibleSpace X

name: comp_pi_eq_pi_comp
informal: Composition and products commute. This is `Path.trans_pi_eq_pi_trans` descended to path homotopy classes.
signature: (γ₀ : ∀ i, Path.Homotopic.Quotient (as i) (bs i)) (γ₁ : ∀ i, Path.Homotopic.Quotient (bs i) (cs i)) : pi γ₀ ⬝ pi γ₁ = pi fun i ↦ γ₀ i ⬝ γ₁ i

name: Continuous.specialization_monotone
informal: A continuous function is monotone with respect to the specialization preorders on the domain and the codomain.
signature: (hf : Continuous f) : Monotone f

name: Ico_ext
informal: If functions on AddCircle agree on the image of the interval `[a, a + p)` then they are equal
signature: {α : Type*} {f g : AddCircle p → α} (a : 𝕜) (h : ∀ x ∈ Ico a (a + p), f x = g x) : f = g

name: Ioc_ext
informal: If functions on AddCircle agree on the image of the interval `(a, a + p]` then they are equal
signature: {α : Type*} {f g : AddCircle p → α} (a : 𝕜) (h : ∀ x ∈ Ioc a (a + p), f x = g x) : f = g

name: dense_addSubgroupClosure_pair_iff
informal: The additive subgroup of real numbers generated by `a` and `b` is dense iff `a / b` is an irrational number. Here we rely on the fact that `a / 0 = 0` in Mathlib, so we don't need to add `b ≠ 0` as an assumption.
signature: {a b : ℝ} : Dense (AddSubgroup.closure {a, b} : Set ℝ) ↔ Irrational (a / b)

name: denseRange_zsmul_coe_iff
informal: The multiples of a number `a` are dense on a circle of length `p` iff `a / p` is irrational.
signature: {a p : ℝ} : DenseRange (· • a : ℤ → AddCircle p) ↔ Irrational (a / p)

name: denseRange_zsmul_iff
informal: The multiples of a number `a` are dense on a circle of length `p > 0` iff `a` has infinite additive order.
signature: {p : ℝ} [Fact (0 < p)] {a : AddCircle p} : DenseRange (· • a : ℤ → AddCircle p) ↔ addOrderOf a = 0

name: dense_addSubgroup_iff_ne_zmultiples
informal: A subgroup of the circle `ℝ⧸pℤ`, `p > 0`, is dense iff it is not generated by a single element of finite additive order.
signature: {p : ℝ} [Fact (0 < p)] {s : AddSubgroup (AddCircle p)} : Dense (s : Set (AddCircle p)) ↔ ∀ a, addOrderOf a ≠ 0 → s ≠ .zmultiples a

name: ofDigits_zero_two_sequence_mem_cantorSet
informal: If `x = 0.d₀d₁...` in base-3 (ternary), and none of the digits `dᵢ` is `1`, then `x` belongs to the Cantor set.
signature: {a : ℕ → Fin 3} (h : ∀ n, a n ≠ 1) : ofDigits a ∈ cantorSet

name: ofDigits_zero_two_sequence_unique
informal: If two base-3 representations using only digits `0` and `2` define the same number, then the sequences must be equal. This uniqueness fails for general base-3 representations (e.g. `0.1000... = 0.0222...`).
signature: {a b : ℕ → Fin 3} (ha : ∀ n, a n ≠ 1) (hb : ∀ n, b n ≠ 1) (h : ofDigits a = ofDigits b) : a = b

name: continuousAt_add
informal: The addition on `EReal` is continuous except where it doesn't make sense (i.e., at `(⊥, ⊤)` and at `(⊤, ⊥)`).
signature: {p : EReal × EReal} (h : p.1 ≠ ⊤ ∨ p.2 ≠ ⊥) (h' : p.1 ≠ ⊥ ∨ p.2 ≠ ⊤) : ContinuousAt (fun p : EReal × EReal => p.1 + p.2) p

name: continuousAt_mul
informal: The multiplication on `EReal` is continuous except at indeterminacies (i.e. whenever one value is zero and the other infinite).
signature: {p : EReal × EReal} (h₁ : p.1 ≠ 0 ∨ p.2 ≠ ⊥) (h₂ : p.1 ≠ 0 ∨ p.2 ≠ ⊤) (h₃ : p.1 ≠ ⊥ ∨ p.2 ≠ 0) (h₄ : p.1 ≠ ⊤ ∨ p.2 ≠ 0) : ContinuousAt (fun p : EReal × EReal ↦ p.1 * p.2) p

name: Real.tendsto_atTop_csSup_of_monotoneOn_bddAbove_nat_Ici
informal: A monotone, bounded above sequence `f : ℕ → ℝ` on `Ici k` has the finite limit `sSup (f '' Ici k)`.

signature: {α} [TopologicalSpace α] [TopologicalSpace β] [DiscreteTopology β] {f : α → β} : Continuous f ↔ ∀ b : β, IsOpen (f ⁻¹' {b})

name: discreteTopology_iff_nhds
informal: This lemma characterizes discrete topological spaces as those whose singletons are neighbourhoods.
signature: [TopologicalSpace α] : DiscreteTopology α ↔ ∀ x : α, 𝓝 x = pure x

name: exists_countable_generateFrom_Ioi_Iio
informal: In a second countable topological space with the order topology, the topology is generated by half-infinite open intervals with endpoints in a countable set.
signature: [OrderTopology α] [SecondCountableTopology α] : ∃ (c : Set α), c.Countable ∧ ts = generateFrom { s | ∃ a ∈ c, s = Ioi a ∨ s = Iio a }

name: StrictMono.isEmbedding_of_ordConnected
informal: A strictly monotone function between linear orders with order topology is a topological embedding provided that the range of `f` is order-connected.
signature: {α β : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [LinearOrder β] [TopologicalSpace α] [h : OrderTopology α] [TopologicalSpace β] [OrderTopology β] {f : α → β} (hf : StrictMono f) (hc : OrdConnected (range f)) : IsEmbedding f

name: OrderEmbedding.isEmbedding_of_ordConnected
informal: An `OrderEmbedding` is a topological embedding provided that the range of `f` is order-connected
signature: {α β : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [LinearOrder β] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] [TopologicalSpace β] [OrderTopology β] (f : α ↪o β) (hc : OrdConnected (range f)) : Topology.IsEmbedding f

name: SecondCountableTopology.of_separableSpace_orderTopology
informal: Let `α` be a densely ordered linear order with order topology. If `α` is a separable space, then it has second countable topology. Note that the "densely ordered" assumption cannot be dropped, see [double arrow space](https://topology.pi-base.org/spaces/S000093) for a counterexample.
signature: [DenselyOrdered α] [SeparableSpace α] : SecondCountableTopology α

name: countable_of_isolated_left'
informal: The set of points which are isolated on the left is countable when the space is second-countable.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] : Set.Countable { x : α | ∃ y, y < x ∧ Ioo y x = ∅ }

name: LeftOrdContinuous.continuousWithinAt_Iic
informal: An order-theoretically left-continuous function is topologically left-continuous, assuming the function is between conditionally complete linear orders with order topologies.
signature: (hf : LeftOrdContinuous f) : ContinuousWithinAt f (Iic x) x

name: Continuous.of_ordContinuous
informal: A function that is order-theoretically both left- and right-continuous is continuous, assuming the function is between conditionally complete linear orders with order topologies.
signature: (hl : LeftOrdContinuous f) (hr : RightOrdContinuous f) : Continuous f

name: Continuous.exists_forall_le
informal: The **extreme value theorem**: if a continuous function `f` tends to infinity away from compact sets, then it has a global minimum.
signature: [ClosedIicTopology α] [Nonempty β] {f : β → α} (hf : Continuous f) (hlim : Tendsto f (cocompact β) atTop) : ∃ x, ∀ y, f x ≤ f y

name: Continuous.exists_forall_ge
informal: The **extreme value theorem**: if a continuous function `f` tends to negative infinity away from compact sets, then it has a global maximum.
signature: [ClosedIciTopology α] [Nonempty β] {f : β → α} (hf : Continuous f) (hlim : Tendsto f (cocompact β) atBot) : ∃ x, ∀ y, f y ≤ f x

name: closure_Iio'
informal: The closure of the interval `(-∞, a)` is the closed interval `(-∞, a]`, unless `a` is a bottom element.
signature: (h : (Iio a).Nonempty) : closure (Iio a) = Iic a

name: DenselyOrdered.subsingleton_of_discreteTopology
informal: If the order topology for a dense linear ordering is discrete, the space has at most one point. We would prefer for this to be an instance but even at `(priority := 100)` this was problematic so we have deferred this issue. TODO Promote this to an `instance`!
signature: [DiscreteTopology α] : Subsingleton α

name: exists_countable_dense_no_bot_top
informal: If `α` is a nontrivial separable dense linear order, then there exists a countable dense set `s : Set α` that contains neither top nor bottom elements of `α`. For a dense set containing both bot and top elements, see `exists_countable_dense_bot_top`.
signature: [SeparableSpace α] [Nontrivial α] : ∃ s : Set α, s.Countable ∧ Dense s ∧ (∀ x, IsBot x → x ∉ s) ∧ ∀ x, IsTop x → x ∉ s

name: mem_nhdsGT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset
informal: A set is a neighborhood of `a` within `(a, +∞)` if and only if it contains an interval `(a, u)` with `a < u`.
signature: [NoMaxOrder α] {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ∈ 𝓝[>] a ↔ ∃ u ∈ Ioi a, Ioo a u ⊆ s

name: countable_setOfPred_isolated_right
informal: The set of points which are isolated on the right is countable when the space is second-countable.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] : { x : α | 𝓝[>] x = ⊥ }.Countable

name: countable_setOfPred_isolated_left
informal: The set of points which are isolated on the left is countable when the space is second-countable.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] : { x : α | 𝓝[<] x = ⊥ }.Countable

name: countable_setOfPred_isolated_right_within
informal: The set of points in a set which are isolated on the right in this set is countable when the space is second-countable.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] {s : Set α} : { x ∈ s | 𝓝[s ∩ Ioi x] x = ⊥ }.Countable

name: countable_setOfPred_isolated_left_within
informal: The set of points in a set which are isolated on the left in this set is countable when the space is second-countable.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] {s : Set α} : { x ∈ s | 𝓝[s ∩ Iio x] x = ⊥ }.Countable

name: mem_nhdsGT_iff_exists_Ioc_subset
informal: A set is a neighborhood of `a` within `(a, +∞)` if and only if it contains an interval `(a, u]` with `a < u`.
signature: [NoMaxOrder α] [DenselyOrdered α] {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ∈ 𝓝[>] a ↔ ∃ u ∈ Ioi a, Ioc a u ⊆ s

name: mem_nhdsLT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset
informal: A set is a neighborhood of `a` within `(-∞, a)` if and only if it contains an interval `(l, a)` with `l < a`.
signature: [NoMinOrder α] {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ∈ 𝓝[<] a ↔ ∃ l ∈ Iio a, Ioo l a ⊆ s

name: mem_nhdsLT_iff_exists_Ico_subset
informal: A set is a neighborhood of `a` within `(-∞, a)` if and only if it contains an interval `[l, a)` with `l < a`.
signature: [NoMinOrder α] [DenselyOrdered α] {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ∈ 𝓝[<] a ↔ ∃ l ∈ Iio a, Ico l a ⊆ s

name: mem_nhdsGE_iff_exists_Ico_subset
informal: A set is a neighborhood of `a` within `[a, +∞)` if and only if it contains an interval `[a, u)` with `a < u`.
signature: [NoMaxOrder α] {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ∈ 𝓝[≥] a ↔ ∃ u ∈ Ioi a, Ico a u ⊆ s

name: nhdsGE_basis_Icc
informal: The filter of right neighborhoods has a basis of closed intervals.
signature: [NoMaxOrder α] [DenselyOrdered α] {a : α} : (𝓝[≥] a).HasBasis (a < ·) (Icc a)

name: mem_nhdsGE_iff_exists_Icc_subset
informal: A set is a neighborhood of `a` within `[a, +∞)` if and only if it contains an interval `[a, u]` with `a < u`.
signature: [NoMaxOrder α] [DenselyOrdered α] {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ∈ 𝓝[≥] a ↔ ∃ u, a < u ∧ Icc a u ⊆ s

name: mem_nhdsLE_iff_exists_Ioc_subset
informal: A set is a neighborhood of `a` within `(-∞, a]` if and only if it contains an interval `(l, a]` with `l < a`.
signature: [NoMinOrder α] {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ∈ 𝓝[≤] a ↔ ∃ l ∈ Iio a, Ioc l a ⊆ s

name: mem_nhdsLE_iff_exists_Icc_subset
informal: A set is a neighborhood of `a` within `(-∞, a]` if and only if it contains an interval `[l, a]` with `l < a`.
signature: [NoMinOrder α] [DenselyOrdered α] {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ∈ 𝓝[≤] a ↔ ∃ l, l < a ∧ Icc l a ⊆ s

name: nhdsLE_basis_Icc
informal: The filter of left neighborhoods has a basis of closed intervals.
signature: [NoMinOrder α] [DenselyOrdered α] {a : α} : (𝓝[≤] a).HasBasis (· < a) (Icc · a)

name: isLowerSet_of_isOpen
informal: Every set open in the lower topology is a lower set.
signature: (h : IsOpen s) : IsLowerSet s

name: isUpperSet_of_isOpen
informal: Every set open in the upper topology is an upper set.
signature: (h : IsOpen s) : IsUpperSet s

name: MonotoneOn.countable_setOfPred_two_preimages
informal: If a function is monotone on a set in a second countable topological space, then there are only countably many points that have several preimages.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] (hf : MonotoneOn f s) : Set.Countable {c | ∃ x y, x ∈ s ∧ y ∈ s ∧ x < y ∧ f x = c ∧ f y = c}

name: Monotone.countable_setOfPred_two_preimages
informal: If a function is monotone in a second countable topological space, then there are only countably many points that have several preimages.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] (hf : Monotone f) : Set.Countable {c | ∃ x y, x < y ∧ f x = c ∧ f y = c}

name: AntitoneOn.countable_setOfPred_two_preimages
informal: If a function is antitone on a set in a second countable topological space, then there are only countably many points that have several preimages.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] (hf : AntitoneOn f s) : Set.Countable {c | ∃ x y, x ∈ s ∧ y ∈ s ∧ x < y ∧ f x = c ∧ f y = c}

name: Antitone.countable_setOfPred_two_preimages
informal: If a function is antitone in a second countable topological space, then there are only countably many points that have several preimages.
signature: [SecondCountableTopology α] (hf : Antitone f) : Set.Countable {c | ∃ x y, x < y ∧ f x = c ∧ f y = c}

name: MonotoneOn.countable_not_continuousWithinAt_Ioi
informal: In a second countable space, the set of points where a monotone function is not right-continuous within a set is at most countable. Superseded by `MonotoneOn.countable_not_continuousWithinAt` which gives the two-sided version.
signature: (hf : MonotoneOn f s) : Set.Countable {x ∈ s | ¬ContinuousWithinAt f (s ∩ Ioi x) x}

name: MonotoneOn.countable_not_continuousWithinAt_Iio
informal: In a second countable space, the set of points where a monotone function is not left-continuous within a set is at most countable. Superseded by `MonotoneOn.countable_not_continuousWithinAt` which gives the two-sided version.
signature: (hf : MonotoneOn f s) : Set.Countable {x ∈ s | ¬ContinuousWithinAt f (s ∩ Iio x) x}

name: MonotoneOn.countable_not_continuousWithinAt
informal: In a second countable space, the set of points where a monotone function is not continuous within a set is at most countable.
signature: (hf : MonotoneOn f s) : Set.Countable {x ∈ s | ¬ContinuousWithinAt f s x}

name: Monotone.countable_not_continuousAt
informal: In a second countable space, the set of points where a monotone function is not continuous is at most countable.
signature: (hf : Monotone f) : Set.Countable {x | ¬ContinuousAt f x}

name: Antitone.countable_not_continuousAt
informal: In a second countable space, the set of points where an antitone function is not continuous is at most countable.
signature: (hf : Antitone f) : Set.Countable {x | ¬ContinuousAt f x}

name: Monotone.tendsto_nhdsLT
informal: A monotone map has a limit to the left of any point `x`, equal to `sSup (f '' (Iio x))`.
signature: {α β : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder β] [TopologicalSpace β] [OrderTopology β] {f : α → β} (Mf : Monotone f) (x : α) : Tendsto f (𝓝[<] x) (𝓝 (sSup (f '' Iio x)))

name: Monotone.tendsto_nhdsGT
informal: A monotone map has a limit to the right of any point `x`, equal to `sInf (f '' (Ioi x))`.
signature: {α β : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder β] [TopologicalSpace β] [OrderTopology β] {f : α → β} (Mf : Monotone f) (x : α) : Tendsto f (𝓝[>] x) (𝓝 (sInf (f '' Ioi x)))

name: Antitone.tendsto_nhdsLT
informal: An antitone map has a limit to the left of any point `x`, equal to `sInf (f '' (Iio x))`.
signature: {α β : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder β] [TopologicalSpace β] [OrderTopology β] {f : α → β} (Af : Antitone f) (x : α) : Tendsto f (𝓝[<] x) (𝓝 (sInf (f '' Iio x)))

name: Antitone.tendsto_nhdsGT
informal: An antitone map has a limit to the right of any point `x`, equal to `sSup (f '' (Ioi x))`.
signature: {α β : Type*} [LinearOrder α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder β] [TopologicalSpace β] [OrderTopology β] {f : α → β} (Af : Antitone f) (x : α) : Tendsto f (𝓝[>] x) (𝓝 (sSup (f '' Ioi x)))

name: exists_Ioo_extr_on_Icc
informal: A continuous function on a closed interval with `f a = f b` takes either its maximum or its minimum value at a point in the interior of the interval.
signature: (hab : a < b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hfI : f a = f b) : ∃ c ∈ Ioo a b, IsExtrOn f (Icc a b) c

name: exists_isLocalExtr_Ioo
informal: A continuous function on a closed interval with `f a = f b` has a local extremum at some point of the corresponding open interval.
signature: (hab : a < b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hfI : f a = f b) : ∃ c ∈ Ioo a b, IsLocalExtr f c

name: exists_isExtrOn_Ioo_of_tendsto
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on an open interval and tends to the same value at its endpoints, then it has an extremum on this open interval.
signature: (hab : a < b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Ioo a b)) (ha : Tendsto f (𝓝[>] a) (𝓝 l)) (hb : Tendsto f (𝓝[<] b) (𝓝 l)) : ∃ c ∈ Ioo a b, IsExtrOn f (Ioo a b) c

name: exists_isLocalExtr_Ioo_of_tendsto
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on an open interval and tends to the same value at its endpoints, then it has a local extremum on this open interval.
signature: (hab : a < b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Ioo a b)) (ha : Tendsto f (𝓝[>] a) (𝓝 l)) (hb : Tendsto f (𝓝[<] b) (𝓝 l)) : ∃ c ∈ Ioo a b, IsLocalExtr f c

name: exists_uIoo_isExtrOn_uIcc
informal: A continuous function on an unordered closed interval with `f a = f b` takes either its maximum or its minimum value at a point in the interior of the interval.
signature: (hab : a ≠ b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (uIcc a b)) (hfI : f a = f b) : ∃ c ∈ uIoo a b, IsExtrOn f (uIcc a b) c

name: exists_isLocalExtr_uIoo
informal: A continuous function on a unordered closed interval with `f a = f b` has a local extremum at some point of the corresponding unordered open interval.
signature: (hab : a ≠ b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (uIcc a b)) (hfI : f a = f b) : ∃ c ∈ uIoo a b, IsLocalExtr f c

name: exists_isExtrOn_uIoo_of_tendsto
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on an unordered open interval and tends to the same value at its endpoints, then it has an extremum on this unordered open interval.
signature: (hab : a ≠ b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (uIoo a b)) (ha : Tendsto f (𝓝[uIoo a b] a) (𝓝 l)) (hb : Tendsto f (𝓝[uIoo a b] b) (𝓝 l)) : ∃ c ∈ uIoo a b, IsExtrOn f (uIoo a b) c

name: exists_isLocalExtr_uIoo_of_tendsto
informal: If a function `f` is continuous on an unordered open interval and tends to the same value at its endpoints, then it has a local extremum on this unordered open interval.
signature: (hab : a ≠ b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (uIoo a b)) (ha : Tendsto f (𝓝[uIoo a b] a) (𝓝 l)) (hb : Tendsto f (𝓝[uIoo a b] b) (𝓝 l)) : ∃ c ∈ uIoo a b, IsLocalExtr f c

name: isEmbedding
informal: A partial homeomorphism whose source is all of `X` defines an embedding of `X` into `Y`. The converse is also true; see `IsEmbedding.toPartialHomeomorph`.
signature: (h : e.source = Set.univ) : IsEmbedding e

name: UpperHemicontinuousWithinAt.union
informal: Pointwise unions of upper hemicontinuous maps are upper hemicontinuous.
signature: (hf : UpperHemicontinuousWithinAt f s x) (hg : UpperHemicontinuousWithinAt g s x) : UpperHemicontinuousWithinAt (fun x ↦ f x ∪ g x) s x

name: UpperHemicontinuousOn.union
informal: Pointwise unions of upper hemicontinuous maps are upper hemicontinuous.
signature: (hf : UpperHemicontinuousOn f s) (hg : UpperHemicontinuousOn g s) : UpperHemicontinuousOn (fun x ↦ f x ∪ g x) s

name: UpperHemicontinuousAt.union
informal: Pointwise unions of upper hemicontinuous maps are upper hemicontinuous.
signature: (hf : UpperHemicontinuousAt f x) (hg : UpperHemicontinuousAt g x) : UpperHemicontinuousAt (fun x ↦ f x ∪ g x) x

name: UpperHemicontinuous.union
informal: Pointwise unions of upper hemicontinuous maps are upper hemicontinuous.
signature: (hf : UpperHemicontinuous f) (hg : UpperHemicontinuous g) : UpperHemicontinuous (fun x ↦ f x ∪ g x)

name: UpperHemicontinuousWithinAt.isInducing_comp
informal: Post-composition with the preimage of an inducing function whose range is closed preserves upper hemicontinuity.
signature: (hf : UpperHemicontinuousWithinAt f s x) (hi : IsInducing i) (h_cl : IsClosed (range i)) : UpperHemicontinuousWithinAt (fun x ↦ i ⁻¹' (f x)) s x

name: UpperHemicontinuousOn.isInducing_comp
informal: Post-composition with the preimage of an inducing function whose range is closed preserves upper hemicontinuity.
signature: (hf : UpperHemicontinuousOn f s) (hi : IsInducing i) (h_cl : IsClosed (range i)) : UpperHemicontinuousOn (fun x ↦ i ⁻¹' (f x)) s

name: UpperHemicontinuousAt.isInducing_comp
informal: Post-composition with the preimage of an inducing function whose range is closed preserves upper hemicontinuity.
signature: (hf : UpperHemicontinuousAt f x) (hi : IsInducing i) (h_cl : IsClosed (range i)) : UpperHemicontinuousAt (fun x ↦ i ⁻¹' (f x)) x

name: UpperHemicontinuous.isInducing_comp
informal: Post-composition with the preimage of an inducing function whose range is closed preserves upper hemicontinuity.
signature: (hf : UpperHemicontinuous f) (hi : IsInducing i) (h_cl : IsClosed (range i)) : UpperHemicontinuous (fun x ↦ i ⁻¹' (f x))

name: eq_of_comp_eq
informal: If `p` is a locally injective separated map, and `A` is a connected space, then two lifts `g₁, g₂ : A → E` of a map `f : A → X` are equal if they agree at one point.
signature: [PreconnectedSpace A] (h₁ : Continuous g₁) (h₂ : Continuous g₂) (he : p ∘ g₁ = p ∘ g₂) (a : A) (ha : g₁ a = g₂ a) : g₁ = g₂

name: IsClosed.exists_closed_singleton
informal: Given a closed set `S` in a compact T₀ space, there is some `x ∈ S` such that `{x}` is closed.
signature: [T0Space X] [CompactSpace X] {S : Set X} (hS : IsClosed S) (hne : S.Nonempty) : ∃ x : X, x ∈ S ∧ IsClosed ({x} : Set X)

name: exists_isOpen_singleton_of_isOpen_finite
informal: Given an open finite set `S` in a T₀ space, there is some `x ∈ S` such that `{x}` is open.
signature: [T0Space X] {s : Set X} (hfin : s.Finite) (hne : s.Nonempty) (ho : IsOpen s) : ∃ x ∈ s, IsOpen ({x} : Set X)

name: insert_mem_nhdsWithin_of_subset_insert
informal: If `t` is a subset of `s`, except for one point, then `insert x s` is a neighborhood of `x` within `t`.
signature: [T1Space X] {x y : X} {s t : Set X} (hu : t ⊆ insert y s) : insert x s ∈ 𝓝[t] x

name: Dense.sdiff_singleton
informal: Removing a non-isolated point from a dense set, one still obtains a dense set.
signature: [T1Space X] {s : Set X} (hs : Dense s) (x : X) [NeBot (𝓝[≠] x)] : Dense (s \ {x})

name: Dense.sdiff_finset
informal: Removing a finset from a dense set in a space without isolated points, one still obtains a dense set.
signature: [T1Space X] [∀ x : X, NeBot (𝓝[≠] x)] {s : Set X} (hs : Dense s) (t : Finset X) : Dense (s \ t)

name: Dense.sdiff_finite
informal: Removing a finite set from a dense set in a space without isolated points, one still obtains a dense set.
signature: [T1Space X] [∀ x : X, NeBot (𝓝[≠] x)] {s : Set X} (hs : Dense s) {t : Set X} (ht : t.Finite) : Dense (s \ t)

name: continuousWithinAt_congr_set'
informal: If two sets coincide locally around `x`, except maybe at `y`, then it is equivalent to be continuous at `x` within one set or the other.
signature: [TopologicalSpace Y] [T1Space X] {x : X} {s t : Set X} {f : X → Y} (y : X) (h : s =ᶠ[𝓝[{y}ᶜ] x] t) : ContinuousWithinAt f s x ↔ ContinuousWithinAt f t x

name: infinite_of_mem_nhds
informal: If the punctured neighborhoods of a point form a nontrivial filter, then any neighborhood is infinite.
signature: {X} [TopologicalSpace X] [T1Space X] (x : X) [hx : NeBot (𝓝[≠] x)] {s : Set X} (hs : s ∈ 𝓝 x) : Set.Infinite s

name: Set.InjOn.exists_mem_nhdsSet
informal: If a function `f` is - injective on a compact set `s`; - continuous at every point of this set; - injective on a neighborhood of each point of this set, then it is injective on a neighborhood of this set.
signature: {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y] {f : X → Y} {s : Set X} (inj : InjOn f s) (sc : IsCompact s) (fc : ∀ x ∈ s, ContinuousAt f x) (loc : ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ u ∈ 𝓝 x, InjOn f u) : ∃ t ∈ 𝓝ˢ s, InjOn f t

name: Set.InjOn.exists_isOpen_superset
informal: If a function `f` is - injective on a compact set `s`; - continuous at every point of this set; - injective on a neighborhood of each point of this set, then it is injective on an open neighborhood of this set.
signature: {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y] {f : X → Y} {s : Set X} (inj : InjOn f s) (sc : IsCompact s) (fc : ∀ x ∈ s, ContinuousAt f x) (loc : ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ u ∈ 𝓝 x, InjOn f u) : ∃ t, IsOpen t ∧ s ⊆ t ∧ InjOn f t

name: SeparatedNhds.of_isClosed_isCompact_closure_compl_isClosed
informal: In a `R1Space X`, for disjoint closed sets `s t` such that `closure sᶜ` is compact, there are neighbourhoods that separate `s` and `t`.
signature: [R1Space X] {s : Set X} {t : Set X} (H1 : IsClosed s) (H2 : IsCompact (closure sᶜ)) (H3 : IsClosed t) (H4 : Disjoint s t) : SeparatedNhds s t

name: Continuous.isClosedEmbedding
informal: A continuous injective map from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a closed embedding.
signature: [CompactSpace X] [T2Space Y] {f : X → Y} (h : Continuous f) (hf : Function.Injective f) : IsClosedEmbedding f

name: Topology.IsQuotientMap.of_surjective_continuous
informal: A continuous surjective map from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a quotient map.
signature: [CompactSpace X] [T2Space Y] {f : X → Y} (hsurj : Surjective f) (hcont : Continuous f) : IsQuotientMap f

name: two_pow_mk_le_two_pow_mk_dense
informal: Let `s` be a closed set in a normal space and `d` be a dense set. If the induced topology on `s` is discrete, then `𝒫 s` has cardinality less than or equal to `𝒫 d`.
signature: [NormalSpace X] {s d : Set X} (hs : IsClosed s) [DiscreteTopology s] (hd : Dense d) : (2 : Cardinal) ^ #s ≤ 2 ^ #d

name: mk_lt_continuum
informal: Let `s` be a closed set in a separable normal space. If the induced topology on `s` is discrete, then `s` has cardinality less than continuum.
signature: [NormalSpace X] {s : Set X} (hs : IsClosed s) [DiscreteTopology s] : #s < 𝔠

name: loc_compact_Haus_tot_disc_of_zero_dim
informal: A locally compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space has a basis with clopen elements.
signature: [TotallyDisconnectedSpace H] : IsTopologicalBasis { s : Set H | IsClopen s }

name: connectedComponent_eq_iInter_isClopen
informal: In a compact T₂ space, the connected component of a point equals the intersection of all its clopen neighbourhoods.
signature: [T2Space X] [CompactSpace X] (x : X) : connectedComponent x = ⋂ s : { s : Set X // IsClopen s ∧ x ∈ s }, s

name: mem_closure_iff_seq_limit
informal: In a Fréchet-Urysohn space, a point belongs to the closure of a set iff it is a limit of a sequence taking values in this set.
signature: [FrechetUrysohnSpace X] {s : Set X} {a : X} : a ∈ closure s ↔ ∃ x : ℕ → X, (∀ n : ℕ, x n ∈ s) ∧ Tendsto x atTop (𝓝 a)

name: IsSeqCompact.range
informal: The range of sequentially continuous function on a sequentially compact space is sequentially compact.
signature: [SeqCompactSpace X] (f_cont : SeqContinuous f) : IsSeqCompact (Set.range f)

name: apply_eq_of_chain
informal: If two partial refinements `v₁`, `v₂` belong to a chain (hence, they are comparable) and `i` belongs to the carriers of both partial refinements, then `v₁ i = v₂ i`.
signature: {c : Set (PartialRefinement u s p)} (hc : IsChain (· ≤ ·) c) {v₁ v₂} (h₁ : v₁ ∈ c) (h₂ : v₂ ∈ c) {i} (hi₁ : i ∈ v₁.carrier) (hi₂ : i ∈ v₂.carrier) : v₁ i = v₂ i

name: nhdsSet_diagonal_eq_uniformity
informal: On a compact uniform space, the topology determines the uniform structure, entourages are exactly the neighborhoods of the diagonal.
signature: [CompactSpace α] : 𝓝ˢ (diagonal α) = 𝓤 α

name: compactSpace_uniformity
informal: On a compact uniform space, the topology determines the uniform structure, entourages are exactly the neighborhoods of the diagonal.
signature: [CompactSpace α] : 𝓤 α = ⨆ x, 𝓝 (x, x)

name: Continuous.tendstoUniformly
informal: A continuous family of functions `α → β → γ` tends uniformly to its value at `x` if `α` is weakly locally compact and `β` is compact.
signature: [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace α] [CompactSpace β] [UniformSpace γ] (f : α → β → γ) (h : Continuous ↿f) (x : α) : TendstoUniformly f (f x) (𝓝 x)

name: uniformContinuous_extend
informal: Given a path `γ`, it extension to the real line `γ.extend : C(ℝ, X)` is a uniformly continuous function.
signature: (γ : Path x y) : UniformContinuous γ.extend

name: eq_convexComb
informal: A point between two points in a closed interval can be expressed as a convex combination of them.
signature: {a b : ℝ} {x y z : Icc a b} (hxy : x ≤ y) (hyz : y ≤ z) : y = convexComb x z ⟨((y - x) / (z - x)), eq_convexComb.zero_le hxy hyz, eq_convexComb.le_one hxy hyz⟩

name: exists_monotone_Icc_subset_open_cover_Icc
informal: Any open cover `c` of a closed interval `[a, b]` in ℝ can be refined to a finite partition into subintervals.
signature: {ι} {a b : ℝ} (h : a ≤ b) {c : ι → Set (Icc a b)} (hc₁ : ∀ i, IsOpen (c i)) (hc₂ : univ ⊆ ⋃ i, c i) : ∃ t : ℕ → Icc a b, t 0 = a ∧ Monotone t ∧ (∃ m, ∀ n ≥ m, t n = b) ∧ ∀ n, ∃ i, Icc (t n) (t (n + 1)) ⊆ c i
